Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain
articles.abstract: Background We aimed to establish thresholds for assessing clinically meaningful pain improvement after spinal injections using numerical rating scale (NRS) and patient-reported relative reduction (PRR) of pain. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,828 patients who received spinal injections at our spinal intervention center and completed a 2-week follow-up telephone interview in 2017. NRS absolute and relative reductions were calculated using the NRS scores before injection and at follow-up. The PRR and 5-point global perceived effect (GPE; 1, completely recovered; 2, much improved; 3, slightly improved; 4, no change; and 5, worsened) were recorded. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of NRS absolute reduction, NRS relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and 3 subgroups were calculated. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the cutoffs for NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR in predicting the substantial clinically important difference (SCID, GPE 1–2) and minimal clinically important difference (MCID, GPE 1–3). Results The mean ± SD of NRS absolute and relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and GPE 3 were 4.5 ± 1.8, 65.4% ± 21.1%, and 67.7% ± 14.8% and 2.4 ± 1.4, 36.8% ± 22.5%, and 35.7% ± 16.1%, respectively. The cutoffs for predicting SCID and MCID were NRS absolute reduction of ≥3 and ≥1, NRS relative reduction of ≥50% and ≥10%, and PRR of ≥50% and ≥20%, respectively. Conclusions The NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR thresholds were established to differentiate SCID and MCID in terms of pain improvement after spinal injections.

articles.title: Dissociation between muscle activation, spinal joint load, and subjective perception in passive back support exoskeleton use
articles.abstract: One important purpose of back support exoskeletons (BSEs) is to reduce the stress to the lumbar spine and alleviate the low back pain. However, most previous studies introducing BSEs have argued for their effectiveness based only on easily measurable physiological outcomes such as muscle activation. Motivated by this gap, we examined whether the muscle activation of the back muscle during load handling with a passive BSE can faithfully reflect the estimated L5–S1 joint reaction forces and subjective perceptions. Experiments involving 12 healthy young adults revealed that the BSE significantly reduced average thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during both lifting and lowering the load, and lumbar erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. The BSE also reduced integrated thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. L5–S1 joint reaction forces were also significantly reduced by the BSE (p < 0.001). Participants reported a lower rate of perceived exertion (p < 0.05). However, the lack of associations among all metrics suggests that inferring one measure from another remains limited when evaluating the efficacy of a BSE.

articles.title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates
articles.abstract: Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students’ confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates (N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero (r = −.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = −.276, p p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.

articles.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh
articles.abstract: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6–18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0–24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3–14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9–15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2–5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001–1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8–10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4–6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2–6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.

articles.title: Exploratory baseline mucosal transcriptomics and vedolizumab response in ulcerative colitis
articles.abstract: Currently, there are still no reliable pre-treatment biomarkers for vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis. To investigate baseline mucosal signals, we reconstructed the discovery cohort from GSE73661 and evaluated the derived panel in the blood samples from GSE191328 and the independent mucosal RNA-seq cohorts from E-MTAB-7845. The reconstructed cohort comprised 24 baseline samples, including 14 composite responders and 10 non-responders. Through repeated LASSO variable selection, the study identified an exploratory gene set consisting of ZNF689, TPRXL, ZC3H10, and MRPL55. The selection procedure yielded a mean held-out AUC of 0.611 across 18 complete nested-validation repetitions; this does not independently validate the final gene set. When the fixed gene set was projected exploratorily, the AUC for 17 blood samples was 0.458 (95% CI 0.162–0.755), and the AUC for 27 independent UC mucosal samples was 0.534 (95% CI 0.293–0.775). The apparent AUC of this gene set on the discovery set was 1.000, and 500 full-process bootstrap analyses indicated that gene selection was unstable. Among the three targeted inflammatory panels, interferon-γ showed a directional difference that was not statistically significant (mean GSVA score difference −0.425; nominal P = 0.066; adjusted P = 0.197). Expression scales and clinical endpoints differed across cohorts. The above results describe post-selection separation within the discovery cohort and do not establish reproducible predictive performance, tissue specificity, or a definitive four-gene signature.

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Spatial and temporal differences and convergence analysis of multidimensional relative poverty in ethnic areas
From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children
articles.abstract: This longitudinal study examines how preschool children’s phonological awareness and emergent literacy skills relate to their early writing performance in first grade. Conducted within the context of a transparent Turkish orthography, the study aims to identify early cognitive-linguistic correlates of subsequent writing development. A total of 97 children (aged 66–77 months) from preschools in a socioeconomically diverse Turkish district were followed over two academic years. In the first year, participants were assessed using the LAP-3 Early Literacy Subtest and the Phonological Awareness Test to measure their emergent literacy and phonological skills. One year later, their writing performance was evaluated using a validated sentence construction assessment. Non-parametric statistical tests and correlation analyses were conducted to examine developmental variations and relationships among the variables. Results revealed statistically significant correlations between early writing performance and both phonological awareness (r = .46, p < .01) and emergent literacy (r = .32, p < .01). Specific sub-skills such as syllable segmentation, rhyming awareness, and letter-sound correspondence showed the strongest associations with writing performance. These skills did not differ significantly by age or gender. The findings highlight the foundational role of preschool phonological and emergent literacy skills in early writing development. This study contributes empirical data from a transparent orthography. Given the correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with developmental literacy theories rather than as confirmation of causal or predictive mechanisms; they emphasize the importance of early identification and instructional support in preschool settings to promote future writing success.

articles.title: Gene density homogeneity is disrupted by repetitive DNA Expansion
articles.abstract: The democratization of sequencing has led to a wealth of high-quality genome assemblies from across the Tree of Life. One pattern that has emerged is that chromosomes within a genome can vary drastically in their gene density (e.g., human chromosomes 13 and 19, with gene densities of 17.5 and 60.5 genes per megabase, respectively). To our knowledge, the cause of this variation in gene density has not been explored. In this study, we leveraged genome assemblies of 262 vertebrate species to examine the range of within-genome variation in gene density. We combined gene density data with repeat landscape analyses in each species. We predicted that genomes with more recently expanded repeat families should show greater variation in gene density, because repetitive elements accumulate unevenly across the genome, while chromosomal rearrangements such as fusions, fissions, insertions, deletions, and inversions homogenize gene density over time. Our empirical analysis reveals a significant yet variable effect of repeat expansions, with additional processes likely contributing to variation in gene density.

articles.title: Grb2 phosphorylation antagonizes EGFR-driven ras activation by interfering with condensate assembly
articles.abstract: by Henry T. Phan, Chun-Wei Lin, Brittany L. Stinger, Joseph B. DeGrandchamp, L. J. Nugent Lew, Serena J. Huang, Jay T. Groves Upon ligand binding, the kinase domain of EGFR phosphorylates multiple tyrosine residues on the receptor cytoplasmic tail through a trans-autophosphorylation process. Phosphotyrosine sites on activated receptors recruit Grb2, which further recruits SOS to initiate downstream signaling by activating Ras. Multivalent binding between SOS and Grb2, as well as direct Grb2:Grb2 interactions, contribute to formation of a protein condensate of activated EGFR. The condensed state of EGFR facilitates autoinhibition release in SOS and exerts regulatory control over signal propagation from activated EGFR to Ras. While kinase activity of EGFR is an essential driver of this signaling process, phosphorylation at residue Y160 on Grb2 blocks Grb2:Grb2 binding and can interfere with EGFR condensation. Here, using a reconstituted system, we examine how titrating kinase activity in the EGFR system can both promote and inhibit signal output to Ras. The results reveal how effects of tyrosine kinase inhibition can, under some circumstances, promote Ras activation by inhibiting negative feedback through Grb2 phosphorylation and disruption of a Grb2 SH2/SH3 dimer interface.

articles.title: Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit
articles.abstract: Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure–flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens—separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm—in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol–water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50–300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136–137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from −1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2–3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.

articles.title: Intersectional stereotypes: How age and race shape perceptions of women in the United States
articles.abstract: This study examined the influence of older age and race (White/Black/Arab) on stereotypes of women. To evaluate whether age and race shape stereotype content for an intersectional group relative to its superordinate racial or superordinate older age identities, 525 Amazon Mechanical Turk participants were asked to list up to five words or short phrases that most people associated with these target groups. Overall, the study found stronger support for a distinctiveness hypothesis, whereby the most distinct identity of an individual’s intersectional identity influenced their associated characteristics. For example, because being White is common in the United States, old White women had more stereotypes in common with their old superordinate identity than their White identity. This suggests that the nation’s population characteristics may be predictive of the stereotypes associated with different intersectional groups. Overall, this research reveals the complex interplay between stereotypes of age and race for women, underscoring the need to acknowledge intersectional identities and cultural norms. Such insights can enhance our pursuit of inclusive and accurate societal perceptions.

articles.title: MIF inhibitor ISO-1 attenuates ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of donation after circulatory death liver transplantation
articles.abstract: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is an early mediator of ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI), however, the evidence on its role in orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT), particularly with donation after circulatory death (DCD) grafts is limited. Given its key regulatory function, this study investigated the effects of IRI on graft injury and assessed whether the use of ISO-1, a small-molecule MIF-inhibitor, affect IRI in a rat DCD-OLT model. 196 male Lewis rats were randomized into DBD control, DCD-30 min, DCD-60 min, DCD-30 + ISO-1, and DCD-30 + vehicle groups (n = 7/group/time-point). ISO-1 was administered before controlled cardiac arrest (0–60 min) and 3 h cold preservation before arterialized OLT. Animals were sacrificed at 1, 3, 24, and 168 h post-reperfusion. DCD grafts showed marked injury, with the DCD-60 group exhibiting lethal IRI. ISO-1 significantly reduced early hepatocellular injury compared with vehicle (AST:294 ± 63 vs 867 ± 211 IU/L, p = 0.017) and resulted in values comparable to DBD controls. Serum HMGB-1 (11 ± 2.8 vs 26 ± 6.2 pg/mL, p = 0.045) and MIF (45 ± 5.3 vs 144 ± 27.5 ng/mL, p = 0.034) levels were similarly decreased following ISO-1 application. ISO-1 improved graft microcirculation at 24 h, attenuated histological injury, and was associated with an altered time course of CD163 + macrophage infiltration. ISO-1 pre-treatment attenuated hepatocellular injury and was associated with improved graft microcirculation and reduced DAMP release, supporting further mechanistic and translational evaluation in DCD liver transplantation.

articles.title: Multi-scale feature fusion network optimization and edge intelligent detection for transmission line insulator
articles.abstract: In response to the accuracy loss caused by lightweight networks on edge devices and the difficulty in accurately detecting small defect targets, this paper studies the lightweight You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) transmission line insulator defect detection algorithm based on Three-Branch Attention Mechanism (TBAM) and Enhanced Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network (EMSFFN), which can perform high-precision detection on edge intelligent devices of unmanned aerial vehicles. Aiming at the problem of significant differences in the number of image categories in the current aerial insulator defect dataset, the dataset was expanded through image data augmentation to generate more minority class samples, balance the number of samples in each category. Experiments show that compared with YOLOv7, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, Detection Transformer (DETR) and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN), the model parameters and computational complexity of TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN are relatively low. Its AP reaches 99.2% and the mAP reaches 98.7%. Therefore, the TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN model is suitable for unmanned aerial vehicles carrying edge intelligent devices to achieve power inspection.

articles.title: Perceived consequences of extreme risk protection orders: A qualitative study of respondents from California
articles.abstract: by Veronica A. Pear, Christopher E. Knoepke, Lisa B. Geller, Amy Barnhorst, Ari Davis, Rose Kim, Garen J. Wintemute Background Extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs) temporarily prohibit the purchase and possession of firearms by people at high risk of harming themselves or others. This study drew on the experiences of ERPO respondents to learn about the perceived short- and long-term consequences of the law. Methods For this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted 24 semi-structured interviews between March and November 2024 with respondents to ERPOs issued in California between 2016 and 2020. We purposively sampled 250 respondents for whom we had previously abstracted ERPO court case data to ensure adequate representation across domains of interest (e.g., demographics, location) and invited respondents to participate in the study by mail. All interviews were recorded, double coded, and thematically analyzed. Results Our diverse participants described heterogeneous consequences across 4 domains: violence risk, legal/economic outcomes, opinions/attitudes, and social/emotional wellbeing. Two participants believed their ERPOs prevented violence and 1 was unsure; the rest believed that they would not have committed violence irrespective of the ERPO. Some perceived the ERPO to have had negligible effects on their lives, while others described both positive consequences, including self-reflection and behavior change, and negative consequences, including employment or housing difficulties, stigmatization, damaged relationships, loss of trust in legal institutions, and perceived exacerbation of violence risk. Participants reported that they were not connected to mental health care or other supportive services through the ERPO process. Conclusions Participants perceived ERPOs to have varied and mixed consequences. These accounts identify outcomes that warrant consideration in ERPO research, policy, and implementation. Future research should assess the prevalence and distribution of these consequences and evaluate whether policy refinements can reduce adverse experiences without compromising the public health benefits of these laws.

articles.title: Performance evolution in Olympic swimming over the last 100 years: A retrospective stroke-based analysis
articles.abstract: This retrospective study examined the historical progression of Olympic swimming performance across 24 Olympic Games from Paris 1924 to Paris 2024. Finalist race data for 1553 women and 1641 men were extracted from the official World Aquatics database, including final times, reaction times, and calculated swimming speeds across all strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly) and Olympic distances (50–1500 m). Across all strokes and distances, final times demonstrated substantial reductions over the century, with the most pronounced improvements observed in freestyle and long-distance events. The largest percentage improvements in performance were observed during specific Olympic cycles, including 1956, 1972, and 2008, which coincided with major developments in pool engineering, competition regulations, training methodologies, and swimsuit technology. Swimming speeds increased consistently in all events, while reaction-time analyses revealed significant improvements across Olympic Games during the period in which reaction-time data were recorded. Overall, these findings demonstrate substantial long-term improvements in Olympic swimming performance and provide a comprehensive historical overview of performance changes across strokes, distances, and sexes. The periods associated with the largest performance improvements coincided with major technological, biomechanical, and regulatory developments in the sport. The results may serve as valuable benchmarks for coaches, athletes, and sports scientists to evaluate long-term performance trends and prepare for future international competitions.

articles.title: Repurposing the phospholipase A2 inhibitor, darapladib, to combat multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens, including Candida auris
articles.abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen and a major global health threat, highlighting the urgent need for new therapeutics. We screened ~2,600 FDA-approved drugs and clinical compounds and identified darapladib (DAL), a phospholipase A2 inhibitor, as a potent antifungal agent against multidrug-resistant C. auris. DAL exhibited antifungal activity against all tested C. auris isolates and showed broad-spectrum activity against other tested clinically important fungal pathogens, including other Candida, Cryptococcus, and mucormycosis-associated species, with minimum inhibitory concentrations of 4–16 μg/mL. DAL also displayed rapid fungicidal activity against C. auris and synergized with amphotericin B against C. auris and filamentous fungal pathogens. More importantly, serial exposure of C. auris to subinhibitory concentrations of DAL for 16 passages did not result in detectable resistance. Mechanistic studies indicated that DAL acts through an ergosterol-dependent membrane targeting mechanism, as exogenous ergosterol attenuated its activity and ergosterol-related haploinsufficient mutants showed reduced susceptibility. Consistent with this mechanism, DAL increased membrane permeability, nucleic acid leakage, and reactive oxygen species. In a Caenorhabditis elegans–C. auris infection model, DAL reduced the C. auris burden to below the limit of detection. Together, these findings support further investigation of DAL as a repurposed antifungal candidate against drug-resistant fungal infections.

articles.title: Retraction: Environmental concentrations of metformin exposure affect aggressive behavior in the Siamese fighting fish, Betta splendens
Retraction: Resveratrol eliminates cancer stem cells of osteosarcoma by STAT3 pathway inhibition
Single-cell analysis of COPD: Microenvironmental interactions driven by immune-fibrotic imbalance
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a respiratory disease with a high degree of cellular heterogeneity and molecular complexity, characterized pathologically by persistent airflow limitation and an inflammatory-tissue remodeling cascade involving multiple cell types. Traditional transcriptomics lack the resolution to precisely define cell subpopulation roles in COPD. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) overcomes this limitation by enabling high-resolution analysis of cell-type-specific mechanisms in COPD. A total of 101,009 cells from three scRNA-seq datasets were integrated to profile COPD-related molecular features and cell interactions at single-cell resolution. Analysis identified four major cell types and 17 distinct cell subtypes. Cell–cell communication analysis revealed a significant reduction in signaling activity of macrophages and fibroblasts, whereas certain immune cells exhibited enhanced signaling, suggesting that immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in COPD pathogenesis. Further analysis focused on macrophage-dominant myeloid cells and fibroblasts, uncovering their critical roles in inflammation modulation and fibrosis progression. Meanwhile, this study also identified 19 chemicals that may influence COPD progression by modulating cellular gene expression. This study provides an important molecular basis for unraveling the cell-cell interaction network of COPD and elucidating the mechanism of each cell subpopulation in the disease process.

articles.title: Survival modeling and assessing prognostic factors of colorectal cancer in Ethiopia: Addressing violation of statistical assumptions
articles.abstract: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, with rapidly rising incidence in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Survival outcomes are compromised by late-stage presentation, limited therapeutic capacity, and weak post-treatment follow-up. Although survival analysis is critical for characterizing CRC prognosis, insufficient attention has been given to the performance and validity of commonly applied survival models in Ethiopian populations, particularly when statistical assumptions are violated. Objective To identify key clinical and treatment-related prognostic factors influencing overall survival among Ethiopian CRC patients and to assess the robustness and interpretability of Cox proportional hazard model (Cox PH model), stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty model, and Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models, focusing on model adequacy under assumption violations. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 161 colorectal cancer patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2016. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis, with group comparisons via log-rank tests. Multivariable modeling employed Cox proportional hazards, stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty, and accelerated failure time models. Model adequacy was evaluated through Akaike Information Criterion, concordance indices, and the Global Schoenfeld test for proportional hazards assessment. Results The Cox proportional hazard model violated the proportional hazards assumption (global p = 0.043), primarily due to histological subtype effects, indicating that the standard Cox proportional hazard model was not appropriate for this dataset. Assumption violations were mitigated using the stratified Cox proportional hazard model (global p = 0.122). Among accelerated failure time models, the log-logistic distribution provided superior model fit (AIC = 649.88; concordance = 0.724). Time-ratio (TR) interpretation showed that surgery extended survival by approximately 2.4-fold, whereas elevated baseline carcinoembryonic antigen levels and metastatic disease reduced survival duration by nearly half. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, distant metastasis, vascular invasion, and squamous cell histology were consistently associated with poorer prognosis, while surgery and chemotherapy remained protective across models. Conclusion Rigorous model checking indicates that the conventional Cox proportional hazards model is inappropriate for this cohort due to proportional hazard assumption violations. Accelerated failure time modeling, particularly the log-logistic form, offered improved fit and clearer time-based interpretation of covariate effects. These findings underscore the importance of model validation in CRC survival research and highlight the need for improved early detection, surgical access, and targeted management of aggressive tumor subtypes to enhance patient outcomes in Ethiopia.

articles.title: The antibacterial and antifungal activity of honey and propolis from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria
articles.abstract: The global rise of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens has increased interest in bee-derived natural products as sources of novel antimicrobials. While most research has focused on European honey bee (Apis mellifera) products, the 550 species of stingless bees found globally also produce honey and other hive products, representing a largely unexplored source of novel bioactives. This study investigates the antimicrobial activity of propolis extracts and honey from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria against 16 clinically significant bacterial and fungal pathogens, using broth microdilution methodology. T. carbonaria propolis and honey exhibited distinct antimicrobial profiles: propolis showed selective activity against a subset of bacteria and certain filamentous fungi, while honey showed broad-spectrum activity against all tested bacteria and selective activity against dermatophyte fungi. The level of H2O2 production in T. carbonaria honey was only moderately correlated with its antimicrobial activity, and the total phenolic content of propolis did not correlate significantly with its antimicrobial activity, suggesting other bee- or plant-derived compounds are important contributors. These findings highlight T. carbonaria propolis and honey as promising antimicrobials and potential sources of novel bioactive compounds.

articles.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Background Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort. Methods This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, −4.20; 95% CI, −4.53 to −3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period. Conclusions The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up. Trial registration Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004

articles.title: The configurational pathways associated with executive function in preschool children: An fsQCA analysis based on gross motor skill development
articles.abstract: The preschool years are a critical period for the rapid development of executive function in children. While executive function in preschool children is influenced by multiple factors, existing research has been limited by its theoretical and empirical perspectives, resulting in singular pathways for promoting executive function. To address this, the study adopted a systems theory perspective to explore the configurational pathways through which subsystems of gross motor skills are associated with higher levels of executive function in preschoolers. The study included test data from 67 children aged 3–6 years. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), six subsystems of gross motor skills (running, jumping, throwing, catching, kicking, and striking) were treated as antecedent conditions to explore the configurational associations of gross motor skill subsystems with executive function. Necessary condition analysis indicated that no single gross motor skill subsystem constituted a necessary condition for higher executive function in preschool children. Subsequent configurational analysis identified three distinct pathways that are associated with higher levels of executive function (with a total consistency of 0.906 and an overall coverage of 0.496). The development of executive function in preschool children is not associated with single gross motor actions in a linear manner but rather with multiple concurrent combinations of gross motor skill subsystems characterized by “multiple concurrent pathways leading to the same goal.” This is reflected in the three configurational pathways: “a combination of jumping, throwing, and striking actions,” “a combination of running, kicking, and striking actions,” and “a combination of running, throwing, and catching actions.” These findings provide preliminary insights and hypothesis-generating evidence for future research on gross motor skill activities and executive function development in preschool children.

articles.title: The effect of STAT1 expression and the Y701 phosphorylation on primary Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma cells
articles.abstract: by Victoria S. Coward, Nalan Gokgoz, Kim M. Tsoi, Jay S. Wunder, Irene L. Andrulis Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma (UPS) is a genetically complex type of soft tissue sarcoma (STS) and there are few therapeutic options for advanced disease. Immune checkpoint blockade therapy may be of benefit to a subset of UPS patients, particularly those with elevated tumoral Programmed Cell Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and an inflamed tumour microenvironment. From transcriptomic analyses we previously identified Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (STAT1) expression, a key mediator of interferon-γ (IFN-γ) signaling, as enriched in a cohort of UPS cases with elevated PD-L1 levels that were observed to have an improved clinical outcome. This led us to investigate the role of STAT1 in UPS biology. We examined the effects of STAT1 loss, and overexpression of either wild type or tyrosine phosphorylation-deficient STAT1 in primary human UPS cell lines. We observed that IFN-γ treatment decreased cell counts, increased cell death, and induced the secretion of CXCR3 ligands in a STAT1-dependent manner. Overexpression of wild type STAT1, but not a tyrosine to phenylalanine phospho-mutant (Y701F), restored IFN-γ-mediated cell death and cytokine secretion, highlighting the importance of Y701 phosphorylation in STAT1-associated antitumour functions. STAT1 Y701 phosphorylation status was associated with gene expression changes that were cell line specific. Together, these findings shed light on the central role of STAT1, and specifically the Y701 phosphorylation, in mediating IFN-γ signaling and related phenotypes. This study underscores the need for further exploration of the role of STAT1 phosphorylation in tumor-immune interactions within UPS.

articles.title: When nematodes take flight: Multi-scale dispersal of the beech leaf disease nematode in forest ecosystems
articles.abstract: Beech leaf disease, caused by the invasive foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae, is an emerging threat to Fagus grandifolia across North America. Since its initial detection in 2012, the disease has spread to a total of 16 U.S. states and the Canadian Province of Ontario; however, the mechanisms underlying nematode dispersal remain poorly understood. This study evaluated multiple potential dispersal pathways across two forest sites in central Pennsylvania through integrated field surveys, environmental monitoring, and experimental validation. Weekly sampling was conducted to characterize nematode population dynamics in relation to temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Long distance water-mediated dispersal was assessed through creek sampling, while biotic dispersal was investigated through field sampling from migratory bird feet during high-moisture events and a controlled greenhouse transmission experiment. Wind dispersal was further examined in a pilot study using unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater collection during precipitation events. Nematode presence was detected across all investigated pathways, supporting dispersal via water flow, rain splash, and biotic vectors. Funnel-based sampling recovered Litylenchus crenatae up to 90 m from infected trees, demonstrating movement beyond the immediate canopy area. Confirmed downstream transport of nematodes suggests waterways may facilitate long-distance dispersal across forested landscapes. Litylenchus crenatae was recovered from the feet of migratory birds, and greenhouse experiments confirmed that bird-associated nematodes could infect healthy beech seedlings, providing evidence for avian-mediated transmission. Desiccation assays demonstrated that live Litylenchus crenatae specimens could survive up to 10 days in the absence of available moisture, indicating that the nematodes may remain viable during transport on bird feet or exposed surfaces. In addition, unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater sampling detected Litylenchus crenatae within canopy-associated precipitation samples, providing additional evidence for short-distance aerial dispersal during wind and rain events. Together, these findings demonstrate that beech leaf disease spread is driven by multiple interacting abiotic and biotic dispersal mechanisms operating across spatial scales.

articles.title: Crossword: I see right through you
Xinru Huang influences how shoppers pay at the register
AI in bioceramics: A perspective on data-driven material design, discovery, and translation
Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
articles.abstract: Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.

articles.title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.

articles.title: Children bear brunt of NHS waiting times in England, report finds
articles.abstract: Tens of thousands of young people in England have been waiting more than a year for an NHS appointment, a report warns.1While waiting times for most adult services are improving overall, the opposite is happening in children’s services, the Care Quality Commission’s (CQC) annual state of care report showed. This contrast was sharpest in waiting times for community health services.While the report found that the number of adults waiting more than a year for an appointment had reduced, the number of young people waiting more than a year increased by 129% in the two years to March 2026.Most of those waits were for community paediatric services, including diagnosis of neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism and ADHD. Just a few weeks ago a major government backed review found that the process for diagnosing ADHD and autism in England needed a “fundamental shift” to ensure that children receive timely support.2The CQC said...

articles.title: Consultants’ strike: Senior doctors in England announce industrial action
articles.abstract: Consultants in England will strike for two days in November after negotiations on pay and working conditions broke down, the BMA says.The NHS’s most senior hospital doctors plan to walk out from 7 am on 25 November to 6 59 am on 27 November.The BMA’s Consultants Committee has been locked in a dispute with the government since May 2025. In July this year consultants voted for strike action1 unless an improved offer was made. Current proposals would raise pay by only 2.4% in 2027-28.2The BMA has now given the government four weeks to respond to the strike announcement. Should November’s industrial action go ahead, emergency cover will continue at hospitals, akin to Christmas Day levels of staffing.The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said that the plans to strike during the winter period were “irresponsible” and would place the NHS “under even greater pressure at this crucial time.” She added, “NHS England...

articles.title: Doctors leaders slam all male panel at London Breast Meeting
articles.abstract: An all male panel at an international conference for breast surgeons has sparked outrage among senior doctors.The 14 member panel at the London Breast Meeting (LBM), staged last month, was described as “shameful” by commentators but has been defended by the organisers.The LBM describes itself as an international meeting dedicated to advancing the field of breast surgery through collaboration, innovation, and education.“With a rich history of bringing together leading surgeons, practitioners, and experts from around the world, our mission is to foster excellence in breast surgery and patient care,” it says.But a photograph of the all male panel (or “manel”) has prompted much criticism online.In a LinkedIn thread, Stella Vig, consultant surgeon and NHS England’s former medical director for secondary care said, “This is not a good look!”1Helen Cocks, head and neck and endocrine surgeon said it was “shameful.”“It is not a reflection of a leaky pipeline but shows a...

articles.title: Financial incentives may have a role in driving care quality, but they must be meticulously designed
articles.abstract: A notable feature of the government’s 10 year health plan for England, Fit for the Future, was its insistence that incentives and a pay-for-performance culture would drive better value and outcomes.123 The recent publication of the National Quality Board’s quality strategy4 reaffirms the role of incentives in driving change. The strategy is optimistic that, with careful design, incentives could help in achieving many of the 10 year plan’s objectives.4Some of the proposals in the strategy are radical, including “patient power payments” that—starting with gynaecology services—will allow patients to decide whether provider organisations are fully reimbursed for their care on the basis of their experience.14 The aim of tackling persistent failures to listen to women56 is surely right, as is the broader aim of creating mechanisms to stimulate and sustain improvement. But whether financial incentives can drive the desired change is uncertain.The evidence base for incentivisation isn’t straightforward. Studies show that...

articles.title: Trump’s aid cuts risk killing women around the world
articles.abstract: “Women’s rights are human rights. Reproductive rights are human rights. Sexuality rights are human rights. We are seeing an erosion of the narrative around that.”Those are the words of JE Musoba Kitui, director of the Ipas Africa Alliance, a non-profit focused on advancing access to safe abortions and contraception, in reaction to the “hugely problematic” cuts to health aid. A huge proportion of the cuts are being made by the US, the biggest global health funder at the time.On 20 January 2025, President Donald Trump ordered a 90 day pause on US foreign development assistance. By March, his administration said it had cancelled more than 80% of USAID programmes. Other health specific initiatives, including the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the World Health Organization (WHO), also experienced major funding losses and disruption. US funding for Gavi, the vaccine alliance, was initially withheld before $600m allocated by Congress...

articles.title: [Articles] First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

articles.title: [Articles] Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2– breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2– breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

articles.title: [Articles] Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
articles.abstract: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody–drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

articles.title: [Articles] Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
articles.abstract: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

articles.title: [Articles] Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

articles.title: [Comment] Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?
articles.abstract: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

14-3-3 Enables β-Adrenergic Regulation of the Cardiac Sodium Channel at the Intercalated Disc
articles.abstract: Background: Beta-Adrenergic stimulation enables the heart to adapt electrical activity to increased physiological demand. Although the cardiac sodium channel Nav1.5 is essential for impulse propagation, the mechanisms underlying its acute beta-adrenergic regulation, particularly within distinct cardiomyocyte membrane domains, remain poorly understood. We investigated whether the phosphorylation-sensitive adaptor protein 14-3-3 mediates this regulation. Methods and Results: Using automated patch-clamp electrophysiology in HEK293 cells and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs), we found that isoproterenol rapidly increased sodium current (INa) and promoted channel activation at more hyperpolarized potentials, whereas PKA inhibition reduced INa. Disruption of 14-3-3 function abolished these responses without substantially altering basal sodium current or Nav1.5 surface expression. Macropatch recordings from ventricular myocytes revealed that isoproterenol preferentially enhanced INa at the intercalated disc, an effect prevented by 14-3-3 inhibition. Proximity ligation assays further demonstrated increased Nav1.5/14-3-3 proximity following beta-adrenergic stimulation. Systematic mutagenesis identified S460 in the Nav1.5 DI-DII linker as a critical determinant of acute PKA-dependent regulation. Molecular modeling predicted that S460 phosphorylation stabilizes the Nav1.5/14-3-3 interaction. In CRISPR-engineered S460A iPSC-CMs, acute beta-adrenergic regulation of INa was abolished, whereas the isoproterenol-induced increase in conduction velocity was significantly attenuated. Computational simulations further predicted that enhanced intercalated-disc sodium current supports increased conduction velocity across varying conditions of electrical coupling and pacing rate. Conclusions: Our findings identify 14-3-3 and S460 as critical determinants of spatially selective beta-adrenergic regulation of Nav1.5 at the cardiac intercalated disc. This mechanism provides a molecular link between sympathetic signaling and cardiac sodium current regulation, supporting the concept that localized enhancement of Nav1.5 function contributes to the adaptation of cardiac conduction during increased sympathetic demand.

articles.title: A Pipeline for Predicting Variant Associations with Complex Disorders via Functional Annotations
articles.abstract: The study of complex disorders is limited by the lack of structured data sets that integrate genetic association signals with rich functional annotations. While genome wide association studies (GWAS) provide large collections of associated variants, these are heterogeneous, studydependent, and not directly suitable for machine learning applications. Although frameworks such as Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) offer comprehensive variant-level features, there is no standardised procedure to construct curated, balanced, and reproducible data sets for the systematic study of complex traits. We introduce a scalable and reproducible pipeline for generating CADD-annotated variant data sets associated with complex disorders defined via Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) terms. The pipeline integrates GWAS summary statistics, genome mapping, chromosomestratified negative sampling, and large-scale annotation, while addressing class imbalance and feature redundancy. The resulting data sets provide curated, balanced, and annotation-rich representations of variant-trait associations, suitable for statistical learning, systematic model evaluation and comparison, and analysis of functional annotation contributions and interactions.

articles.title: A Specific Ancestral Sequence Reconstruction of Flagellin Can Drive Motility in Salmonella enterica but not Escherichia coli
articles.abstract: The bacterial flagellar filament, built from thousands of flagellin subunits, is essential for flagellar motility. Here, we aimed to use ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) to generate conservative, ancestral flagellin sequences that surround the divergency point between Escherichia and Salmonella species and tested their ability to restore motility in flagellin deleted Escherichia coli and Salmonella Typhimurium. Only one (N131) out of three candidates restored motility in S. Typhimurium but not E. coli, despite high structural similarity to native FliC/FljB. S. Typhimurium expressing N131 showed reduced motility relative to wild-type Salmonella FliC, alongside increased tumbling frequency. Serial passage across swim plates produced a derivative, N131.10, containing a single flagellin mutation (M144I), with a larger swim ring diameter but also increased tumbling frequency. Comparison of structural interaction networks among the residues of S. Typhimurium LT2 FliC with those of other filament proteins showed that non-motile candidates (N132 and N134) carried substitutions that disrupted key core-domain atomic interactions. These results demonstrate that flagellar filament assembly tolerates only limited sequence variation and that this capacity for tolerance differs between E. coli and S. Typhimurium despite their close phylogenetic relationship.

articles.title: A molecularly defined recurrent CA3 circuit regulates network dynamics and spatial working memory
articles.abstract: The hippocampal CA3 region supports coordinated network activity and memory processes, but how molecularly distinct CA3 neuronal populations contribute to recurrent circuit function remains poorly understood. Here we identify St18 as a molecular marker of a distinct population of deep-layer, burst-firing CA3 pyramidal neurons and generate an St18-Cre mouse line for their selective genetic targeting. In contrast to canonical CA3 pyramidal neurons, St18 neurons preferentially innervate CA3 bilaterally, with only sparse projections to CA1. Moreover, St18 neurons are highly active during endogenous CA3 sharp-wave ripples, and their optogenetic activation evokes local ripple-like activity in CA3 but not in CA1. Furthermore, chemogenetic suppression markedly reduces CA3 ripple occurrence without significantly affecting CA1 ripple occurrence and selectively impairs spatial working memory performance. Together, these findings reveal the functional significance of a molecularly defined CA3 recurrent circuit, linking neuronal heterogeneity to hippocampal network dynamics and spatial working memory.

articles.title: A ribosome exit tunnel component is required for robust expression of the Drosophila hox gene, abdominal A
articles.abstract: Ribosomes, the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis, are fundamental to all cellular life. Although the higher-level architecture of ribosomes is conserved, a small subunit acting as the mRNA decoding site and a large subunit that catalyses peptide bond formation, there are differences in the numbers of components of each of the subunits between the 3 domains of life. Despite their well-established role in translating genetic information into functional proteins, many complexities in ribosome biology and functionality are only just being revealed. Defects in ribosomal components contribute to a class of disorders termed ribosomopathies that come with a range of symptoms and severities. Here we show that a mutation in the Drosophila ribosomal protein RpL39 causes an anterior-posterior embryonic patterning defect through impaired accumulation of the hox protein Abdominal-A (abdA). Deletions uncovering subunits of the Nascent peptide-Associated Complex (NAC) and Ribosome-Associated Complex (RAC) act as genetic enhancers of the RpL39 mutation leading us to speculate that RpL39 forms a relay between the nascent peptide in the exit tunnel and the exterior surface of the ribosome, modulating the interaction with these ribosomally-associated complexes. This work enhances our knowledge of the roles played by individual ribosome components and feeds into our understanding of the mechanisms of ribosome quality control.

articles.title: A sensitive and specific microchimerism detection method using custom designed genotyping and companion qPCR assays
articles.abstract: Since first reports of the presence of a small number of cells from one individual persisting in another, researchers have developed a number of methods to detect microchimerism. Molecular based detection platforms range from gel electrophoresis to quantitative PCR to Next-Gen Sequencing. Central to all approaches is the need for informative polymorphic loci to effectively distinguish microchimeric cells from the host. However, we observed in our studies of maternal microchimerism that currently published approaches can limit the number of samples available for assessment due to the inability to identify an informative marker of the donor in the recipient. This was most striking in our studies of populations of African descent in which the use of HLA-based markers, a common approach, prevented the testing of 30-50% of participants. Other potential options were cost prohibitive or lacked sufficient sensitivity. To address this challenge, we developed a novel, simple, and low-cost approach that leverages global population frequency databases for polymorphism selection, reduces cost by amplifying multiple targets in one multiplex assay to complete genotyping, and has high sensitivity and specificity using rigorously designed qPCR assays to quantify microchimerism. Herein, we outline our design process, detailed assay protocol, and assessment of maternal microchimerism using this approach in two different populations of infants from the United States and South Africa.

articles.title: A thioester-thiol exchange reaction in Salmonella Invasion acyl carrier protein transfers the 4PP-bound acyl chain to a distal cysteine
articles.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium encodes two functionally distinct acyl carrier proteins: AcpP, involved in fatty acid synthesis, and the invasion acyl carrier protein (IacP), which mediates the acylation of SipB (Salmonella invasion protein B), a modification essential for SipB maturation and efficient host invasion. Despite growing insights, the IacP-dependent machinery governing acyl chain transfer remains largely enigmatic. Therefore, a multidisciplinary approach combining biochemistry and NMR was employed. A D35NIacP mutant (IacPN) that expresses in the apo-form was enzymatically converted into acyl-IacPN intermediates. Unexpectedly, the 1H15N HSQC spectra of the acyl-IacPN intermediates displayed two sets of resonances for several of the amides. The first was a less intense set of peaks, positioned close to the holo-peak, displaying a progressive chemical shift change with increasing acyl-chain length, reminiscent of the 4-phosphopantetheine (4-PP)-bound conformer of type II ACPs. The second, a more intense, acyl-chain-length-independent, previously uncharacterized set of peaks, was clustered near the longer 4PP-bound acyl-chain conformers (C14-). The origin of this new conformer was investigated by generating three cysteine-to-alanine mutants, C16A, C54A, and C69AIacPN. The C54AIacPN mutant displayed a single set of peaks in the acyl-IacPN intermediates, corresponding to the 4PP-bound IacPN conformer, establishing the critical role of Cys 54 in generating the uncharacterized peak and identifying it as a Cys-bound conformer. The acyl-S-carboxyamidomethyl-IacPN intermediates also displayed a single conformer, supporting the role of a cysteine in giving rise to the new peak. Collectively, our studies uncover a unique thioester-thiol exchange reaction in which the 4PP-tethered acyl chain is chemically transferred to a distal cysteine (Cys 54). Given that Cys 54 lies within the SipB interaction interface of IacP, this acyl chain relay process may contribute to IacP-mediated SipB acylation and Salmonella virulence.

articles.title: Accelerated discovery and optimization of a potent andselective MMP12 inhibitor with the machine learningplatform CAMOLE-1
articles.abstract: Machine learning techniques are being readily utilized to accelerate drug discovery pipelines. Peptide therapeutics are an emerging modality that offer the advantage of increased potency with reduced toxicity that are amenable to machine learning discovery and optimization. This work describes the Calico All-Atom Molecule Engine (CAMOLE-1), a machine learning platform for de novo peptide inhibitor design. CAMOLE-1 incorporates an all-atom diffusion model that enables rapid non-canonical peptide discovery and optimization, and integrates physics based computational filtering, and biochemical testing. We applied CAMOLE-1 towards the discovery of peptide inhibitors of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), a target class that has essentially evaded therapeutic development. Starting from canonical amino acid-based design, an MMP12 peptide inhibitor was identified and further optimized to improve potency. From these initial peptides, we used our all-atom diffusion model to determine a predicted structure, allowing us to design a potent and selective inhibitor over the course of about one year and 270 synthesized peptides. Predicted structures of both canonical and non-canonical peptide inhibitors showed high fidelity to our experimentally determined peptide-bound crystal structures. To our knowledge, this is the first described effort to use machine learning techniques to iteratively drive peptide inhibitor design beyond initial hit discovery into the development of selective, potent lead peptide inhibitors with improved pharmacokinetic properties. Our study illustrates the power of machine learning-driven design of peptide inhibitors, an exciting emerging therapeutic modality.

articles.title: Adeno-associated virus serotype tropism and transduction in murine dorsal root ganglia following direct injection.
articles.abstract: The peripheral nervous system (PNS) is highly heterogeneous, comprised of diverse subclasses of motor and sensory neurons. Optogenetics offers a high-resolution approach for interrogating neural circuits; however, optogenetic proteins must be selectively delivered to defined neuronal circuits in order to elucidate circuit-specific functional mechanisms. Adeno-associated viral vectors (AAVs) are widely used to deliver transgenes to the nervous system due to their relative safety and strong transgene expression. Multiple AAV serotypes are in common use, each capable of preferentially transducing distinct tissues and neuronal populations. However, characterization of the transduction behavior of these serotypes in the PNS, particularly in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and sensory nervous system (SNS), remain limited. This study evaluated the transduction efficiency of AAV8, AAV9, AAV2re, and PHP.S following direct intraganglionic injection into the DRG. AAV8, AAV9, and PHP.S exhibited comparable transduction efficiencies, whereas AAV2re transduced more than twofold fewer neurons. Despite similar overall efficiencies between AAV8, AAV9, and PHP.S, the neuronal volume distributions of transduced neurons were serotype-dependent. These results demonstrate that AAV serotype selection influences both the extent and size of transduced DRG neurons, indicating that serotype selection should be considered carefully when designing experiments that target peripheral sensory circuits.

articles.title: Affinity Maturation Enables Dual Targeting of Cancer-Associated MUC1-Tn/STn and Drives Potent Tumor Control
articles.abstract: A major challenge in solid tumor immunotherapy is identifying tumor-restricted antigens while overcoming intratumoral antigen heterogeneity. The truncated O-glycans Tn (GalNAcα-O-Ser/Thr) and STn (Neu5Acα2-6GalNAcα-O-Ser/Thr) are aberrantly displayed on the transmembrane glycoprotein MUC1 across a broad spectrum of epithelial malignancies, making MUC1-Tn/STn an attractive shared tumor-associated antigen class. However, heterogeneous intratumoral Tn/STn expression renders single-glycoform-specific antibodies vulnerable to antigen-driven escape. To address this challenge, we used structure-guided directed evolution and yeast surface display to affinity-mature the anti-MUC1-Tn antibody 5E5, generating variants with high-affinity dual recognition of MUC1-Tn and MUC1-STn. Co-crystal structures revealed that heavy-chain CDR loops cooperatively engage the GalNAc moiety primarily through hydrogen-bonding networks, in which HCDR3 residue 98 fine-tunes glycoform preference: Tyr98 favors MUC1-Tn recognition, whereas His98 enhances MUC1-STn engagement, while both support high-affinity recognition of both glycoforms. When reformatted as bispecific T-cell engagers, the affinity-matured variants mediated potent and durable cytolytic activity against cancer cells with heterogeneous glycan profiles, suppressed mixed Tn/STn tumors in vivo where the parental antibody failed, and showed enhanced activity in patient-derived tumor-like clusters. Together, these findings establish functional glycoform coverage as a design principle for antibody engineering, whereby a single paratope is optimized to recognize a defined spectrum of tumor-associated glycoforms while preserving antigen specificity, providing a strategy to overcome glycan heterogeneity in solid tumor immunotherapy.

articles.title: Aquaporin-4 Regulates Edema, Sustains Astrocyte Differentiation, and Constrains Immunosuppressive Remodeling in Glioblastoma
articles.abstract: Vasogenic cerebral edema is a severe complication that affects most patients with glioblastoma (GBM). It leads to an increase in intracranial pressure, neurological deficits, and increased mortality rates. While there is considerable research on edema formation, the molecular and cellular mechanisms of edema resolution in GBM, particularly in response to dexamethasone or other anti-edema therapies, remain largely undefined. Our findings demonstrate that the water channel aquaporin-4 (AQP4), a key regulator of brain water homeostasis, is upregulated in human GBM compared to the normal brain. AQP4 expression correlates with peritumoral edema in GBM patients, with the classical (CL) GBM subtype exhibiting the highest AQP4 levels but the lowest edema content relative to the proneural (PN) and mesenchymal (MES) subtypes. Using the RCAS/tv-a system, we generated de novo GBM with defined driver mutations in Aqp4-proficient and -deficient mice. Loss of Aqp4 shortened survival and exacerbated edema, accompanied by reduced astrocytic coverage within the tumor core, but not at the tumor margin. Single-cell RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics revealed that Aqp4 loss reprograms astrocytes toward an immature, progenitor-like state and alters their crosstalk with other cell types in the GBM microenvironment. Additionally, loss of Aqp4 skewed myeloid populations toward immunosuppressive phenotypes while reducing lymphoid infiltration. Treatment with anti-VEGFA antibody, an established anti-edema therapy, increased expression of Aqp4 and reduced vessel leakage, underscoring the role of AQP4 in the therapeutic modulation of brain water balance. Overall, this study highlights the important role of AQP4 in resolving edema and its critical function in maintaining astrocyte identity and shaping the immune landscape of GBM.

articles.title: Auto-AVS: A Novel Framework for Automated Autophagic Vacuole Simulation
articles.abstract: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is widely used to quantify autophagic bodies in yeast, but ultra-thin sectioning provides only two-dimensional cross-sections of inherently 3D structures. Inferring the underlying size and number of autophagic bodies therefore requires assumptions about their geometry, spatial organization, and distribution within the vacuole. We introduce Auto-AVS, an open-source computational stereology framework that combines configurable 3D autophagic-vacuole simulation, optional CompuCell3D-based body deformation, virtual TEM sectioning, and statistical comparison with experimental data. We first validate the virtual sectioning pipeline against analytical stereology and an existing spherical R-based simulation. We then use Auto-AVS to examine whether explicitly modeling autophagic-body deformation alters observed section statistics and find no consistent measurable effect under the tested simulation parameters. Finally, we apply the framework to experimental wild-type and mutant TEM datasets. Auto-AVS produces body-size estimates closely consistent with conventional stereological estimates, while body-number fitting reveals substantial discrepancies between simulated and experimental distributions despite similar average count estimates. These discrepancies implicate spatial clustering and vacuole geometry as important limitations of current body-number models. Rather than replacing conventional stereology, Auto-AVS provides a computational framework for testing its underlying assumptions and determining which aspects of 3D organization affect inference from two-dimensional microscopy.

articles.title: Auxin and cytokinin antagonistically regulate Arabidopsis root distal stem cell fate through opposing pairs of HD-Zip II transcription factors
articles.abstract: The antagonistic action of auxin (IAA) and cytokinin (CK) regulates several aspects of plant development including stem cell specification and maintenance. In the Arabidopsis thaliana root, the fate of distal stem cells (DSCs) is mainly regulated by IAA, while the function of CK is still ill-defined. Here, by investigating the role of the HD-Zip II transcription factor family in distal tissues, we uncover CK as a proliferative input for DSCs, acting in opposition to IAA. We show that opposing pairs of HD-Zip II proteins regulate DSCs fate by integrating IAA and CK signals. The {delta} module, composed of HAT3 and ATHB4, is activated by CK and promotes DSCs division. Conversely, the {gamma} module, constituted by HAT1 and ATHB2, acts downstream of IAA to repress CK biosynthesis and DSCs division. The mutual inhibition between {delta} and {gamma} modules downstream of opposite hormone inputs sustains the precise regulation of DSCs homeostasis.

articles.title: Berkson's Paradox: A Common Statistical Error in Genomics Analyses
articles.abstract: Berkson's paradox describes a scenario where a spurious correlation arises between two independent variables within a subset of samples selected based on a third variable which the first two variables cause. The conditions for Berkson's paradox are perfect in genomics due to many variables we study being causally intertwined, common selection criteria being biased either intentionally or not by the variables of interest, and our propensity to look towards correlations for windows into underlying mechanism. Here, we provide examples of cases where spurious correlations are likely to arise in common genomics analyses, and suggest analysis approaches to avoid misinterpreting spurious correlations.

articles.title: Broadband Rheometry of Native Soft Tissues via i-Rheo-Indent
articles.abstract: Characterising the frequency-dependent viscoelasticity of soft biological tissues is important for mechanobiology, disease phenotyping, and the design of biomimetic materials. However, conventional oscillatory rheometry becomes increasingly compromised by instrumental inertia at high frequencies and often requires specimens to be cut, reshaped, or compressed to conform to predefined measuring geometries, while local indentation methods probe only limited tissue volumes. Here, we apply i-Rheo-Indent, a macroscale indentation approach that transforms the measured force-relaxation and indentation histories from a single experiment directly into the broadband viscoelastic spectrum, without fitting to a predefined constitutive model. Measurements on a 3D-printed porcine liver analogue and murine quadriceps and brain showed good agreement with conventional oscillatory rheometry over the frequency range in which the latter remained reliable, while extending the accessible response up to 500 rad/s, beyond the regime increasingly dominated by instrument inertia. The method also enabled direct characterisation of intact tubular murine colon, yielding an elastic response consistent with published indentation measurements while additionally resolving the frequency-dependent viscous contribution. Intact murine livers exhibited substantially larger viscoelastic moduli than biopsy-punched specimens prepared for parallel-plate rheometry, indicating that specimen preparation can materially influence the measured mechanical response.
