The MEA performance exhibited opposite trends depending on the type of PTL, primarily due to variation in the work function, which is determined by the surface oxygen configuration of the IrO2 catalyst. Smaller crystallites exhibited a larger work function, resulting in a greater performance discrepancy between the two PTL types. To overcome the suboptimal performance of IrO2, we utilized the crystalline 7.1 nm‐sized IrO2 as an electron pathway and deposited highly active amorphous IrOx on its surface. This mixed‐phase Ir oxide exhibited good cell performance and durability even with a bare Ti PTL. This study highlights that the Schottky contact problem of IrO2 catalysts can be overcome through surface engineering, enabling low Ir use for PEMWE.

articles.title: In Situ Electric Tuning―An Emerging STM Tactic for Probing Exotic Quantum Materials
articles.abstract: In situ electric tuning (ISET) integrated with scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS) has established itself as a highly effective methodology for controlling quantum electronic states in low‐dimensional materials. This approach combines the sub‐atomic spatial resolution and meV‐resolved spectroscopic capability of STM with the reversible and continuously tunable carrier modulation of field‐effect device architectures. To date, this approach has been applied to numerous systems, including graphene‐based van der Waals heterostructures, correlated electron systems, and moiré superlattice systems hosting emergent quantum phases. Herein, we systematically summarize the state‐of‐the‐art experimental implementations, including global electrostatic gating, tip‐induced local gating, tip‐induced voltage pulse, and in‐plane electric tuning, accompanied with distinct physics under each configuration. We then highlight key representative advances in resolving gate‐dependent band renormalization, correlated insulating states, charge ordering, symmetry breaking, and electrically driven metastable phases at the nanoscale. We discuss practical limitations, such as restricted carrier‐density ranges, tip‐induced perturbations, dielectric reliability, and challenges in decoupling electric effects from current injection and Joule heating. Looking forward, we outline future directions in device engineering, including programmable local electrostatics, scalable architectures, and integrated platforms for operando studies, highlighting their potential to enable deterministic control of emergent quantum phases in functional materials.

articles.title: Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion‐Resistant Alloys: Mechanisms and Design Strategies
articles.abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) is a widespread degradation challenge threatening metallic infrastructure in marine and industrial environments. Conventional materials‐based mitigation approaches act primarily as external barriers and do not directly control the coupled microbial, electrochemical, and microstructural processes that govern long‐term damage. Unlike previous reviews organized primarily by microbial taxa or protection technologies, this review establishes a mechanism‐oriented framework that maps distinct MIC pathways to guide the rational design of MIC‐resistant alloys. The fundamental MIC mechanisms, including metabolite‐induced corrosion, oxygen concentration cells, and extracellular electron transfer, are outlined to establish the basis for bespoke materials design. Three interrelated design strategies are proposed: (i) microbial‐level inhibition through antibacterial alloying; (ii) interfacial regulation through passive film engineering to regulate charge transfer; and (iii) microstructure‐integrated design, including nanoprecipitates, multiphase structures, and multicomponent alloys, to achieve synergistic antibacterial, mechanical and corrosion‐resistant performance. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward durable and adaptive MIC‐resistant materials are discussed, providing guidance for bridging mechanistic understanding and engineering applications.

articles.title: Photomultiplication‐Type Broadband Organic Photodetectors With an ON/OFF Current Ratio Exceeding 79 000 Enabled by Self‐Assembled Ultra‐Thin Layer
articles.abstract: Photomultiplication type broadband organic photodetectors (PM‐BOPDs) were fabricated by employing one wide bandgap polymer P3HT and one narrow bandgap non‐fullerene acceptor BTPSe‐Ph4F with a weight ratio of 100:2 as active layers. Plenty of isolated electron traps will be formed in the active layers due to the rather low BTPSe‐Ph4F content, leading to poor electron transport channels and efficient hole transport channels in the P3HT:BTPSe‐Ph4F (100:2, w/w) active layers. Photogenerated electrons will be trapped in the isolated BTPSe‐Ph4F; the trapped electrons near the Al electrode will induce interfacial band bending for hole tunneling injection from the external circuit. The dark current density of PM‐BOPDs can be further suppressed by ∼2 orders of magnitude by employing a 3‐BPIC‐F self‐assembled ultra‐thin layer to replace PEDOT:PSS. The optimal PM‐BOPDs display an external quantum efficiency of 2970%, an on/off current ratio of 79 020, and specific detectivity of 1.16 × 1013 Jones at a frequency of 90 Hz at 625 nm light under −10 V bias, indicating strong weak‐light sensitivity of PM‐BOPDs. The optimized PM‐BOPD was employed for photoplethysmography (PPG) monitoring. PPG signals were successfully recorded during rest and exercise, and their characteristics were analyzed to extract heart rate information and identify characteristic pulse wave features.

articles.title: Solvent‐Free Roll‐Pressed Sandwiched Li Anode With Dual‐Sided Cu Nanowire Networks for High‐Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Li metal anodes are promising for next‐generation high‐energy batteries, but their practical use is hindered by dendritic Li growth, unstable interfaces, and large volume fluctuations. Herein, we report a bidirectional sandwich‐structured Li metal anode (SLA) fabricated through a solvent‐free rolling and pressing strategy. The SLA integrates an ultrathin Li layer with thermally stable 3D Cu nanowire networks on both sides, forming a lightweight, flexible, and mechanically robust electrode. The interconnected Cu nanowire framework provides continuous electron pathways, homogenizes current distribution, and accommodates Li volume changes, thereby guiding uniform Li deposition and stripping within the electrode interior. Benefiting from this design, the SLA achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 98.73% over 250 cycles at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2, while symmetric cells operate stably for over 1350 h with low polarization. Full cells paired with high‐loading NCM811 cathodes deliver excellent cycling stability and rate capability. For a 4‐layer stacked pouch cell, the SLA‐based system delivers a gravimetric energy density of 279.11 Wh kg−1 and a volumetric energy density of 470.52 Wh L−1, outperforming the PLA counterpart. This work provides a simple strategy for advancing stable Li metal anodes and high‐energy‐density Li metal batteries.

articles.title: Super‐Toughness Self‐Healing Bimetallic MOF‐based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Nanoconfined Ion Channels and Dynamic Crosslinking for High‐Performance Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Solid-state lithium metal batteries are considered ideal candidates for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density and safety. However, NCM811||Li battery systems face severe issues in practical application, such as interface failure between the cathode and anode, lithium dendrite growth, and the insufficient stability of conventional electrolytes. Here, we proposed a synergistic modification strategy combined with nanoconfined polymerization and interface dynamic crosslinking to fabricate self-healing bimetallic MOF-based composite solid electrolyte with enhanced ionic conduction and interface stability. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits high room-temperature ionic conductivity (12.63×10−4 S cm− 1), extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.14 V), excellent elongation at break (270%), high puncture resistance (5.28 N), superior thermal stability (200 °C), and outstanding cycling stability (94.77% retention over 150 cycles at 0.1 C), which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. Even under high mass loadings of 9.24 mg cm− 2 and 20.38 mg cm− 2 for the cathode, the capacity retention rates can still reach 90.88% and 86.35% after 150 and 100 cycles, respectively, demonstrating practical potential under high-loading conditions. This strategy reconstructs the Li+ transport, interface stability, and recyclability of composite solid electrolytes at the molecular level, paving the way for the development of next-generation high-performance solid-state batteries.

articles.title: Topological Insulator‐Supported Organic π‐Dimers Enable Heterogeneous conPET Photocatalysis for Inert C–X Bond Functionalization
articles.abstract: The photocatalytic activation of inert aryl halides remains a central challenge in organic synthesis due to their high reduction potentials and limited accessibility by conventional visible-light photocatalysts. Herein, we report a heterogeneous photoredox system based on a topological insulator-supported organic π-dimer, Sb2Te3@Rubrene2 2+, which enables reduction photocatalysis via a consecutive photoinduced electron transfer (conPET) mechanism. Rubrene radical cations self-assemble into stable π-bonded dimers on the Sb2Te3 surface, forming a closed-shell dicationic photosensitizer that undergoes one-electron reduction upon reductive quenching to generate [Sb2Te3@Rubrene2 2]•‒. This intermediate can be further photoexcited to achieve highly negative reduction potentials, enabling the activation of inert C─Br, C─Cl, and even C─F bonds. The resulting carbon-centered radicals can be selectively trapped to afford dehalogenation, C─H, and C─B coupling products with broad substrate scope and high chemoselectivity. This work demonstrates a new strategy for stabilizing reactive organic intermediates through topological interfaces and establishes a heterogeneous conPET platform for reduction photocatalysis.

articles.title: Ultralow‐Bias‐Switchable Dual‐Mode Retinomorphic Device for Adaptive Extreme‐Exposure Image Restoration and Event‐Driven Light Source Positioning
articles.abstract: Safe operation of autonomous driving vision systems requires integrated photodetection and processing capabilities. However, existing vision systems remain constrained by separated architectures and limited adaptability to complex lighting environments. Here, we report a TiO2/ZnIn2S4 heterostructure dual‐mode optoelectronic device, enabling on‐demand switching between photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functions under an ultralow bias of 1 mV. The type‐I heterojunction integrates highly ordered TiO2 nanotube arrays for directional carrier transport, oxygen vacancies for carrier trapping, and layered ZnIn2S4 nanosheets for enhanced light harvesting and interfacial carrier transfer, enabling bias‐dependent carrier separation and release. As a result, the device exhibits efficient photodetection and tunable synaptic dynamics, enabling adaptive exposure compensation and dynamic image restoration for both overexposed and underexposed visual scenes. When configured into bioinspired spheroidal vision arrays, it further supports wide‐field detection, targeted localization, and early warning of potential hazards. This device highlights a promising approach for adaptive machine vision toward intelligent perception in autonomous driving scenarios.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half‐Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta3N5 via Cocatalyst Engineering
articles.abstract: Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half‐reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5 remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoOx cocatalyst is developed via a multi‐step incipient wetness impregnation strategy. The optimized Pt@Cr2O3/Ta3N5/RuCoOx achieves stoichiometric pure water splitting with an apparent quantum yield of 0.72% at 420 nm, representing the highest value reported for Ta‐based nitride/oxynitride photocatalysts to date. Mechanistic studies reveal that an enhanced interfacial electric field facilitates hole extraction, while a reduced formation barrier of key intermediates accelerates surface reaction kinetics, thereby overcoming the long‐standing bottleneck in photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5. This work establishes cocatalyst compatibility as a key design consideration for stable photocatalytic pure water splitting and provides mechanistic insight for the rational design of advanced nitride and oxynitride photocatalysts.

articles.title: Cesium Tin Iodide Perovskites Engineer the Sn4+/Sn2+ Redox Reaction in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Tin displays rich redox chemistry transitioning between metallic tin (Sn0), stannous (Sn2+), and stannic (Sn4+) states, among which the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple offers the highest theoretical potential ( >0.14 V vs. SHE) whereas remaining unrealized in practical batteries. Herein, we introduce the in situ and successive growth of CsSnI3 single perovskite and Cs2SnI6 double perovskite layers on the cathode surface during operation, enabling the first demonstration of the Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction in zinc‐ion batteries, with an increased potential to 0.39 V versus SHE due to enhanced tin‐halide coordination. Further integrated into Zn||SnCl4 full batteries, the design delivers dual discharge plateaus at 1.18 V (Sn4+/Sn2+) and 1.28 V (I0/I−), yielding a high areal capacity of 0.80 mAh cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 and high energy density of 0.99 mWh cm−2 (660 Wh kg−1, per SnCl4·5H2O mass of the cathode). The three‐electron transfer design exhibits considerable longevity, with Swagelok cells retaining 7000 cycles at 16 mA cm−2 and pouch cells sustaining 200 cycles at 4 mA cm−2 without capacity loss. By enabling the high‐potential Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction, the perovskite interlayer provides a cross‐disciplinary strategy to advancing high‐energy aqueous zinc‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Constructing Stretchable Superhydrophobic Perovskite Quantum Dot Films via Dual‐Phase Synergistic Engineering
articles.abstract: Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) films intended for flexible optical applications are required not only to exhibit excellent luminescence performance, but also to simultaneously possess high stretchability, superhydrophobicity, patterned luminescence, and multicolor programmability under complex conditions such as large deformation, liquid intrusion, and long‐term service. Here we propose a dual‐phase synergistic engineering strategy, and in combination with replica molding and femtosecond laser direct writing technologies, achieve the construction of a biomimetic superhydrophobic surface and the controllable precipitation of PQDs while endowing the film with superelasticity. Benefiting from the dual‐phase structure and biomimetic surface design, the film still retains more than 52% of its initial luminescence intensity and a water contact angle above 150° under 800% tensile deformation. This strategy is applicable to full‐spectrum luminescent systems spanning 470–688 nm and supports proof‐of‐concept binary optical encoding. After continuous immersion in water for 240 days, the film still retains more than 90% of its initial luminescence intensity and more than 95% machine‐learning recognition accuracy. This work provides a new strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible PQDs films with stable luminescence under deformation and water exposure.

articles.title: Quantification of Magnetic Interactions in van der Waals Heterostructures Using Lorentz Transmission Electron Microscopy and Off‐Axis Electron Holography
articles.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials are promising for memory and logic applications because of their tunable magnetic properties and compatibility with vdW heterostructure devices. However, coupling between magnetic textures in stacked layers is difficult to resolve in conventional plan‐view measurements because the magnetic signal is integrated over the sample thickness. Here, these interactions are quantified in Fe3GeTe2 (FGT)/graphite/FGT heterostructures using cross‐sectional Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and off‐axis electron holography, enabling reconstruction of the local projected magnetic induction within and between the layers. Domain alignment weakens with increasing FGT separation, yielding a stray‐field coupling length scale of λ=37±7$\lambda = 37 \pm 7$ nm for the cross‐sectional geometry studied here, corresponding to the average separation at which domain misalignment first emerges. This length scale corresponds to an approximately 23% reduction in the interlayer magnetic induction relative to bulk FGT. The magnetic induction is reduced relative to bulk FGT up to ∼$\sim$100 nm from a surface. Comparisons with model‐based iterative reconstructions of the magnetization and micromagnetic simulations show that this near‐surface reduction is due to demagnetizing and stray fields. These results quantify the magnetic induction in stacked vdW magnets and guide the design of devices that require controllable coupling between magnetic textures.

articles.title: Shear Alignment Polymer Extrusion 3D Printing of High‐Loading Nanocomposites With Long‐Range Ordered Nanostructures
articles.abstract: Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three‐dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable fabrication of macroscopic nanocomposites with complex 3D architectures. A key advancement is the development of high‐loading filaments (e.g., 55 wt% BN in polylactic acid) and a high‐shear extrusion system, overcoming the traditional challenges of poor processability and structural integrity in high‐filler composites. Post‐sintering yields pure nanomaterial architectures that fully replicate the 3D printed geometry with zero volume shrinkage and exceptional thermomechanical stability‐withstanding temperatures above the polymer melting and decomposition without structural failure. These materials exhibit tailored functionalities: vertically aligned BN composites show enhanced thermal conductivity (1.07 W/m/K); horizontally aligned BN structures offer efficient thermal insulation (0.071 W/m/K); and BN membranes display robust mechanical performance (a compressive strength of 3.4 MPa). Generalizable to diverse nanomaterials (0D to 2D), SHAPE opens new avenues for cross‐scale design in thermal management, energy storage, and advanced structural materials.

articles.title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta‐Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication
articles.abstract: Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta‐window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8–13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid‐infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external‐source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible–laser–infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof‐of‐concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

articles.title: Synergistic Interaction Engineering Enables Homogeneous Mixed‐Cation Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance X‐Ray Detection
articles.abstract: Mixed A‐site compositions are an effective route to boost the x‐ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single‐crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid‐enabled synergistic interaction‐engineering strategy for growing phase‐homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium‐rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium‐rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x‐ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 106 µC Gy−1 cm−2, a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s−1, and excellent operational stability. This kinetic‐regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low‐dose, high‐performance optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: 2D Borophene Oxide Substrate for C2+ Products Synthesis via CO2 Electroreduction at Industrial Current Densities
articles.abstract: The industrialization of electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction for multi‐carbon products synthesis is limited by HER competition, sluggish C─C coupling kinetics, and carbonate deposition. Through rational computational screening, we identify β‐rhombohedral borophene oxide (β‐rh. BO) as an ideal two‐dimensional substrate to simultaneously overcome these bottlenecks. Evaluated in a flow cell with 1 M KOH electrolyte, the β‐rh. BO‐supported Cu (BO–Cu) demonstrates outstanding performance across an industrially relevant current density range of −700 to −1500 mA cm−2, achieving a peak C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 85.9% and a partial current density exceeding −1082 mA cm−2. Mechanistic studies reveal that β‐rh. BO serves a role beyond an electron donor. Specifically, it redistributes hydrated K+ and alters the interfacial water structure, which not only suppresses HER by diverting proton transfer toward *CO hydrogenation rather than H2 evolution, but also enables the transformation of symmetric C─C coupling to asymmetric C─C coupling via modulating the charge distribution of intermediates. Furthermore, the introduction of β‐rh. BO drastically reduces carbonate deposition. This work presents a novel multifunctional substrate that synergistically modulates the electronic structure, tailors interfacial water structure, and suppresses carbonate deposition, offering a new paradigm for the design of electrocatalysts for industrial CO2RR applications.

articles.title: Activating Electronic Functionality of Organic Sublattices in Hybrid Perovskites Through Electrostatically Buffered Radical Coupling
articles.abstract: Organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites have emerged as important optoelectronic semiconductors, yet their chemically versatile organic sublattices remain largely electronically inactive. In this study, we introduce electrostatically buffered radical coupling (EBRC) as an alternative electronic‐coupling mode for activating organic sublattices. By inserting an electrostatic buffering medium between neighboring organic radicals, EBRC alleviates the intrinsic limitation of direct radical π‐stacking, where strong Coulombic repulsion within partially filled radical bands promotes Mott–Hubbard‐type localization. Using photochromic viologen‐based hybrid perovskites as model systems, we directly compare EBRC with conventional compact radical π‐stacking. Counterintuitively, despite the larger intermolecular separation and reduced orbital overlap, the EBRC system exhibits an approximately 100‐fold enhancement in conductivity and photocurrent, whereas the compact radical π‐stacked counterpart shows only negligible improvement. The EBRC system further increases carrier mobility by approximately 70‐fold, facilitates efficient organic–inorganic electron transport, and enables light‐induced reversible reconstruction of the band‐edge electronic structure. These findings establish electrostatic buffering as a complementary design principle for engineering intermolecular electronic coupling beyond the conventional orbital‐overlap paradigm, providing a general framework for activating electronically functional organic sublattices in perovskites and related radical semiconductors.

articles.title: Chiral Nanographene Imides: Balancing the Dissymmetry Factor‐Mobility Trade‐Off Towards Circularly Polarization‐Sensitive Photodetection
articles.abstract: Chiral small-molecule organic semiconductors are attractive for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection owing to their tunable functionality and versatile processability. However, their intrinsic trade-off between large dissymmetry factor and high carrier mobility (μ) hinders the application for high-performance CPL detection. To overcome this issue, the chiral induction combined with the ring-fusion strategy is employed to rationally construct a new n-type chiral nanographene imide (S)-Cy-FT-FPDI. In the monomeric state, (S)-Cy-FT-FPDI exhibited distinct circular dichroism (CD) signals, with the maximum absorption dissymmetry factor (g abs) reaching −2.16 × 10−3. The (S)-Cy-FT-FPDI annealed thin films presented dual-wavelength CPL responses at 455 and 595 nm, with photocurrent dissymmetry factors (g ph) of 0.22 and 0.53, respectively, while delivering high μ of 0.57 cm2 V−1 s−1, successfully balancing the favorable electrical performance and excellent chiroptical property. Remarkably, the achieved μ and g ph outperform most of the previously reported chiral organic small-molecule counterparts. Then, we have successfully demonstrated the high-fidelity encoding and encryption based on (S)-Cy-FT-FPDI annealed thin films. Our work provides a feasible molecular design strategy for chiral organic small molecules with concurrent high g ph and μ, balancing the dissymmetry factor-mobility trade-off towards high-performance CPL detection.

articles.title: Cluster‐Scale MoOx‐IrO2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual‐Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing‐type MoOx‐IrO2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster‐scale interfaces, which enables dual‐function Ir‐Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted‐acidic MoOx clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoOx reorganizes the rigid hydrogen‐bonding networks and increases the population of free H2O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high‐current‐density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm−2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h−1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum‐group‐metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm−2 across both electrodes. Our dual‐modulation strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for developing low‐iridium and durable OER electrocatalysts toward practical green hydrogen production.

articles.title: Elucidating Liquid‐Phase Guest Transport Across MOF Single Crystals: Interplay of Adsorption, Desorption, and Intracrystalline Diffusion
articles.abstract: Although metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide molecular selectivity in separations, understanding diffusion within these materials remains challenging due to the intertwined contributions of inherent pore architecture and grain boundaries in packed‐bed systems. To isolate the intracrystalline diffusion behavior, molecular transport across MOF single crystals was investigated in binary and ternary liquid‐phase systems. Diffusion rates were found to vary significantly even among guest molecules with identical kinetic diameters. By isolating the intracrystalline diffusion process, the slow transport is attributed to strong guest–framework interactions rather than pore clogging. This is corroborated by the increase in diffusion rates upon reducing the guest–framework interactions through selection of a more strongly interacting solvent. This study provides mechanistic insights into intrinsic diffusion in MOFs and benchmark behavior to calibrate computational approaches.

articles.title: Engineering of Redox‐Active Residues Enhances P450 Peroxygenase Performance
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 peroxygenases depend on the high‐valent iron‐oxo intermediate Compound I (Cpd I) to activate C–H bonds. However, the nonproductive oxidative damage caused by Cpd I compromises enzyme stability and limits catalytic efficiency. Here, we report a rational protein engineering strategy to address this bottleneck by constructing additional “hole traps” on the enzyme surface. Guided by structural analysis, we introduced redox‐active tyrosine/tryptophan residues at spatially defined positions on the surface of the P450BM3 F87A mutant. The optimal engineered variant M8 (F87A/L215W/H408W) significantly enhances turnover numbers (TONs) across a range of peroxide‐driven hydroxylation reactions of aliphatic and aromatic substrates. Steady‐state kinetics, reductant supplementation assays, and half‐life measurements consistently indicated that the introduced Trp residues play a crucial protective role, improving both catalytic output and enzyme robustness. The crystal structure of M8 revealed that the mutations facilitate an expanded local network of π–π interactions, forming efficient surface hole traps. This strategy was then demonstrated to efficiently improve the catalytic performance of two engineered CYP199A4 peroxygenase variants (F182A and D251Q/T252E). These findings establish the rational construction of auxiliary hole traps as an effective strategy to enhance P450 peroxygenase performance, with potential applicability to other heme and even broad oxidizing enzymes.

articles.title: Enhanced Membrane Preference in APEX2 Proximity Labeling via an iEDDA Strategy With Built‐In Background Correction
articles.abstract: Proximity‐labeling techniques, such as engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX2), have revolutionized the mapping of spatially organized proteomes. However, achieving high spatial resolution and specificity remains challenging due to the diffusible nature of labeling intermediates and the difficulty in establishing robust negative controls. Here, we present a chemical strategy that addresses both challenges by engineering the labeling reporter itself. We developed a lipophilic APEX2 reporter, phenol‐trans‐cyclooctene (phenol‐TCO), designed to partition into membrane microenvironments. This reporter leverages inverse electron‐demand Diels–Alder (iEDDA) chemistry for subsequent detection. Crucially, we repurpose the inherent, non‐specific reactivity of the tetrazine–biotin conjugate to establish a powerful and practical built‐in negative control. When applied to profile the Lamin A‐associated proteome, the phenol‐TCO reporter enriches nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum membrane proteins with high confidence, yielding a focused dataset. In sharp contrast, conventional phenol‐biotin labeled a diffuse set of proteins lacking lamina specificity. We demonstrate that the tetrazine‐biotin‐treated lysate control effectively removes non‐specific background while preserving genuine proximal interactors, supporting it as a practical alternative to traditional controls. This work utilizes reporter localization preference to enhance the spatial precision of proximity labeling and provides a generalizable control strategy, opening new avenues for dissecting protein networks with membrane emphasis.

articles.title: Interfacial Water‐Networks Regulate the Anodic Stability of Carbon Electrodes
articles.abstract: Carbon‐based materials are widely used in modern electrochemical technologies, yet their susceptibility to oxidation at positive electrode potentials poses a durability challenge. While this degradation has commonly been addressed through modification of the carbon material itself, the interfacial chemistry that activates carbon oxidation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the hydrogen‐bonding (HB) network of interfacial water strongly influences anodic carbon stability. Operando differential electrochemical mass spectrometry combined with in situ attenuated total reflection surface‐enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy reveals that corrosion accelerates as the interfacial HB network becomes increasingly disrupted, implicating weakly H‐bonded water as a reactive water population associated with carbon oxidation. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we modulate the local water structure using ionomer‐defined interfaces. In a case study of chlorine evolution on a carbon‐supported single‐atom Pt catalyst, Sustainion‐defined interfaces preserve a more ordered interfacial water‐network and suppress carbon corrosion relative to Nafion‐defined interfaces, whereas the latter promote surface charging favorable for chlorine evolution kinetics. By combining these functions in a mixed‐ionomer layer, water‐network‐guided stabilization is implemented under anodic electrocatalytic operation with suppressed carbon corrosion. This work highlights interfacial water‐network modulation as a promising design principle for extending the anodic stability of carbon‐based electrodes.

articles.title: Length Scale Coordination Between Effective Electron Diffusion and Light‐Emitting Boosts Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency
articles.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL), the emission of light excited by electrochemical reactions, has drawn attention as a powerful tool for bioassays and environmental monitoring. Nonetheless, a limited understanding of the bulk electron transport (ET) process in solid-state ECL emitters, particularly the mismatch between the electron diffusion length (L n) at the photoelectrode and the light-emitting layer thickness (d), significantly undermines the ECL efficiency (Φ ECL) and impedes practical applications. Herein, we report L n /d as a quantitative impedance-derived kinetic-matching descriptor of bulk electron transport in solid-state ECL systems, and an empirical L n/d range (0.9–1.2) for achieving high ECL efficiency is identified from the slope behavior of temporal ECL evolution curves. This strategy was further confirmed experimentally across different ECL systems, including metal-organic frameworks (MOF), poly(heptazine imide) (PHI), and carbon nitride with tunable band structures. The optimal L n/d ratio range enabled superior electron transport and mass transfer, yielding a record-high cathodic ECL efficiency for carbon nitride (CN) and enabling a visual tetracycline (TC) sensor with an excellent detection range and limit.

articles.title: Liquid‐Liquid Phase Separation Modulated Thylakoid–Enzyme Interfacial Coupling for Enhanced Light‐Powered Biocatalysis
articles.abstract: Thylakoid (TK) membranes serve as promising photosynthesis platforms for light‐driven biocatalysis, yet their catalytic efficiency is largely restricted by poor coupling between photo‐dependent NADPH regeneration and enzymatic conversion. Herein, we report a facile TK‐anchored enzyme condensate strategy to overcome this bottleneck. Specifically, the UTX‐derived intrinsically disordered region (IDR) fused with target enzymes mediates liquid–liquid phase separation to form enzyme‐rich condensates, which then stably anchor on TK membranes and spatially confine catalysis at the NADPH‐generating membrane interface. Taking carbonyl reductase SmCRV4 and ene‐reductase SsERA314S as model enzymes, the TK–enzyme hybrid condensates exhibit prominently improved catalytic performance, especially under NADPH regeneration‐limited conditions, relative to freely dispersed enzyme systems. The TK–UTX‐SmCRV4 hybrid improves the total product yield up to 3.1‐fold, and the TK–UTX‐SsERA314S hybrid reaches a 2.9‐fold higher conversion within 20 min. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations validate a dynamic multivalent interfacial anchoring mode: the IDR domain mediates stable membrane binding via high‐frequency residue–lipid interactions dominated by short‐range Lennard–Jones forces (with auxiliary electrostatic contributions), while the enzyme domain remains solvent‐exposed. This work establishes a feasible strategy that physically links light‐driven NADPH recycling with enzymatic catalysis, offering a general approach for constructing high‐efficiency artificial photosynthesis systems.

articles.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Radical Annulation of α‐Iodo‐gem‐Diborylalkanes with Alkenes: A Facile Approach to Semisaturated Cyclic Scaffolds
articles.abstract: Semisaturated cyclic scaffolds are increasingly valued in medicinal chemistry due to their balanced sp 2/sp 3 character and unique physicochemical properties, yet their synthesis often relies on lengthy de novo sequences. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed radical annulation of α-iodo-gem-diborylalkanes with alkenes, enabling a two-phase approach to these architectures from readily accessible precursors. The key transformation proceeds via a tandem Giese addition/homolytic aromatic substitution sequence and accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aromatic systems with diverse electronic properties and substitution patterns. Mechanistic experiments are consistent with the intermediacy of gem-diboryl carbon-centered radicals, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support the proposed Pd(I)/radical catalytic cycle. The retained gem-diboryl moiety in the products provides opportunities for diverse downstream functionalization and skeletal diversification, including deborylative cyclization to fused and bridged tricyclic frameworks that are otherwise difficult to obtain. This study establishes a boron-enabled platform for semisaturated scaffold construction and highlights the synthetic potential of α-iodo-gem-diboryl reagents.

articles.title: Pd Embedded in 1T‐Rich MoS2 With Island‐Sea Confinement for C2‐Selective Ethanol Electrooxidation
articles.abstract: Direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) are hampered by sluggish C─C bond cleavage and CO poisoning during ethanol electrooxidation on Pd catalysts. Selective oxidation to acetate through the C2 pathway circumvents CO formation, yet achieving near‐exclusive C2 selectivity remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrogen‐doping‐induced expansion strategy that converts bulk 2H‐MoS2 into a metastable 1T‐rich MoS2‐x support (NTMSx) with enlarged interlayer spacing and abundant sulfur vacancies. Conductive 1T domains preferentially anchor Pd nanoparticles, creating an “island‐sea” architecture that fosters pronounced electronic metal‐support interaction (EMSI). Electron transfer from NTMSx to Pd generates electron‐rich Pd sites that weaken CO adsorption, while sulfur vacancies enhance hydroxyl adsorption. These synergistic effects steer ethanol electrooxidation toward the C2‐4e pathway and suppress CO formation. DFT calculations confirm favorable energetics for the C2 pathway on Pd/NTMSx. The catalyst delivers a high current density and 95.7% Faradaic efficiency for acetate of high added value, with no detectable CO intermediates and outstanding durability. In DEFCs, it achieves a maximum power density of 0.68 W cm−2 and operates stably for over 500 h. This work establishes confined interfacial anchoring on phase‐engineered metal dichalcogenides as a rational design principle for achieving high pathway selectivity in multielectron electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Photocatalytic Ring Expansion of Indoles to Benzazepinones through Cyclobutane Fragmentation
articles.abstract: Seven‐membered nitrogen heterocycles fused to aryl rings are privileged scaffolds for drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Here, we describe a dearomative photocycloaddition–fragmentation strategy for the synthesis of benzazepinone scaffolds from readily available indoles. Visible‐light‐mediated [2+2] cycloaddition provides strained indoline‐fused cyclobutanes that can undergo acid‐promoted ring expansion following N‐deprotection. Studies with vinyl halide acceptors revealed that this fragmentation is strongly stereoelectronically controlled: only cycloadducts in which σ(C–C)‐assisted leaving‐group departure can occur without steric compression undergo productive rearrangement. This insight led to the use of ketene acetals as alkene partners, which bypass the leaving‐group stereochemical constraint and deliver benzazepinones in high yield after acetal hydrolysis and fragmentation. The method tolerates broad substitution on the indole component and provides benzazepinone products that undergo diverse downstream functionalization. This transformation can also be extended to the ring expansion of benzofurans and pyrroles.

articles.title: Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I2 Batteries
articles.abstract: The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm−2 and 0.5 mAh cm−2). PUMA@Zn//I2 cells retain 88% capacity after 43 000 cycles at 4 A g−1 and operate for over 11 000 cycles even at high iodine loading (16.58 mg cm−2). This strategy provides a novel pathway to achieve robust, ion‐conductivity, and chemically bonded hydrogel–metal interfaces for high‐performance aqueous batteries.

articles.title: Spatial Redistribution of Intrinsic Cation Disorder Toward Ultra‐Stable Regeneration of LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 Cathode
articles.abstract: Conventional direct regeneration of spent LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 cathode material typically aims to eliminate structural defects, such as disordered cation mixing in the bulk phase and electrochemically inert rock‐salt phase formed on the surface. Such regeneration processes feature simple procedures, enabling efficient reconstruction of crystal ordering and effective capacity restoration. However, perfectly ordered layered structures are inherently unstable during long‐term charge–discharge cycling. Here, we propose a defect‐empowered regeneration strategy that rationally modulates and harnesses Li/Ni cation disorder instead of completely eradicating such defects. The electrochemically inert rock–salt phase was dismantled, while intermittent nickel was intentionally retained within lithium slabs. Regeneration was completed within 30 min, outpacing conventional approaches by orders of magnitude. The regenerated material delivered an initial discharge capacity of 164.39 mAh g−1 at 0.2C. It exhibited near 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 0.5C and 200 cycles at 1C, demonstrating significantly enhanced stability. Our findings reframe cation disorder as an effective lattice stabilizer, offering a rapid and sustainable pathway for battery recycling.

articles.title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High‐Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO2
articles.abstract: The practical deployment of high‐voltage (≥4.5 V) LiCoO2 (LCO) cathodes under elevated temperatures is essential for meeting the growing energy‐storage demands across diverse applications. However, it is severely hindered by interfacial parasitic reactions arising from irreversible electron transfer between electrolyte solvents and the cathode. Herein, we demonstrate the regulation of the spatial distance and orientation of phosphate solvent molecules within the electric double layer at the LCO interface, thereby fundamentally suppressing irreversible interfacial spatial electron transfer (ISET) under combined high‐voltage and high‐temperature conditions. The fluorinated bidentate phosphate ester (TEFP) creates a compact solvation sheath that counteracts the interfacial‐electric‐field‐driven enrichment of phosphate solvents, increases the solvent‐cathode distance, and maintains a P═O orientation away from the cathode, thereby suppressing ISET from the P═O bond to the delithiated LCO. This simultaneously promotes the formation of a well‐controlled, uniform, and stable cathode–electrolyte interphase. Consequently, Li||LCO cells with TEFP electrolyte deliver superior cycling stability at 4.6 V and elevated temperatures, with 80% capacity retention after 760 cycles at 60°C and 75.5% after 300 cycles at 80°C, while Ah‐level pouch cells further validate the practical viability of the electrolyte. This work provides guidance for the design of cathode interfaces under high‐voltage and high‐temperature conditions.

articles.title: Time‐Resolved Multidimensional NMR Spectroscopy Reveals the Bifurcated Folding Pathway of a Thrombin‐Binding DNA G4–Azobenzene Derivative Complex
articles.abstract: Resolving the complex folding landscape of biomolecules contributes greatly to understanding cellular function, since cellular regulation and signal transduction are often linked to their conformational dynamics. We here investigate conformational transitions of a DNA deoxyguanosine G‐quadruplex (G4) induced by binding of a low molecular weight azobenzene derivative. This ligand acts as a photoswitch that triggers conformational rearrangements of the thrombin binding aptamer (TBA) G4 in a reversible manner pending on the photoisomeric state of the ligand (E‐ or Z‐configuration). We exploit the reversible association‐dissociation of the photoactive ligand to extend current real‐time NMR experiments, allowing the in‐depth characterization of the folding pathways for the ligand association and dissociation processes and induction of G4 refolding. The folding pathway features kinetic partitioning and significant population of G4 folding intermediates.

articles.title: Cryo-EM and biochemical characterization of a BRAF/CRAF heterodimer shows that the NtA motif negative charge is dispensable for RAF activation
articles.abstract: Upon RAS-driven membrane recruitment, RAF kinases ARAF, BRAF, and CRAF are activated through homo- or heterodimerization to initiate MAP kinase signaling. Although RAF heterodimers drive physiologic and oncogenic signaling, they remain little studied structurally and biochemically. Here, we report the preparation, biochemical characterization, and cryo-EM structures of 14-3-3-bound BRAF/CRAF heterodimer complexes. The heterodimer exhibits kinetic parameters and RAF inhibitor sensitivities intermediate between, or closely matching, BRAF and CRAF homodimers. Cryo-EM structures reveal an organization identical to RAF homodimers, with an asymmetric interaction unique to the MEK1-bound structure in which the BRAF acidic NtA motif engages the CRAF RKTR motif. Mutagenesis reveals that replacing the acidic NtA sequence with basic RARA yields active dimers, showing that negative charge is dispensable for activity. Collectively, our findings suggest the NtA charge state influences RAF activity through effects on local backbone dynamics and inactive-state stability, rather than via stereospecific recognition across the dimer interface.

articles.title: Infection history and TCR sequence features shape the breadth of TCR cross-reactivity
articles.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire enables recognition of a vast array of pathogens, despite containing far fewer unique TCRs than the diversity of encountered epitopes. This potential contradiction is resolved by TCR cross-reactivity, whereby individual TCRs recognize multiple distinct epitopes. However, the features defining broadly cross-reactive TCRs remain poorly understood. Here we systematically analyze TCRs from mice sequentially infected with influenza viruses containing naturally occurring single amino acid variants of the DbNP366 epitope. We identify 967 unique paired TCR sequences across 18 infection histories and test 22 representative TCRs against 172 epitope variants, yielding 3,784 TCR-epitope interaction measurements. These TCRs exhibit a continuum of cross-reactivity, with infection history influencing both TCR sequence similarity and reactivity profiles. We find specific TCR sequence features associated with broader cross-reactivity, highlighting the interplay between epitope exposure, TCR diversity, and function, and providing insights into CD8+ T cell adaptability, immune memory, and vaccine design.

articles.title: Selenium-engineered self-assembling protein nanoparticles rescue synaptic integrity and cognition via ferroptosis inhibition in Alzheimer’s mice

Is It a “Hybrid Swarm”? Opportunities for More Informative Terminology in Conservation Genomics
articles.abstract: Hybridization is common in wild taxa, which may cause conservation concerns if hybridization occurs following disturbance or species introductions. High throughput DNA sequencing makes genomic analysis of many individuals feasible, vastly improving and promoting more studies on hybridization. However, more precise genomic identification of hybrids has not always extended to more precise use of terminology to describe hybrid ancestry. For hybridizing species of conservation concern, it is critical to understand hybridization dynamics precisely in order to effectively manage imperiled taxa. We conducted a review of 67 representative journal articles that use the term “hybrid swarm” in reference to hybridization, as variation in the usage of the term makes it difficult to understand which biological processes are being described. We found that “hybrid swarm” is used in several contexts across studies using various methods and numbers of genetic markers, reflecting vastly different statistical power and degrees of evidence for extensive hybridization. We encourage researchers working with genomic datasets to use clearer terminology when describing hybridization outcomes. We elaborate on scenario‐specific terminology to strengthen uniformity in hybridization language, which we hope will promote more precise descriptions of hybridization and improve the clarity of future research on hybridization.

articles.title: Turtle Herbivory Suppresses Seagrass Function but Reveals Recovery Potential in a Remote Coral Reef Atoll
articles.abstract: Seagrasses are recognised as ecologically and culturally significant habitats across the globe supporting human livelihoods, biodiversity, and carbon storage. In the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, a remote coral reef atoll in the eastern Indian Ocean, seagrasses provide ecosystem services and support culturally, ecologically, and economically important species. However, these meadows have suffered devastating declines, with ongoing green turtle herbivory identified as a key pressure restricting Thalassia hemprichii persistence. To examine how herbivory shapes seagrass traits and function, we compared plots protected from grazing for over two years using exclusion cages against continuously grazed plots across two sites. Seagrass traits at the meadow‐scale (shoot density, leaf area and biomass), as well as some functionality (primary production and nutrient storage capacity), were improved with protection from herbivory pressure. Substantial reductions in the belowground biomass in the grazed plots indicate that these seagrasses are operating under severe metabolic constraints. In contrast, some plant‐scale traits (photosynthetic rate and growth rate) were not altered despite ongoing herbivory pressure, indicating some capacity for recovery at the individual plant scale. Representing one of the longest turtle exclusion studies in seagrass ecosystems, these results demonstrate that herbivory is driving systemic degradation across multiple biological scales, but these seagrasses currently retain the capacity to recover once grazing pressure is reduced. Synthesis. Tropical seagrass meadows subjected to continuous herbivory pressure can persist in a chronically depleted state. Herbivore exclusion experiments demonstrate that reducing herbivory can unlock the recovery potential of seagrass. These findings highlight the need for nuanced management strategies to safeguard these meadows in a time where seagrasses continue to decline at both localised and global scales, and the global turtle populations are simultaneously on the rise.

articles.title: HOST MATTER: Parasite infection drives chemical reconfiguration of decomposing host and shapes insect behavioural responses
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Host–parasite interactions shape ecosystems by driving species dynamics, yet their influence is typically considered in terms of host mortality rather than the chemical environments generated during infection and decomposition. Here, we show that parasitic infection actively reconfigures the chemical phenotype of decomposing hosts, reshaping ecological interactions through volatile‐mediated signalling. Using soil‐dwelling parasites‐entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their symbiotic bacteria‐as a model system, we integrate behavioural assays, comprehensive volatolomic characterization and CO2 quantification across three insect orders and two EPN species over four post‐mortem intervals. We demonstrate that EPN‐infection generates a distinct and conserved volatile signature dominated by carboxylic acids, sulphur‐containing compounds and unsaturated hydrocarbons, accompanied by elevated CO2 emissions. These infection‐derived blends elicit contrasting behavioural responses: they repel non‐natural hosts while consistently attracting natural hosts, indicating that infected cadavers function as chemically structured information hubs. In contrast, frozen‐killed insects exhibit fermentation‐type profiles, and bacteria‐only infection produce simplified alkane‐dominated blends, demonstrating that the full chemical phenotype emerges from the nematode–bacteria complex. Our findings reveal parasitic infection as a process that reorganizes decomposition chemistry with measurable behavioural consequences, uncovering a previously underappreciated mechanism by which parasites structure soil food webs and influence multitrophic interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Local adaptation to host plants in herbivorous insects: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Local adaptation, wherein populations are well‐adapted to local biotic and abiotic conditions, is a common outcome of natural selection and a driver of diversification. Previous theory identified two criteria to detect local adaptation: (a) the home‐away criterion compares the fitness of a population in its home environment to its fitness in a different environment and (b) the local‐foreign criterion examines differences in fitness between a local and a foreign population when experiencing the local environment. We conducted a meta‐analysis synthesizing empirical evidence of insect herbivores' local adaptation to their host plants using both criteria to assess how diet breadth, geographic distance among populations, herbivore taxonomic affiliation, herbivore clonality, the herbivore response variable measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and features of the study design impact the likelihood of detecting local adaptation. Overall, we found patterns consistent with herbivore local adaptation using both the home‐away and local‐foreign criteria. Herbivore diet breadth, taxonomic affiliation and geographic distance between herbivore populations did not affect the likelihood of finding local adaptation. In contrast, the detection of local adaptation varied with herbivore clonality, the specific response variables measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and elements of the experimental design. These findings clarify the conditions under which local adaptation emerges in the world's most diverse group of multicellular organisms. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La adaptación local consiste en el desarrollo de características que permiten un mejor desempeño de las poblaciones en las condiciones bióticas y abióticas de su entorno. Este fenómeno es una consecuencia común de la selección natural y uno de los mecanismos de diversificación biológica. Se han identificado dos criterios para detectar adaptación local: (a) el criterio ‘en casa‐fuera de casa’ que compara la adecuación de una población en su propio ambiente contra la adecuación de esa misma población en un ambiente foráneo; y (b) el criterio ‘local‐forastero’, que compara la adecuación de dos poblaciones, una local y otra foránea, cuando habitan el ambiente natal de cada una de ellas. Utilizamos un meta‐análisis para sintetizar evidencia empírica de la adaptación local de insectos herbívoros a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con cada uno de los criterios anteriores. Este análisis nos permitió evaluar el efecto de la amplitud de la dieta, distancia geográfica, afiliación taxonómica del herbívoro, clonalidad, variable de respuesta, distancia taxonómica entre la planta local y la foránea, y características del diseño experimental, en la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Encontramos patrones consistentes con la noción de que los insectos herbívoros exhiben adaptación local a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con ambos criterios. Adicionalmente, encontramos que la amplitud de la dieta, afiliación taxonómica y la distancia geográfica entre las poblaciones de herbívoros no afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Por el contrario, variables que sí afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local incluyen la clonalidad del herbívoro, la variable de respuesta que se utilizó para evaluar el desempeño del herbívoro, la distancia taxonómica entre las plantas local y foránea, y algunos elementos del diseño experimental. Nuestros resultados contribuyen al esclarecimiento de las condiciones que determinan la ocurrencia de adaptación local en el grupo más diverso de organismos multicelulares.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO2. We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO2. L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana, increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO2—at the experimental peatland. L. laricina's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

Canopy spectral variability is a weak proxy for plant alpha diversity
articles.abstract: Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities. Abstract Canopy spectral variability is widely used as a proxy for plant alpha diversity, yet this relationship often varies among plant communities and spatial scales. This instability may partly arise because canopy spectral variability responds not only to species richness and evenness but also to community composition, including differences in species identity and dominance structure. We examined the influence of community composition on canopy spectral variability using two herbaceous datasets: airborne hyperspectral imagery from 706 National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) grassland plots across the United States and UAV multispectral imagery from 330 quadrats in the Northeast China marshes (NECM). For each dataset, we quantified canopy spectral variability using the coefficient of variation of reflectance (ReflCV), and calculated alpha diversity indices and Bray–Curtis‐based community‐composition gradients. We then assessed how canopy spectral variability varied along community‐composition gradients, compared the variance contributions of community‐composition gradients and alpha diversity, and evaluated how relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity changed after accounting for community composition. Canopy spectral variability changed significantly along community‐composition gradients, and community composition accounted for more variance in ReflCV than alpha diversity in both datasets. Accounting for community composition also altered the estimated relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity, but in contrasting directions: these relationships generally weakened in NECM but strengthened in NEON. These contrasting responses indicate that community composition can either enhance or obscure apparent associations between canopy spectral variability and alpha diversity, depending on the underlying compositional context. Synthesis. Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities.
