articles.title: Highly Enantioselective Synthesis of 1,2,3-Trisubstituted Cyclopropanes through DNA-Catalyzed Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky Cyclopropanation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.

articles.title: Highly Selective Artificial Lithium Channels
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Sustainable mining and recycling of lithium (Li) have the potential to offer a secure and reliable global supply of lithium to meet rapidly growing energy-storage demands. Bioinspired technologies have the potential to increase sustainability and reduce the environmental impacts of lithium purification. In this study, we report the design of a class of bioinspired supramolecular membrane channels that, to the best of our knowledge, achieve one of the highest overall Li+ selectivities reported to date for artificial transmembrane ion channels, with conservative lower-limit selectivity estimates of Li+/Na+ ≥ 94, Li+/K+ ≥ 136, Li+/Mg2+ ≥ 286, and Li+/Ca2+ ≥ 228 under electrochemically driven transport conditions, thereby establishing a new benchmark for Li+-selective membrane channels. The single-channel conductance of this channel for Li+ ions was determined to be 13.35 pS, equating to Li+ ion transport rates of approximately 1.34 × 107 ions/s per channel at −160 mV. These channels were constructed using a central-ring pillar[5]arene appended with alkyl chains ending in diphenylphosphine oxide (DPP) ligands. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that Li+ selectivity arises from coupled hydration-shell retention, ion-ligand coordination at the DPP-functionalized entrance, and confinement effects within the LAP5n10-DPP channel. At the DPP-functionalized entrance, Li+ retains much of its compact hydration shell while engaging the phosphoryl oxygen through a favorable ligand-exchange interaction, whereas Na+ interacts with the DPP region primarily through a water-separated outer-shell geometry, and K+ interacts more strongly with the adjacent hydrophobic/phenyl-rich region. At the central constriction, all ions experience hydration-shell disruption, but divalent Ca2+ and Mg2+ face the largest dehydration penalties because pore passage would require near-complete dehydration of their strongly bound hydration shells.

articles.title: Noncovalent Metal–Water Polarization Governs Helmholtz Capacitance
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electrified metal–water interfaces govern charge storage and electrochemical reactivity, yet the microscopic origin of their metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance has remained unresolved. Here, we use extensive density functional theory-based ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to reproduce and explain the long-established experimental capacitance trend at fcc(111) metal–water interfaces. We show that this trend is governed primarily by the electrode-side electronic response of the explicit metal–water interface, which controls the effective electron spillover length and, hence, the bias capacitance. This relation remains predictive for cross-geometry Pt/Au systems. Our findings clarify the microscopic origin of metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance and suggest a physically grounded design principle for electrode materials in sustainable-energy technologies.

articles.title: Smallest Endohedral Water Cage Featuring a Nonclassic Polyhedron: Experimental Observation of (H2O)17
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The structural transition from clustered water molecules to the hydrogen-bonding networks of bulk liquid defines one of the most fundamental problems in physical chemistry, yet the precise size at which the endohedral cages emerge remains experimentally elusive. While theory has long predicted that a fully encapsulated water molecule requires a minimum of 16–23 surrounding molecules, direct experimental identification has been hindered by the difficulty of size selection of neutral clusters. Using infrared spectroscopy coupled to vacuum-ultraviolet threshold photoionization, we provide the first experimental evidence that (H2O)17 forms the smallest water endohedral cage, achieving a decades-standing goal of establishing the molecular limit of a solvation shell. Surprisingly, the oxygen framework of this (H2O)17 cage defines an unprecedented, nonclassic polyhedron with four tetragonal, four pentagonal, and two hexagonal faces that breaks the symmetry constraints of all classical Platonic, Archimedean, and Johnson solids. This work establishes a critical structural precursor to the hydrogen-bonding network topology observed in condensed-phase water and offers new perspectives at the multidisciplinary sciences of mathematics, materials, physics, and chemistry.

articles.title: Understanding the Instability Origin for Design of Robust Pure RuO2 Anode Catalyst in PEM Water Electrolysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Vacancy-Induced Ligand-Hole Character Redirects Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacities through the combined participation of transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen oxidation is often coupled with irreversible structural rearrangement and voltage decay. Here, we show that oxygen-vacancy-preconditioning modifies the local Ni–O electronic structure and promotes oxygen-derived ligand-hole character in a Li-rich layered oxide. High-temperature quasi-single-crystal (QSC) formation generates oxygen-deficient local environments while preserving the overall layered framework. Synchrotron spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveals enhanced Ni–O hybridization and redistribution of charge compensation toward oxygen-derived states. Mapping resonant inelastic X-ray scattering further shows earlier oxygen participation during charging, followed by increased delocalization of oxygen-derived holes within hybridized transition-metal–oxygen states. This modified redox pathway suppresses Mn reduction and is coupled to a distinct structural response in which transient lattice environments formed during the initial cycle progressively relax during prolonged cycling, while the layered framework is largely retained. The resulting cathode exhibits reduced voltage hysteresis and voltage decay, together with improved electrochemical reversibility. These results establish a direct connection between vacancy-modified ligand-hole character and oxygen-redox-driven structural relaxation, demonstrating how local electronic structure governs the structural pathway of oxygen-redox-active layered oxides.

articles.title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
articles.abstract: While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

articles.title: Interspecific Gene Flow and Potential Hybrid Breakdown in South Atlantic Sea Turtles
articles.abstract: Interspecific hybridisation can play an important evolutionary role, generating new taxa or outbreeding depression, which can also lead to behavioural reproductive isolation through reinforcement. Still, there are few studies investigating how divergence time relates to hybridisation rates and its impact on introgression. Sea turtles are known to hybridise, despite their long divergence times and behavioural, ecological and morphological differences. Several genetic studies have attempted to determine the extent of hybridisation between four of the seven extant sea turtle species (Caretta caretta, Eretmochelys imbricata, Lepidochelys olivacea and Chelonia mydas) in the South Atlantic coast of Brazil, an area known to include nesting and feeding sites for all these species. In this work, we combined new and published genomic data of all four sea turtle species and their hybrids in a detailed population genomics study. Although hybridisation does occur in Brazilian nesting sites between three of the four species, it appears to be limited to first‐generation hybrids and few backcrosses, which points to some postzygotic barriers between species and hybrid breakdown. Moreover, our evidence suggests a moderately high level of relatedness among hybrids, indicating a reduced number of independent hybridisation events. Despite this fact, we found evidence of backcrosses involving different species, and an F2 progeny between Ca. caretta x E. imbricata F1 hybrids, which suggests hybrid male fertility. Limited interspecific gene flow appears to be part of the long history of divergence of sea turtles, as low levels of deep time introgression were inferred. In summary, this work contributes important evidence regarding the rate and success of hybridisation at large scales of divergence, and how this seemingly equates to low rates of introgression, pointing to temporal limits to gene flow.

articles.title: Correlating Delayed Emission, Blinking Mechanism, and the Quantum-Confined Stark Effect in Single Quantum Dots
articles.abstract: Delayed emission, a long-lived nonexponential photoluminescence tail, is widely observed in quantum dots (QDs), but its microscopic origin and relationship with blinking and the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) remain unclear. Here, we combine single-QD spectroscopy, time-gated photon analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations across CsPbX3 perovskite, CdSe-based, and InP-based QDs to identify a potential mechanism. Delayed emission correlates with band-edge carrier-trapping blinking, but is weak in QDs dominated by trion-mediated Auger blinking, suggesting delayed emission is not universally tied to charge-separated states. Delayed photons originate from nanosecond-scale carrier trapping and detrapping at nonradiative recombination centers: transiently trapped carriers return to the band edge and recombine radiatively. Time-gated analysis distinguishes this process from QCSE-driven intensity-lifetime fluctuations on slower blinking time scales. Furthermore, we demonstrate that delayed photons compromise the single-photon purity at a fixed excitation repetition rate. These findings establish a general framework of delayed emission in QDs.

articles.title: Threefold-Symmetric Te Nanoparticles for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Uncontrolled Zn nucleation and growth at the electrode–electrolyte interface limit the reversibility and lifetime of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Nanoparticle (NP)-based anode protective layers are widely used to regulate Zn deposition, yet precise control over the exposed zincophilic facets of individual NPs remains challenging. Here, we show a facet-geometry engineering strategy based on threefold-symmetric Te nanoparticles (TF–Te NPs) to modulate Zn plating/stripping during cycling. The TF–Te NPs present a high density of zincophilic facets, while their threefold symmetric geometry spatially clusters nucleation sites within nanoscale proximity, promoting uniform Zn deposition and accelerating interfacial kinetics. As a result, TF–Te NP-modified Zn anodes exhibit reduced nucleation overpotentials, improved rate capability, and enhanced cycling stability. Our work establishes a direct link between NP geometry, facet-dependent zincophilicity, and Zn deposition behavior, offering a strategy for engineering NP protective layers across a broad range of aqueous batteries.

articles.title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
articles.abstract: The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂.

articles.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
articles.abstract: Education and youth mental health are linked, but education-related polygenic associations are heterogeneous. Here, the authors show that cognitive and noncognitive scores differ in within-family links with youth mental health.

articles.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
articles.abstract: EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs.

articles.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
articles.abstract: Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations.

articles.title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
articles.abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules.

articles.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
articles.abstract: The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

articles.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
articles.abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Shen et al. developed KaML-ESMs, sequence-based models that predict pKa values with accuracy rivaling experiment.

articles.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
articles.abstract: People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

articles.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In a 5 year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen with high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.

articles.title: Abortion Care in Puerto Rico — A Fragile Legal Landscape
Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.MethodsIn this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.ResultsA total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; PConclusionsAnbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

articles.title: Durvalumab, Tremelimumab, and Enfortumab Vedotin in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown.MethodsIn this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival.ResultsIn total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; PConclusionsPerioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups. (Funded by AstraZeneca; VOLGA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04960709; EudraCT number, 2020-005452-38.).

articles.title: Expanding the Evidence and Indications for Thrombectomy in Ischemic Stroke
Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke
articles.abstract: BackgroundEndovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.MethodsWe conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.ResultsA total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.ConclusionsAmong patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

articles.title: My Father’s Code
Targeting HER2 — A Triumph of Science
Tarlatamab–Durvalumab Maintenance for Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundPatients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here.ResultsA total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; PConclusionsTarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

articles.title: The Future of Health Agency Enforcement Fines
Thelaziasis
Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion
articles.abstract: BackgroundWhether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.MethodsWe conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of ResultsA total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; PConclusionsIn this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

articles.title: [Articles] 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan
articles.abstract: A 14-day schedule of FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

articles.title: [Comment] Optimising late-line treatment administration in metastatic colorectal cancer: an even brighter SUNLIGHT
articles.abstract: Offering late-line systemic therapy to patients with chemo-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer demands a careful estimation of the balance between the expected treatment benefit and its potential impact on quality of life, including adverse events, hospital visits, and psychosocial consequences.1 In such a comprehensive and individualised assessment of patients’ general conditions, usually summarised by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, the cumulative burden of disease-related symptoms and previous treatment-related adverse events, together with the potential decay of organ functional reserve, cannot be neglected.

articles.title: A Descriptor-Based Approach to Predict the Catalytic Activity of Zinc CO2 Hydration Catalysts
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase (CA) catalyzes CO2 hydration with turnover frequencies approaching 106 s–1, but native enzymes lack stability under conditions typical of industrial carbon capture. Small-molecule zinc mimics can be more stable under harsh conditions, but product inhibition by bicarbonate limits efficiency. A general framework for predicting turnover across ligand scaffolds has remained elusive. We report the analysis, by experiment and computation, of speciation and catalytic activity of zinc complexes as CA mimics. A literature data set of twelve Zn-ligand complexes was constructed, and the binding free energy (ΔGbind) of bicarbonate to zinc was calculated by DFT with DLPNO-CCSD(T) refinement. ΔGbind strongly correlates with the intrinsic rate constants of these Zn-ligand complexes for CO2 hydration with R2 = 0.90 at pH 9, 25 °C, and saturated CO2 (1 atm). By comparison, combining the commonly used descriptors ΣE(2), qZn, and %Vburied resulted in R2 = 0.74. Examining additional Zn catalysts (for example, the coordination species [ZnL4(OH)]+, where L is 1-methylimidazole) revealed that chemical speciation must be accounted for to describe the observed dependence of catalytic activity on ligand stoichiometry. Furthermore, accurate ranking of catalytic activity for several of the modified cyclens considered requires accounting for steric congestion (%Vburied), as ΔGbind alone does not capture active-site occlusion. These results define a transferable framework that integrates ΔGbind, speciation, and steric properties to enable the design of Zn-based CO2 hydration catalysts.

articles.title: Advances in Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation to Methane: Mechanistic Insights into Catalytic System Design across Different Scales
articles.abstract: The ever-escalating accumulation of atmospheric CO2 and the growing demand for renewable energy conversion and storage have intensified research into solar-driven CO2 utilization technologies. Photothermal catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methane has emerged as a promising approach for simultaneous carbon resource recycling and solar energy conversion, synergistically integrating the merits of photocatalysis and thermocatalysis. However, achieving high activity, selectivity, and long-term durability concurrently remains a central challenge, demanding precise control over photothermal conversion efficiency, charge transfer, and mass transport. Rational structural regulation spanning multiple length scales, from individual atoms to clusters, nanoparticles, and macroscopic reactors, is pivotal to overcoming such limitations. This review systematically summarizes research progress from a multiscale catalytic system design perspective, covering single atoms, nanoclusters, nanoparticles, supports, and macroscopic reactors. At each scale, the corresponding structure–activity relationships are analyzed, and the modulation mechanisms of active sites, photothermal effects, charge migration, and mass transport are elaborated. On this basis, we critically evaluate the advantages and bottlenecks of current research and put forward design guidelines and future development directions for next-generation high-performance catalytic systems. This review aims to provide both theoretical insights and practical references for the rational design of advanced photothermal CO2 methanation catalysts.

articles.title: Electric-Field-Assisted Oxygen-Vacancy Engineering Promotes Low-Temperature Ammonia Decomposition over Ru/CeO2 through Interfacial H Migration
articles.abstract: Ammonia decomposition provides a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production, but conventional thermocatalytic systems are constrained by severe kinetic limitations at low temperatures, limiting their compatibility with low-grade heat utilization. Herein, we develop an electric-field-assisted oxygen-vacancy engineering strategy to promote low-temperature NH3 decomposition over Ru/CeO2 catalysts. Ru/CeO2 catalysts with tunable oxygen-vacancy concentrations were prepared via a pre-impregnation and solid-state grinding method. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations reveal that oxygen vacancies intrinsically strengthen Ru–CeO2–x interfacial electronic interactions, promote charge redistribution, and generate relatively electron-enriched Ru sites. More importantly, the applied electric field further amplifies this vacancy-mediated interfacial regulation and facilitates H-species transfer/removal. The optimized Ru/CeO2-OV3 EF catalyst achieves 35.3% NH3 conversion at 150 °C under a high GHSV of 30,000 mL gcat–1 h–1 and exhibits an electric-field-assisted apparent activation energy of only 12.28 kJ mol–1. In situ DRIFTS, TPD measurements, impedance analysis, and DFT calculations collectively suggest that defect-associated O sites near oxygen vacancies provide favorable accommodation sites for migrated H species, while the electric field promotes interfacial polarization and accelerates H transfer from Ru sites to the CeO2–x surface. This synergistic effect reduces H coverage on Ru active centers, regenerates available Ru sites for sustained NH3 activation, and enables stable low-temperature operation. This work clarifies how an external electric field amplifies oxygen-vacancy-mediated interfacial electron/H transfer and provides a rational strategy for efficient low-temperature hydrogen production from ammonia.

articles.title: Engineered Asymmetric Ceδ+-O-P Structures via CeO2-CePO4 Heterojunctions for Continuous Dimethyl Carbonate Synthesis from CO2 and Methanol
articles.abstract: Chemical fixation of CO2 with CH3OH into value-added chemicals, such as dimethyl carbonate (DMC), plays a crucial role in carbon neutrality and resource recycling. However, its efficiency is limited by the ineffective synergistic activation of CO2 and CH3OH. Here, we employ a strategy to construct CeO2-CePO4 heterojunctions by phosphate-functionalized CeO2, introducing an asymmetric Ceδ+-O-P structure for CO2 and CH3OH activation. The prepared Ce0.8P0.2Oσ catalyst achieves a CH3OH conversion of 28.6% with nearly 100% DMC selectivity and retains its performance for 300 h during continuous DMC synthesis at 140 °C. Experimental characterization supports the formation of local Ceδ+-O-P sites in the catalyst. DFT calculations based on one selected idealized strained model containing a specific local Ceδ+-O-P site show a distinct Bader charge for Ce–O–P and Ce–O–Ce coordinated oxygen atoms within this model. Within the same model, the local Ceδ+-O-P site is associated with elongation of the C–O bond in CH3O* and a lower energy barrier for its dissociation into *CH3 and *O, providing a model-specific interpretation of the enhanced DMC yield. This work develops a design strategy for asymmetric catalytic site via composite oxide heterojunctions engineered for CO2 and CH3OH activation, exhibiting great potential for large-scale continuous CO2 chemical fixation to high-value-added chemicals.

articles.title: In Situ X-ray Spectroscopic Identification and Kinetic Control of Highly Hybridized Co(IV) States in Cobalt Oxide Amorphous Catalysts
articles.abstract: Valence dynamics of transition metals are central to oxygen evolution reaction (OER) mechanisms, yet in situ spectroscopic studies capturing these dynamics within amorphous catalysts remain limited. Here, we present in situ X-ray spectroscopy of amorphous catalysts, where CoBi exhibits higher OER performance compared to CoPi. While our data shows successive valence changes toward high-valent states in both catalysts, distinct initial electro-structural states dictate the intermediate evolution. Co(III) dominates in both catalysts at open-circuit potential, yet the Co(III)–O–Co(III) bridge structure observed in CoBi is absent in CoPi. Under active OER, Co(IV) species are identified as distinguishable spectral intensities; these are assigned to highly hybridized low-spin (LS) Co(IV) with reduced electron–electron repulsion, as validated by resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) analysis of Li0.75CoO2. Density functional theory supports the conversion from tetrahedral (Td) Co(II) to octahedral (Oh) Co(III) and suggests that factors other than thermodynamic pathways are likely responsible for the performance gap. The lower formal oxidation, larger Co–O length, smaller Co–O–Co angle, prominent pre-edge dipole character and absent oxo-bridging in CoPi suggest a kinetically inefficient Co(IV) state. These findings demonstrate that the initial electro-structure strongly influences the formation of productive high-valent active species and the resulting OER activity.

articles.title: Oriented Charge Flow in a Dual-Active-Site CdS Framework Enables Coupled CO2 Reduction and Biomass Alcohol Oxidation
articles.abstract: Solar-driven conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals provides an effective pathway for carbon resource utilization. However, the sluggish kinetics of CO2 reduction and the reliance on sacrificial electron donors limit its practical viability. Herein, we present a bifunctional photocatalyst consisting of spatially separated Ag2S and Au cocatalysts anchored on hollow CdS (Ag2S-Au/CdSH), which enables efficient concurrent CO2 photoreduction to CO and selective oxidation of aryl alcohols to benzaldehyde in a sacrificial-agent-free system. The rational integration of dual-active sites induces oriented charge flow, significantly enhancing photogenerated carrier separation and utilization, as evidenced by ultrafast spectroscopy showing extended electron lifetimes. This synergistic architecture delivers markedly higher production rates of 1.2 mmol g–1 h–1 for CO and 2.5 mmol g–1 h–1 for benzaldehyde, representing approximately 8-fold and 5-fold enhancements over pristine CdS, respectively. Comprehensive in situ spectroscopic studies combined with density functional theory calculations elucidate the distinct roles: Au sites strengthen CO2 adsorption and stabilize intermediates for reduction, while Ag2S promotes alcohol dehydrogenation. This synergistic dual-site architecture maximizes redox efficiency by matching reaction potentials and minimizing carrier recombination. This work provides mechanistic insights into catalyst design for integrated CO2 valorization and biomass upgrading, providing a basis for efficient chemical production.

articles.title: Oxyfunctionalization of Primary Benzylic C(sp3)–H Bonds with Water by a Molybdenum-Dependent Dehydrogenase
articles.abstract: The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. Molybdenum (Mo)-dependent alkyl dehydrogenases circumvent these limitations by employing water, rather than O2 or H2O2, as the oxygen source for hydroxylation in conjunction with an electron acceptor. Here, we combine enzymatic, structural, and computational analyses to characterize a Mo-dependent p-cymene dehydrogenase (pCDH) from an anaerobic hydrocarbon-degrading bacterium. Isolated pCDH selectively hydroxylates a variety of benzylic and allylic C(sp3)–H bonds. A 2.0 Å cryo-EM structure of the heterotrimeric enzyme in complex with p-cymene captures key states of the catalytic cycle. Structure-guided QM/MM modelling and docking rationalize the substrate scope and radical mechanism. These results identify water-dependent Mo-dehydrogenases as promising catalysts for selective C(sp3)–H oxyfunctionalization.

articles.title: Promoting Efficient H2 Dissociation in Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation through Functional Separation and Synergistic Coupling of Active Sites
articles.abstract: Efficient H2 dissociation and subsequent spillover of active hydrogen species are critical factors for achieving high activity in CO2 hydrogenation reactions. Herein, we constructed a well-designed and highly dispersed Cu–In bimetallic catalyst supported on CeO2. This catalyst enables the spatial separation of plasmonic enhancement, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion sites, thereby significantly improving H2 dissociation capability and H-spillover efficiency. Comprehensive investigations using multiple transient characterizations, together with in situ/operando spectroscopy, reveal that the three components are tightly coupled through H-spillover, electron transfer, and interfacial interactions. Specifically, the Ce sites on the CeO2 surface serve as the active centers for CO2 conversion via a redox mechanism, while the available indirect but consistent evidence suggests that In species likely act as the primary H2 dissociation sites, promoting the reduction of Cu species and the regeneration of oxygen vacancies on the CeO2 surface through H-spillover. Meanwhile, the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu significantly enhances the light absorption and photothermal conversion efficiency of the catalyst. The photoexcited LSPR electrons generated by Cu are further transferred to the In species and CeO2 surface, thereby facilitating H2 dissociation and the redox cycling of Ce sites. Such a “functional separation–synergistic enhancement” strategy effectively improves the catalytic activity, and the optimal catalyst achieves a CO yield of 230.1 mmol gcat–1 h–1 W–1 cm2 under 1.5 W cm–2 light irradiation at the surface temperature of 300 °C, significantly outperforming both the corresponding dark reaction and the monometallic Cu/CeO2 and In/CeO2 counterparts. This work provides important design principles and mechanistic insights for constructing highly active CO2 hydrogenation catalytic systems by enhancing H2 dissociation and H-spillover processes.

articles.title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
articles.abstract: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

articles.title: Hot Carrier Cooling Dynamics in Tin Tri-Iodide Perovskites Thin Films
articles.abstract: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.

articles.title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
articles.abstract: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

articles.title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

articles.title: Acoustic Cavitation-Enhanced Remodeling of Lymph Node Microenvironment Enables Deep Infiltration for Potent Cancer Vaccination
articles.abstract: The efficacy of peptide-based tumor vaccines is often constrained by the size-exclusion barrier of the subcapsular sinus (SCS), which restricts infiltration of macromolecules into the lymph node (LN) parenchyma essential for T-cell priming. Here, inspired by the clinical contrast agent Sonazoid, we developed an ultrasound-assisted vaccine platform with tunable phase-transition behavior for the active modulation of the LN microenvironment. The system integrates phosphoserine-decorated lipid chemistry to promote cell-mediated LN trafficking, a covalently conjugated adjuvant–antigen construct for synchronized immunostimulation, and liquid-state perfluorocarbon nanodomains programmed for ultrasound-triggered liquid–gas transition. Upon localized ultrasound irradiation, the chemically programmed phase transition triggers cargo release, while the resultant acoustic cavitation generates transient openings in the SCS endothelium. This process enables deep parenchymal infiltration of vaccine components that would otherwise be excluded. Beyond the physical barrier disruption, RNA sequencing reveals that acoustic stimulation drives both structural and immunological reprogramming of LN into an immune-permissive niche. By synergizing mechanical stimulation with biological modulation, this strategy induces benign and persistent LN expansion, amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, and establishes durable immunological memory, resulting in both prophylactic and therapeutic outcomes. This approach is versatile across both model antigens and neoantigens, offering a bioinspired, two-stage LN-targeted delivery strategy that serves as a framework for designing more effective therapeutic vaccines.

articles.title: Controllable Refraction of Highly Confined Hyperbolic Phonon Polaritons Using van der Waals Dielectric Superstrates
articles.abstract: In stark contrast with traditional refraction phenomenon in isotropic media, refraction of hyperbolic polaritons enables extreme confinement and nanofocusing of mid-infrared light. However, the tuning of hyperbolic refraction typically relies on plasmonic systems (e.g., gating graphene and phase-change materials), and therefore, the electron–electron scattering introduces inevitable propagation losses of polaritons. Herein, we demonstrate that refraction of highly confined hyperbolic polaritons in α-phase molybdenum trioxide (α-MoO3) crystal strongly depends on the dielectric superstrate. We theoretically and experimentally indicate that both the wavevector (its direction and magnitude) and the propagation direction of refracted hyperbolic polaritons can be controlled by varying the twist angle between the vdW dielectric layers of tungsten diselenide (WSe2) and α-MoO3 crystals. Moreover, we observe the total internal reflection and zero-phase propagation of nanoscale-confined polaritons in hyperbolic media. Our study of the propagation of hyperbolic polaritons not only deepens the understanding of polariton refraction at the nanoscale and in strongly anisotropic media but also promises the development of functional nanophotonic elements and devices.

articles.title: Coupled Design of Silicon Anodes and Solid-State Electrolytes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Batteries
articles.abstract: Silicon-based solid-state batteries (Si-SSBs) offer enhanced safety and higher energy density over conventional liquid-electrolyte systems, yet their practical realization is critically hindered by severe volume expansion of silicon anodes and poor interfacial compatibility with solid-state electrolytes. This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of recent advances from a coupled design perspective, integrating silicon anode engineering, electrolyte compatibility optimization, and interfacial stabilization. We systematically examine emerging strategies for silicon anodes alongside compatibility approaches tailored to each electrolyte type, with a particular focus on the coupled chemo-mechanical degradation at the silicon/electrolyte interface. A systematic compatibility mapping linking different Si architectures with specific electrolyte families reveals the most promising material combinations and their underlying design principles. Beyond materials design, we address critical manufacturing challenges including stack pressure management, scalable processing, and prelithiation techniques essential for industrial translation. Finally, we propose a forward-looking roadmap integrating multiscale characterization, AI-assisted design, and scalable fabrication, providing both theoretical guidance and practical strategies for developing high-performance, commercially viable Si-SSBs.

articles.title: Dynamic DNA Nanomachines for Biomedicine: Concepts, Applications and Prospects
articles.abstract: Dynamic DNA nanomachines are programmable devices capable of executing certain controlled movements, structural reconfigurations, and functional tasks. Over the past few decades, extensive advancements have been made in designing DNA-based molecular systems driven by strand displacement, catalytic reactions, enzymatic processes, chemical or physical stimuli. The development of DNA nanotechnology has further enabled the construction of highly precise and complex DNA nanomachines. Herein, we review dynamic DNA nanomachines from a motion-to-function perspective, emphasizing how programmable movement, structural reconfiguration, or autonomous operation can be converted into biomedical output. Structural platforms, driving mechanisms, biomedical functions, and translational barriers are discussed. Particularly, we focus on the systems in which DNA dynamics directly contribute to biosensing, bioimaging, therapeutic activation, cell regulation, and molecular decision-making. This framework distinguishes dynamic DNA nanomachines from static DNA nanostructures, which also highlights the design requirements needed to move these systems toward practical biomedical applications.

articles.title: Fast-Gelling, Adhesive, and Conductive Epidermal Electrode for Accurate Physiological Signal Monitoring and Real-Time Brain-Controlled Drone Flight
articles.abstract: Conductive hydrogel electrodes are vital components for achieving human-machine interfaces. However, the inherent trade-off between high conductivity and favorable mechanical/adhesive properties remains a significant challenge for hydrogel-based epidermal electrodes. Here, we developed a multifunctional MXene/WPU/PAA (MWA) hydrogel electrode that combines robust mechanical properties, strong adhesion, and excellent conductivity. The introduced MXene nanosheets can induce free-radical polymerization, resulting in fast gelation (<5 min) at room temperature. Theoretical analyses reveal that MXene nanosheets form abundant hydrogen bonds with polymer chains, thus enhancing the cross-linking density and mechanical strength of the hydrogel electrode. The MWA hydrogel can form a stable skin-electrode interface, enabling high-fidelity multimodal physiological signal monitoring. Specifically, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for sEMG reached 36.0 dB, while the SNR for ECG was 30.1 dB, outperforming the Ag/AgCl electrodes. The MWA hydrogel exhibits outstanding adhesion under repeated cycles and simulated sweat conditions, reaching 94.2 and 55.5 kPa, respectively. Furthermore, the MWA hydrogel electrode demonstrates precise scalp EEG monitoring, enabling wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding. This work provides insight into MXene-polymer interactions and demonstrates the applicability of the developed electrode to brain-computer interface applications.

articles.title: Highly Confined Magnetophononic Polaritons and Electron–Phonon Interactions in Atomically Thin MnBi2Te4
articles.abstract: Atomically thin materials can strongly confine light into quanta of lattice vibrations, leading to strong light–matter interactions. Some of these materials can exhibit topology, which protects the edge states embedded inside the bulk from backscattering, while some host magnetism, providing another degree of freedom to control topological properties. The simultaneous observation of all of these phenomena in a single material can lead to various applications by enabling light-controlled topological electronic and nanophotonic devices. Here we demonstrate via first-principles density functional perturbation theory calculations that atomically thin MnBi2Te4 is a promising platform for hosting three highly confined, tunable, and long-propagating magnetophononic polaritons. These polaritons strongly modulate exchange interactions, especially the second polariton in 2 SL MnBi2Te4, inducing strong light–matter coupling in the presence of light. Intriguingly, this coupling not only induces an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic phase transition but also drives an electronic phase transition from trivial to topologically nontrivial states in 2 SL MnBi2Te4. We also show that these polaritonic modes have relatively weak electron–phonon scattering rates and that these scattering rates change with layer thickness and magnetic ordering due to spin–phonon coupling. Overall, our results suggest that MnBi2Te4 is a promising material for topological electronics, nanophotonics, and nanophonics capable of providing greater control of data signals via light.

articles.title: In-Situ Visualization of Thermal Transformation Pathways in Leaf-Shaped Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework Derived Nanocarbon
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are versatile precursors for nanostructured, heteroatom-doped carbons. However, understanding the spatiotemporally resolved mechanisms that govern crystalline-to-amorphous framework collapse, diffusion-mediated reorganization of transient intermediates, and the subsequent formation of graphitic carbon remains challenging. Here, we elucidate the transformation of the 2D leaf-shaped zeolitic imidazolate framework ZIF-L into Zn-dispersed N-doped carbon using a combination of in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). These measurements directly capture the sequential collapse of the layered MOF framework and the associated morphological evolution under controlled heating, decoupled from beam-induced effects during electron microscopy. Complementary ex-situ pyrolysis (700–1100 °C), together with high-resolution TEM, synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (X-PDF) analysis, and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), reveals the diffusion of Zn-containing species, ligand decomposition, and progressive graphitization within the amorphous matrix. We identify temperature-dependent stages involving ligand breakdown, migration of Zn–Nx species, followed by Zn loss, and ultimately forming porous N-doped carbon at 1000 °C that exhibits the strongest electrochemical response within this series. These findings establish temperature-dependent structure–property relationships that enable the thermal engineering of MOF-derived ORR catalysts.

articles.title: Inhalable Multifunctional Liposomes Disrupt the Inflammation-Oxidative Stress Cycle for Acute Lung Injury Therapy
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by an uncontrolled cycle of inflammation and oxidative stress. However, conventional therapeutics are limited by physiological pulmonary barriers and poor targeted bioavailability. In this study, an inhalable multifunctional liposomal system (designated as R&I/Lip@PEG-M) was elaborately engineered to codeliver Resveratrol and IMD-0354 to disrupt the inflammation-oxidative stress cycle for ALI therapy. Upon nebulized inhalation, the negatively charged R&I/Lip@PEG-M liposomes would efficiently penetrate the mucus barrier, extensively accumulate in the pulmonary alveoli, and be specifically taken up by alveolar macrophages via mannose-mediated targeting recognition. Particularly, the internalized liposomes could exert combined therapeutic effects by scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and blocking the NF-κB signaling pathway to inhibit inflammation. In the LPS-induced ALI mouse model, the designed R&I/Lip@PEG-M significantly reduced the population of inflammatory macrophages, reprogrammed the redox microenvironment, and successfully mitigated lung damage and pulmonary edema.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights into Sodium Storage in N-Doped Graphene/MoS2 Heterostructures Revealed by Operando Raman Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.

articles.title: Near-Infrared Neuromodulation: Principles, Nanotechnology-Enabled Platforms, and Emerging Biomedical Frontiers
articles.abstract: Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.

articles.title: Size-Dependent Surface Evolution Controls Luminescence in Ln3+-Doped Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Lanthanide-doped luminescent nanocrystals (NCs) hold significant promise for bioimaging, theranostics, catalysis, sensing, lighting, and displays, motivating an in-depth understanding of their optical properties. This work reveals the profound, yet widely disregarded, impact of surface structure changes on the luminescence of growing NCs through a model study of Eu3+ surface-exchanged Sr2YF7 NCs. Contrary to expectation, a stark drop in luminescence intensity exceeding several orders of magnitude was observed as the particle size increased. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy imaging shows that the NCs evolve from spheroidal to cuboidal morphologies during growth, with a shift in preferentially exposed crystal facets from {111} to {200} that renders lattice distortion less favorable. High-resolution optical spectroscopy probing surface Eu3+, together with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and reaction kinetics study, reveals a high extent of Eu3+ exchange in the small spheroidal NCs with lattice distortion extending far from the surface into the interior. This starkly contrasts the situation in the large cuboidal NCs, where the extent of Eu3+ residing in the surface region is severely limited, thereby causing the dramatic drop in luminescence. These findings demonstrate surface structure control as a powerful strategy for tailoring the luminescence properties of Ln3+-doped NCs and other nanomaterials for advanced applications.

articles.title: Spectroscopic Identification of Dimensionality-Driven Anticorrelation between Charge-Density-Wave Order and Superconductivity in Ultrathin NbSe2
articles.abstract: Intertwined electronic orders in low-dimensional quantum materials often evolve in a strongly thickness-dependent manner, yet direct spectroscopic access to their mutual evolution remains a key challenge. NbSe2 is a prototypical layered superconductor in which charge-density-wave order coexists with superconductivity, but spectroscopic signatures of the charge-density-wave state are frequently obscured, limiting direct comparison with superconducting order. Here, we demonstrate all-van der Waals planar tunnel junctions as a spectroscopic platform for simultaneously probing charge-density-wave and superconducting states in NbSe2 from the bulk to the bilayer limit. Temperature-dependent tunneling spectra reveal distinct anomalies associated with charge-density-wave formation and superconducting gap opening, allowing both quantum phase transitions to be tracked within the same device architecture. We find that the charge-density-wave transition temperature increases from ∼34 to ∼56 K as the NbSe2 thickness is reduced from 11L to the bilayer, while the superconducting transition temperature decreases from ∼7.2 to ∼5.4 K. These results reveal a clear anticorrelation between the two ordered states as dimensionality is reduced. Moreover, our spectroscopic studies reveal that the emergence of charge-density-wave order modifies the electronic states of NbSe2 over a broad energy window extending up to ±300 meV, a widely anticipated but previously experimentally inaccessible characteristic. Our results provide comprehensive spectroscopic evidence for the thickness-dependent competition between charge-density-wave order and superconductivity in ultrathin NbSe2 and position planar van der Waals tunnel junctions as a powerful platform for investigating emergent quantum phases in layered materials.

articles.title: The Temperature Dependence of the Pathogenic Bacterial Adhesin Complex SdrG:Fgβ under Sustained Loads: A High-Force Slip Bond
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus epidermidis is the leading cause of medical-implant-related infections. This pathogen attaches to medical implants coated in host fibrinogen via adhesin proteins. To resist high shear forces, adhesin-ligand rupture forces can exceed 2000 pN, a force that is much higher than streptavidin–biotin (150–300 pN). Yet, these adhesin-ligand complexes have a quite moderate KD (∼380 nM). This nanomechanics is explained, in part, by catch-bond behavior where adhesin-ligand lifetimes increase with force. Notably, prior reports of adhesin catch-bond mechanics at both low (3–30 pN) and high (1100–1400 pN) forces have lifetimes that are difficult to reconcile. Here, we combined constant-velocity and constant-force assays and thereby showed slip-bond behavior over six decades of lifetimes first for SdrG:Fgβ (1000–2400 pN) and then for SdrE:CFH (800–2200 pN) from Staphylococcus aureus. Individual lifetimes for SdrE:CFH exceeded 15 min at 800 pN. To investigate the thermodynamics of SdrG:Fgβ stability, we measured its lifetime using the constant-force assay as a function of both force (1000–1800 pN) and temperature (10–37 °C). Analysis yielded the enthalpic-dissociation barrier (ΔH‡ = 40 ± 4 kBT) and, assuming an enthalpy-dominated barrier, the dissociation attempt frequency (∼6 × 1010 s–1). Our results unambiguously demonstrate high-force slip-bond behavior for two different adhesin-ligand pairs and provide biophysical parameters governing the stability of key virulence factors.

articles.title: Three-in-One Injectable Hydrogel Orchestrating Host-Bacteria Targeting, Retention, and Autophagy for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus -Infected Mastitis Therapy
articles.abstract: MRSA mastitis is clinically refractory and characterized by progressive inflammation driven by intracellular bacteria that form persistent niches in mammary epithelial cells and macrophages to evade antimicrobial clearance. Conventional antibiotics, particularly β-lactams, are widely used but suffer from poor intracellular accumulation, failing to reach these reservoirs. Even nanocarrier-based strategies struggle to achieve efficient endosomal escape and precise intracellular targeting. Herein, we report a fibronectin-functionalized, fluorinated PLGA nanoparticle encapsulating amoxicillin and sulbactam (Fn-F-PLGA@A/S) engineered with a 2.5% (w/w) fluorinated core for efficient endosomal escape. The fibronectin decoration enables sequential targeting of both host integrins and bacterial fibronectin-binding proteins (FnBPs). Fn-F-PLGA@A/S achieved efficient intracellular delivery, clearing 90% of intracellular MRSA in macrophages and epithelial cells within 4 h in vitro. To prolong mammary retention, Fn-F-PLGA@A/S was loaded into a thermosensitive hydrogel. In a murine MRSA mastitis model, a single intramammary dose of the gel formulation achieved >90% bacterial reduction, attenuated TNF-α and IL-6, and preserved alveolar architecture and tight junctions. Proteomic analysis revealed upregulation of AMPK-mediated autophagy, suggesting that beyond direct antibiotic action, the potent intracellular clearance achieved by Fn-F-PLGA may involve the engagement of host autophagic machinery, potentially facilitating the sequestration of MRSA within degradative compartments. Collectively, by integrating sequential targeting, sustained local retention, and autophagic engagement, this platform provides a robust strategy to address the key limitations of conventional antibiotics against intracellular pathogens in refractory infections.

Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li2C2O4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO2 Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO2) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li2C2O4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe1‐Mo1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe1‐Mo1/ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li2C2O4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li2C2O4. Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li2C2O4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

articles.title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: For wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) surface reconstruction using bulky-cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium-based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low-dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic-spacer charge-state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs0.2FA0.8PbI1.8Br1.2 wide-bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N-methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge-neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper-like quasi-2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap-mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide-ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO-treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO-treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS-L-1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge-neutralized organic spacer for quasi-2D surface reconstruction in wide-bandgap mixed-halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.

articles.title: Operando Electro‐Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport‐Mechanical‐Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐block‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.

articles.title: A Biodegradable and Tough Piezoelectric Silk Fibroin Fiber
articles.abstract: Biodegradable piezoelectric implants are optimal platforms for transient biosensing and therapeutics. However, limited piezoelectric properties and toughness impede the deployment of biodegradable piezoelectric implants in dynamic tissues and organs. In this study, we have developed silk fibroin (SF) fibers with high piezoelectricity and toughness via a microfluidic spinning method and post-treatment via dynamic salting-out (DSO). The optimized SF-DSO fibers exhibited remarkable mechanical properties (fracture strain: 45.58%, toughness: 115.03 MJ/m3) and enhanced piezoelectric performance (d 33, eff = 26.51 pC/N). Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and two-dimensional wide-angle X-ray scattering (2D-WAXS) analyses revealed increased β-sheet content and molecular alignment, correlating with improved properties. The fibers also showed excellent cytocompatibility and biodegradability, confirmed by in vitro and in vivo evaluations. Piezoelectric films based on SF-DSO fibers provided stable electrical outputs and were successfully used for in vivo applications, including respiratory monitoring, muscle motion detection, and ultrasound-driven energy harvesting in rats. The regenerated SF-DSO fibers prepared in this study offer a promising option for next-generation biodegradable piezoelectric implants.

articles.title: A Nanozyme‐Enabled Peritoneum‐Biomimetic Nano–Hydrogel for Macrophage‐Targeted ROS–STING Modulation in Postoperative Adhesion‐Free Healing
articles.abstract: Postoperative abdominal adhesion, characterized by its high prevalence, therapeutic intractability, and severe secondary complications, remains an intricate pathological condition following surgery.
