Here, using a peritoneal adhesion model integrated with multi‐omics analyses, we identify ROS‐driven activation of the cGAS–STING pathway as a central mechanism underlying macrophage activation and adhesion formation. To address this, black phosphorus nanosheets functionalized with Cu2+ and NH2–PEG–polyinosinic acid (BPNS@Cu@PI) are engineered as a peritoneal macrophage‐specific nanozyme to scavenge ROS. Furthermore, a silk fibroin‐based Janus hydrogel with an MMP‐responsive porous layer and a dense barrier layer (MMP‐JSF) is constructed to mitigate copper‐associated impairment of tissue repair. In vitro, this nano‐hydrogel system enables targeted delivery, redox regulation, mitochondrial homeostasis restoration, cGAS‐STING pathway inhibition, inflammation suppression, and wound healing promotion. In a 7‐day rat model, the BPNS@Cu@PI demonstrated significant efficacy in inhibiting adhesions, with the accompanying MMP‐JSF further enhancing therapeutic outcomes for tissue healing. Mechanistically, in a 3‐day model, the platform not only inhibited adhesions but also exhibited robust therapeutic effects in suppressing the ROS‐STING pathway and restoring mitochondrial function, as evidenced by both pathological and transcriptome analysis. Collectively, this work establishes a pathway‐specific nano–hydrogel strategy for adhesion‐free healing with translational potential.

articles.title: A Polyoxoniobate‐Based Molecular Heterojunction Orchestrates Heat and Vapor Transport for Efficient Solar Evaporation
articles.abstract: Efficient solar‐driven interfacial evaporation requires precise coordination of heat and mass transport, yet achieving such synergy within conventional molecular systems remains challenging. Here, we address this limitation using an atomically precise polyoxoniobate (PONb)‐based molecular heterojunction, [Te5Cu0.2Nb15O57H5.6][(CuL)7(OH)]·21H2O (PONb‐CuL, L = 2,2′‐bipyridine), in which hydrophilic PONb clusters are covalently integrated with photothermal organocopper CuL units. This Janus molecular architecture couples broadband solar absorption with interfacial water‐cluster regulation within a single framework. Under one‐sun irradiation, a two‐dimensional PONb‐CuL evaporator delivers an evaporation rate of 2.87 kg m−2 h−1. Incorporation into a three‐dimensional aerogel architecture further boosts the evaporation rate to 5.34 kg m−2 h−1, affording a freshwater yield of 29.25 L m−2 under outdoor operation. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the PONb domain promotes hydrogen‐bonded water‐cluster formation, whereas the organocopper domain reduces the energy barrier for interfacial water transport and vapor escape. This work introduces polyoxometalate‐based molecular heterojunction engineering as a strategy for orchestrating coupled heat and mass transport, offering critical insights into the rational design of efficient solar‐to‐vapor conversion systems.

articles.title: A Redox‐Responsive Nano‐Immune Coupling Strategy Enables Synergistic Pathogen Eradication and Host Resistance Activation Against Bacterial Wilt
articles.abstract: Here, we develop a redox‐responsive nano‐immune coupling strategy for synergistic control of tomato bacterial wilt. The CuO@MON nanocomposite consists of copper oxide nanoparticles embedded within glutathione‐responsive mesoporous organosilica (MON), enabling selective disassembly in the thiol‐rich bacterial microenvironment. Under in vitro conditions, Ralstonia solanacearum was treated with CuO@MON at concentrations ranging from 0 to 500 mg/L for 24 h, with CuO, MON, and zhongshengmycin as controls. CuO@MON exhibited concentration‐dependent antibacterial activity and higher efficacy than CuO alone, with an EC50 value of 96.96 mg/L. Mechanistic analyses showed that CuO@MON enhanced intracellular ROS generation (2.054 ± 0.098‐fold increase), promoted glutathione depletion, and induced membrane damage and genomic DNA degradation in R. solanacearum. In tomato plants, CuO@MON treatment (250 mg/L) reduced stem colonization by R. solanacearum by 84.0% after 4 days of inoculation compared with infected controls, while zhongshengmycin achieved a 94.9% reduction as a conventional positive control. Moreover, CuO@MON enhanced defense‐related responses, increasing PR‐1 expression from 400 ± 96‐fold to 533 ± 140‐fold and PR‐5 expression from 340 ± 50‐fold to 807 ± 121‐fold relative to healthy controls. Collectively, CuO@MON integrates pathogen suppression with host defense activation, providing a nano‐immune coupling strategy for sustainable bacterial disease management.

articles.title: A Self‐Assembled Zincophobic/Zincophilic Bilayer Interphase from a Hydrated Eutectic Electrolyte for Dendrite‐Free Zn Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous Zn batteries are promising for safe and low‐cost large‐scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by severe Zn anode instability arising from coupled hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and dendritic electrodeposition, particularly under temperature extremes. Here we report a solvation–interphase coupled strategy enabled by a hydrated eutectic electrolyte formulated from zinc trifluoromethanesulfonate (Zn(OTf)2), ethylene glycol (EG), and an SnF2 additive (optimized as ZOTF‐16/SF30), which delivers stable Zn electrochemistry over an exceptionally wide temperature window from −40°C to 60°C. Spectroscopic and physicochemical analyses reveal that EG confines H2O within a reinforced hydrogen‐bond network and reconstructs the Zn2+ coordination environment, thereby suppressing active‐water reactivity and mitigating hydrogen evolution and corrosion. Concurrently, SnF2 programs interfacial chemistry to generate an in situ zincophobic/zincophilic bilayer interphase, wherein the zincophobic component blocks water penetration and parasitic reactions while the zincophilic component homogenizes Zn2+ flux and nucleation, enforcing uniform Zn deposition and dendrite‐free growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit ultrastable cycling for over 2400 h at 1 mA cm−2. Moreover, Zn||I2 full cells deliver remarkable long‐term durability over 120 000 cycles, sustaining extended lifetimes at 60°C and −40°C. This work establishes a practical electrolyte‐interphase co‐design blueprint for climate‐resilient aqueous Zn batteries, highlighting hydrated eutectic chemistry as a versatile platform for stabilizing reactive metal anodes.

articles.title: AI‐Enabled Organoid Chips for Modeling and Decoding Nerve‐Tumor Interactions
articles.abstract: The nervous system is emerging as a central regulator of tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. However, the dynamic mechanisms linking neural activity to malignant, immune, and barrier states remain difficult to dissect in vivo. Animal models capture key aspects of cancer neuroscience, but poorly control human‐specific multicellular interfaces, neural activity, secreted signals, and real‐time readouts. AI‐enabled organoid chip platforms offer a complementary route to reconstruct and interrogate the nerve‐tumor interface by integrating human‐derived organoids, microfluidic control, sensing, and computational modeling. Here we review advances in nerve‐tumor organoids and integrate relevant progress in microfluidics, in situ functional sensing, and AI‐driven modeling. These systems can enable controlled studies of perineural invasion, nerve‐mediated immune regulation, trans‐barrier drug responses, and longitudinal functional states. Key challenges include model standardization, long‐term stability, multimodal data interpretation, and clinical translation. AI‐enabled organoid chip platforms could help shift cancer neuroscience from descriptive observation towards perturbable, human‐relevant and data‐rich systems for mechanism discovery and precision therapy assessment.

articles.title: Accelerating Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution via Interface‐To‐Surface Proton Transfer Relays on Ru‐RuO2−δ Heterostructure
articles.abstract: Ru has been investigated as a promissing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalyst in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, its excessive oxophilicity blocks active sites and over-structures interfacial water, limiting alkaline HER kinetics. In this work, we report a Ru-RuO2−δ heterostructure that overcomes these kinetic bottlenecks via an engineered interface-to-surface proton transfer relay. This architecture promotes a more flexible interfacial water network that facilitates Grotthuss-type proton transport, coupled with facilitated hydrogen spillover from high-affinity Ru clusters to low-affinity RuO2−δ surfaces. By decoupling proton delivery from surface binding, the Ru-RuO2−δ achieves an intrinsic activity 26-fold higher than pristine Ru, requiring ultra-low overpotentials of only 15 ± 4 and 165 ± 6 mV at 10 and 1000 mA cm−2, respectively. Notably, the catalyst demonstrates long-term durability under high-current-density operation (> 470 h at 1 A cm−2) with a degradation rate 2,000-fold lower than commercial Pt/C. In a practical AEMWE, it delivers 1 A cm−2 at a cell voltage of 1.67 ± 0.02 V (45.1 ± 0.5 kWh kgH2 −1), meeting the U.S. DOE energy-consumption target. Beyond providing a high-performance alternative to platinum, this work introduces a design principle for accelerating electrocatalytic kinetics through the engineering of interface-to-surface transport relays.

articles.title: Advances in Electrospun Stimuli‐Responsive Smart Fibers: A Review
articles.abstract: With the rapid evolution of flexible electronics and biomedical systems, stimuli‐responsive smart fibers have emerged as important functional materials. Electrospinning serves as a versatile fabrication route for micro/nanofibers, enabling tunable fiber morphologies, high porosity, and large specific surface areas to regulate the structure–property relationships of stimuli‐responsive smart fibers. This review systematically summarizes the fundamentals, structural design strategies, fabrication technologies, and applications of electrospun stimuli‐responsive smart fibers. The response mechanisms underlying seven typical stimuli, including temperature, light, pH, humidity, force, magnetism, and electricity, are first discussed. Subsequently, material selection, electrospinning strategies, and structural design approaches are discussed, highlighting how architecture and interfacial regulation govern response speed, sensitivity, and cycling stability. Furthermore, recent advances in five core application domains, including optical responses, wettability switching, shape‐morphing actuation, energy harvesting/storage, and signal transduction, are summarized. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, with emphasis on multi‐stimulus coupling, artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted fabrication, and green scalable production. Overall, this review provides comprehensive theoretical guidance for the development and industrial translation of high‐performance intelligent fiber materials.

articles.title: Antisolvent Engineering Enabled Stretchable and Transparent Thermogalvanic Hydrogels with High Thermoelectric Properties
articles.abstract: Ionic thermogalvanic hydrogels with high ionic thermopower are promising for wearable power supply. However, due to the presence of solid network, their ionic conductivities are still low, limiting their power densities. Herein, a facile and effective enhancement strategy on ionic conductivities and thus ionic thermoelectric properties of PVA(poly(vinyl alcohol))/CMC(carboxymethyl cellulose) hydrogels is proposed through antisolvent engineering. An antisolvent (ethanol) of PVA is introduced into PVA/CMC precursor solution prior to the hydrogel formation, which can change the conformation of PVA and CMC molecular chains as well as hydrogen bond network of prepared hydrogel. It can decrease PVA crystalline domains, and present higher water content and more sub-micron porous structure through freeze-thaw cycles to form stretchable and transparent hydrogel with faster ionic transport. This PVA/CMC hydrogel with antisolvent engineering presents the high ionic conductivity of 57.9 mS cm−1 and elongation at beak of 256%, which are 3.75 and 1.8 times higher than pristine hydrogel, respectively. This boosts its Pmax /∆T2 to a high value of 0.67 mW m−2 K−2, higher than that of most PVA hydrogels. During this configuration with 27 hydrogels, it can output a high voltage of 718.1 mV under 10 K temperature difference, which is potential for wearable power supply.

articles.title: Architecture‐Driven Functional Coupling in Vertically Aligned Nanocomposites
articles.abstract: Vertically aligned nanocomposites (VANs) are self‐assembled thin‐film architectures in which phase distribution, interfacial density, and strain fields are defined concurrently during growth. Nanoscale vertical alignment and coherent interfaces generate anisotropic confinement and directional connectivity, thereby modifying ionic, electronic, optical, and magnetic responses across oxide, oxide‐metal, oxide‐nitride, and oxide‐alloy systems. This review examines how growth kinetics, elastic mismatch, and interfacial energetics control pillar morphology, defect distribution, and transport anisotropy in VAN platforms. Studies spanning electrochemical electrodes, dielectric materials, and magneto‐optical systems demonstrate enhanced oxygen exchange kinetics, anisotropic permittivity, strain‐stabilized phases, and coupled magnetic–optical behavior arising from architectural control. By correlating structural parameters with functional outputs, the literature establishes VANs as a versatile strategy for engineering coupled phenomena in complex oxides. Emerging design guidelines and open challenges are discussed to outline future directions for energy conversion and nanoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Atomic‐Scale Cation Partitioning Links Reaction‐Product Chemistry to Molten‐Silicate Passivation in Rare‐Earth Tantalates
articles.abstract: Molten silicates can be immobilized by protective reaction products or continue to penetrate oxide ceramics, but the structural features that distinguish these pathways remain unclear. Here we examine CMAS reactions with RETa3O9 and connect crystallographic cation partitioning in corrosion products with passivation across rare‐earth chemistry, melt composition, and multicomponent design. EuTa3O9 forms a durable bilayer comprising a dense AX2O6 barrier and a cation‐sequestering B2Y2O7 layer; a related consumption–barrier architecture persists in Fe‐rich lunar‐ and Martian‐regolith analogue melts. Across 11 RETa3O9 compositions, rare‐earth size acts as a structural descriptor for access to AX2O6‐, B2Y2O7‐, and CZO4‐containing reaction pathways. Using this relationship as a design constraint, Eu‐centred high‐entropy RETa3O9 compositions retain resistance to bulk penetration while reducing thermal conductivity. HEC‐2 forms an 84.4 µm reaction layer after 100 h at 1300°C and exhibits an 8.3% lower calculated effective thermal conductivity than EuTa3O9 at 1200°C. These results link reaction‐product chemistry to mechanism‐constrained composition design for high‐temperature protective ceramics.

articles.title: Balancing the Activity‐Adsorption Trade‐Off in Biomass Valorization via Electron‐Reconstructed High‐Entropy Oxides
articles.abstract: The directional anchoring of heteroatoms into a high‐entropy oxides (HEOs) platform offers substantial scientific and technological promise, yet achieving atomic‐level control over such doping remains challenging and rarely demonstrated. Here, we precisely anchor B atoms into an HEO framework (BS‐HEO), possessing a distinct O‐Mn‐B coordination unit in which Mn acts as an electronic hub that triggers an electron‐siphoning effect, thereby redistributing the interfacial electron configuration. Theory and experiments confirm that the electron‐reconstructed surface enables the optimization of the balance between intrinsic activity and adsorption toward 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (5‐HMF) within the potential window (1.40–1.45 V vs. RHE), consequently enhancing interfacial mass transport efficiency. As a result, when the carbon balance is taken into consideration, the BS‐HEO catalyst delivers impressive HMFOR performance at 1.42 V versus RHE, achieving 96.0% selectivity for 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 99.1% faradaic efficiency (F.E.), which surpasses most previously reported benchmarks. This work not only demonstrates precise B anchoring into a HEO but also introduces a new strategy for tailoring and identifying active sites in high‐entropy materials for high‐performance electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Bio‐Derived Polyelectrolyte Additive–Induced Interfacial Ion‐Diffusion Barriers for Nonvolatile Organic Artificial Synapses
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic platforms, yet their nonvolatile operation is fundamentally limited by rapid ion back‐diffusion governed by interfacial ion relaxation at the electrolyte–semiconductor boundary. Channel‐level optimization alone cannot prevent post‐bias ion relaxation driven by concentration gradients in the electrolyte. In this context, polymer additives offer an effective route to regulate interfacial ion transport without modifying the semiconductor channel. Here, bio‐derived sodium alginate is incorporated into a Na–TFSI electrolyte to reconstruct the electrolyte/channel interface and modulate ion redistribution. The resulting interfacial ion‐trapping barrier suppresses back‐diffusion and prolongs relaxation times of doped ions. This electrolyte‐level control markedly enhances synaptic retention and improves linearity and dynamic range in long‐term potentiation/depression (LTP/D) characteristics. These findings establish interfacial ion regulation at the electrolyte level as a decisive design principle for organic neuromorphic systems and highlight naturally derived polyelectrolytes as promising additives for stable synaptic operation.

articles.title: Bio‐Derived Polyelectrolyte Additive–Induced Interfacial Ion‐Diffusion Barriers for Nonvolatile Organic Artificial Synapses (Adv. Funct. Mater. 85/2026)
articles.abstract: Neuromorphic Computing In the Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77301), Eunho Lee and co‐workers present a bio‐derived interfacial network strategy for organic electrochemical synaptic transistors. The bio‐ polymer network effectively suppresses TFSI− anion back‐diffusion from the channel into the electrolyte after bias removal, stabilizing the electrochemically doped state. This prolonged interfacial ion retention enables highly persistent nonvolatile synaptic memory, establishing bio‐based polymer networks as a powerful design tool for advanced neuromorphic electronics.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Spatial Encoding in Cellulose‐Based Electroluminescent Textiles for Real‐Time Gas Leak Localization
articles.abstract: Spatially resolved electroluminescent (EL) textiles are highly desirable for flexible hazard detection, yet conventional systems limit real‐time localization of dynamic stimuli. Inspired by insect olfaction, where spatial information emerges from distributed sensing and spatiotemporal signal differences, we report a cellulose‐based EL sensing textile for real‐time gas leak localization via material‐architecture‐governed spatial encoding. Plant‐derived cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) serve as fundamental building blocks, organizing functional components through blending or surface modification and being assembled via wet‐spinning into continuous fibers with hierarchical porosity, flexibility, and volumetric stimulus accessibility essential for rapid gas sensing. Conductive fibers are fabricated through in situ polymerization of polyaniline (PANI) on CNF surfaces, enabling reversible, gas‐responsive electrical modulation with detection limits of 1 ppm for HCl and 3.6 ppm for NH3. Coaxial electroluminescent fibers comprising a PANI@CNF conductive core and ZnS‐embedded CNF shell provide stable light emission over 100 h of continuous operation. Intersections between these fibers form self‐defined units that translate localized gas exposure into spatiotemporally resolved EL patterns, mapping propagation pathways with a naked‐eye detection threshold of 100 ppm, while maintaining stable emission after washing and bending. This work establishes a bio‐inspired, architecture‐driven strategy for smart textiles, highlighting cellulose‐based nanocomposites as key components for next‐generation smart technologies.

articles.title: Boosting Energy Storage of AgNbO3‐Based Capacitors by Constructing Low‐Atomic‐Displacement Region and M2‐M3 Two‐Phase Coexistence Strategy
articles.abstract: Dielectric capacitors with excellent energy-storage performance are highly desirable for next-generation advanced high/pulsed power capacitors that require miniaturization and integration. However, the low energy-storage density arising from insufficient breakdown strength (BDS), inadequate maximum polarization (P max), and large remanent polarization (P r), remains a critical challenge for the practical application of dielectric capacitors. Herein, we propose a strategy to synergistically incorporate the M2-M3 two-phase coexistence and low-atomic-displacement (LAD) region into the AgNbO3 system, thereby achieving high BDS, large P max and extremely low P r simultaneously. Ultrahigh U rec ∼ 17.1 J·cm−3, excellent η ∼ 89% are achieved in the (Ag1-3 x Eu x )(Nb0.7Ta0.3)O3 (Eu x ANT) multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) at x = 0.03, representing a breakthrough in the overall energy-storage performance of lead-free antiferroelectric (AFE) capacitors. This study not only develops a promising high-performance lead-free energy-storage dielectric, but also offers a novel microstructural design strategy for the synergistic optimization of multiple energy-storage parameters to improve the energy storage performance of AFE system.

articles.title: Breaking the Diffusion‐Limited Aggregation for Ordered Zn Deposition via Interfacial Structure‐Directing Engineering
articles.abstract: Uncontrolled dendrite growth during zinc plating/stripping hinders the practical application of aqueous zinc metal batteries in energy storage systems. In this study, the classical diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) theory was employed to understand the mechanisms of zinc dendritic growth fundamentally and then to guide the design of interfacial structure-directing engineering. [EMIm]EtSO4 ionic liquid as a structure-directing agent was developed to successfully overcome the disordered Zn dendrite growth following the rules of “random motion” and “contact-stick”. Comprehensive characterizations suggest that EMIm+ cations guide the interfacial ordering process by building a buffer layer and a hydrophobic barrier on the Zn anode, while EtSO4 − anions orchestrate the reconstruction of the Zn2+ solvation structure. This synergistic regulation transforms zinc deposition morphology from stochastic fractal growth to highly ordered epitaxial growth. As a result, the zinc anode achieves 99.3% Coulombic efficiency at 1 mA cm−2 and stable cycling over 2000 h. It further endows the Zn||NVO battery with significantly improved stability and anti freezing performance (−40°C). This work demonstrates an interfacial engineering strategy that effectively suppresses DLA-type dendritic growth, providing a new perspective for high-performance aqueous zinc batteries.

articles.title: CO2‐to‐CO Conversion in a Gas‐Fed, Zero‐Gap, PEM Electrolyzer Enabled by Polycations and Nitrogen‐Doped Carbon‐Supported Cobalt Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (ECO2R) into value‐added chemicals is challenging due to the high overpotential of reaction intermediates, the instability of adsorbed species in the absence of mobile cations, and requiring acidic aqueous electrolyte feed to prevent salt precipitation. A gas‐fed, zero‐gap proton exchange membrane (PEM) ECO2R setup utilizing hydrogen (H2) as anodic feed and nitrogen‐doped carbon‐supported cobalt nanoparticles (Co/N‐C) as catalyst may be a solution to these problems but is observed to be ineffective at suppressing the H2 evolution reaction (HER). Immobilizing poly‐diallyldimethyl ammonium (PDDA+) cations with finely milled Co/N‐C results in a change of selectivity from HER toward coordinating CO2 intermediates on active sites. Optimizing Co loading at 1.20 wt.% for Co/N‐C delivers a peak faradaic efficiency toward carbon monoxide production (FECO) of 65% and sustains 5 h electrolysis with FECO above 50% under a constant current density of 100 mA cm−2. The effects of acid‐wash, cobalt content, mass loading, and PDDA+ on the gas‐diffusion electrode and secondary particle size in catalyst ink are optimized to improve FECO against a prohibitively low pH environment. These results highlight the intrinsic properties of PDDA+ on Co/N‐C electrocatalyst for a modular, humidified gas‐fed, zero‐gap PEM CO2 electrolyzer technology.

articles.title: Cartilage‐Mimicking Hybrid Avascular Hydrogel Scaffold for Stable Auricular Cartilage Regeneration in Microtia Reconstruction
articles.abstract: A major challenge in auricular reconstruction is the endochondral ossification of engineered cartilage after subcutaneous implantation. To overcome this, we developed a functionally tailored, hybrid hydrogel scaffold that integrates anti‐angiogenic therapy with biomimetic architecture to stabilize the chondrogenic phenotype. The core consists of a DLP‐printed, bevacizumab‐eluting pNAGA‐GT hydrogel framework with 200‐µm resolution, exhibiting a compressive modulus of 5.35 MPa and a tensile modulus of 0.34 MPa, providing robust mechanical support. Sustained bevacizumab release suppresses local angiogenic activity and is accompanied by increased TIMP3 and reduced MMP9/MMP13 expression, thereby contributing to cartilage matrix preservation and reduced ossification. Encapsulating this core, a visible‐light–crosslinked GelMA‐Tyr hydrogel creates a soft (∼15 kPa), degradable (60‐day) microenvironment that spatially organizes chondrocytes and perichondrium‐derived stem/progenitor cells (PSPCs) into a cartilage‐mimetic construct, thereby preserving cell viability and chondrogenic function. This dual‐phase design enables the generation of stable, multilayered ectopic cartilage, offering a clinically translatable strategy for microtia reconstruction.

articles.title: Chemical‐Gradient‐Induced Marangoni Flows Boost Solar‐Brine Desalination and Enable Concurrent Power Generation
articles.abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers decentralised freshwater production with concurrent electricity generation, yet capillary-driven water supply imposes a kinetic ceiling in high-flux or high-salinity conditions, where boundary-layer buildup drives salt accumulation and performance decay. Here we establish a dual-driving transport regime that couples capillary flow with chemically induced Marangoni convection in low-tortuosity, vertically aligned channels. A longitudinal gradient of oxygen-containing functional groups, introduced into a graphene-oxide aerogel by thermal-gradient reduction, generates a persistent surface-tension disparity that sustains Marangoni microcirculation, continuously refreshing the evaporation interface by displacing concentrated boundary layers into the bulk. A miniaturised evaporator achieves 540 kg m− 3 h− 1 (2.7 kg m− 2 h− 1) in 20 wt% NaCl under 1-sun illumination, sustaining stable operation for 12 h without observable salt accumulation, while simultaneously delivering a short-circuit current of 25 µA and an open-circuit voltage of 0.7 V. Series-integrated devices directly power an LED. These results demonstrate that chemical-gradient programming can recruit Marangoni convection as a robust co-driver to surpass capillary-limited transport, offering a generalizable strategy for high-flux brine desalination with concurrent energy harvesting.

articles.title: Comprehensive Insights Into Electrolyte and Electrode–Electrolyte Interface for Aqueous Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous lithium‐ion batteries (ALIBs) stand out as promising grid‐scale energy storage candidates, leveraging aqueous electrolytes to address the safety hazards and environmental concerns of traditional nonaqueous batteries. Their development, however, has long been constrained by the narrow electrochemical stability window of water, which limits cell voltage and promotes parasitic reactions. This review summarizes recent progress in ALIBs from the synergistic perspectives of electrolyte regulation, interfacial reaction mechanisms, and cell‐level engineering considerations in relation to practical metrics, including energy density and long‐term cycling durability. Particular emphasis is placed on the control of Li+ solvation environments and the formation of functional interphases, which collectively suppress water‐induced side reactions and expand the accessible operating window. By integrating these tightly linked aspects, this review delineates the mechanistic foundations and design principles that redefine the effective stability boundary of aqueous batteries and support the continued evolution of ALIBs toward scalable, high‐energy, and durable technologies.

articles.title: Concentration‐Driven Energy‐Bridge Synergistic Sensitized High‐Efficiency Rare‐Earth NIR Emitters Enable Colorful High‐Fidelity Hyperspectral Imaging
articles.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combines imaging and spectroscopy for diverse applications in agriculture, industry, and medicine. However, current broadband and visible light based HSI systems suffer from limited spectral range, poor environment‐resistant capabilities and severe emission overlap. Here, we propose a innovative HSI approach based on narrow‐band near‐infrared (NIR, 900–1700 nm) rare‐earth luminescent materials. First, through concentration triggered multi‐site synergistic sensitization strategy, we developed high‐efficiency narrow‐band NIR emitters, LaZnGa11O19:Cr,RE$\text{Cr,RE}$ (RE = Yb, Er, Nd, Tm and Ho), achieving FWHM of 28 nm and 50% external quantum efficiency. Subsequently, we integrated as‐developed emitters with HSI technology to construct a novel narrow‐band NIR‐enhanced HSI system. Compared to wide‐band emitters, its theoretical signal isolation in dual‐channel mode significantly improved from 1.84 dB and 0.14 dB to 14.62 dB and 9.08 dB, effectively extending the spectral range of imaging systems while avoiding signal crosstalk between multiple wavelength signals. Furthermore, when applied to real‐world image information scenarios, the as‐constructed system achieves isolation of 11.8 dB (channel to background) and 10.2 dB (channel‐to‐channel) close to theoretical values, demonstrating the feasibility of narrow‐band NIR‐enhanced HSI approach. These results provide unique ideas and inspirations for the design of high‐performance NIR luminescent materials as well as advanced imaging applications.

articles.title: Decoupled Temperature‐Pressure Sensing via Hierarchical Porous Sponge for Thermo‐Tactile Perception
articles.abstract: Precise and crosstalk‐free discrimination of pressure and temperature remains a fundamental challenge in artificial sensory systems due to the intrinsic coupling of mechanical and thermal transduction. Herein, we present a flexible, high‐fidelity dual‐modal sensor based on an ultralight hierarchically porous conductive sponge. The engineered porous architecture synergistically integrates piezoresistive and thermoelectric effects within a single carbon nanomaterial, achieving physical decoupling between resistance‐type pressure signals and voltage‐type temperature outputs, effectively suppressing dual‐modal interference. Owing to its compressibility, conductive network, and thermal insulation, the sensor delivers a pressure sensitivity of 4.43 kPa−1, a detection limit of 25 Pa, a response time of 91 ms, and durability over 20 000 cycles, alongside a Seebeck coefficient of 9.96 µV K−1 and a temperature resolution of 0.5 K. As a proof of concept, it enables real‐time Morse code communication and physiological monitoring. Moreover, a 3 × 3 sensor array integrated with machine learning demonstrates robust tactile‐thermal fusion perception, highlighting its potential as a multifunctional sensing platform. This work presents a material‐driven strategy to overcome multimodal signal interference, significantly promoting sensory perception in complex environments.

articles.title: A Novel pH‐Activatable Nanozyme for Treating Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis by Regulating Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and the Tumor Microenvironment
articles.abstract: Multi‐omics analyses implicate enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in breast cancer bone metastasis (BCBM). To target this metabolic vulnerability, we develop SPMMPA, a bone‐targeted nanozyme comprising a Prussian blue core, a disulfide‐bridged mesoporous silica interlayer, and a manganese oxide shell, functionalized with polyethylenimine, alendronate, and the Ser‐Asp‐Ser‐Ser‐Asp peptide. Its acid‐enhanced catalytic activity promotes reactive oxygen species production and glutathione depletion, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced OXPHOS and adenosine triphosphate production, and downregulation of peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma coactivator 1‐alpha. Alendronate and silicon release contribute to reduced osteoclast activity and preservation of bone structure. Near‐infrared irradiation further enhances treatment efficacy through photothermal heating below 48°C. In mouse models of BCBM, SPMMPA suppresses tumor growth and alleviates osteolysis, without overt toxicity in the assays performed. These findings support a pH‐responsive catalytic strategy that couples disruption of tumor energy metabolism with protection of bone homeostasis.

articles.title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8-tetraamino-5,10-dihydrophenazine-1,4,6,9-tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m2 g−1, delivers 242.8 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR-FTIR and EQCM-D measurements reveal that NH4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H3O+ for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe-PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Moreover, the first Ah-level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

articles.title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors
articles.abstract: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state‐centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history‐dependent state trajectories. A problem‐specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion‐specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden‐state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy‐storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical‐state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

articles.title: Grain‐Boundary‐Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity‐Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
articles.abstract: Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity‐tolerant catalytic H2 sensor based on a grain‐boundary‐rich palladium nanostructure (PdGB) that operates without any external heating. The PdGB sensor functions reliably at 22°C–80°C and 0%–90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m−3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000‐fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H2), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine‐learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature‐programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdHx formation for weakening H2O adsorption and suppress humidity‐induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials‐design strategy for next‐generation humidity‐tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

articles.title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications
articles.abstract: Rare earth‐proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE3+) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE3+, enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth‐protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.

articles.title: Machine‐Learning‐Potential‐Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Ionic transport in solid‐state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large‐scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum‐level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale‐accuracy gap in halide‐tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl−/Br− ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP‐driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl‐enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br− enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion‐engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP‐enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid‐state materials.

articles.title: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Carbon electrodes are ubiquitous in organic electrochemistry, yet the structural origin of their selectivity in radical‐mediated reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that carbon microstructure is a primary determinant of product selectivity in Kolbe electrolysis, a prototypical electrochemical C─C coupling reaction central to fuel, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical production. We investigated eight carbon electrodes in two complementary libraries: five commercial carbons spanning diverse macroarchitectures, and carbon nanofibers with controlled graphitization. Both reveal a consistent structure–selectivity trend for various carboxylic acids and a mixed‐acid feed. Counterintuitively, the most disordered electrodes, despite the highest charge‐transfer resistance, give about an order of magnitude more Kolbe dimer than highly graphitized ones, which give little or none. Disordered, sp3‐rich surfaces bearing oxygen functionalities strongly favor both Kolbe coupling (alkane) and Hofer–Moest products (alcohol/aldehyde), whereas graphitized, sp2‐rich surfaces favor further oxidation to carbocations, yielding mainly alkenes and esters. Density functional theory calculations suggest that oxygen‐functionalized sites bind the alkyl radical about three times more strongly than pristine graphene, consistent with longer‐lived surface‐bound radicals that can couple. These findings help rationalize the widely used but poorly understood performance of reticulated vitreous carbon in organic electrosynthesis and offer guiding principles for rational carbon electrode design.

articles.title: Dual‐Electrode Catalytic Engineering for Sustainable C─C Bond Construction via Paired Electrochemical α‐Alkylation of Nitriles
articles.abstract: Efficient paired electrochemical synthesis requires precise synchronization between anodic intermediate generation and cathodic consumption. However, uncontrolled adsorption and mismatched reaction kinetics often result in intermediate accumulation and competing side reactions. Here, we address this challenge through interfacial regulation of both anodic and cathodic catalysts, enabling a synchronized electrocatalytic platform for α‐alkylation of nitriles using alcohols as sustainable alkyl sources. An Fe‐doped NiO anode and Pb/C cathode are rationally integrated to regulate alcohol oxidation, carbon–carbon coupling, and selective C═C hydrogenation. Fe incorporation tailors the electronic structure and adsorption behavior of Ni sites, accelerating alcohol activation while mitigating nitrile‐induced inhibition, whereas Pb/C selectively promotes alkene hydrogenation without affecting nitrile functionalities. The optimized paired system achieves 91.68% yield and >99% conversion for 2,3‐diphenylpropionitrile at 20 mA cm−2, enabling continuous and efficient synthesis across a broad range of aromatic and aliphatic alcohols with excellent functional‐group tolerance and robust operational stability. This work provides a general catalyst design principle for paired electrochemical synthesis by coordinating interfacial reaction kinetics and intermediate flux between two electrodes.

articles.title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
articles.abstract: Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

articles.title: Extending the Stretchability Limit of Elastomers Through Mechanical Bond Motion
articles.abstract: Elastomers with superior mechanical properties are imperative for next generation technologies spanning soft robotics, implantable bioelectronics, and adaptive aerospace systems. However, in conventional chemically crosslinked elastomers, increasing crosslinking density usually enhances modulus while reducing the attainable deformation before fracture, leading to a persistent stiffness–extensibility trade‐off. Here, we report polymer networks incorporating a single type of [2]rotaxane crosslinker that combines hidden length activation and stress redistribution through mechanical bond motion, enabling greater extensibility at comparable stiffness. Increasing the rotaxane crosslinker content raises Young's modulus from 0.08 to 1.83 MPa while decreasing fracture strain from 10.24 to 2.70. The resulting networks exhibit an empirical stiffness–extensibility relationship of E∝λmax−2.84$E \propto \lambda _{{\mathrm{max}}}^{ - {\mathrm{2}}{\mathrm{.84}}}$, compared with the classical scaling E∝λmax−2$E \propto \lambda _{{\mathrm{max}}}^{ - {\mathrm{2}}}$. This relationship corresponds to a smaller proportional loss of extensibility for the same proportional increase in modulus. The fracture energy reaches 5.57 kJ/m2, compared with 1.01 kJ/m2 for control networks, demonstrating enhanced fracture resistance. Similar stretchability enhancements are observed in networks prepared from other acrylate monomers, supporting the applicability of this design across different acrylate matrices. This work provides a molecular strategy for designing stiff, stretchable, and damage tolerant elastomers.

articles.title: Fluxional Monomers Remodel Crystallinity at Low Loadings in Diketopyrrolopyrrole Co‐Thienothiophene Conjugated Polymers
articles.abstract: Conjugated polymers (CPs) are a class of semiconducting materials in which electrical conductivity and mechanical extensibility can coincide. Despite advances in synthesis and processing, these key properties are typically negatively correlated and derive from the semicrystalline microstructure of the polymer film. Here, we introduce a new strategy to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of CPs through the introduction of bullvalene‐based fluxional comonomers, in which bonds rearrange constantly at ambient temperatures. By comparing bullvalene‐containing poly(diketopyrrolopyrrole‐thienothiophene) (p(DPP‐TT)) with static controls, we show that fluxional backbones resist thermal annealing induced crystallization, creating smaller crystallites even at low comonomer loadings (5 mol%). While comonomers produce minimal mechanical differences in low‐molecular weight CPs, when the network is reinforced through crosslinking, bullvalene strongly enhances stretchability, yielding a crack onset strain more than twice that of the controls. Additional experiments indicate that crosslinking enables the network to realign micro crystallites under stress to delay crack onset, but only when large crystallites are absent, as in fluxional CPs. Despite the incorporation of non‐conjugated comonomers, electrical mobility remains similar to controls at all levels of strain. This work demonstrates that fluxional components can outperform static analogues as structural modifiers in diketopyrrolopyrrole co‐thienothiophene CPs, leading to significant macroscopic effects.

articles.title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
articles.abstract: This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

articles.title: Interfacial Hydrogen Spillover in Partially Alloyed PdNi Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Hydrogen spillover can decouple elementary steps in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet conventional bimetallic catalysts often suffer from discontinuous interfaces that block spillover pathways. Herein, an interfacial hydrogen spillover mechanism is engineered in a Pd–PdNi–Ni catalyst via a partial interface alloying strategy for pH‐universal hydrogen evolution. The graded PdNi interface serves as a recombination sink integrating two synergistic pathways: primary spillover, in which strongly adsorbed H* generated on Ni spontaneously migrates across the interface, and secondary spillover, in which H* produced on Pd also diffuses to the same interfacial sites. The dual spillover is driven by a favorable hydrogen intermediate gradient resulting from Ni‐to‐Pd electron transfer and an optimized d‐band center. The optimal catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 60 mV (alkaline) and 37 mV (acidic) at 10 mA cm−2, with robust durability, and the corresponding anion exchange membrane electrolyzer exhibits 1.73 V at 0.5 A cm−2 and 452 h stability in simulated seawater. Operando Raman spectroscopy detects Pd–H and Ni–H vibrations, providing direct evidence for hydrogen migration from both domains to the interface, and theoretical calculations confirm the electronic origin and spillover pathways. This work demonstrates a rational design for high‐performance HER catalysts by harnessing dual hydrogen spillover.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Reveals Radical Stability in Native Biofilms and Its Role in Bacterial Resistance
articles.abstract: Bacterial cells embedded in biofilms exhibit enhanced antimicrobial resistance compared with planktonic cells, contributing to persistent infections and failure of conventional antibiotic treatments. This resistance is influenced by the extracellular matrix (ECM), a heterogeneous network of polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids surrounding embedded cells. However, how the ECM regulates the accessibility of redox‐active small molecules remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), solid‐state NMR (ssNMR), and dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) ssNMR to determine how native Pseudomonas fluorescens Pf0‐1 colony biofilms differentially reduce nitroxide radicals across morphologies. EPR reveals that radical reduction depends on biofilm morphology, hydration, and ECM composition. Wild‐type biofilms exhibit slower nitroxide reduction than planktonic cells, while isolated ECM and dehydrated biofilms show negligible reduction, highlighting the importance of cellular accessibility. ssNMR identifies preferential spatial proximity of nitroxides to ECM polysaccharides and lipids, while DNP ssNMR reveals increasing polysaccharide content across biofilm morphologies that correlates with slower reduction kinetics. These findings support a model of protection in which the ECM provides the barrier to nitroxide access, and cellular reduction is the final step. Our integrated magnetic resonance approach provides molecular insight into how biofilm composition and structure determine the fate of therapeutically relevant redox‐active small molecules.

articles.title: Mechanoimmuno‐Engineered Dendritic Cell Membrane Nanodiscs Presenting Diverse Antigens for Potent Antibacterial Vaccination
articles.abstract: Conventional antibacterial vaccines often fail to elicit robust immunity against multifaceted virulence factors, including bacterial surface antigens and secreted toxins, particularly lacking the strong T‐cell responses essential for effective infection prevention. To overcome this limitation, we engineered dendritic cell (DC) membrane‐derived nanodiscs (aDCNDs) with stiffness‐tuned topology as a mechanoimmunological antibacterial nanovaccine. aDCNDs uniquely co‐present multi‐antigens from bacterial membranes and secreted toxins alongside upregulated immune‐stimulatory molecules, eliciting potent adaptive immunity that simultaneously targets Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells and neutralizes cytotoxic exotoxins for dual protection. Their precisely controlled sub‐50 nm size enables superior lymph node accumulation versus larger nanovesicles. Importantly, aDCNDs engage T cell mechanotransduction to promote TAZ nuclear translocation, augmenting T cell activation and the secretion of IFN‐γ, IL‐17A, and IL‐4, an effect not observed with conventional soft nanovesicles. The increased stiffness of aDCNDs represents an important and likely contributor to this mechano‐stimulatory effect. In lethal murine models of septicemia and pneumonia, aDCNDs vaccination achieved profound reductions in bacterial burdens (up to 99.99%) and markedly improved survival without systemic toxicity. This work establishes the aDCND platform as a safe and effective antibacterial strategy, highlighting mechano‐immunology as a critical design principle for next‐generation antibacterial vaccines.

articles.title: Non‐Fluorinated Electrolytes Enable Long‐Cycling Micron‐Sized Silicon Anodes
articles.abstract: Microsized silicon (µm‐Si) anodes offer lower cost and higher tap density than their nanosized counterparts, however, their practical application remains challenging. A LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is widely considered essential for µm‐Si stable operation. However, potential environmental hazards of fluorides challenge the conventional use of lithium salts and additives for constructing LiF‐rich SEIs. Here, we present a non‐fluorinated electrolyte combining inorganic lithium salts (LiI/LiBr) with reduction‐resistant monoether solvents (tetrahydrofuran and hexyl methyl ether) forms a LiF‐free SEI that effectively addresses the rapid capacity fading of µm‐Si anodes. Unlike conventional mosaic‐structured SEI composed of oligomers and inorganic components (LiF and Li2O), our electrolyte forms high‐molecular‐weight polymers with binder‐like functionality at the silicon surface, preserving µm‐Si particle integrity and maintaining electrical connectivity even after pulverization. As a result, the µm‐Si electrode (D50 = 4.65 µm) with an areal capacity of 3.15 mAh cm−2 achieves a Coulombic efficiency exceeding 99.95% and retains 92.12% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 0.3°C and 25°C. Furthermore, Li3.75Si||SPAN full cells achieve a capacity retention of over 79.43% after 150 cycles. This work provides an unconventional SEI design strategy for µm‐Si anodes.

articles.title: Proton‐Induced Perthionitrite‐Mediated Zinc Thiolate Persulfidation
articles.abstract: The perthionitrite anion, SSNO−, has been proposed as a S0 source for persulfidation of biological thiol and thiolate compounds. Here, SSNO− reacts with an iminopyridine‐supported zinc thiolate complex to form a perthiolate‐supported zinc perthionitrite complex, acting as both a ligand to zinc and as a sulfur source for persulfidation of the thiolate moiety. A related zinc thionitrite complex was also prepared, enabling comparison of zinc thionitrite and zinc thiolate persulfidation. In these compounds, the zinc‐bound SNO− ligand is selectively persulfidated over the zinc‐bound thiolate moiety upon addition of S8, cleanly forming SSNO− rather than the perthiolate. This work therefore demonstrates that direct S0 transfer from SSNO− to thiolate anions is thermodynamically unfavorable and must instead be mediated by preceding SSNO− decomposition.

articles.title: Suppressing Ostwald Ripening Enables Programmable Growth of Radially Hierarchical MOF Superstructures Toward Multichannel Optical Waveguiding
articles.abstract: Metal‐organic frameworks (MOF) homostructures or heterostructures with domain‐controlled emissive colors have demonstrated significant potential for high‐throughput sensing, anti‐counterfeiting, and information encryption. However, the precise construction of heterostructures with radially branched units remains challenging, primarily because the Ostwald ripening effect during crystal growth tends to drive one‐dimensional elongation. Here, we propose a programmable nucleation‐controlled strategy to spatially construct radially hierarchical MOF superstructures. During crystal growth, suppression of the Ostwald ripening effect triggers stable nucleation events in the system. Subsequently, the relatively high surface energy at the tips of 1D microrods promotes the secondary nucleation on the terminal facets, thereby leading to the formation of radially hierarchical superstructures. The acquired radial architectures with small angular deviations enable efficient multichannel optical signal output. The suppressing‐Ostwald‐ripening‐driven programmable growth paradigm provides a new route for the synthesis of multichannel waveguiding heterostructures and shows broad application prospects in advanced optoelectronic devices, multi‐channel information transmission, and encryption technologies.

articles.title: Surfactant‐Mediated “Oil‐in‐Water” Electrolyte Design via Sonochemical Assembly: Low‐Dielectric Interfacial Regulation for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries are plagued by severe performance degradation originating from the Zn anode's instability. Although electrolyte engineering has been widely established as a primary strategy to address this challenge, the utility of numerous promising species is intrinsically limited by their poor aqueous solubility. Herein, a surfactant‐mediated “oil‐in‐water” (denoted as SMOW) electrolyte design is proposed to unlock the potential of hydrophobic species. A long‐term stable micellar electrolyte is developed via sonochemically engineered self‐assembly, in which hydrophobic species are encapsulated within the surfactant micelles. Driven by interfacial electrostatic repulsion, these micelles release the hydrophobic species on the zinc anode surface. The enriched interfacial layer acts as an effective low‐dielectric shield, intrinsically accelerating Zn2+ desolvation while physically isolating the Zn anode from reactive water molecules. Owing to the synergistic effect between the hydrophobic species and the surfactant, highly compact and dendrite‐free Zn deposition with suppressed parasitic side reactions is realized, enabling an ultralong cycling lifespan of over 3900 h for the Zn anode at 10 mA cm−2. Furthermore, the assembled Zn||I2 full cells deliver cycling for over 10000 cycles at 5 A g−1 with negligible capacity fading. This work provides a universal paradigm to break through the design constraints of aqueous electrolytes.

articles.title: Ideal Quantum Geometry for Fractional Chern Insulators
articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.

articles.title: From Optimization to the Pontryagin Maximum Principle
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.

articles.title: Proactive Biological Control of Invasive Exotic Arthropod Pests and Weeds
articles.abstract: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.

articles.title: T Cell Receptor–Engineered T Cell Therapy in Solid Tumors: Where We Stand and What's to Come
articles.abstract: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Biomolecular Condensates in Bacteria
articles.abstract: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.

articles.title: Biophysics of Microbial Locomotion
articles.abstract: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.

articles.title: Computational Peptide Design: Emerging Concepts in Antibiotics, Immunity, and Evolution
articles.abstract: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.

articles.title: Ecological Kinetics and Evolutionary Dynamics of Antibiotic Resistance in Complex Environments
articles.abstract: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.

articles.title: Mg2+, ATP, and the Control of Bacterial Metabolism
articles.abstract: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.

articles.title: New Horizons for Incretin-Based Therapeutics
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.
