articles.title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: SCLC cell states dictate how cancer cells respond to metabolic stress, revealing how metabolic plasticity determines whether the cells undergo ferroptosis or apoptosis.

articles.title: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity
articles.abstract: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.

articles.title: Taurine lowers inflammaging by regulating the NLRP3 inflammasome in macrophages
articles.abstract: Taurine levels increase with age in mice and humans. Boosting taurine levels even further in aged mice increases health span and dampens inflammation through its regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

articles.title: Secretory bile salt hydrolases regulate niche displacement and gut colonization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus
articles.abstract: Hasegawa et al. show that a class of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) harbored by Bacteroidales species promote elimination of vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE) in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. In the gut, bacteria producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production.

articles.title: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing in ischemic cardiomyopathy reveals common transcriptional profile underlying end-stage heart failure
Heterogeneity propagation and surface homogenization for pouch-cell-sized Li metal anodes
Using NMR to predict molecular reactivity
articles.abstract: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.

articles.title: Mechanochemical crystallization of covalent organic frameworks: from the linkage up
articles.abstract: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.

articles.title: Ferroelectricity in Single-Layer Ruddlesden−Popper Oxyfluorides Enabled by Low-Temperature Fluorination of Amorphous Precursors
articles.abstract: The development of ferroelectric materials relies on cation engineering of pure oxide systems. However, the discovery of new polar frameworks in pure oxides has become increasingly difficult because of their chemical and structural limitations. We report an approach to realize ferroelectricity in the n = 1 Ruddlesden−Popper (RP) family (A2BX4), a structure that is typically nonpolar in the oxide form because of its high crystalline symmetry. To stabilize the polar order in this rigid framework, we utilized anion engineering, specifically the partial substitution of O2− with F−. Although traditional topochemical fluorination requires a stable crystalline parent oxide, the parent n = 1 oxide Pb2MO4 (M = Fe, Co, Ni) is thermodynamically unstable and cannot be synthesized as a crystalline template. A low-temperature fluorination method using amorphous oxide film precursors was used to overcome this challenge. c-Axis-oriented epitaxial thin films of metastable Pb2M(O,F)4 were obtained, because a stable parent crystal was not required. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and electrical measurements (P−E) hysteresis and positive-up-negative-down (PUND) measurements confirmed that these layered oxyfluorides exhibited clear and switchable ferroelectricity. This behavior probably originates from the strong O/F anisotropy, which forces significant off-center cation displacements within the single perovskite layers. Thus, amorphous-based low-temperature fluorination provides a universal route for exploring novel functional materials across various mixed-anion systems.

articles.title: High Defect Formation Energies Limit Ionic Conductivity in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12
articles.abstract: Lithium-conducting fluoride garnets exhibit ionic conductivities of ∼10–10 S cm–1, far below those of their oxide counterparts. Here, we investigate the origin of this poor transport in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12 through a combination of structural characterization and first-principles calculations. Both compounds are highly ordered, with no significant antisite disorder, and exhibit intrinsic ionic conductivities of ∼2 × 10–11 S cm–1 at 100 °C. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal low Li-ion migration barriers (0.16 to 0.29 eV), indicating that the fluoride garnet framework does not inherently restrict Li-ion diffusion. However, the formation energies for lithium Frenkel and Schottky defect pairs are high (1.9 to 2.4 eV), indicating that the intrinsic concentrations of mobile Li-ion defects are negligibly small. These results establish that the low conductivity of stoichiometric fluoride garnets arises from high defect-formation energies, rather than high migration barriers.

articles.title: Revisiting 2-Isopropylthioxanthone: Direct and Reactivable Photopolymerization of Acrylates from Near-UV to Blue Light. Efficient 3D Printing and Surface Modification
articles.abstract: Reversible-deactivation radical photopolymerization (photoRDRP) enables precise spatiotemporal control of polymer architectures. Because of embedded active chain ends, photoRDRP offers straightforward reactivation and chain extension, providing unmatched flexibility for fine-tuning structural, mechanical, and physicochemical properties for targeted applications. Nevertheless, its application to 3D printing remains limited by the cost and synthetic effort of the control agent, as well as by a limited reactivity under common near-UV and blue light sources, which requires printers working in the visible range and results in usually low printing rates. Herein, we show the unexpected ability of 2-isopropylthioxanthone (ITX) to promote both a direct acrylate photopolymerization, (with no need for any conventional co-initiator and a printing rate close to those of conventional photoinitiators) and a subsequent surface-initiated (SI) photopolymerization via reactivable surface-bound species, yielding postfunctionalization results that are equivalent to, or surpass, those of RAFT systems. Compared to benzyldithiocarbamate (BDC) and N-(tert-butyl)-N-(2-methyl-1-(4-benzoylphenyl)propyl)-O-(1-phenylethyl) hydroxylamine (MBA), two model photoinitiators for photoRDRP in the near-UV range, ITX enabled controlled SI photopolymerization of neat acrylate monomers over thicknesses of several hundred micrometers, with higher molar reactivity and a broader spectral response. This allowed for direct photopolymerization and photostructuring using wavelengths from 365 to 405 nm. This straightforward and scalable approach opens promising avenues for the on-demand functionalization and assembly of complex 3D-printed architectures and is expected to bridge the gap between academic precision and industrial accessibility.

articles.title: Air and Water Environmental DNA Enable Detection of a Large Terrestrial Bird: A Case Study of the Southern Cassowary (Casuarius casuarius)
articles.abstract: The southern cassowary, Casuarius casuarius, is a large‐bodied terrestrial frugivore that plays a critical role in tropical rainforest ecosystems but can be challenging to locate and survey using traditional methods. Across much of its range, populations are threatened by habitat loss, fragmentation and other anthropogenic pressures, and key aspects of distribution and movement remain poorly understood. Environmental DNA (eDNA) offers a non‐invasive approach to monitoring elusive species, yet applications for large, mobile terrestrial vertebrates—particularly using air as a sampling medium—remain limited. Here, we develop and validate a highly sensitive, species‐specific TaqMan‐based eDNA assay to detect the southern cassowary and evaluate its performance using both air and water samples collected in captivity and in the field at sites of known presence. Cassowaries represent a biologically challenging test case for eDNA detection due to their mobility, low local densities and terrestrial ecology. Despite this, we demonstrate that eDNA from both air and water sources provides a practical, non‐invasive tool to monitor this keystone rainforest species across landscapes where traditional surveys are logistically constrained. Importantly, this approach provides a scalable method for rapidly assessing cassowary presence, supporting landscape‐scale conservation planning and management. Our results highlight the potential of airborne eDNA for detecting large terrestrial vertebrates, with broader implications for biodiversity monitoring.

articles.title: Divergent Root and Shoot Trait Strategies Shape Competition–Facilitation Shifts Between Conspecific and Heterospecific Neighbors Under Contrasting Soil Moisture Conditions
articles.abstract: Soil moisture availability is a key driver of plant growth and competitive interactions among plant species. Trait differences among species are expected to influence competitive outcomes, with stronger competition often occurring among functionally similar species due to niche overlap. However, most studies have focused on aboveground traits, whereas belowground traits involved in water acquisition remain less explored. Here, we investigate how above‐ and belowground traits vary along soil moisture gradients and how they shape plant responses to intra‐ and interspecific competition. Seedlings of four tropical legume species were grown in a glasshouse for 30 weeks under three soil moisture levels (low, medium, and high) and three neighbor treatments: intraspecific competition, interspecific competition, and no‐competition. At harvest, above‐ and belowground morphological and physiological traits, as well as biomass accumulation, were measured using standardized protocols. Plant performance was strongly influenced by competition and soil moisture. Intraspecific competition increased belowground traits, including specific root length, average root diameter, and root–shoot ratio, particularly under low moisture conditions, and resulted in greater belowground biomass. In contrast, interspecific competition enhanced aboveground traits, including leaf area, average leaf mass, and specific leaf area, leading to higher aboveground biomass and total biomass. Nodule number and nodule dry mass increased with soil moisture, whereas antioxidant enzyme activity was highest under low moisture. Relative interaction index analyses further showed stronger belowground competitive effects under intraspecific interactions and greater aboveground facilitative effects under interspecific interactions. These findings highlight that plant–plant interactions in tropical legumes are highly context‐dependent, with neighbor identity and soil moisture together influencing competitive outcomes. Divergent below‐ and aboveground investment strategies reveal how plants adjust resource allocation, shaping growth performance under changing environmental conditions.

articles.title: High‐Quality Annotated ZZ Male Genome Assembly of Eulimnadia texana
articles.abstract: In many animals, sexual differences are predominantly determined by sex chromosomes and therefore understanding the underlying evolutionary mechanisms that affect these chromosomes is crucial. Most studies on sex chromosome evolution have employed model organisms with ancient sex chromosome systems, which have already undergone evolutionary degradation thereby hindering the detection of early evolutionary processes. Androdioecious crustaceans in the genus Eulimnadia have a unique sex‐determining system that allows examination of evolutionary models of early sex chromosome evolution. In typical ZW sex chromosome systems, the Z is usually homogametic (i.e., ZZ) and the W is heterogametic (i.e., ZW), the latter being prone to long‐term degeneration due to a lack of recombination. In Eulimnadia texana, both Z and W chromosomes are found in homogametic form (i.e., ZZ and WW) retarding the buildup of deleterious recessive alleles thereby keeping these chromosomes in the “proto‐sex chromosome” stage of evolutionary development. Therefore, the E. texana system allows exploration of the early stages of W and Z sex chromosome development. Although there is a high‐quality assembly of WW hermaphrodites, there is no complementary high‐quality male (ZZ) genome assembly yet for E. texana. In the current study, we generate PacBio HiFi sequencing data from a ZZ male, construct a contamination‐filtered de novo genome assembly, and then scaffold this assembly against the WW hermaphrodite reference. The de novo ZZ contig assembly spans ~113 Mb with an N50 of 3.5 Mb and 98.1% complete Arthropoda BUSCO genes, and scaffolding against the WW reference yields a chromosome‐scale ZZ genome (12 scaffolds, total length ~113 Mb, scaffold N50 18 Mb, 0.18% gaps). Together with its gene annotation, this scaffold‐level ZZ genome complements the WW assembly and enables future comparative analyses of the Z and W proto‐sex chromosomes.

articles.title: Macrofauna Associated With Submarine Groundwater Discharge Sites and a Cold Seep in Svalbard Fjords
articles.abstract: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) is the flow of subsurface water into the ocean. To assess its impact on the Svalbard benthos, the composition of macrobenthos was investigated in relation to sediment physico‐chemical conditions. SGD has been seen to generate seep‐like ecosystems in subarctic locations through the transport of reduced chemicals such as methane. Therefore, we compared the benthos of three Svalbard fjord SGD locations to a Svalbard shelf seep location. However, contrary to our expectations, the SGD locations did not resemble the sampled cold seep. Methane was not detectable in sediment porewater, free sulfide concentrations were low, and diversity and abundance were extremely low, despite shallow water depths (40–117 m). It is possible that the combination of freshwater stress, limited chemosynthetic primary production, and high glacimarine sedimentation rates typical of glacier‐proximal fjord environments together result in an inhospitable environment for many marine benthic taxa at Svalbard fjord SGD locations. As the Arctic warms and glaciers transition from marine‐ to land‐terminating, SGD fluxes may change and the sedimentary overprint on SGD‐related ecological effects may diminish. Whether SGD will eventually emerge as an ecologically relevant process in Arctic fjord systems remains an open question, but one that will become increasingly pertinent as permafrost thaws and glaciers continue to retreat.

articles.title: Overcoming Alpine Barriers: The First Documented Case of Golden Jackal (Canis aureus) Settlement in a Subalpine Environment
articles.abstract: The golden jackal (Canis aureus) continues to expand across Europe, yet fine‐scale behavioural data on dispersal—particularly in mountainous regions—remain scarce. Reproducing individuals are recorded further and further to the North and West of the continent, crossing major anthropogenic and natural barriers in the landscape and settling within new habitats. Since jackals are already present or at the doorstep of almost every country on the European mainland, monitoring this range expansion is of great interest to the public and policymakers. The dispersal capacity of jackals is pivotal for their current expansion across Europe. However, research on their movement patterns, particularly natal dispersal, remains limited. Here, we analysed the full dispersal trajectory of a GPS‐collared subadult male originating from the Julian Alps (Slovenia). Using T‐LoCoH utilisation distributions, Net Squared Displacement modelling and Bayesian movement models, we reconstructed its pre‐dispersal behaviour, dispersal phase and subsequent settlement. After several initial exploratory excursions, the young male left its natal home range in mid‐November 2023 and travelled a cumulative distance of 170 km (96 km straight‐line distance), overcoming natural and anthropogenic barriers along the way. After 11 days, it established a stable home range in the Austrian Malta Valley, where reproduction was later confirmed in spring 2024—the first documented case of successful settlement and breeding by a golden jackal in a subalpine environment. During dispersal, the jackal's step length increased in areas with a higher aggregation index as well as at night, suggesting more extensive movement between consecutive GPS acquisitions in more homogeneous areas and during nighttime. Our study provides the first fine‐scale GPS documentation of dispersal, settlement, and subsequent reproduction of a golden jackal in a European subalpine environment. It highlights how both natural and human‐dominated landscapes shape movement behaviour during range expansion.

articles.title: Threatened Conifers Need Targeted and Integrated Conservation: A Case Study of Pinus dabeshanensis
articles.abstract: Due to global warming, over‐exploitation, habitat degradation, environmental pollution, and alien species invasion, around 28% of assessed global species are threatened, with conifers being especially endangered. China has attached great importance to biodiversity conservation, and implemented a series of targeted initiatives over the past two decades to protect and conserve the endangered species in China. Pinus dabeshanensis W.C.Cheng et Y.W.Law is a conifer species with an extremely small population and is listed as Grade I in the national key protected wild plants in China. Despite conservation efforts, the effectiveness of these measures remains unknown. In this study, we have assessed the conservation effectiveness of this critically endangered conifer species, and identified conservation gaps to achieve a new conservation plan for the species. This paper should also be helpful for planning conservation of other endangered conifers. We conducted a systematic assessment of the current state of P. dabeshanensis, and the effectiveness of in situ and ex‐situ conservation, artificial propagation, and reintroduction based on field investigations and a comprehensive review of the published literature, and thereby identified the conservation gaps. The results suggest that the natural population of P. dabeshanensis is extremely small, being composed of only 320 recorded individuals sporadically distributed in Henan, Hubei, and Anhui. Although populations in Yingshan of Hubei, Shangcheng in Henan, and Jinzhai of Anhui are protected in national nature reserves, the largest known wild population in Dawanggou of Yuexi in Anhui is not protected by any nature reserve. Ex‐situ conservation is still at a preliminary stage, with very small numbers planted in botanical gardens and lacking the full range of the species' genetic diversity. We also found that the species suffers from reproductive failure including low pollination success and poor seed set. While reintroduction practices have been conducted at several localities, seedling survival rates vary greatly due to a lack of subsequent management/protection. The lack of standardized reintroduction protocols and management guidelines hinders a consistent and effective implementation of these practices. Although many Chinese institutions including universities, nature reserves, and botanical gardens have been involved in the conservation of P. dabeshanensis, the overall effectiveness has been limited due to inadequate coordination and fragmented efforts. To substantially advance conservation effectiveness, there needs to be a targeted species conservation plan. Within this framework, it will be necessary to combine different approaches in order to ensure the effective protection of this endangered pine. The present study has involved a comprehensive investigation into the conservation effectiveness of P. dabeshanensis, identified critical conservation gaps, and proposed an integrated conservation strategy. Our findings and suggestions will also be valuable for the conservation of other endangered gymnosperm species.

Coordinated development of the “water-energy-land-carbon” system in nine provinces and regions of the Yellow River Basin and analysis of obstacle factors
articles.abstract: Water resources, energy, land, and carbon emissions are the core resource and environmental factors that support the ecological protection and high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin. Using the panel data of nine provinces and regions in the Yellow River Basin from 2000 to 2024 as the research sample, by constructing the “water-energy-land-carbon” comprehensive coupling and coordination index (WELCNI), this study analyzes the coupling and coordinated development characteristics of the four subsystems and the composite system from both temporal evolution and spatial differentiation dimensions. The obstacle degree model is used to identify the core single obstacle factor restricting the system’s development, and the geographical detector model is used to reveal the interactive coupling driving mechanism of the obstacle factors. Combined with the upper, middle, and lower divisions of the basin for comparative analysis, this study systematically explores the evolution laws and constraint mechanisms of the basin system’s collaborative development. The research results show: (1) During the study period, the four subsystems of water resources, energy, land, and carbon emissions in the Yellow River Basin and the comprehensive coupling and coordination level of WELCNI have all continuously increased, and the quality of system collaborative development has significantly improved. (2) The coupling and coordinated development of the basin system presents a stable spatial gradient pattern of east being stronger a0nd west being weaker. The downstream areas of Shandong and Henan are the core areas of high-level coordination, while the upstream provinces such as Qinghai and Sichuan have weak development foundations and are the main bottleneck areas restricting the overall balanced development. (3) The constraint intensity of single obstacle factors shows a hierarchical characteristic of energy dimension > water resources dimension > carbon emissions dimension > land dimension. The energy consumption volume is the main obstacle factor, water resource endowment insufficiency is the secondary constraint key, and the land system has the weakest constraint effect. (4) Each obstacle factor has a significant collaborative enhancement interaction effect. The water, energy, and carbon systems form a complex linkage constraint network. Coal production, water resources volume, and total carbon emissions are the core factors with strong coupling effects. The cross-system superimposed constraint effect is prominent, and only unit GDP energy consumption is an independent constraint factor with weak linkage influence. This study systematically clarifies the evolution mechanism and obstacle mechanism of the “water-energy-land-carbon” system coupling and coordination in the Yellow River Basin, providing scientific references and theoretical support for differentiated zoning control, multi-factor collaborative governance, breaking through system development bottlenecks, and promoting the high-quality collaborative development of the basin.

articles.title: Enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in the red soil region of Southern China
articles.abstract: Red soil is the second most extensively eroded soil type in China, predominantly distributed in the southern regions. Vegetative measures are widely recognized as an effective approach for controlling soil erosion in red soil areas, as they enhance slope stability and substantially reduce soil loss. However, during the early growth stages, the short and fine roots of plants are unable to extend beyond the shear failure surface, which constrains their capacity to stabilize the surface soil. To address this limitation, researchers have introduced seaweed polysaccharides as a soil ameliorant. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms by which seaweed polysaccharides influence plant growth, root-soil complex mechanics, and the erosion resistance of red soil remain poorly understood. Accordingly, an experimental study was conducted to investigate the enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in red soil. The results indicate that (1) seaweed polysaccharides exhibited an optimal concentration range for improving red soil. At concentrations below 2%, seed germination, plant height, and stem growth were promoted, whereas concentrations exceeding 2% exerted inhibitory effects. (2) In terms of mechanical properties, seaweed polysaccharides significantly enhanced the shear strength of the soil. Compared with the control group, application of seaweed polysaccharides increased the cohesion and internal friction angle by 103.68% ~ 180.52% and 13.92% ~ 31.76%, respectively. When seaweed polysaccharides acted in conjunction with plant roots, the improvement was further amplified, with increases of 143.33% ~ 220.65% in cohesion and 14.83% ~ 39.45% in the internal friction angle. (3) Under simulated rainfall conditions, the sediment yield from the slope significantly decreased with increasing seaweed polysaccharide addition. The synergistic effect of seaweed polysaccharides and plant roots arises from the formation of a “seaweed polysaccharide-red soil-root” three-phase unit structure, in which the polysaccharides encapsulate and connect roots with soil particles, thereby enhancing the integrity and flexibility of the root-soil complex. These findings not only broaden the selection of soil reinforcement materials but also provide theoretical guidance for vegetation restoration and soil and water conservation in red soil regions.

articles.title: Mean temperature determines whether winter variability accelerates or buffers energy loss
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Winter survival in dormant animals depends on conserving finite energy reserves, yet winter temperatures fluctuate around shifting means. In ectotherms, metabolic rate increases exponentially with temperature, so thermal variability is expected to accelerate energy loss, with consequences for overwinter survival under climate change. Whether dormant ectotherms can compensate physiologically, however, remains unclear. We overwintered Bombus impatiens queens under constant (2, 3, 4°C) or variable (2 ± 6°C or 4 ± 6°C) temperature regimes for 6 weeks, then measured metabolic rates across the temperature range. Thermal experience altered the temperature dependence of metabolism, but responses depended on mean temperature: variability centred on 2°C elevated metabolic rate at 11°C and increased thermal sensitivity of O2 consumption relative to constant 2°C, whereas variability centred on 4°C reduced baseline metabolism and thermal sensitivity estimated from CO2 production relative to constant 4°C. Using these responses, we simulated subsequent lipid depletion from a standardized energetic state. Variability around 2°C was predicted to shorten the time to lipid depletion, whereas variability around 4°C produced trajectories similar to those predicted for constant 4°C. Thus, identical thermal variance produced opposite physiological and predicted energetic outcomes depending on the mean temperature around which fluctuations occurred. Integrating both temperature means and variability is, therefore, essential for predicting overwintering energetics in a changing world. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Monospecific cover crops perpetuate soil biotic homogenization in croplands across diverse soils
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Croplands are known to support significant soil biotic homogenization. Cover crops are commonly used as a sustainable agriculture practice; however, many times these cover crops are composed of single‐species. Unfortunately, the influence of monospecific cover crops on soil biotic homogenization remains virtually unknown. Here, we performed a common garden experiment including soils from 27 agricultural fields across mainland China and two major cover crops grown separately in monoculture: a legume (Vicia villosa Roth) and a gramineae (Lolium multiflorum Lam.). We found that, on average, monocultures of both legume and gramineae cover crops significantly promoted soil biotic homogenization (i.e. lower β diversity) for bacteria, fungi and protists compared with control soils without cover cropping (p < 0.05). Moreover, gramineae cover crops also promoted multifunctionality homogenization (i.e. lower β multifunctionality), which was also connected with increasing biotic homogenization. Conversely, legume cover crops reduced the homogenization of bacterial generalists, thereby mitigating multifunctionality homogenization. Importantly, the homogenizing effects of monospecific cover crops on soil communities and multifunctionality were counteracted by the heterogeneity of initial soil properties, highlighting its key role in maintaining ecological heterogeneity. Our results suggest that monospecific cover crops contribute to soil biotic homogenization across diverse soils under controlled greenhouse conditions, with profound implications for managing soil biodiversity and ecosystem functioning in agroecosystems. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Nitrogen stimulation of soil carbon content differs between two types of mycorrhizal‐dominated ecosystems
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Increasing nitrogen (N) deposition has been suggested to favour arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) plants over ectomycorrhizal (ECM) plants, but how mycorrhizal association mediates N impacts on soil organic carbon (SOC) remains unclear. By synthesizing 315 N addition studies globally, we investigated the effects of N addition on SOC content in ecosystems dominated by ECM and AM plants (ECM and AM ecosystems). Our results showed that SOC increased by 4.1% in ECM ecosystems, likely due to reduced ligninase activity. In AM ecosystems, SOC did not change during the first 5 years of N addition, but increased by 7.3% over long‐term N addition (≥5 years), driven by increased litter inputs and progressive soil acidification. These findings highlight that N addition enhances SOC in both ECM and AM ecosystems via distinct mechanisms and temporal dynamics, implying that the potential of soil C sequestration may differ between the two ecosystems from short‐ to long‐term N addition. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in EBBR2-Low Metastatic Breast Cancer
Trastuzumab Rezetecan in ERBB2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer
articles.abstract: Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) has demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in a global phase 1 trial involving heavily pretreated patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)–low metastatic breast cancer. To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer. This open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial was conducted at 73 hospitals across China. Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]–negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor–positive disease. Enrollment began on June 30, 2023, and ended on August 20, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the final analysis for progression-free survival in the current study was March 20, 2026. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician’s choice of chemotherapy (n = 274). The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population. Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, a total of 551 patients were randomized, with a mean (SD) age of 54.9 (9.9) years. At the data cutoff (March 20, 2026), trastuzumab rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with chemotherapy in the chemotherapy-naive patients (median, 16.6 [95% CI, 14.0-19.4] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-7.0] months; hazard ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.19-0.33]; P &lt; .001) and the overall population (median, 16.4 [95% CI, 14.0-16.8] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-6.9] months; hazard ratio, 0.27 [95% CI, 0.21-0.34]; P &lt; .001). The benefit was consistent in hormone receptor–negative disease (median progression-free survival: 16.5 vs 6.8 months; hazard ratio, 0.34, [95% CI, 0.22-0.54]) and hormone receptor–positive disease (median progression-free survival: 16.4 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.18-0.33]). Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% of patients (232/276) with trastuzumab rezetecan and 67.9% (184/271) with chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (180 [65.2%] vs 147 [54.2%]). Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05814354

articles.title: Biologging and mechanistic niche modelling reveal thermal dependence of individual lizard movement patterns
articles.abstract: We combine animal‐borne biologging with mechanistic niche modelling to reveal how individual differences in thermal physiology shape lizard locomotor performance and movement patterns. Our framework links fine‐scale thermal variation with climate change responses, providing a new approach to understanding how ectotherm phenotypes may influence vulnerability to environmental change. Abstract Assessing how variation in thermal physiology and body size influences locomotor performance under ecologically relevant conditions is essential to predicting population vulnerability to climate change. We combined fine‐scale animal biologging and individual‐level mechanistic niche modelling to unravel animal–environment interactions in ocellated lizards (Timon lepidus) kept in semi‐natural mesocosms. We classified mobility states from accelerometer data to describe individual movement patterns. We produced continuous body temperature predictions through individual mechanistic models and used thermal performance curves (TPCs) to assess how body temperature influences locomotor performance. We further tested for evolutionary trade‐offs and simulated mobility windows under warming scenarios. Our results provided high‐resolution estimates of body temperature across mobility states, revealing how variation in thermal physiology is associated with movement. We found that individuals occupied different positions along a ‘specialist–generalist’ continuum of thermal strategies: some achieved higher locomotor performance but within narrower thermal ranges, while others displayed broader mobility windows but lower locomotor maxima. On the other hand, body size did not affect movement patterns under current climatic conditions, but warming simulations indicated that larger individuals may experience disproportionately greater increases in mobility under extreme warming. These findings demonstrate that even subtle variations in thermal physiology and body size can translate into differences in locomotor performance and mobility. By integrating physiological, behavioural and microclimatic data, our framework provides a powerful approach for predicting how climate change may reshape the spatial and temporal niches of ectotherms.

articles.title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks
articles.abstract: Using realistic simulations, this manuscript highlights that monitoring expectations for species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks should be much lower than for species richness. Yet, available information can optimize BON design to monitor interactions with higher efficiency, with a level of tolerance regarding the precision of the information needed for optimization. Abstract Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. Here, we used simulations to test the efficiency of monitoring species interactions within Biodiversity Observations Networks (BONs). We tested several methods for designing and optimizing BONs to monitor species interactions and examined efficiency when increasing the number of monitored sites. We showed that the required sampling effort is considerably higher for interactions, especially when considering that interaction realization and detection realistically depend on species abundance. Thus, expectations to monitor a relevant proportion of interactions within a BON should be lower than expectations to monitor its species. However, from a single‐species perspective, optimizing monitoring designs based on a known species range proved an efficient strategy to retrieve its interactions, outperforming designs based on total species or interaction richness. Further efficiency gains required detailed knowledge of where realized interactions occurred, highlighting the need for better knowledge of where interactions are likely to take place and integration of factors influencing interaction realization, such as species abundances. Our results were consistent even when the total species range was over‐ or underestimated by 10%, which shows a tolerance in the precision of the information required for optimization. These findings highlight how attainable levels of information can lead to efficiency improvements when designing BONs. With the right target and optimization strategy, and readily available information, such as species ranges, we can therefore guide observation network designs to monitor species interactions as central biodiversity components.

articles.title: Parental death destabilizes wolf packs despite the benefits of larger pack size
articles.abstract: Larger wolf packs were associated with improved demographic performance overall, but these general benefits did not buffer the demographic consequences of parental death. Compared with packs in which both parents survived, packs experiencing parental death were substantially more likely to dissolve and fail reproductively and recruited fewer pups, demonstrating that parents perform demographic functions that cannot be fully replaced by additional group members. Abstract Cooperative breeding is a fundamental feature of many animal family groups. However, few studies have quantified whether variation in group size meaningfully buffers social and reproductive consequences following parental death. Using 17 years of data from a grey wolf (Canis lupus) population in Oregon, USA, we evaluated how parental death (the death of one or both parents) influenced pack dissolution, reproductive failure and pup recruitment and whether larger pack sizes mitigated these effects. Across 303 pack‐years, we recorded 69 parental deaths, 39 pack dissolutions and 112 reproductive failures. Packs that experienced parental death were nearly five times more likely to dissolve (95% CI: 2.12–11.12), nearly 16 times more likely to fail reproductively (95% CI: 5.34–47.26) and recruited 66% fewer pups (95% CI: 49%–78% fewer) than packs in which both parents survived. Larger packs were associated with improved demographic outcomes overall, but these group‐size benefits were insufficient to fully offset the elevated risks associated with parental death. Our results show that numerous individuals can provide generalized pack‐level demographic resilience but do not functionally replace parental roles, highlighting the importance of evaluating social structure in addition to population size. By clarifying the limits of social buffering in a cooperatively breeding carnivore, this study advances understanding of how social systems respond to parental death.

articles.title: A DNA Origami Nanodevice Programs CD20 Spatial Organization for Selective Apoptosis of Malignant B Cells in Lymphoma Therapy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Triggering CD20 clustering to induce B cell apoptosis is considered a promising therapeutic strategy for dysregulated, B cell-driven diseases, yet current methods lack the spatial precision to organize CD20 into defined clusters and fail to discriminate malignant from normal B cells. Here, we describe an intelligent DNA origami nanodevice that integrates an optimized anti-CD20 antibody array with a conformational switch to selectively induce CD20 clustering and apoptosis in B-cell lymphoma. Benefiting from the nanometric precision of DNA origami, we found that arranging anti-CD20 antibodies into a pentavalent array with approximately 10 nm spacing most effectively drives CD20 clustering and downstream apoptosis. Under resting conditions, the nanodevice stays in a closed, tubular shape that conceals the antibody array inside and therefore remains harmless to normal B cells. Upon encountering c-Met expressed on lymphoma B cells, the device unrolls into a planar sheet and exposes the antibody array, triggering potent apoptotic signaling specifically in these malignant cells. In a Raji xenograft mouse model, intravenously injected nanodevices specifically unrolled at the tumor site, inhibited tumor growth by more than 70%, and produced no significant systemic toxicity. By coupling programmable ligand nanopatterning with a shape-changing switch, this DNA origami platform offers a generalizable strategy for receptor-mediated disease therapy.

articles.title: Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide Liquid Crystals with Enhanced Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization. The biphasic nature of this medium enables straightforward extraction of ΔRCSAs from a single one-dimensional 13C NMR experiment on a single sample, without requiring specialized instrumentation, devices, or postcorrection. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach by measuring ΔRCSAs for eight structurally diverse natural products and organic molecules. The resulting 13C ΔRCSAs are sufficiently large to enable reliable structural verification and stereochemical elucidation. Notably, the method allowed us to unambiguously resolve previously questionable 13C NMR assignments in cryptotanshinone. In addition, the chiral LLC medium exhibits pronounced enantiodiscrimination, as demonstrated for indanol enantiomers as well as significant enantiodifferentiating capabilities for several natural alkaloids. Furthermore, 19F RCSA measurements enable direct differentiation of two enantiomers even within a racemic mixture. Together, these results establish biphasic polyarylisocyanide LLCs as a simple, robust, and broadly applicable alignment platform for ΔRCSA measurements, thereby expanding the utility of anisotropic NMR for structural elucidation and chiral molecular characterization.

articles.title: Breaking Symmetry Cancellation: Heterovalent Substitution Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet Tetrahedral Crystals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ < 200 nm). In tetrahedron-based materials, the hyperpolarizabilities of constituent tetrahedra usually nearly cancel due to structural symmetry, resulting in weak SHG and small birefringence─a classic example being α-SiO2. Breaking this symmetry-driven cancellation while retaining deep-UV transparency thus represents a key chemical design challenge. Here, we report a deep-UV transparent NLO crystal BeSO4 derived from α-SiO2 via stepwise heterovalent tetrahedral substitution. This crystal crystallizes in the noncentrosymmetric tetragonal space group, with alternating BeO4 and SO4 tetrahedra forming [Be3S3O18] six-membered rings. By effectively breaking the symmetry cancellation via alternating low-valence (Be2+) and high-valence (S6+) tetrahedra, BeSO4 achieves a deep-UV cutoff at 176 nm, an exceptional SHG response of 5.1 × KDP at 1064 nm─the strongest among all deep-UV sulfates and Be-containing deep-UV crystals, and a birefringence of 0.038 at 590 nm, almost seven times that of the isostructural BPO4. Unlike BPO4 and α-SiO2, BeSO4 exhibits SHG behavior consistent with phase-matchability, and under 532 nm excitation, it produces a detectable second-harmonic signal at 266 nm. First-principles calculations reveal that the enhanced performance originates from shorter S–O bonds, stronger orbital hybridization, a narrower bandgap, and highly anisotropic electron density, all stemming from the successful cancellation-breaking strategy. It should be noted that the main novelty of this work lies in single-crystal growth, linear/nonlinear optical properties, and mechanistic analysis, since the crystal structure of BeSO4 has been previously reported.

articles.title: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.

articles.title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Isomerization Strategy Enables Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All” Tumor Phototheranostics
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a powerful tool for balancing radiative and nonradiative decays, aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) are emerging as a promising frontier in developing “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents, while their phototheranostic performance needs to be further improved. In this contribution, we designed and synthesized two positional isomers, 5BT-PBPT and 6BT-PBPT, by attaching donors at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo[b]thiophene (BT) segment, respectively, to investigate the effect of positional isomerism on the phototheranostic performance of NIR-II AIEgens. Interestingly, both experimental and computational results demonstrate that the isomerization affords great strength in tuning energy levels, structural conformations, aggregation behaviors, and excited-state energy dissipation. Consequently, a sweet spot for fully utilizing excitation energy was achieved in 5BT-PBPT nanoparticles (NPs), which exhibited not only strong NIR absorption but also high NIR-II fluorescence brightness, strong ROS production, and excellent photothermal conversion efficiency (η). Benefiting from this, 5BT-PBPT NPs afforded superior performance in the “one-for-all” phototheranostics for orthotopic breast tumor treatment. This study fully demonstrates the effectiveness of the isomeric engineering strategy in comprehensively improving the phototheranostic capabilities of NIR-II AIEgens and thereby provides an effective approach for the construction of high-performance NIR-II “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents.

articles.title: Hybrid Solid Oxide Cell Enables Efficient and Robust High-Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route toward a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but balancing mechanical robustness and electrochemical performance remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by introducing a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that spatially decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport, and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell combines high mechanical robustness (fracture load > 7 N) with 1.5–3.0-fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over 600–800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm2, achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes an effective strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

articles.title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal–organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous conditions. The PdcNi@UiO-66 catalyst with dispersed Pd clusters anchored on Ni clusters not only maximizes Pd utilization but also establishes a new pathway for the recycling of plastics. Importantly, when employed as a catalyst for phenylacetylene semihydrogenation, PdcNi@UiO-66 exhibited outstanding activity and selectivity, achieving a turnover frequency (TOF) of up to 67,470 h–1 at 65 °C. This performance significantly surpasses that of previously reported catalysts and is nearly 20 times higher than that of the commercial Lindlar catalyst. DFT calculations combined with experimental results reveal that the PdcNi cluster exhibits a moderate adsorption strength toward both reactants and target products, compared with its nanoparticle and single-atom counterparts. This balanced adsorption leads to a more favorable thermodynamic tendency for styrene desorption rather than overhydrogenation, ultimately contributing to the high activity and selectivity. This study demonstrates a direct route to transforming PET waste into high-performance MOF-based catalysts for selective hydrogenation, offering a cost-effective and sustainable solution for plastic recycling and the development of high-performance catalysts.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

articles.title: MetaTag: A Biochemical Reaction-Guided Design Strategy for New Metabolite Discovery
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Most small-molecule features detected in untargeted metabolomics remain unannotated, representing the dark matter of the metabolome. Here, we introduce MetaTag, a biochemical-reaction-guided framework that generates high-probability novel metabolites by combining abundant endogenous metabolites with common enzymatic transformations derived from KEGG pathways. In this proof-of-concept implementation, we focused on N-acylation and N-alkylation reactions. We synthesized and characterized a physical library of 1068 compounds, creating a public MS/MS database (https://mtdb-website.vercel.app). Screening against 27 rat tissues matched 180 previously unreported metabolites with 6 at level 1 (confirmed by RT, formula, MS/MS) and 174 at level 2 (confirmed by RT, formula). These metabolites exhibited tissue-specific distributions and participated in the interorgan exchange during fasting. Functional interrogation of one such metabolite, N-propionyltaurine, demonstrated its role as a redox-sensitive regulator in brown adipocytes. This biochemistry-guided strategy provides a scalable platform for the discovery of previously uncharacterized bioactive metabolites.

articles.title: Operando Time-Resolved Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed Divergent Functionalization of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We report a photoinduced Ge(II)-catalyzed strategy for divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides that leverages in situ electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex formation to catalytically generate pyridyl radicals, enabling aryl, alkynyl, and alkenyl couplings under mild, protic conditions without an external photocatalyst. Notably, the protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity for pyridyl C–X bonds, leaving other aryl halides, including those bearing electron-withdrawing substituents, intact. The protocol further enables unique transformations, including complete C8-selective coupling with 7-aminoquinoline and the modular assembly of benzo[f]isoquinolines from alkenyl boron reagents. Mechanistic studies support an EDA-mediated radical pathway. This work provides a sustainable platform for the divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides and expands the application of main-group elements in catalytic EDA chemistry.

articles.title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

articles.title: Solid-State NMR Reveals a Bifunctional Disordered Linker That Couples Katanin Microtubule Anchoring to Condensate-Activated Severing
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Microtubule severing by katanin drives rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for cell fate decision, yet how the catalytic subunit p60 (Kp60) recognizes the microtubule lattice to achieve efficient severing remains unresolved. Here, we report that the N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of Kp60 is an essential bifunctional module for severing activity. Using solid-state NMR (ssNMR), we identified a microtubule-binding domain (MTBD) within the IDR which directly engages the lattice to guide substrate anchoring. Surprisingly, the same IDR also enables Kp60 phase separation. Our ssNMR analyses of the condensed phase pinpointed three discrete interaction regions within the IDR which cooperatively orchestrate this multivalent assembly. Importantly, Kp60 phase separation was associated with markedly increased ATPase activity, supporting a functional link between condensation and enzymatic activation. Using function-separation-mutation analyses, our studies show both microtubule binding and condensation are essential for severing: microtubule targeting provides spatial specificity, while condensation provides the catalytic threshold through local enrichment. Thus, the Kp60 IDR constitutes a bifunctional interface that integrates substrate recognition with enzymatic robustness, thereby establishing phase separation as a fundamental and efficient regulator of microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling.

articles.title: Solid–Liquid Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol. Structural characterization using small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography (smSFX) reveals a 1D wire crystal motif. These 1D wire lattices exhibit green-yellow photoluminescence that disappears upon melting. The low melting temperature is attributed to the conformational flexibility of the secondary alkanethiol ligands, providing entropic benefits for the amorphous state. Furthermore, the transition from a nonmolecular, infinite covalent (Ag-SR)∞ network in the solid state to oligomolecular species (Ag-SR)x in the molten state contributes to a higher enthalpy of fusion. Large crystallites are observed to evolve from the liquid near the phase transition temperature. Notably, unmixing of chiral domains occurs in the racemic crystals while the inorganic network remains unchanged.

articles.title: Uncovering Microbial Nitrogenous Chemical Diversity through Isotope-Guided Molecular Networking
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nitrogen-containing natural products are pivotal sources of bioactive molecules. However, their comprehensive investigation by metabolomics remains challenging due to background interference from primary metabolites and their high structural diversity including peptides, alkaloids, nucleosides, and others. Here, we present NitroVISION, an integrated pipeline that combines stable isotope labeling with targeted molecular networking to selectively detect nitrogen-containing metabolites from a complex mixture. Applied to five well-characterized Streptomyces strains, NitroVISION identified 42 nitrogen-containing natural products across 23 distinct compound classes, from which we characterized menaxinnamide, a new subclass of nonribosomal peptides incorporating a methylnaphthoquinone unit, and octapiperamide, a novel ribosomal peptide featuring a unique piperazine ring. Our work reveals the hidden chemical space of nitrogenous natural products and paves the way for the systematic exploration of microbial metabolic dark matter.

articles.title: Unraveling Water Balances behind Salt Formation in CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation. We revealed that although the inlet CO2 stream typically flows through a water bubbler, it is often not fully saturated with water vapor and thus results in significant liquid water evaporation inside the cathode chamber. Although water crossover from the anolyte to the cathode is, in principle, sufficient to dissolve the cotransported K+ as carbonate species (or even bicarbonate in some cases), evaporation reduces the effective local liquid water-to-K+ ratio, leading to salt precipitation. Conversely, excessive humidification suppresses salt formation but induces electrode wetting and flooding, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between dehydration-induced crystallization and overhumidification-driven mass transport limitations. Together, these findings establish water management as a governing principle for stabilizing CO2 electrolyzers and provide engineering guidelines for controlling salt formation in electrochemical reactor systems.

articles.title: Oxygen-framework stabilization and stress-relief engineering via Mo/Ca co-substitution for durable sodium layered oxide cathodes
Breaking the Activity–Stability Trade-Off in Electrochemical NO2– Reduction to NH3 over a Robust Fe3C/CN Catalyst
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrite reduction coupled with plasma nitrogen oxidation offers a promising route for ambient ammonia synthesis, yet simultaneously achieving high activity and stability remains challenging owing to high kinetic barriers and catalyst deactivation. Here, we develop a robust hybrid electrocatalyst for active and durable nitrite reduction to ammonia by leveraging Fe3C nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (Fe3C/CN). As a benefit from strong interactions between Fe3C and CN, this hybrid catalyst delivers a high faradaic efficiency of 89.6% at −0.7 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (vs RHE) and a record ammonia yield rate of 16 956.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.9 V vs RHE, along with no apparent performance decay over 1000 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential for sustainable electrochemical ammonia production. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergistic effect between Fe3C nanoparticles and a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix enhances catalytic performance by optimizing reactant adsorption, water dissociation, and promoting reaction kinetics.

articles.title: Decoupling Josephson Coupling and Supercurrent Nonreciprocity in Twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 van der Waals Junctions
articles.abstract: The microscopic origin of supercurrent nonreciprocity in van der Waals Josephson junctions remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of twist-angle engineering. Here, we investigate twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 vertical Josephson junctions with controlled crystallographic alignment and clean interfaces. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly determines the twist angle and interface quality. While Josephson coupling exhibits a pronounced twist-angle dependence, the supercurrent diode efficiency remains small and shows no systematic angular dependence. In contrast, enhanced diode responses emerge in weakly coupled junctions with reduced transparency and interfacial disorder. Deliberate interface degradation further enhances the diode efficiency to nearly 30% and produces irregular magnetic-field dependence. These results demonstrate a clear decoupling between Josephson coupling and supercurrent nonreciprocity, indicating that interfacial disorder rather than twist-angle-controlled momentum matching plays a dominant role in the observed diode response. Our findings establish an important benchmark for understanding nonreciprocal superconducting transport in van der Waals Josephson devices in the future.

articles.title: Engineering a Dynamic Alloy–Fluoride Interface via a Co-Placement Gas-Phase Strategy for Stable Lithium Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy-density energy storage systems, but suffer from uneven Li nucleation and unstable interfaces. Here, a scalable coplacement gas-phase reaction strategy is developed to construct an adaptive alloy–fluoride interface on nickel mesh current collectors, enabling one-step in-situ formation of a uniform Ni3Sb/NiF2 layer. The lithiophilic Ni3Sb alloy effectively lowers the lithium nucleation barrier and guides uniform lithium deposition. Upon cycling, NiF2 is transformed into a LiF-rich interphase, which stabilizes the electrode/electrolyte interface and homogenizes Li+ flux. The combined interface enables durable and uniform Li plating/stripping under long-term cycling. Consequently, the Ni3Sb/NiF2-modified anode achieves stable cycling for over 2600 h in symmetric cells and delivers 83.1% capacity retention after 240 cycles in LiFePO4 full cells with a high areal capacity of 10 mAh cm–2. This work provides a facile and scalable strategy for engineering multifunctional interfaces toward practical LMBs.

articles.title: Revealing Intrinsic Anisotropy of Collective Magnetic Excitations in Twinned Crystals of a Kitaev–Heisenberg Quantum Magnet
articles.abstract: Quantum magnets with competing interactions often emerge from delicate balances among microscopic parameters, making it essential to disentangle the intrinsic spin dynamics from extrinsic disorder effects. Here we introduce a multimodal optical approach combining infrared and domain-resolved micro-Raman spectroscopies at high magnetic fields to reconstruct the intrinsic magnetic excitation spectrum of twinned crystals of the Kitaev–Heisenberg antiferromagnet Na3Co2SbO6. Far-infrared spectroscopy reveals multiple field-tunable magnetic excitations, but the intrinsic response is obscured by replica features arising from twin domains. By correlating magneto-infrared and domain-resolved Raman spectra, we isolate the single-domain magnon response and uncover a pronounced 2-fold in-plane magnon anisotropy. This anisotropy far exceeds that expected from the measured in-plane g factor anisotropy and is instead dominated by anisotropic bond-dependent exchange interactions. By unifying high-field, high-resolution, and spatially selective optical probes, our work establishes a broadly applicable framework for revealing intrinsic spin dynamics and constraining the spin Hamiltonian in multidomain quantum magnets.

articles.title: Structure-Guided Conversion of a TonB-Dependent Transporter into a Functional β-Barrel Nanopore
articles.abstract: Protein nanopores are valuable platforms for single-molecule sensing; however, expanding the range of structurally defined nanopores remains challenging. We describe a minimal, structure-guided redesign strategy that converts BtuB, a TonB-dependent vitamin B12 transporter, into a functional β-barrel nanopore. Using protein structure prediction and molecular dynamics, we eliminated the internal plug domain, selected extracellular loops, and preserved the 22-stranded β-barrel scaffold. BtuBΔ1–136_Δloops formed single channels in planar lipid bilayers, exhibiting an approximately linear current–voltage relationship and a single-channel conductance of ∼1.2 nS. Polymer exclusion analysis revealed an apparent PEG-accessible diameter of approximately 4 nm, indicating a highly accessible pore entrance. Noise analysis showed that extracellular loop architecture influences the stability of ion transport. These findings highlight the distinction between geometric pore accessibility and functional ion-conducting pathways in redesigned β-barrel nanopores, suggesting that TonB-dependent transporters may serve as useful scaffolds for β-barrel nanopore engineering.

articles.title: X-ray-Triggered Nanoadjuvant Enabling Spatiotemporal Immunometabolic Modulation for Pyroptosis-Enhanced Radiotherapy
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy efficacy is limited by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Current immunometabolic strategies using nonselective inhibitors or exogenous stimulus-activated nanomedicines suffer from off-target toxicity, insufficient antitumor responses, and procedural complexity. Herein, we developed PLG@OMVs-VP, an X-ray-activatable nanoadjuvant, to remodel the immunosuppressive TME and amplify the radiotherapy efficacy. PLG@OMVs-VP comprises outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) modified with verteporfin (VP) and an indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase inhibitor (NLG-919) via a PEGylated singlet oxygen (1O2)-cleavable linker. Upon X-ray radiation, VP absorbs X-rays and generates 1O2, which not only induces immunogenic tumor cell death via radiodynamic therapy but also triggers the selective release of NLG-919 for immunometabolic regulation. Moreover, the intrinsic lipopolysaccharide on OMVs activates pyroptosis, further enhancing the tumor immunogenicity. This strategy integrates pyroptosis-induced immunogenicity, radiodynamic therapy, and spatially controlled immunometabolic regulation, synergistically alleviating TME immunosuppression and eliciting antitumor immunity in both primary and distant tumors. This X-ray-activatable nanoplatform enables TME remodeling and an enhanced radiotherapy.
