articles.title: An enriched methane D/H ratio in the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS
articles.abstract: JWST spectra of interstellar object 3I/ATLAS reveal an enhanced D/H ratio in methane compared with measurements of Solar System objects. The high value is comparable with that calculated for pre- and protostellar regions, indicating a primitive origin.

articles.title: An intertwined short and long γ-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
articles.abstract: GRB 160425A emitted two sub-bursts in short succession with differing properties, indicative of two distinct progenitor types: collapsar and stellar merger. This event raises questions about γ-ray burst progenitor scenarios.

articles.title: Apparent magnetic field decay in a solar flare from Zeeman splitting of the Mg I 12.32-µm line
articles.abstract: AIMS mid-infrared spectroscopy of the Mg I 12.32 µm line during an X1.5 flare reveals magnetic field weakening beneath impulsive-phase ribbons via Zeeman splitting. These changes may arise from an elevated line-formation height or local magnetic redistribution.

articles.title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
articles.abstract: Zr(III) complexes have been historically challenging to isolate owing to their tendency to dimerize or disproportionate. Now, bulky aryloxide ligands have been used to kinetically stabilize mononuclear Zr(III) ions at room temperature. The electronic and electronuclear transitions of these complexes can also be coherently manipulated as competitive molecular qudits.

articles.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
articles.abstract: This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

articles.title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
articles.abstract: Climate change and economic activity are reshaping when and where water stress occurs in the United States. This study identifies the drivers and locations of water stress and shows how targeted water management policies can reduce future scarcity.

articles.title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
articles.abstract: The authors combine two flat optical elements to achieve high numerical apertures at visible and extreme ultraviolet wavelengths, reducing the fabrication demands on each element.

articles.title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
articles.abstract: This study finds that the brain maintains sequences in working memory by organizing items according to their position in a low-dimensional neural subspaces, rather than by repeatedly replaying individual items in order.

articles.title: Prefrontal cortex and striatum dissociate modality and learning order in cross-modal sensorimotor learning in mice
articles.abstract: The authors show that the prefrontal cortex and anterior striatum develop distinct sensory responses in sensorimotor learning, differentially reflecting sensory modality, context, and learning order.

articles.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
articles.abstract: In this study, authors show that serum metabolites measured before symptoms appear can predict which people with chronic Chagas disease will later develop heart damage, offering a way to identify patients at risk years in advance.

articles.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter
articles.abstract: OSTα/β mediates bile-acid transport within enterohepatic circulation. Here, authors report cryo-EM structures of human OSTα/β together with its substrate taurocholate, revealing a facilitated lateral-diffusion transport mechanism

articles.title: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
articles.abstract: Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

articles.title: Cytokine circuits in CNS homeostasis and disease
articles.abstract: In their Review, Becher et al. discuss how selected cytokine networks preserve, destabilize and restore central nervous system integrity.

articles.title: GutPath links immune archetypes and single-cell landscapes in the infected gut
articles.abstract: A single-cell gene expression atlas, spanning six phylogenetically diverse infections, reveals pathogen-specific reprogramming of the intestinal epithelium and a novel Yersinia-induced enterocyte state that is spatially linked to tissue pathology.

articles.title: Bispecific dual T cell agonist invikafusp alfa in solid tumors: the phase 1/2 START-001 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress 2026, in a phase 1/2 trial in participants with solid tumors, invika, a first-in-class bispecific agonistic antibody that selectively targets the prevalent Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, was well tolerated, enabling the selection of a recommended phase 2 dose for further testing, and showed a preliminary efficacy signal in both immunologically hot and cold tumors.

articles.title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
articles.abstract: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10−5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies. A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

articles.title: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026, in a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating an off-the-shelf lymph node-targeting peptide vaccine in patients with mutated KRAS pancreatic cancer within 6 months of standard curative intent therapy, the primary endpoint of disease-free survival was not met, but prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant disease-free survival benefit in the vaccine arm for patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative disease and in those without prior radiation treatment.

articles.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
articles.abstract: A patient-facing conversational AI showed promising feasibility and safety in a single-center primary care setting, providing a basis for larger-scale evaluation.

articles.title: The human microbiome and chronic disease: ten strategic priorities for research and public health
articles.abstract: The human microbiome has emerged as one of the most consequential frontiers in biomedical science. An international group of leading microbiome scientists, convened by the US Department of Health and Human Services, presents a strategic vision for realizing its potential to transform public health.

articles.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
articles.abstract: This Analysis benchmarks segmentation methods across different datasets and presents Nextflow, a pipeline for standardized method selection for spatial transcriptomics.

articles.title: NanostarDB: an interactive knowledgebase for standardized annotation, discovery and reuse of nucleic acid nanostructure designs
articles.abstract: The lack of standardized reporting and annotation of nucleic acid nanostructures limits reproducibility, interoperability and the efficient reuse of published designs. NanostarDB is a community-driven knowledgebase that standardizes nucleic acid nanostar designs through persistent identifiers, structural annotations, and integrated computational tools for design exploration, analysis and reuse, and is compliant with principles of findability, accessibility, interoprability and reusability (FAIR).

articles.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
articles.abstract: The authors developed methods to identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the blood that come from the brain by capturing EV surface proteins. This could be used in the future to diagnose neurological diseases.

articles.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
articles.abstract: This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

articles.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
articles.abstract: Conventional quantum error correction requires repeated measurements and real-time feedback, which are technically complex. An autonomous implementation that eliminates these while beating the break-even point is demonstrated in a trapped-ion system.

articles.title: Maxwell’s demon with memory
articles.abstract: Maxwell’s demon may produce work using the information it obtains by measuring the system as fuel. Now, it is shown that the amount of produced work increases if the demon takes information about the dynamical correlations of the system into account.

articles.title: Particle collisions on a quantum computer
articles.abstract: Elementary particle physics rests on the discovery of particles produced in high-energy collider experiments. Now, a model collision above the threshold for particle production has been simulated on a quantum computer.

articles.title: The physical chemistry behind porous liquids
articles.abstract: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.

articles.title: Understanding porous liquids
articles.abstract: Becky Greenaway, Associate Professor (Reader) and Royal Society University Research Fellow at Imperial College London, talks to Nature Synthesis about developing automated high-throughput experimentation to design porous liquids as well as persistent challenges in the field.

articles.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy
articles.abstract: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL. In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria. A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups. Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

articles.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy — Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial
articles.abstract: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9. In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed. In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred. In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

articles.title: Embryonal degreening and seed longevity require plastid LEA proteins
articles.abstract: Working model of how plastidial LEA proteins aid the remodelling of photosynthetic structures during degreening of Arabidopsis seed embryos. LEA42 and LEA48 support thylakoid proteostasis and membrane remodelling in embryonal cells during late seed maturation by maintaining a local physicochemical environment compatible with protein turnover and membrane re‐organisation. ATP synthase F1 subunits, ClpP4 and HSP90‐5, as pinpointed as potential LEA interactors by proteomic approaches, are highlighted as candidate molecular entry points. Summary Seeds enable plant embryos to endure extended periods and environmental extremes. Orthodox seeds acquire desiccation tolerance during maturation, before metabolic quiescence. Coordinated thylakoid disassembly and Chl degradation lead to embryo degreening, a hallmark of orthodox seed maturation. While degreening is hormonally controlled, our understanding of the molecular players involved and its physiological significance remains incomplete. By serendipity, we observed a stay‐green seed phenotype in an Arabidopsis thaliana mutant lacking two LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) proteins, LEA42 and LEA48, which we identified as the most abundant LEA proteins in seed mitochondria and plastids. Using lea48xlea42 as a model for impaired LEA function in seed mitochondria and plastids, proteomic, transcriptomic and transmission electron microscopy analyses indicate incomplete thylakoid degradation. Freshly harvested lea48xlea42 seeds were unaffected in germination but were impaired in germination after high‐temperature/high‐humidity ageing. Genetic complementation with specifically targeted LEA expression in either mitochondria or chloroplasts revealed that seed longevity support is associated with plastidial, but not mitochondrial, LEA. Light exposure of mature seeds (‘light storage’) reduced longevity, providing a physiological framework for embryo degreening. Our data identify a role for LEA proteins in remodelling seed plastids before maturation drying and highlight LEA‐dependent embryo degreening as a decisive contributor to seed longevity. Zusammenfassung Samen ermöglichen Pflanzenembryonen, lange Zeiträume und extreme Umweltbedingungen zu überdauern. Orthodoxe Samen erlangen während der Reifung und vor dem Eintritt in einen metabolischen Ruhezustand Trocknungstoleranz. Der koordinierte Abbau von Thylakoiden und Chlorophyll führt zur Entgrünung des Embryos, einem charakteristischen Merkmal der Reifung orthodoxer Samen. Obwohl die Entgrünung hormonell reguliert wird, ist unser Verständnis der daran beteiligten molekularen Komponenten und ihrer physiologischen Bedeutung bislang unvollständig. Durch Zufall beobachteten wir unvollständig entgrünte Samen in einer Arabidiopsis thaliana Mutante, der zwei LATE EMBRYOGENESIS ABUNDANT (LEA) Proteine, LEA42 und LEA48, fehlten. Diese identifizierten wir als die am häufigsten vorkommenden LEA‐Proteine in den Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen. Wir verwendeten lea48xlea42 als Modell für eine beeinträchtigte LEA‐Funktion in Mitochondrien und Plastiden von Samen. Proteomische und transkriptomische Analysen sowie elektronenmikroskopische Daten deuteten auf einen unvollständigen Abbau der Thylakoide hin. Frisch geerntete lea48xlea42‐Samen zeigten keine Beeinträchtigung der Keimung. Nach Alterung der Samen bei hoher Temperatur und Luftfeuchtigkeit war die Keimfähigkeit jedoch verringert. Die genetische Komplementation durch gezielte LEA‐Expression entweder in Mitochondrien oder Chloroplasten zeigte, dass der Beitrag zur Samenlanglebigkeit mit plastidären, nicht jedoch mit mitochondrialen LEA‐Proteinen verbunden ist. Die Lichtexposition reifer Samen (‘Lichtlagerung’) verringerte ihre Langlebigkeit und liefert damit einen physiologischen Erklärungsrahmen für die Entgrünung des Embryos. Unsere Daten zeigen eine Rolle von LEA‐Proteinen bei der Umstrukturierung von Samenplastiden vor der Austrocknung während der Reifung.…

articles.title: Field generation of triparental sugar beet plants through polyspermy‐induced three‐parent breeding
articles.abstract: Polyspermy, the fertilization of an egg by two sperm cells, can generate viable triparental offspring in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. To explore the potential for three‐parent breeding in a crop species, male‐sterile sugar beet plants were grown alongside genetically distinct pollen donors carrying dominant, traceable selection markers. Progeny carrying genetic signatures from two fathers were identified and subjected to further genetic analysis. The combined detection of paternal markers from two pollen donors and an additional chromosome set confirms the triparental origin of these plants, demonstrating the potential for three‐parent breeding in sugar beet under field conditions.

articles.title: Leaf‐to‐root ROS signaling recruits rhizosphere Bacillus: a synbiotic mechanism for rice adaptability under foliar Cd stress
articles.abstract: Foliar cadmium (Cd) exposure triggers systemic reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling from leaves to roots in rice, accompanied by calcium (Ca2+) responses, increasing root membrane permeability and promoting the exudation of L‐valine (Val) and L‐leucine (Leu). These amino acids enhance chemotaxis and root colonization by beneficial Bacillus strains. The recruited Bacillus promotes leaf lignification, enhances rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress, and reduces grain Cd accumulation. Combining Val and Leu with Bacillus as a synbiotic further strengthens these beneficial effects and improves rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress. Summary In paddy fields near mining sites or transport corridors, elevated foliar cadmium (Cd) exposure is an emerging threat to rice (Oryza sativa) production. While rice recruits beneficial rhizosphere microbes against environmental stress, how this recruitment is coordinated under foliar Cd stress remains elusive. We assessed physiological responses to foliar Cd exposure in 26 rice cultivars and characterized rhizosphere bacterial communities and root exudates in six representative cultivars. Foliar Cd reduced leaf biomass by 6–29% and induced pronounced oxidative stress. In parallel, this foliar stress reshaped the rhizosphere microbiota, with consistent enrichment of Bacillus. This microbial shift was accompanied by increased root exudation of L‐valine and L‐leucine, which was associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and increased root membrane permeability. Crucially, these amino acids promoted chemotaxis and root colonization by the representative Bacillus strains SRS50 and SRS107, selected from 11 candidates among 241 rhizosphere isolates, whereas colonization was reduced in ROS‐deficient mutants. Functionally, application of a ‘synbiotic’ (amino acid‐Bacillus combination) reduced grain Cd concentrations by 40.5–43.3%, associated with Bacillus‐induced leaf lignification. These findings highlight a plant–microbe feedback loop that contributes to rice adaptation to foliar Cd stress.

articles.title: Ten rules for identifying horizontal gene transfers in deep plant phylogenies
articles.abstract: Deep‐level clustering in the GH32 gene family is unsupported and is not robust to the alignment substitution matrix or the rooting method. Summary Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is one of the most intriguing aspects of genome evolution, challenging classical views of vertical inheritance. Growing genome availability across the tree of life offers opportunities to discover HGT, yet recent reanalyses suggest many reported cases may not withstand scrutiny. Detecting ancient transfers is especially difficult, as phylogenetic signal erodes over time and analytical choices strongly shape conclusions. Here we propose 10 practical rules for evaluating HGT in deep plant phylogenies, organised around three themes: genomic foundation, rigorous analytical framework, and biological interpretation. A reliable genomic foundation requires excluding contamination, verifying genomic integration, and avoiding biased taxon sampling. Rigorous phylogenetics is essential, as deep phylogenies are sensitive to alignment parameters, substitution model, rooting strategy, and branch support. We illustrate this with three glycosyl hydrolase families: for GH9 and GH32, analytical choices can eliminate apparent HGT signals entirely, while GH18 shows why complex, multi‐domain families resist confident inference. Finally, HGT signatures demand cautious, biologically plausible interpretation. Recurrent gene duplication, loss, and domain shuffling commonly produce HGT‐like patterns and should always be considered as alternatives. Our rules offer a pragmatic checklist helping authors and reviewers distinguish robust HGT from artefacts, fostering more reliable evidence on HGT in plants.

articles.title: An integrated experimental–computational framework for elasto-plastic characterization and spatial mapping of canine bone properties
articles.abstract: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental–computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load–displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

articles.title: Cross-cultural adaptation, validation, and measurement invariance of the First Aid Willingness Questionnaire (FAWQ) among Turkish adolescents
articles.abstract: Background This study translated, culturally adapted, and evaluated the First Aid Willingness Questionnaire for Schoolchildren to assess adolescents’ self-reported readiness to help and potential barriers to first-aid provision. Methods This cross-sectional psychometric study included 470 high school students in Aksaray, Türkiye. The questionnaire underwent forward–backward translation, review by 12 experts, and pilot testing with 35 students. Exploratory factor analysis derived the structure, which was subsequently evaluated via ordinal confirmatory factor analysis in the same sample. Content and construct validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance across gender, grade level, and perceived family income were assessed. Results All item-level content validity ratios exceeded 0.83; the scale-level content validity index was 0.90. Removing two items yielded a 16-item, three-factor structure: First Aid Willingness, Negative Emotions, and Perceived Knowledge. The model showed acceptable fit: scaled χ²(101) = 288.09, p < 0.001; comparative fit index = 0.95; Tucker–Lewis index = 0.94; root mean square error of approximation = 0.06, 90% confidence interval [0.05, 0.07]; standardized root mean square residual = 0.06. Composite reliability ranged from 0.79 to 0.90. Average variance extracted ranged from 0.49 to 0.59, with borderline convergent validity for Negative Emotions. Discriminant validity was supported. Cronbach’s alpha ranged from 0.72 to 0.87, and McDonald’s omega from 0.74 to 0.87. Configural, threshold, metric, and scalar invariance were supported across all grouping variables. Strict invariance was supported across grade level and perceived family income, but not gender. Conclusion The results provide preliminary evidence for the Turkish questionnaire’s psychometric properties and support subscale interpretation and latent mean comparisons within the study sample. Independent replication and evaluation of temporal stability, responsiveness, and external validity are needed.

articles.title: Decoding motor imagery EEG signals by a deep learning network integrating multiscale filtering and temporal-channel attention mechanisms
articles.abstract: Due to their low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity, accurately classifying EEG signals is still one of the main hindrances that limit the real-world applications of a brain-computer interface (BCI). Deep learning (DL) is a potential method for addressing the problem. However, how to create a suitable DL network for motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs poses severe challenges in the case of insufficient training data. In this paper, a DL network based on multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal and channel attention mechanisms is proposed for decoding MI tasks. Temporal and spatial features are extracted by four parallel CNN branches, each of which is followed by a Transformer block for learning the global correlations of local time features. The outputs from the four Transformer blocks are concatenated along channel dimension and then input into a channel attention module for channel fusion. The subsequent feature map is classified by a CNN, which replaces the commonly used fully connected layer for reducing computational complexity. The proposed network was evaluated on three publicly available BCI datasets and compared with five state-of-the-art DL networks. The training data sets are augmented using the approach segmentation and reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 80.21% on Dataset 1 (4-class tasks), 90.19% on Dataset 2 (2-class tasks), and 97.32% on Dataset 3 (4-class tasks), surpassing the strongest baselines FBCNet on Dataset 1, MSFBCNN on Dataset 2 and MSFBCNN on Dataset 3 by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99% respectively. The network effectively decoded the MI-based EEG signals, providing a potential method for BCI applications.

articles.title: Disentangling leaf day respiration from photorespiration in C3 leaves: A single-curve An/Ca approach validated under photorespiration-suppressed conditions
articles.abstract: Leaf day respiratory rate (Rd), a pivotal component of plant carbon metabolism that directly modulates net photosynthetic carbon gain and plant fitness, has long been challenging to accurately quantify due to overlapping CO2 fluxes with photosynthesis and photorespiration (Rp). This study aimed to disentangle Rd from Rp in C3 crops using a high-CO2/low-O2 (>1200 μmol mol–1 CO2 + 2% O2) An/Ca (net photosynthetic rate-ambient CO2 concentration) model. We integrated two datasets: An/Ca curve data of four C3 species (Trifolium pratense, Silphium perfoliatum, Lolium perenne, Triticum aestivum) under ambient O2 (21% O2) from Ye et al. (2025) and newly collected data under low O2 (2% O2) for the same species. A dedicated model (Eqn 1) was developed to extract key parameters [e.g., the maximum net photosynthetic rate (Anmax), CO2 compensation point (Γ) in the presence of Rd, photorespiratory rate at Ca = 0 μmol mol–1 (RC0)] from An/Ca curves, with ANOVA confirming no significant differences between calculated and observed parameter values (p > 0.05). Under 2% O2, Rp was strongly suppressed, making the gross photorespiratory rate (RC = Rp + Rd) a reliable proxy for approximate Rd. Results showed that Rd estimates from the high-CO2/low-O2 approach (0.74–1.12 μmol m–2 s–1) were consistent with literature ranges (0.74–2.89 μmol m–2 s–1) for four C3 crops. Interspecific differences in Rd were observed: L. perenne had the highest Rd, while T. aestivum had the lowest, which correlated with species-specific photosynthetic traits (e.g., carboxylation efficiency). Rd remained stable across O2 levels (21% vs. 2%), indicating independence from short-term photorespiratory flux changes. The RC ≈ Rd assumption is supported by the substantial decrease in Γ (50–67%) and RCO (40–55%) under 2% O2, and by the consistency of Rd estimates with literature ranges, although independent ground-truth measurements remain to be conducted. This study suggests the high-CO2/low-O2 An/Ca model as a new tool for Rd quantification in C3 crops. The findings enhance understanding of non-photosynthetic carbon flux dynamics and provide critical parameters for refining crop carbon cycling models to predict growth and yield under current and future atmospheric conditions.

articles.title: Do community pharmacies unnecessarily recommend oral emergency contraception? A nationwide mystery caller investigation in Germany
articles.abstract: Background Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors. Methods A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology – considered the “gold standard” – was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21–24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer. Results Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff. Conclusion The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.

articles.title: Efficient phenotyping of banana (Musa spp.) germplasm for resistance to five biotic constraints using Partially replicated (P-rep) design
articles.abstract: Banana breeding programs prioritize improving yield with resistance to biotic stresses while maintaining fruit quality. This study focused on identifying genotypes with resistance to five major biotic constraints including Cosmopolites sordidus, Radopholus similis, banana Xanthomonas wilt, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense – Race 1 and Pseudocercospora fijiensis. A diverse set of diploid and tetraploid genotypes was phenotyped under controlled screenhouse and field conditions to identify potential sources of. A partially replicated (P-rep) design, was used to accommodate unequal plant availability arising from asynchronous multiplication. P-rep design enabled robust phenotypic comparisons and identification of genotypes expressing resistance to multiple biotic stresses. Several diploid genotypes exhibited resistance to multiple constraints, highlighting their potential as parental lines for resistance introgression and broadening the genetic base for banana improvement. Leveraging on the efficiency and precision of the P-rep experimental design, these findings accelerate the phenotyping of genotypes.

articles.title: Factors influencing elderly people’s intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research
articles.abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users’ medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people’s intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users’ data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users’ perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users’ intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = −0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users’ intentions to adopt mHealth apps.

articles.title: How unequal is unequal? Turn-taking simulation for benchmarking participation and opportunity inequality in small-group collaboration
articles.abstract: Participation equity is essential for ensuring that students gain cognitive and social benefits from collaborative learning, yet there is a lack of quantitative benchmarks for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in small-group collaboration. This study focuses on two turn-based analytical dimensions of participation equity: participation equality, measured by students’ shares of speaking turns, and opportunity equality, measured by students’ shares of addressed opportunities. Using the standard deviation of these rates, the study establishes preliminary, context-specific simulation-based reference values for identifying departures from an idealized triadic turn-taking baseline. The empirical dataset included 117 fourth-grade primary school students from two classes in mainland China, who worked in heterogeneous triads on mathematical and reading tasks. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulation, the study estimated local turn-taking parameters from empirical data, generated reference distributions under an ideal-equity baseline, and conducted sensitivity analyses to examine model stability. Results support the internal stability of the model and provide turn-count-specific reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity inequality. The findings offer preliminary reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in collaborative learning and highlight the importance of turn count when evaluating structural patterns of participation and opportunity in triadic classroom dialogue. These reference values describe structural participation patterns rather than collaboration quality and require recalibration and independent validation before application in other educational settings.

articles.title: Immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology design of self-amplifying RNA vaccine against marburg virus with structural dynamics and immune simulation analysis
articles.abstract: by Md. Aftabur Rahman, Lamyea Kabir, Nadia Ahmed, Atish Barua, Mohammad Hasan, Ahmad Abdullah Mahdeen Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.

articles.title: Intratracheal microspray delivery of iohexol for sustained lung-parenchymal enhancement in preclinical micro-computed tomography: A feasibility and acute-safety study in mice
articles.abstract: Preclinical thoracic micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is constrained by the brief pulmonary enhancement window of intravenously (IV) administered iodinated contrast, which the kidneys clear rapidly. We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. IV delivery produced vascular and cardiac opacification with progressive bladder accumulation, which was the largest signal in every IV animal by 120 min. Intratracheal delivery produced widespread, comparatively uniform lung-parenchymal opacification at 5, 15 and 30 min with no discrete bladder opacity at any time; coronal thoracic signal was 0.77 at 5 min and 0.72 at 30 min, against 0.09 to 0.19 after IV injection. Acute safety was assessed at 5 and 29 h by serum biochemistry and histopathology against untreated controls. ALT, AST and blood urea nitrogen did not differ among groups. Creatinine was modestly higher than in controls after both routes, with no difference between routes, consistent with renal excretion of absorbed iohexol. Lung, heart, liver, spleen and kidney showed preserved architecture without acute injury. These data identify intratracheal microspray delivery as a practical way to hold iodine in the lung parenchyma across a thoracic micro-CT acquisition and provide the basis for a confirmatory quantitative study.

articles.title: Lens dislocation, OCTA, and archived FBN1 reports: An exploratory study
articles.abstract: Purpose Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) is a recognized anterior-segment manifestation of fibrillinopathy. This exploratory phenotype-first study compared macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters between participants with and without documented lens dislocation and descriptively reviewed available archived clinical FBN1 reports. Methods This retrospective, availability-based study included 16 participants classified by verified current or historical lens-dislocation status. Participant-level superficial capillary plexus (SCP) vessel density was calculated by averaging valid bilateral measurements or using the single valid eye. Five OCTA endpoints were compared using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests; Benjamini–Hochberg q values were used as a multiplicity sensitivity analysis. Seven archived clinical FBN1 reports from lens-dislocation-positive (LD+) participants were summarized without variant reclassification. No genotype–OCTA association was assessed. Results The cohort comprised 7 LD+ and 9 lens-dislocation-negative (LD−) participants; 15 participants (6 LD+ and 9 LD−) contributed quantitative OCTA data. Foveal SCP vessel density was lower in LD+ participants (median [IQR], 19.38% [18.68–20.04] vs 30.20% [29.20–31.85]; p = 0.036), but the finding was not retained after multiplicity sensitivity analysis (q = 0.180). Whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal vessel-density comparisons were not significant (p = 0.328, 0.272, and 0.238; q = 0.410 each), and OD-only foveal avascular zone area did not differ (n = 14; p = 0.606; q = 0.606). Six of seven archived reports documented an FBN1 variant; one was negative within its assay scope. Conclusions The unadjusted foveal signal was not robust to multiplicity analysis, and other OCTA endpoints did not differ significantly. Marked between-group differences in spherical equivalent and axial length, the small sample, and heterogeneous routine-care genetic reports limit interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish OCTA as a diagnostic or prognostic test or demonstrate an individual-level genotype–OCTA association.

articles.title: Multi-horizon forecasting for decision support in a thermally delayed biomass-fired boiler system
articles.abstract: Thermally delayed biomass-boiler systems exhibit heterogeneous temporal responses that complicate forecasting and operational warning. This study analysed long-term field data from a biomass-fired boiler system to characterise thermal-response lags and evaluate multi-horizon forecasting of the P1 thermal-storage-tank temperature at 60-, 120-, and 180-min horizons. Robust cross-correlation analysis showed statistically detectable but weak associations between P1 temperature and the combustion-related operational inputs, while daily lag estimates exhibited broad and heterogeneous distributions, indicating that the system could not be represented by a single deterministic response time. Benchmark comparison showed that increasing model complexity did not necessarily improve forecasting performance. The Linear AR model achieved the lowest test RMSE and highest R2 at all three horizons, with RMSE values of 1.3774, 2.1605, and 2.6182 °C and R2 values of 0.7809, 0.4616, and 0.2104 at 60, 120, and 180 min, respectively. Lag coverage increased with forecasting horizon, whereas predictive accuracy progressively decreased, demonstrating a trade-off between pointwise accuracy and coverage of delayed thermal responses rather than a universally optimal horizon. Retrospective out-of-band warning analysis further showed that XGBoost recall decreased from 0.5343 at 60 min to 0.1761 at 120 min and 0.0538 at 180 min, while specificity increased from 0.9095 to 0.9546 and 0.9854, respectively. These results indicate that longer-horizon forecasts became increasingly conservative and detected progressively fewer future out-of-band states. Overall, the findings demonstrate that simple temporal models remain highly competitive for this strongly persistent thermal system and that multi-horizon forecasts should be interpreted as predictive risk indicators rather than evidence of causal improvements in boiler control or operational performance.

articles.title: Multienzyme cascade biotransformation of L-Tyrosine to Danshensu by engineered Escherichia coli
articles.abstract: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble bioactive compound with significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, is widely utilized in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. In this study, we established a multi-enzyme cascade system in engineered Escherichia coli to synthesize DSS from L-Tyrosine. The initial co-expression of 4-hydroxyphenylacetate 3-monooxygenase (HpaBC), L-amino acid deaminase (aadL), glucose dehydrogenase (gdh) and D-lactate dehydrogenase (ldhD) yielded 5.1 mM DSS. The production of DSS increased to 6.53 mM through optimizing plasmid copy number. After optimizing the conditions, the yield of DSS reached 8.66 mM from strain 6. Finally, whole cell biotransformation using strain 6 in bioreactor yielded 19.47 mM DSS within 32h. These findings provide valuable insights for the scalable biosynthesis of pharmaceutically important compound of DSS from naturally available substrates of L-Tyrosine.

articles.title: No phenotypes in Ttc22 knockout mice
articles.abstract: The TTC22 gene encodes a protein containing seven tetratricopeptide repeats (TPRs), which mediate protein‒protein interactions as chaperones. We previously reported that the level of TTC22 transcript variant 1 (TTC22v1) was downregulated in human colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and that TTC22 upregulated m6A-mediated WTAP and SNAI1 expression via the TTC22‒RPL4 interaction and subsequently promoted COAD metastasis. Thus, a commercially available C57BL/6N mouse model in which the Ttc22 exon 2&3 encoding the TPR4 (equal to the human TTC22 TPR3) domain was knocked out via CRISPR-Cas9 was used to evaluate the contribution of Ttc22 to the development of mice and COAD. To determine the status of Ttc22 expression in Ttc22 knockout mice, we prepared a rabbit polyclonal antibody against the mouse Ttc22 protein, which could bind both wild-type Ttc22 and TPR4-deleted Ttc22 proteins overexpressed in HEK293T cells, as determined by Western blot analysis. Ttc22 proteins were detected in colon tissue samples from wild-type mice and Ttc22 hemi-knockout (Ttc22+/-) mice but not in those from fully Ttc22 knockout (Ttc22-/-) mice. Unfortunately, the long-term observation results demonstrated that Ttc22 knockout (KO, including Ttc22+/- or Ttc22-/-) did not affect the body weight, development, fertility, or spontaneous tumor incidence of male or female mice. No differences in the incidence of AOM/DSS-induced COAD were observed between these mouse groups, although Ttc22 deletion partially resulted in the upregulation of genes related to the host adaptive response to inflammation in the colon mucosa. In conclusion, no phenotypes were induced by Ttc22 inactivation in C57BL/6N mice.

articles.abstract: Nilanjan P. Choudhury left physics for a corporate software job, then returned to it for playwriting.

articles.title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach
articles.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M 3 .I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M 3 .I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family–dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M 3 .I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

articles.title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
articles.abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

articles.title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
articles.abstract: A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in Drosophila remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and Zeugodacus cucurbitae , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

articles.title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8+ T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
articles.abstract: CD8 + T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming d -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8 + T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8 + T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

articles.title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
articles.abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

articles.title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
articles.abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

articles.title: Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
articles.abstract: High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase: r = 0.66 to r = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

articles.title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS-mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
articles.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRAS G12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

articles.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
articles.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

articles.title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
articles.abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of O (10 to 100) m 2 /s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

articles.title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
articles.abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

articles.title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
articles.abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS 2 microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.

articles.title: Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous in rapidly adapting microbial populations
articles.abstract: In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of the Escherichia coli long-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry–based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

articles.title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
articles.abstract: Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa −1 , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

articles.title: Hemolymph pressure-mediated friction in the tarsus of the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria)
articles.abstract: The desert locust ( Schistocerca gregaria ) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

articles.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
articles.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

articles.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8+ T cell fates through the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 axis
articles.abstract: CD8 + T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8 + T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8 + T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8 + T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8 + T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

articles.title: In situ CAR-M engineered by liposomal mRNA nanomedicine remodels fibrotic microenvironment for ameliorating liver fibrosis
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)–incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages.
