Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)–CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

articles.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
articles.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor ( Ifnar1 −/− ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors ( Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

articles.title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
articles.abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

articles.title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
articles.abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

articles.title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
articles.abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5 , or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A , induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes ( Aurka , Aurkb , and Cenpa ). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

articles.title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions
articles.abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system’s multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

articles.title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
articles.abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

articles.title: NAD+ metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease
articles.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD + restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD + is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD + -PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD + nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

articles.title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
articles.abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

articles.title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth
articles.abstract: Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non–rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTS Vglut2 ), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTS Vglut2 projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTS Vglut2 projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTS Vglut2 terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVN CRH ), and inhibition of PVN CRH neurons or knockdown of Slc17a6 (encoding Vglut2), but not Crh , delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

articles.title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
articles.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

articles.title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
articles.abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

articles.title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

articles.title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
articles.abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

articles.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
articles.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys 514 , a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys 514 .

articles.title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
articles.abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662 , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

articles.title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
articles.abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

articles.title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells
articles.abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

articles.title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
articles.abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

articles.title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
articles.abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

articles.title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
articles.abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48 S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

articles.title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia
articles.abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2 -mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

articles.title: The Nematostella synaptonemal complex mediates divergent and sex-specific meiotic programs
articles.abstract: Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components sycp1 , syce2 , and sycp3 resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

articles.title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
articles.abstract: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

articles.title: An autonomous macrophage-nociceptor mechanosensory relay drives chronic visceral pain
articles.abstract: Visceral pain in ulcerative colitis is conventionally attributed to inflammatory cascades, though whether immune cells directly transduce mechanical cues into nociceptive signals remains unclear. Here, we show that the mechanosensitive channel Piezo1 in tissue-resident CX3CR1 + macrophages directly drives colitis-associated visceral hypersensitivity. Piezo1 triggered calcium influx and nuclear factor κB nuclear translocation that occupied the Ngf promoter to induce nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis. This macrophage-derived NGF remodeled and sensitized the peripheral terminals of TRPV1 + nociceptive afferents in neuroimmune units. Using a minimally inflammatory intracolonic zymosan model, we found that this Piezo1-NGF-TrkA axis functions as a direct mechanosensory relay largely independent of cytokine cascades. Genetic deletion of Piezo1 or Ngf in resident macrophages, or Ntrk1 in TRPV1 + neurons, abolished visceral hyperalgesia in both inflammatory and noninflammatory models. These findings reveal tissue-resident macrophages as autonomous mechanical sensors that establish a direct, parallel pain transmission pathway to sensory nerves during disease.

articles.title: ILC2-derived IL-9 promotes eosinophil-mediated antitumor activity
articles.abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) regulate tissue immunity, yet their roles in tumor control remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined analyses of human sequencing datasets with genetic ablation mouse models and adoptive transfer experiments to identify that glucocorticoid-induced tumor necrosis factor receptor (GITR) engagement on tumor-infiltrating group 2 ILCs (ILC2s) induced activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) and robust interleukin-9 (IL-9) production, exceeding the modest coinduction of IL-5 and IL-13. ILC2-derived IL-9 promoted intratumoral eosinophil accumulation by enhancing survival, tissue retention, and cytotoxicity through tumor-induced IL-9 receptor expression. Eosinophil ablation abolished GITR-mediated tumor control, whereas adoptive eosinophil transfer restored it. This IL-9–eosinophil pathway suppressed tumor growth in the absence of adaptive lymphocytes. In human datasets, IL-9 and eosinophil signatures were associated with favorable prognosis in melanoma and lung adenocarcinoma. These findings define an innate pathway linking ILC2s to eosinophil-mediated tumor immunity and support GITR agonism as a therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Competition for specialty training eases for UK graduates after law change
articles.abstract: Competition for NHS specialty training posts eased substantially for UK graduates in 2026, official data show.This follows new legislation to prioritise UK medical graduates over international medical graduates (IMGs) for posts in response to concerns about increasing competition.1The BMA, which pushed for the law change, welcomed the figures.The NHS figures show that overall there were 39 387 applicants for 10 682 posts across all training levels in 2026, or 3.69 per post.2But this fell to 1.86 per post for the priority applicant group—mostly UK graduates—who benefited from the Medical Training Prioritisation Act, which officially became law in March.Data show that applicants in the priority group—UK and Irish graduates and those from other European Economic Area (EEA) countries with which the UK has an agreement—accounted for around half of all applicants and applications to specialty training in 2026 (19 908 of 39 387).3Priority applicants filled 96% of all core training year...

articles.title: Ebola: Nigeria announces first Bundibugyo case, as numbers continue to rise in Kenya and DRC
articles.abstract: Nigeria has announced its first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), becoming the fifth country to be affected by an outbreak that has left thousands dead.Officials said that the patient is a woman who had travelled from Uganda. She began feeling unwell and sought care at a private clinic in Abuja on 11 October and was confirmed positive for BVD on 20 October.It is the first Ebola case in Nigeria in 12 years.The infected woman is currently in isolation and receiving care, said the World Health Organization, which added that investigations continue to establish the likely source of her infection and reconstruct her full travel and exposure history.1So far, 44 of her contacts have been identified and are now being monitored, the Nigerian Ministry of Health has said.Meanwhile Kenya recorded its first BVD infection earlier this month after a citizen travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through...

articles.title: Five AI tools for prostate cancer screening are recommended by NICE
articles.abstract: Five AI tools that can help identify prostate cancer “more accurately” on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans will be made available to doctors, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has announced.NICE has recommended that the technologies be used in the NHS to help detect prostate cancer on MRI while further evidence on their use and accuracy is generated. The tools “are designed to help radiologists by highlighting areas on a prostate MRI scan where cancer might be present,” it said.NICE concluded that the technologies “have the potential” to improve the accuracy and consistency of prostate MRI interpretation, particularly in settings without specialist expertise. But it added that further evidence was needed to understand how the tools would perform in routine NHS practice.Independent experts, while welcoming the announcement, said that the evidence on AI use must also consider how the algorithms could contribute to overdiagnosis.The technologies will be...

articles.title: Measles: “Stagnant” vaccine coverage has led to global resurgence, analysis finds
articles.abstract: Significant global progress towards eliminating measles has been lost since 2020 because of “stagnation” in global vaccine coverage, a new analysis suggests.1Researchers said that this had led to a resurgence in the disease and that “urgent action” was needed to restore routine immunisation.The study assessed measles incidence, mortality, disability adjusted life years, and vaccine coverage among children under 5 years of age across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023.The researchers found that, from 1990 to 2019, global measles incidence and mortality declined “substantially” by around 80% and 90%, respectively. This reflected “decades of progress” in routine immunisation, surveillance, and outbreak response, the researchers said.But the trajectory reversed after 2020, as incidence and mortality rebounded with 40% and 12% increases, respectively, from 2019 to 2023.The resurgence coincided with covid-19 related disruptions to immunisation programmes, health systems, and global health financing. By 2023 the study estimated 15.6 million measles cases...

articles.title: Obesity: “Unambitious” rollout of weight loss ȷab must speed up and double bariatric surgeries, government is told
articles.abstract: People with obesity are being failed by the government, MPs have said, as they demanded a radical upscale and overhaul of the treatment offered to improve care in England.The House of Commons Health and Social Care Committee’s report on obesity treatment called on ministers to accelerate the rollout of tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and double the number of bariatric surgeries being carried out.1MPs labelled the current phased approach to tirzepatide “unambitious” and said that the rollout was currently reaching a “woefully small number of people who could benefit from this life changing treatment.”The committee also warned of the alarming number of children with obesity and urged the government to ensure that they have the “specialised, holistic support they need.”Around one in three adults in England are obese, while two thirds have overweight or obesity. Meanwhile, 1 in 10 reception aged children have obesity.“Successive governments have failed to address the scale of the...

articles.title: What happens when there is no duty of care?
articles.abstract: The Court of Appeal has now settled the legal question arising from the tragic death of Sridharan Suresh: the General Medical Council (GMC) does not owe doctors an actionable common law duty of care when exercising its statutory fitness-to-practise functions.1 The judgment is legally important, but it should not be mistaken for an answer to the wider question raised by Suresh’s death.The question is not simply whether the GMC owes a legal duty of care; it is what responsibility a regulator should assume when it exercises powers capable of profoundly affecting the psychological wellbeing, professional identity, and future of the doctor being investigated.This distinction matters because the GMC itself recognises the potential harm. It has previously stated that “the impact of receiving a complaint can be great for doctors” and has introduced personalised contact, a single point of contact, changes to communications, and other measures intended to reduce that impact....

articles.title: [Articles] Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

articles.title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression
articles.abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group
articles.abstract: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC.MethodsMASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete.FindingsBetween Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24).…

articles.title: Proposed Mexican reform would set 60-day limit for cancer treatment
US EPA research and oversight on carcinogens are in disarray, critics contend
Genome-wide human T cell screens: barriers and design
articles.abstract: Liu et al. enabled genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screening of primary human T cells in vivo and identified P2RY8 and GNAS through complementary readouts. We discuss how context shapes perturbation effects, and how readouts guide prioritization, with implications for T cell engineering in solid tumors.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cells: towering ambitions, shaky foundations
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been a feature of stem cell research since the early 1990s. Despite long-standing questions concerning the identity, characteristics, physiological functions, and potential therapeutic uses of these cells, MSC studies are now published more frequently than those of any other stem cell type. Over the past decade, this increase in the MSC literature is attributable almost entirely to publications by scientists in China. Reviewing the history and present state of MSC research, we explore why this might be and propose steps that stakeholders in China and other countries might take to address what has become one of the more perplexing developments in contemporary stem cell research.

articles.title: Dependency grammar remains the simplest theory of grammar: a reply to Fujita
articles.abstract: In the original article [1], I claimed that dependency grammar is the simplest theory of grammar. All theories of grammar have rules for connecting words together to make larger units. In dependency grammar, these connections are directly between words. In phrase structure grammars, there is slightly more structure than in dependency grammar, consisting of nonterminal categories for the connected elements, such as the noun phrase and the verb phrase. I argued that these two alternatives are somewhat interchangeable.

articles.title: Evidence supports constituency-based syntax, movement, and unpronounced elements
articles.abstract: Gibson advocates dependency grammar [1], contrasting it with constituency-based accounts that posit movement and phonologically null (unpronounced) syntactic elements [2,3]. Dependency grammar represents sentence structure through word-to-word relations, whereas constituency-based accounts represent sentence structure by grouping words into larger hierarchical constituents. Movement accounts for cases in which a constituent appears in one position but is interpreted in another. For example, in ‘Who did you call?’, ‘Who’ appears sentence-initially but is interpreted as the object of ‘call’; this is analysed as movement from the object position to the sentence-initial position.

articles.title: A Foundation Model for Policy In-Context Longitudinal Causal Effect Estimation
articles.abstract: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Existing methods generally require data-specific nuisance-model fitting, and many are tailored to prespecified treatment sequences or prediction horizons, leading to time-consuming computation at deployment. We introduce *Policy In-Context Longitudinal causal Effect estimation with Prior-data Fitted Networks* (**PICLE-PFN**), the first foundation model for longitudinal causal effect estimation that supports *dynamic* treatment policies. PICLE-PFN represents target policies through in-context history-decision demonstrations, providing a unified interface for a broad class of treatment policies. Pretrained over synthetic data sampled from longitudinal structural causal models, PICLE-PFN amortizes causal effect estimation across datasets, policies, and horizons. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.

articles.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
articles.abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .

articles.title: Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding for Mixed Natural Language and Structured Symbolic Corpora
articles.abstract: Modern language models rely on subwording tokenization to define the discrete units of input processing, typically using methods like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) that treat whitespace as a fixed semantic boundary. This design is inherently limited, as many meaningful concepts---including multiword expressions and the structured environments of formal languages like LaTeX---frequently span across whitespaces. While recent superword tokenization methods attempt to address this by relaxing whitespace constraints, they often rely on greedy frequency-driven merging that fails to account for token length or the specific needs of underrepresented domain-specific languages. In this paper, we introduce Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding (AdaBPE), a new tokenization method that leverages an adaptive frequent-pattern mining approach. AdaBPE features a twofold dynamicity: it adapts minimum frequency thresholds based on both the length of a candidate token, to prevent favoring frequent short patterns, and its type, to distinguish between general and formal language patterns, using LaTeX as case in point. This allows the model to efficiently allocate vocabulary capacity to domain-specific notations, such as LaTeX, even when they represent a small fraction of the training data. We evaluate AdaBPE across five datasets spanning LaTeX and natural language, showing consistent gains in encoding efficiency and downstream language-model performance on domain-specific content without compromising general-language performance.

articles.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search
articles.abstract: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. In this work, we address these limitations by introducing Layer-wise Error Modeling Search (LEMS) and KFAC-SVD. LEMS advances rank allocation by introducing a layer-wise error surrogate that integrates local and global layer importance alongside a propagation bias, enabling effective global rank allocation via an ILP formulation. KFAC-SVD improves decomposition quality by utilizing token-wise statistics, mitigating the rank deficiency observed in prior Fisher-based SVD approaches. Across Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 model families, we show that LEMS consistently outperforms existing search strategies, delivering significant zero-shot accuracy gains of up to 4.8 p.p. that generalize to model sizes of 70B parameters, while KFAC-SVD achieves an average perplexity improvement of 15%. Project page and code: https://lems-svd.github.io

articles.title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
articles.abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.

articles.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning
articles.abstract: Replay-based Continual Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by keeping a buffer of past samples, making buffer composition critical under a fixed memory budget. Recent coreset-based replay methods improve buffer quality using model-derived gradients, losses, or auxiliary optimization, but incur substantial computational overhead as memory is repeatedly updated. We propose CARES, a continual model-optimization-free approach for buffer construction that instead exploits the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space using class-aware, density-weighted coverage. We evaluate CARES across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings. On Tiny-ImageNet, CARES is 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than existing coreset-based selectors. Although CARES achieves this speedup using no training signal from the continual learner, it ranks among the state of the art across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 7.58 percentage points under class imbalance while also attaining higher average accuracy on Tiny-ImageNet. Code will be released upon publication

articles.title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
articles.abstract: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $Δ^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.

articles.title: Communicating with the Entire Population: Machine Translation of Emergency Alerts and Warnings
articles.abstract: It is essential that we communicate with the entirety of an affected population during a crisis, including those who do not speak a region's dominant language(s). Commercial Translation tools offer a tempting solution to broaden access and can provide a lifeline when no other resources are available. However, Emergency response managers often operate in the dark regarding the quality and adequacy of these automated outputs. In this paper, we conduct a nationwide survey of emergency managers to understand their current workflows, perspectives, and operational challenges. We then evaluate commercial translation tools against these needs, shedding light on their utility and offering practical guidance on how and when these tools can be safely used in emergency response.

articles.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
articles.abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

articles.title: Do "True" and "False" Add Up to One? Complement Consistency in LLM-Agent Opinion Simulations
articles.abstract: In LLM-agent opinion simulations, each agent reports the probability that a claim is true after seeing its own previous probability and the probabilities reported by its neighbors, and that number becomes its state in the next round. If the number describes the agent's position rather than the sentence it was shown, then rewriting the claim as its complement and replacing every probability p with 1 - p should return the complementary answer, so the two reports should sum to one. We test this with three small open models: Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-3-4B. On 2,304 agent states taken from a running network simulation, Qwen's paired reports sum to 1.18 on average, and on 48 real fact-checking claims from AVeriTeC they again exceed one. A controlled benchmark of 24 worlds, each with exactly two possible outcomes, shows the same failure in all three models. The discrepancy is two to ten times larger than the change produced by a same-meaning paraphrase, and it persists under repeated sampling and across peer group sizes and report strengths. When the reports are fed back into two populations that start from complementary states, the populations do not remain mirror images: their divergence is positive after five rounds for every model. Averaging each answer with the complement of its paired answer restores consistency by construction and lowers Brier loss averaged over the two wordings, but at the final round it beats the better of the two original wordings for only one of the three models. A schedule-by-targeting experiment on the same model gives a small, stable interaction because such sweeps keep the claim wording fixed. Consistency under rewording therefore needs its own test before simulated probabilities are read as beliefs

articles.title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents
articles.abstract: Hospitals regularly buy software that clinicians and patients depend on. Because these purchases are costly, hard to reverse and can affect patient care, buyers look for evidence of which peer institutions already use a product and which systems it connects to. This evidence is public but scattered across vendor websites, press releases and third-party pages. Language-model agents can now collect it at low cost, but the correctness of the extracted claims is difficult to establish, and a wrongly listed customer can mislead buyers and misrepresent an organisation. We present a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph of customer and integration relations from the open web under one rule: every edge must be supported by a verbatim quote from its source page. Pages come from a deterministic crawl of each vendor's site and a budgeted ReAct agent that searches the rest of the web. A permissive extractor proposes relations with quotes, and a layered grounding stage decides which to keep, using a referent step that reads the whole page when a quote names only one side, deterministic checks, and a panel of five model calls voting on nine criteria. On 61 vendors, the pipeline reaches 0.94 precision and 0.71 recall against a page-level key covering the 6,428 candidate relations proposed by its extractor, whose verdicts were drafted by one model and re-checked with a second. Against the golden reference, the marketplace's own curated list, it scores lower, but 89% of the relations it keeps that the reference lacks are stated on a page. A confidence score built from the panel's votes keeps more correct relations than the fixed rule at the same precision, and reaches 0.90 precision at 0.90 recall. We also discuss how narrow, bounded model calls, string-matched evidence and voting address long-context degradation and run-to-run variance.

articles.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
articles.abstract: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.

articles.title: From Deliberately Constructed Systemic Representations of the World of Activity to Dialogue: A Five-Level Communication Architecture for Strong Language-Based ASI
articles.abstract: This paper proposes a five-level organization of message formation and understanding within thinking and activity in which ASI participates. Its central thesis is that a language model's context is fundamentally incapable of presenting the foundations of utterance formation for examination and verification. These foundations are established in advance by acquired schemas, systemic representations of the world of activity, and connections accepted as true within them. Neither context nor trained LLM weights, in themselves, attest to the presence of deliberately constructed systemic representations. The five levels distinguish systemic representations of the world of activity, a particular situation cut out from those representations, its narrative description, the full sense of a message, and text. A situation's schema-model is not identical to a story about it. A recipient reconstructs the full sense from an abbreviated text through jointly constructed and agreed-upon representations and joint activity. Reverse work proceeds from the full sense through an extended description and the situation's schema-model to the reconstruction of systemic foundations. The theoretical foundations draw on the systems methodology of G. P. Shchedrovitskiy, the structural differential of A. Korzybski, and the Meaning-Text theory of I. A. Mel'chuk. The contribution is a specific systemic-activity organization of content for examining and adjusting message foundations and controlling the consequences of their transformation. Further research concerns large graphical models of activity on reconstructible systemic foundations, distinct from text generation from context.

articles.title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond
articles.abstract: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.

articles.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
articles.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.

articles.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
articles.abstract: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

articles.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
articles.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.

articles.title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
articles.abstract: Fine-tuning on datasets of unknown origin can create a backdoor in the trained model when the data includes poisoned examples. Difficult to localise and remove, backdoors can persist through safety training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods capture the full parameter changes introduced during training, they are not easily interpretable. We present the full method of TopKLoRA, extending the preliminary proposal of Masiak et al. (2025), an interpretable-by-design LoRA variant in which only the $k$ largest adapter latents are active at each token. Unlike SAEs, TopKLoRA is trained purely on downstream loss, where optimisation pressure incentivises learning functionally causal latents. We demonstrate this sparse LoRA adapter in a sleeper-agent backdoor case study where we create model organisms by fine-tuning gemma-2-2b, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-7B on a poisoned instruction-following dataset. For each organism, we identify and ablate a circuit that is both necessary and sufficient to implement the backdoor. Furthermore, our new fine-tuning method produces sparse circuits that are up to an order of magnitude smaller than a dense LoRA baseline, allowing surgical ablation of the malicious capability without sacrificing instruction-following performance. Finally, we propose a technique to construct model organisms with localised circuits using TopKLoRA latents and gradient-routing, which we use to validate the findings of our circuit search algorithm. We consider these findings as a step toward interpretable-by-design architectures that provide faithful units of analysis without compromising model performance. We share our code: https://github.com/interpretable-finetuning/TopKLoRA.

articles.title: J-Comm: Jacobian-Guided Latent Communication between LLM Agents
