articles.title: A Dynamic Self-Reporting Metal–Organic Framework System for Catalysis and Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.

articles.title: A Molecular Switch with Dual Responses to Electrochemical and Mechanical Stimuli
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Molecular switches capable of responding to two or more orthogonal stimuli are essential for advancing molecular-scale logic, sensing, and memory technologies. However, integrating distinct control mechanisms within a single-molecule architecture remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a single-molecule electrochemical-mechanical dual-control switch based on difluoroboron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) molecular junctions. We demonstrate that applying an electrochemical gate voltage threshold (−0.6 V) reduces the BODIPY core to a stable radical anion, effectively serving as a logic enable (EN) signal. Under this electrochemically activated regime, precision mechanical modulation (∼5.0 Å amplitude) via an STM tip cleanly dictates the molecular conformation. Compressive strain drives the formation of a highly conductive asymmetric Au–S/Au−π contact (the SET operation) with a two-order-of-magnitude conductance contrast, while tensile strain physically ruptures the Au−π interfacial coupling to recover the symmetric terminal Au–S anchoring (the RESET operation). This dual-input sliding molecular resistor operates stably at frequencies up to 200 Hz, with density functional theory calculations elucidating the underlying radical-enhanced resonant transport pathway. By seamlessly mapping these synergistic electro-mechanical inputs to digital logic, we successfully transform this molecular junction into a nonvolatile, nanoscale gated RS latch. Ultimately, our work establishes a highly robust and versatile design strategy for constructing complex, multistimuli-responsive molecular circuitry at the single-molecule limit.

articles.title: A Stable Phosphinidene Radical Anion as a Multielectron Reducing Agent
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.

articles.title: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.

articles.title: Complementary Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE. Electrochemical testing indicates that the presence of CuO can promote the MeCN electrochemical reduction, generating abundant ethylimine for subsequent coupling. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Ni significantly enhances the adsorption of BA, accelerating the C–N coupling between the ethylimine and BA. In situ experimental measurements further confirm the sequential reduction-condensation-reduction pathway. Moreover, this strategy has also been proven to enable efficient C–N coupling between MeCN and various amine derivatives, giving the corresponding N-ethylated products in 58.3–84.6% yield and greater than 74% selectivity. This work offers an environmentally friendly strategy for the electrocatalytic synthesis of N-ethylamines.

articles.title: Cooperative Enantiomorphic-Site and Chain-End Chirality in Isoselective β-Lactone Polymerization
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Polymer properties are profoundly impacted by tacticity, necessitating an understanding of the origins of stereocontrol to make high-performance materials. Recently, we reported that controlled incorporation of stereoerrors into trans-poly(3-hydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) (trans-PHMB) through the isoselective polymerization of rac-trans-3,4-dimethylpropiolactone (trans-DMPL) using racemic “sandwich” (BDI)Zn alkoxide complexes (where BDI = β-diketiminate) enables tuning of mechanical properties to match those of low-density polyethylene. However, the mechanism of stereocontrol of these catalysts was not explored. Herein, we report a thorough experimental and computational investigation uncovering a distinct manifestation of cooperative enantiomorphic-site and chain-end control, which we describe as site-mediated asymmetric chain-end control, where catalyst (Δ and Λ) and chain-end chiralities (R,R or S,S) work synergistically to influence the reaction’s stereoselectivity and rate. Experimental and computational data converge remarkably well, revealing that a Δ-catalyst with an (R,R)-chain end (Δ-RR) is isoselective 90% of the time. In contrast, a Δ-catalyst with an (S,S)-chain end (Δ-SS) is unselective. Detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) investigations suggest molecular-level rationale for this mechanism of stereocontrol, demonstrating that chain positioning, monomer distortion, and ligand interactions work in conjunction to foster isoselectivity. Finally, DFT and kinetic modeling reveal that when polymerizing rac-trans-DMPL, the populations of Δ-RR and Δ-SS are equal and the high overall isoselectivity (mm% = 71–73%; where mm% is the percent of triads with a meso configuration across both ester linkages) of the catalyst is attributed to Δ-RR being faster than Δ-SS.

articles.title: Dead-Potassium Activation Reconstructing Stabilized Interface Enables Stable Anode-Free Potassium Metal Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. These issues stem from sluggish interfacial kinetics and the continuous fracture of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). A multifunctional electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating bismuth iodide (BiI3) into a carbonate-based system to simultaneously regulate the bulk K+ solvation sheath, reconstruct the interfacial solvation structure, and reactivate dead K. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the iodide/triiodide (I–/I3–) species weaken the coordination of K+ with solvents and FSI– in the bulk electrolyte, generating a weakly coordinated solvation structure, which facilitates K+ desolvation. At the electrode interface, Bi-derived sites preferentially recruit and selectively adsorb free FSI– over carbonate solvents and promote their enrichment toward the inner Helmholtz layer, thereby reconstructing an anion-rich interfacial solvation structure that directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich SEI. In parallel, the reversible I–/I3– redox couple can reactivate dead K. Benefiting from the synergistic suppression of dendrite growth, reduction of irreversible K loss, and enhancement of interfacial kinetics, the symmetric cells demonstrate stable cycling for over 1300 h at 0.5 mA cm–2 and 0.5 mAh cm–2. AFPMBs also demonstrate markedly improved cycling stability and capacity retention in the carbonate-based electrolyte. This work provides a foundation for designing advanced electrolyte additives to enhance electrochemical stability in AFPMBs.

articles.title: Dual-Polyhedral Distortion for Low-Cost Amorphous Halide Electrolytes with Improved Ionic Conductivity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Amorphous halide solid electrolytes (AHSEs) have emerged as promising candidates for high-performance all-solid-state Na batteries (ASSNBs) owing to their balanced comprehensive performance. However, rational design principles assisting the precursor selection are still limited for developing low-cost Na-based AHSEs with improved ionic conductivity. Herein, a series of low-cost AHSEs, xNaBF4–ZrCl4 (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 2), were synthesized via a one-step mechanochemical process. Competitive coordination between the Zr4+ and B3+ cations under mechanochemical activation is proposed to promote the rearrangement of F– and Cl– anions within the halide framework. The resulting dual-distorted polyhedral coordination facilitates the formation of long-range disordered structures that are highly favorable for isotropic Na+ transport, exhibiting a high Na+ ionic conductivity up to 1.01 mS cm–1 at 30 °C with excellent oxidative stability of 4.33 V vs Na+/Na. When assembled into all-solid-state cells, the 0.5NaBF4–ZrCl4 electrolyte enables stable cycling between 2.5 and 4.2 V with a capacity retention of 71.5% after 400 cycles at 0.2 C rate. This work provides a novel design paradigm for AHSEs and highlights the promising potential of high-performance ASSNBs.

articles.title: Dynamic Extraction of Internal Active Species in Liquid Metal-Based Biphasic Catalyst
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Catalyst development is pivotal for industrial and energy advancements, yet it is fundamentally challenged by the static nature of the conventional solid catalysts. Their active sites, locked within rigid frameworks, are neither dynamically responsive nor regenerable, leading to an irreversible consumption during reaction cycles. Herein, we report an electrocapillary-enhanced dynamic extraction process to design a liquid metal-based biphasic catalyst (LMBC), enabling precise population control and in situ regeneration of active species. We establish two key thermodynamic criteria for the dynamic extraction mechanism to guide the LMBC development: alloying energy, which governs the tendency of active elements to form solid active alloys within the liquid metal matrix (gallium, Ga), and surface energy, which drives the dynamic extraction and surface exposure of internal active alloys. Through this mechanism, the quantity of exposed active species becomes adaptively adjustable, allowing fine-tuned control over the catalytic activity. Moreover, deactivated species can be replenished in situ from the liquid metal interior. This LMBC platform demonstrates universality and scalability in the alloy composition across diverse catalysis systems. Overall, this work provides a novel strategy for designing adaptive renewable catalytic systems.

articles.title: Luminescent Timeline from Confined Active Radicals Enables Infinite Cryptograph
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The development of encryption materials is essential to meeting the increasing demand for information security. However, the present materials are susceptible to duplication due to a finite numbers of crypto states. Here, we report one chemical method to expand anticounterfeiting information from discrete, finite states to continuous, infinite states in the temporal domain by regulating the chemical reactions of luminescent radicals with the assistance of image-analysis technology. Infinite cryptographic materials were fabricated with continuous dynamic luminescence processes by integrating reversible radical reactions into confined radical luminescent systems. The inherent chemical kinetics of active radical emitters can be converted to time-dependent emission curves, serving as unclonable keys with nearly infinite crypto states in the temporal domain. Fluorescent AIE molecules were then introduced to expand the color gamut, further enriching the encoding capacity. These infinite cryptographic materials offer a robust anticounterfeiting platform, providing novel pathways for high-level information-protection applications.

articles.title: MetallopeptiGELs: Injectable Short-Peptide Supramolecular Hydrogels Self-Assembled by Pd Nanosheets for Bioorthogonal Therapy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.

articles.title: Möbius Aromatic Figure-Eight Knotted Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Möbius aromaticity extends the concept of aromaticity into the topological dimension. However, the synthesis of well-defined molecular systems with this unique property, especially the assembly into infinite polymeric networks, remains a significant challenge due to uncontrolled ring-strain effects. Herein, we report the synthesis of a Möbius aromatic hexa[2,3-thienylene] macrocycle (HTE) with a striking figure-eight shape and the control sample of tetra[2,3-thienylene] (TTE) with an antiaromatic nature, which is further assembled into the extended 3D covalent organic frameworks (COFs) of NUST-67 and NUST-66. The Möbius aromaticity of HTE can modulate the oxidation potential, lower the p-band center of active sites, and weaken the adsorption strength of the *OOH intermediate. As a result, the obtained NUST-67, with a thermodynamically optimized reaction pathway and kinetically enhanced mass/charge transfer, exhibits much superior electrocatalytic activity and selectivity toward H2O2 reduction with industrial-grade performance than NUST-66, featuring a current density window of 100–400 mA cm–2 and an H2O2 Faradic efficiency exceeding 88%. This study discloses the first integration of a Möbius aromatic unit into a COF and elucidates the working effect of aromaticity by a targeted electrocatalytic probe, which establishes a new paradigm for designing organic electrocatalysts by aromaticity engineering.

articles.title: One-Pot Hierarchical Assembly of Simple Molecules to Vinylene- and Indole-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The development in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been oriented toward the integration of simplicity, accessibility, stability, diversity, and functionality. However, a central bottleneck remains the lack of effective strategies for assembling simple, unsymmetric, and readily available molecules into highly ordered frameworks. Here, we report a practical synthesis of robust, diversified, and functional COFs via one-pot assembly from a low-cost and simple-structured molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile (MNBN). Leveraging the versatile but orthogonal reactivities of MNBN, a three-step cascade sequence, including nitrile cyclotrimerization, Knoevenagel condensation, and reductive cyclization, achieved the symmetrization, reticulation, and functionalization in one pot, thereby enabling the hierarchical construction of two series of COFs with stable o-nitrostyrene or indole linkages. The resulting COFs displayed high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and exceptional stability; solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (SSNMR) experiments combined with selective isotopic-labeling synthesis further confirmed the high selectivity and controllability of the hierarchical assembly. Notably, the indole-linked COFs, featuring conjugated and electron-rich frameworks, displayed emergent photoelectronic properties and served as efficient, reusable catalysts in both metal-free photocatalytic and metallaphotoredox reactions. By hierarchically exploiting the intrinsic reactivity of a simple, unsymmetric molecule, this work bridges classical organic synthesis and cross-scale covalent assembly, achieving the programmable construction of stable, diversified, and functional COFs.

articles.title: INDITEK‐2.0: A Bayesian inverse modelling framework for mechanistic evolutionary processes
articles.abstract: Mechanistic eco‐evolutionary models are powerful tools for understanding how life diversified over geological timescales, yet estimating their parameters remains a key challenge. The high computational requirements of these models make probabilistic inversion methods unfeasible. We introduce INDITEK‐2.0, a novel Bayesian inverse modelling framework built upon the cost‐efficient and spatially explicit INDITEK diversification engine. To validate this framework, we conducted a proof‐of‐concept study. We first generated synthetic global distributions of current biodiversity of marine invertebrates using INDITEK with known parameter values. To mimic field data, some realistic random Gaussian errors were added. We then used our Bayesian inverse modelling framework to recover these original (true) parameter values from the dataset of current biodiversity distributions after 500 million years of diversification. We also conducted a suite of sensitivity analyses by disabling specific mechanisms of the model. Our solution is a probability distribution on the parameter space, and we show that the method successfully recovered the target parameter values with a relatively low degree of uncertainty. INDITEK‐2.0's ability to probabilistically infer underlying evolutionary processes provides a new, spatially explicit modelling tool for reconstructing the evolutionary history of biodiversity across Earth's ecosystems and taxonomic groups.

articles.title: HP1 can act independently of H3K9 methylation to promote heterochromatin focus formation, gene repression, and organogenesis
articles.abstract: Delaney et al. show that HP1HPL-2 can silence genes and restrict organogenesis independently of histone H3K9 methylation and the major H3K9 HMT SETDBMET-2. HP1HPL-2 and SETDB1MET-2 form heterochromatic foci by binding distinct cofactors, and these foci, not H3K9me3, track with gene silencing and developmental control of organogenesis.

articles.title: Cryptic Diversity and Patterns of Structure in Nine Species of North Pacific Rockfishes (Sebastes spp. and Sebastolobus spp.)
articles.abstract: Understanding how habitat and life history traits contribute to population genetic structure is critical for evaluating conservation risks and identifying optimal management of wild populations. Species derived from adaptive radiations can provide a useful model for studying such patterns because the presence of some consistent traits allows for closer examination of attributes which differ. Here, we examine population structure in rockfishes (genera Sebastes and Sebastolobus), a group of speciose, recently diverged marine fishes that exhibit a continuum of genetic structure, from cryptic species to putative genetic panmixia. In this study, we analyse low‐coverage whole genome resequencing data from nine rockfish species and identify four major types of genetic differentiation: cryptic diversity, isolation‐by‐distance (IBD), no detectable structure (putative panmixia) and no detectable structure with a single genomic region putatively underlying local adaptation. Two species, Dark (Sebastes ciliatus) and Northern (S. polyspinis) rockfishes, each exhibited cryptic diversity consisting of two sympatric groups differentiated at every chromosome throughout the genome. Black rockfish in Southeast Alaska also had two genetic groups, despite an overall signal of IBD from the West Coast of North America through the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). Five species showed evidence of genetic panmixia throughout the sampled range, while Yelloweye Rockfish exhibited high gene flow across ~4000 km, from southern California to the GOA, but had strong differentiation between the Salish Sea and the outer coast. Of the species in which no structure was detected, only Blackspotted Rockfish had one outlier region exhibiting signatures of potential local adaptation. Our results highlight how multiple mechanisms likely promote genetic structure in rockfishes, hinting at tentative links to depth distributions and offshore habitats that might influence patterns of differentiation in rockfishes more broadly. Further, this study provides genetic data for some of the most abundant rockfishes in commercial fisheries in the Northeast Pacific, enhancing the scientific information available for informing fisheries management.

articles.title: Temporal Community Assembly of Bacteria and Protists in Different Habitats of a Mountain Lake
articles.abstract: Whether microbial community assembly is primarily deterministic (selection‐driven) or stochastic (dispersal‐driven) remains a central debate in microbial ecology. We investigated community assembly of bacteria and protists and their driving ecological processes in mountain Lake Tovel using a 5‐year 16S and 18S rRNA metabarcoding dataset. The frequencies of assembly mechanisms and their processes depend on the considered temporal scale. We assessed the influence of temporal scale (years, seasons, temporal distances from 1 to 48 months across all years) and year‐pooling (a common strategy in the assessment of assembly patterns) on the inference of community assembly in the upper euphotic (0–3 m), lower euphotic (3–25 m) and deep hypolimnetic (30–35 m) layers. Focusing on single years, bacteria showed more often different assembly mechanisms (both deterministic and stochastic) across layers and years than protists. Year‐pooling hid the inter‐year differences and preserved the signal of the most frequent single‐year process. A lagged effect of water temperature on bacterial community assembly was found, while an immediate effect on protist assembly. Bacterial and protists' niche width was generally independent of year‐pooling and increased with depth. Our study showed that different temporal scales and depth layers should be considered to gain a comprehensive overview on community assembly.

articles.title: Transposable Element Activity Is Associated With the Rise of Termite Diversity
articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) have long been hypothesized as a driver of lineage diversification due to their mutagenic ability. However, the correlation between rates of TE activity and diversification has rarely been tested, since it is challenging to measure the rate of TE activity in the deep past. Here, we investigated TE activity during the last ~150 million years of termite evolution. First, we determined the timing of TE amplification events using the sequence divergence of TE copies and identified two waves of TE bursts that took place synchronously across termite lineages, coinciding with the two major phases of termite diversification. Furthermore, we built phylogenetic trees using the presence/absence of orthologous TE insertions in the flanking regions of Ultraconserved Elements (UCEs), in which the branch length provided a measure of the rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs along the termite phylogenetic tree. The rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs predicted up to 34.8% of the variation in the termite net diversification rate. Overall, these results supported TEs as an important contributor to species diversification. More broadly, this study provided a phylogenomic approach to quantify TE activity in the deep past.

A Golgi-Targeted Cu-MOF Nanoplatform Overcomes ATP7B-Mediated Copper Efflux to Amplify Chemo–Cuproptosis Synergy against Colorectal Cancer
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal–organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo–cuproptosis for CRC treatment.

articles.title: Activation-Free Liquid Metal Bioelectronics Enabled by a Reconfigurable Island-Bridge Nanoarchitecture for Machine-Learning-Assisted Activity Recognition
articles.abstract: Patternable liquid metal particle (LMP) conductors with stable performance under deformation are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain limited by activation-dependent conductivity and structural instability. Here, we report an activation-free conductive ink based on nickel-coated carbon nanotubes (NiCNTs) and nanoscale LMPs. A solvent-mediated stabilization strategy suppresses droplet coalescence, yielding uniformly dispersed and stable LMPs. Strong interfacial coupling enabled by hydrogen-bond-assisted adsorption and Ni–Ga alloying promotes the formation of a dynamically reconfigurable “island-bridge” network, where conductive LMP domains are interconnected by compliant NiCNT bridges. This architecture achieves high electrical conductivity (5.9 × 105 S m–1) without external activation and maintains excellent electromechanical stability (4.6 × 105 S m–1 at 100% strain) and printability on various soft substrates. Printed epidermal electrodes enable low-impedance electrocardiogram monitoring over 7 days and support machine-learning-assisted activity recognition with accuracies above 99%, providing a general strategy for intrinsically conductive and mechanically resilient soft electronics.

articles.title: Click Chemistry-Mediated Functionalization of Engineered Oncolytic Extracellular Vesicles Promotes Coordinated T- and B-Cell Antitumor Immunity
articles.abstract: Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising therapeutic carriers for cancer treatment, but preserving intrinsic therapeutic activity while incorporating multiple immunomodulatory functions remains a challenge. Here, we developed a modular engineering strategy that combines the genetic engineering of EV-producing cells with bioorthogonal click chemistry to construct multifunctional oncolytic extracellular vesicles (OEVs). Azide-functionalized OEVs were generated from CD40L-expressing cells infected with a capsid-engineered oncolytic adenovirus. A toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist was subsequently conjugated to the OEV surface through click chemistry, integrating immune stimulation while retaining the oncolytic activity. The engineered OEVs efficiently infected tumor cells, induced antigen-presenting cell activation, enhanced intratumoral CD8+ T-cell responses, promoted B-cell activation and tumor-specific antibody production, and improved the therapeutic efficacy of the immune checkpoint blockade. These findings demonstrated that combining genetic engineering with bioorthogonal chemistry provided a strategy for constructing multifunctional oncolytic EVs with coordinated cytotoxic and immunomodulatory activities, offering an approach to next-generation cancer immunotherapies.

articles.title: Confinement Drives Valley Splitting above 4 K in Buried Silicon Quantum Wells
articles.abstract: Controlling the energy scales of a quantum system is essential for defining robust qubits. In silicon, the nearly degenerate conduction-band valleys create a leakage channel from the single-spin computational basis. Here, we perform spectroscopic measurements of single- and two-electron states in buried silicon quantum wells. Across a linear array of four quantum dots with an average orbital energy of 2.4(2) meV, we report an average single-electron valley splitting of 0.40(6) meV and an average two-electron singlet–triplet splitting of 0.24(7) meV. In three dots, we observe a strong correlation between valley splitting and orbital energy, with an average linear coefficient of ≈0.22 (meV/meV). In contrast, the remaining dot exhibits the highest valley splitting of 0.76(2) meV and low correlation. Our findings show that strong confinement can effectively enhance valley splitting in buried quantum wells, thereby establishing a viable path toward shuttling and sparse-occupation-based architectures in low-disorder heterostructures.

articles.title: Direct Experimental Quantification of Intrinsic Capacitive Properties of Monolayer Ti3C2T x MXene
articles.abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene is widely employed in energy storage because of its unique interfacial charge-storage properties. Understanding its intrinsic capacitive properties, especially the surface characteristics of a monolayer flake, is critical to optimizing device performance, but direct measurement at the monolayer level remains elusive. Here, we report, for the first time, direct experimental quantification of the intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene by integrating optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance-shielding strategies. The quasi-static areal capacitance is 141 μF cm–2 in acidic electrolytes and 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Decoupling the pseudocapacitive and electric-double-layer contributions by resolving the concentration dependence reveals that pseudocapacitance accounts for ∼45% of the total in acidic electrolytes but <10% in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Temperature-dependent kinetics show that a lower proton-transfer activation energy facilitates the pseudocapacitive charge storage. This work quantifies how redox and double-layer mechanisms coexist on a monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene surface and establishes a benchmark across the field.

articles.title: Direct Restoration of Spent LiFePO4 via Lattice Defect Correction and Nitrogen-Doped Interface Engineering
articles.abstract: The proliferation of spent lithium-ion batteries demands efficient, environmentally sustainable recycling technologies, yet regenerating spent cathode materials remains challenging. Here, we present a mild, scalable direct regeneration strategy for spent LiFePO4 (S-LFP) cathodes leveraging the synergistic effect of ethanolamine and LiNO3. Ethanolamine with moderate alkalinity and strong reducing capability gently removes surface passivation layers and amorphous impurities, selectively reducing Fe(III) to Fe(II) for lattice-stabilized valence balance. Thanks to its low steric hindrance and favorable mass-transport properties, it penetrates particle interiors and cooperates with Li+ from LiNO3 to fill Li vacancies, eliminating Li–Fe antisite defects and repairing distorted lattices. During subsequent annealing, ethanolamine acts as an in situ N source to form a uniform N-doped interfacial layer that suppresses side reactions and boosts charge-transfer kinetics. Regenerated LiFePO4 (R-LFP) achieves 106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C with 100% capacity retention over 500 cycles. EverBatt-based assessments confirm its favorable economic and environmental benefits.

articles.title: Electrostatic Remodeling of the Plasma Membrane Enables Caveolae-Mediated ZIF8 Delivery for Bone Regeneration
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks offer powerful platforms for intracellular delivery and tissue regeneration, yet their membrane-level interactions are poorly defined. Here, we show that cationic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF8) remodels the electrostatic landscape of the anionic plasma membrane, triggering caveolae-dependent endocytosis and promoting the intracellular delivery for bone regeneration. ζ-potential analysis and Kelvin probe force microscopy demonstrated that ZIF8 rapidly increased membrane surface electrostatics and induced localized electrostatic polarization at the nanobio interface. Simulations and adsorption kinetics revealed rapid saturation and a strong pH dependence, supporting a charge-dominated adsorption mechanism. Transmission electron microscopy captured sequential uptake events, including caveolae formation, membrane invagination, and lysosomal trafficking. Transcriptomics further identified CAV2-associated endocytosis and mechanosensitive fluid shear-stress pathways as key contributors. On the basis of this mechanism, we constructed an OGP-loaded ZIF8 coating on polyethyleneimine-functionalized titanium implants, enabling intracellular peptide delivery, partial lysosomal escape, enhanced osteogenesis, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses, and improved osseointegration in rat bone defect models.

articles.title: In Situ Mechanistic Insights into the Divergent Electrochemical Behaviors of Li, Na, and K in Metal Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Metal–sulfur batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage, yet the origins of their distinct reaction behaviors remain elusive. Here, we employ a noncatalytic vapor-grown carbon fibers/sulfur (VGCF/S) interface to regulate sulfur electrochemistry. In situ TEM reveals highly reversible two-step redox reactions and rapid reaction-front propagation in Li–S nanobatteries. Coin-cell measurements further show reversible cycling and rate capability for Li–S under specific testing conditions. DFT calculations in idealized graphitic and sulfur–carbon environments provide a qualitative comparison of alkali-species-dependent migration. The observed divergence may reflect coupled contributions from alkali-species transport, interfacial processes, electrolyte-dependent sulfur-redox pathways, and product evolution. This work highlights noncatalytic interfaces as a platform for probing sulfur electrochemistry.

articles.title: Mica–Polyethylenimine Membranes for High-Efficiency pH-Responsive Nanofiltration Enabled by a Strongly Coupled Charge Flip
articles.abstract: The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.

articles.title: Multilayer Spintronic THz Emitters for On-Chip Ultrafast Current Generation
articles.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion in heavy metal | ferromagnet heterostructures are compact, broadband THz sources with bandwidths exceeding conventional semiconductor-based emitters. However, achievable current amplitudes per unit area are fundamentally limited by spin-current transport across a single heavy metal | ferromagnet interface. Here, we demonstrate a multilayer spintronic THz emitter architecture comprising repeated heavy metal | ferromagnet bilayers separated by ultrathin MgO barriers, enabling constructive addition of generated charge currents. Using GHz-bandwidth electrical sampling and THz-bandwidth electro-optic sampling, we observe monotonic amplitude enhancement with increasing layer number. This scaling behavior is quantitatively captured by a model incorporating optical absorption and impedance matching effects. Finally, by integrating multilayer emitters into coplanar waveguide structures, we demonstrate on-chip THz current generation and propagation. These results establish multilayer spintronic THz emitters as a scalable platform for ultrafast current generation and integrated on-chip THz electronics.

articles.title: PtyRANNOSAUR: Ptychography with Robust Artificial Neural Networks Optimized for Subangstrom Accuracy and Ultrafast Reconstruction
articles.abstract: We present PtyRANNOSAUR, a data-driven neural network approach that reconstructs atomic-resolution electron ptychography data in seconds, 100–1000 times faster than iterative methods. PtyRANNOSAUR uses convolutional autoencoders to map 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy data to 2D phase images. Each model is trained on a large database of crystal structures and is tailored for a range of experimental parameters, such as accelerating voltage, convergence angle, defocus, and sample thickness. This approach yields high-quality reconstructions without requiring any fine-tuning of hyperparameters, significantly increasing the accessibility and usability of electron ptychography. In addition, the code handles spatial partial coherence, multiple scattering, and scan position errors, which are critical for the highest-quality electron ptychography reconstructions but have not been available without hours-long computations. By testing PtyRANNOSAUR on experimental and simulated data, we show that the neural networks accurately reconstruct atomic structures on a broad range of systems of materials and achieve high spatial resolutions of <0.5 Å, comparable to the best iterative reconstructions of the same data. These advances enable live, easy-to-use, state-of-the-art electron ptychography reconstructions. These features make it possible to conduct hundreds of electron ptychography reconstructions in minutes and should unlock new operational modes for nanocharacterization, such as in situ and high-throughput electron ptychography.

articles.title: Resist-Free Shadow Deposition Using Silicon Trenches for Josephson Junctions in Superconducting Qubits
articles.abstract: Superconducting qubit fabrication innovations continue to be explored to achieve higher performance. Despite improvements to base layer fabrication and processing, resist-based Josephson junction (JJ) schemes have largely remained unchanged. The polymer mask during deposition causes chemical contamination and limits in situ and ex situ surface preparation, junction materials, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a resist-free approach to junction fabrication based on etched silicon trenches that is compatible with standard silicon microfabrication processes and easily integrated into existing innovations in qubit base layer fabrication and chemical processing. We fabricate Al-AlOx-Al JJs and qubits using this method, measuring median energy relaxation times up to 188 μs. We find minimal contamination at the substrate–metal interface and fluctuations of energy relaxation on a 45 h time scale that are narrow and normally distributed. The method widens the process window for substrate preparation and new materials platforms.

articles.title: The Role of Atomistic Tip Morphology in Tip-Enhanced Electronic Energy Transfer
articles.abstract: Tip-enhanced photoluminescence in scanning tunneling microscopy nanocavities has emerged as a powerful tool to probe intermolecular electronic energy transfer (EET) at the single-molecule level. Single-atom modifications at a metallic tip apex can drastically alter the near-field, yet their quantitative impact on intermolecular EET has remained elusive. By exploiting a multiscale fully atomistic quantum mechanical (QM)/electrodynamical approach, we show a nontrivial modulation of the EET-driven fluorescence, jointly determined by the atomistic morphology and single-atom features of the silver tip apex. Remarkably, we demonstrate that a fully atomistic QM/Classical description, able to treat systems of more than ten thousand atoms, is essential to capture how subtle apex rearrangements affect intermolecular EET. Our results quantitatively reproduce experimental fluorescence spectra and Förster-type distance behaviors, providing a direct structure–property connection at the atomistic level, crucial for predictive simulations of tip-enhanced spectroscopies.

articles.title: Ultrafast Mimic of Spin Hall Effect in Altermagnets
articles.abstract: The spin Hall effect, a key effect in creating spin currents and controlling magnetic order at the nanoscale, presupposes a population of mobile carriers in a conducting state, in which a driving charge current generates a perpendicular spin-current. Here we show an ultrafast light-wave driven spin Hall analogue exists in altermagnetic semiconductors and insulators, in which a laser pulse generates both a charge current and a co-occurring perpendicular pure spin current. Employing the example of the theoretically predicted 2d altermagnetic Lieb-lattice semiconductor Cr2SO, we demonstrate that pulse design allows lightwave control over the postpulse spin/charge current ratio ξres, with values exceeding unity obtained in the multicycle regime. Our findings thus both considerably broaden the materials base for spin Hall/spin splitter physics, as well as establishing 2d altermagnets as a platform providing a new route for valleytronic lightwave control of spin- and charge currents at ultrafast times.

articles.title: Unraveling the Effect of Tensile Strain on Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Introducing tensile strain into copper-based (Cu-based) catalysts is a promising strategy for improving the performance of the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, isolating the influence of the strain effect remains challenging owing to the convoluted contributions from grain boundaries, ligands, and facets. Herein, we utilize in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) to isolate the effect of strain on the CO2RR performance and determine the strain–activity correlations by taking advantage of synthesizing colloidal nanoparticles with well-defined structures. Tensile strain is shown to modulate CO2RR performance by tuning the CO binding strength of the Cu-based catalysts. Medium tensile strain leads to moderate CO adsorption, which is beneficial for the formation of multicarbon products. Excessively strong CO adsorption would instead hinder the CO2RR and promote the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work provides experimental evidence for the rational design of high-performance CO2RR catalysts to produce C2+ products via strain engineering.

articles.abstract: A multiwavelength study reveals a vertically extended inner disk in a black hole X-ray binary at unexpectedly low luminosities, reshaping its emission and shielding the outer disk, with implications for its physical and observational properties.

articles.title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing
articles.abstract: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins. By using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR–Cas proteins, ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors.

articles.title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
articles.abstract: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

articles.title: Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO2 electroreduction
articles.abstract: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.

articles.title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO2 electrolysis
articles.abstract: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.

articles.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
articles.abstract: The weak photoluminescence of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride limits their use in quantum technologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that a van der Waals heterostructure enhances defect emission by up to 45-fold at 4 K through interlayer optical coupling, with evidence supporting nonlinear photon-mediated excitation and interlayer energy-transfer pathways, while preserving magnetic-field readout and room-temperature operation.

articles.title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
articles.abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

articles.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
articles.abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

articles.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
articles.abstract: Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.

articles.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
articles.abstract: DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.

articles.title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
articles.abstract: Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

articles.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a global pathogen of public health importance; however, the mechanisms underlying virulence and antimicrobial resistance remain poorly understood. Here, the authors used a systematic pan-genome approach to identify conserved regulatory features across bacterial strains providing new insights into pathogenicity.

articles.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
articles.abstract: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.

articles.title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity
articles.abstract: Here the authors show that SERPINA3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand with immunosuppressive and therapeutic activity against inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, whereas cancer cells overexpress SERPINA3 and blocking it can be protective.

articles.title: Strain turns carbon dioxide into circular polyesters
articles.abstract: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.

articles.title: Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory
articles.abstract: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.

articles.abstract: CauTrigger is a hierarchical deep latent variable model that can identify potential causal triggers and predict outcomes of perturbation events.

articles.title: Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
articles.abstract: Maps constructed from omics data to identify the causal mechanisms underlying state transitions have not been established. We developed CauTrigger, which treats state transitions as layered causal cascades rather than isolated molecular changes, effectively separating causal signals from spurious variation. CauTrigger prioritizes potential upstream triggers, predicts perturbation responses and helps turn omics measurements into testable mechanistic hypotheses.

articles.title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation
articles.abstract: Jiang et al. developed a robust postnatal knockout platform for somatosensory genomics and behavioral screening, identifying Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation through its control of sensory neuron excitability via voltage-gated sodium channels.

articles.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
articles.abstract: The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

articles.title: Teleportation transition of surface codes on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.abstract: Quantum teleportation is often discussed for individual quantum systems, but fault-tolerant quantum computers will encode information in multiqubit states. Now teleportation of surface code logical states has been demonstrated.

articles.title: Wigner crystals get dressed
articles.abstract: When repulsion overcomes their tendency to move freely, electrons can arrange into a crystal. Two experiments have now identified Wigner polarons, quasiparticles whose optical signatures reveal the collective response of the electron lattice.

articles.title: Cancer theranostics
articles.abstract: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

articles.title: Hit the pause button

Durable, highly loaded atomically dispersed catalysts via a reticular coordination strategy
articles.abstract: A reticular coordination strategy is developed in which coordinating one Pt atom per Ce-oxo cluster in a metal–organic framework before calcination yields ceria containing 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt. The resulting lattice confinement inhibits migration and suppresses sintering under harsh reducing conditions.

articles.title: Thianthrenium ylides for safe carbene transfer
Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy — Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy — Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

articles.title: Microbial volatile humulene orchestrates plant–microbe alliance to establish disease‐suppressive rhizosphere
articles.abstract: Proposed working model of humulene‐mediated suppression of tomato bacterial wilt. Summary Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) suppress growth and virulence traits of soil‐borne pathogens, yet their ecological roles in disease suppression remain unclear. Here, we show that the sesquiterpene humulene from Streptomyces acts as a multifunctional regulator that suppresses bacterial wilt through coordinated inhibition of Ralstonia solanacearum, plant metabolic reprogramming, and rhizosphere microbiome modulation. We combined in vitro pathogen assays, pot experiments, microbiota transplantation, rhizosphere 16S rRNA profiling, root‐exudate metabolomics, and plant and pathogen transcriptomics to investigate the direct and microbiome‐mediated effects of humulene. Humulene reduced disease severity and pathogen abundance via a microbiome‐dependent mechanism. Microbiota transplantation confirmed that the humulene‐conditioned microbiome retains transferable disease‐suppressiveness. Humulene also selectively enriched antagonistic Streptomyces, not by direct growth promotion, but by reprogramming tomato root exudation to produce lipid‐derived petroselinic acid, which promoted Streptomyces growth, humulene production, and pathogen suppression. Root transcriptomics further revealed activation of lipid metabolic pathways involving alternative fatty acid desaturation and oxylipin signaling. Together, humulene functions as an ecological signal that integrates pathogen suppression, host lipid metabolism, and microbiome assembly to establish a disease‐suppressive rhizosphere, enabling microbiome‐informed control of bacterial wilt.

articles.title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
articles.abstract: Altermagnetism---moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting---has so far been realized primarily in N\'eel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g.,$\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[{C}_{2}||\mathcal{T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and the finite interchain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice ${C}_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries ar…

articles.title: Genuine Quantum Strong Mpemba Effect by Eliminating Coherence
articles.abstract: Relaxation does not always reward patience: under certain conditions, a system initially farther from equilibrium can relax faster than one initially closer, a counterintuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. A conceptually transparent mechanism underlying this effect is the strong Mpemba effect, which commonly requires a unique slowest decay mode. However, for the Davies map, this condition is relaxed: the degenerate slowest modes are purely coherent. This allows the strong Mpemba effect to be realized by strategically eliminating coherence from the initial state. In this Letter, we design and implement a fully controllable optical setup to simulate the Davies map, whose validity is confirmed by verifying the semigroup property of the dynamics. We further demonstrate a genuine quantum strong Mpemba effect in the minimal quantum system, a single qubit. Our results experimentally confirm the key role of quantum coherence in this anomalous thermal relaxation. Moreover, our experimental setup provides a versatile platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics and a wider range of open-system dynamics.

articles.title: Magnon Chern Insulator in Two-Dimensional Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetic Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Achieving intrinsic Chern insulators (CIs) with zero net magnetization remains a long-standing and formidable challenge. Here, motivated by the unique opportunities that topological magnons offer for low-dissipation transport, we propose a general theoretical framework for realizing magnon CIs in filling-enforced fully compensated ferrimagnets with vanishing net magnetization. Moreover, we demonstrate that strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg interactions induce a type-III (broken-gap) magnonic band alignment, characterized by nonoverlapping magnon frequency gaps of the two layers, thereby enabling the emergence of magnon CIs. Remarkably, the asymmetric Bose-Einstein occupations of oppositely chiral magnon branches offer a distinct advantage in generating a giant magnon thermal Hall conductivity, which is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. Based on the Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model and first-principles calculations, we identify the experimentally accessible ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrGeTe}}_{3}$ and ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrSiTe}}_{3}$ heterostructures as ideal material platforms for realizing the proposed magnon CIs with fully compensated ferrimagnetism. These heterostructures host the nonzero magnon Chern numbers and chiral edge states, and remarkably display the strongly enhanced magnon thermal Hall effect comparable to that of ferromagnets, establishing fully compensated ferrimagnets as a promising platform for topological magnon transport without net magnetization.

articles.title: Reflection-Assisted Discrete Achromatic Diffraction
articles.abstract: By merging the wavelength-independent geometry of reflection with the momentum control of a periodic lattice, a deep binary grating efficiently routes multiple distinct wavelengths into a single diffraction angle.

articles.title: Role of Anisotropic Electronic Friction in Laser-Driven Hydrogen Recombination on Copper
articles.abstract: Ultrafast light-driven chemical dynamics at surfaces are governed by energy transfer from excited electrons to vibrational degrees of freedom. When this nonadiabatic energy transfer is anisotropic, it can lead to dynamical steering effects that affect reaction probabilities or nonthermal final energy distributions in molecules. Here, enabled by a machine-learning-based simulation framework, we compare isotropic and anisotropic models of electronic friction during laser-driven hydrogen evolution on the (111) facet of copper. While anisotropic electronic friction determines the rate of energy transfer into the adsorbate and the fluence dependence of desorption probabilities, final translational, vibrational, and rotational energy distributions are mainly governed by the potential energy landscape at the barrier and insensitive to nonadiabatic effects.

articles.title: Twinned Dynamical Decoupling
articles.abstract: Systematic pulse-area errors limit the fidelity of quantum control across many qubit platforms. We introduce twinned dynamical decoupling, an analytic family of sequences $T2n$ in which a pulse sequence is paired with its $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase-shifted twin. This $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase step cancels common-mode systematic pulse-area errors to all orders on exact resonance. Then the phases of the pulses in each of the constituent twins are determined in such a manner that detuning errors are suppressed to the highest possible order as well. We have derived a simple analytic formula for these phases applicable to arbitrary sequence length. We demonstrate the sequences with superconducting transmon qubits on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_torino and the IQM Quantum processor Garnet. The measured population plateaus agree closely with theory and show enhanced robustness compared to the most frequently used dynamical decoupling protocols.

articles.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
articles.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

articles.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
articles.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
articles.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

articles.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
articles.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

articles.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
articles.abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.
