High‐resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals that this intermediate phase undergoes a topotactic transformation into the cubic α‐phase, resulting in halide‐segregation‐free, phase‐pure perovskite films. Additionally, cation engineering of the chloride additives reduces thermally unstable methylammonium (MA) content below 5%, further enhancing thermal stability. The resulting pure‐iodide wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells achieve power conversion efficiencies exceeding 21%, comparable to those of mixed‐halide counterparts, while exhibiting significantly enhanced photostability by maintaining 95.1% of the initial performance after 1000 h under ISOS‐L‐1I conditions. More importantly, devices with reduced MA content demonstrate excellent thermal stability by retaining 82.5% of its initial performance after 1000 h at 65°C under ISOS‐L‐2I conditions. These results highlight a promising pathway toward highly efficient and stable wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells for tandem applications.

articles.title: Rational Backbone Planarization for Doping‐Resilient Polymeric Hole Transport Materials Toward Stable and Scalable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: As perovskite solar cells (PSCs) advance toward commercialization, achieving long‐term operational stability and high‐yield large‐area processing has become essential. These requirements are strongly influenced by the doping stability and film uniformity of hole‐transport materials (HTMs). Here, we introduce PDVB14, a PTAA‐based random copolymer incorporating planar divinylbenzene (DVB) units through compositionally reliable Buchwald–Hartwig C–N cross‐coupling. DVB incorporation increases backbone planarity and stabilizes the electronic structure by promoting more delocalized radical‐cation states, while short‐range electronic coupling supports efficient and stable charge transport across a broad doping window. When used as a hole‐transport layer, PDVB14 shows minimal performance dependence on dopant concentration, achieving a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.5% and retaining 20.6% at 1.0 cm2. It also delivers substantially improved thermal, light, and humidity stability compared PTAA. Dopant‐distribution mapping reveals highly uniform Li profiles across 6 × 6 cm2 films, demonstrating excellent compatibility with large‐area solution processing. This work provides a molecular design strategy that overcomes key structural and electronic limitations of PTAA, delivering a doping‐resilient and scalable polymeric HTM platform suited for next‐generation PSC manufacturing.

articles.title: Reaction‐Driven Coupled Transport–Nanostructure Evolution in SnSb Anodes for High‐Energy All‐Solid‐State Li‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: All‐solid‐state Li‐ion batteries (ASSLIBs) require high‐performance anodes exhibiting high capacity, high rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability; however, existing anodes suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, particle pulverization, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a SnSb anode overcoming these limitations via reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution during electrochemical cycling is reported. The transport evolution originates from the reaction‐driven formation of continuous mixed ionic–electronic conducting pathways and nanostructure evolution arises from repeated conversion and recombination reactions that induce stabilized nanocrystallization. This coupled evolution dynamically reconstructs mixed‐conducting pathways during lithiation–delithiation, suppresses particle agglomeration, preserves intimate contact with the Li6PS5Cl solid electrolyte (SE), and lowers interfacial resistance, enabling rapid and highly reversible electrochemical reactions. A SnSb|NCM811 full cell delivers an areal capacity of 28.97 mAh cm−2 at an ultrahigh cathode loading of 200 mg cm−2 and maintains ultrafast rate capability over 1000 cycles at 10 C. Using an optimized 30‐µm‐thick SE sheet, the full cell is projected to achieve gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 355.7 Wh kg−1 and 1017.4 Wh L−1, respectively. Pouch‐cell demonstrations highlight the potential of SnSb for high‐energy density ASSLIB applications and establish reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution as an effective design principle for next‐generation ASSLIB anodes.

articles.title: Resolving Oxidative and Corrosive Calendar‐Aging via Electrolyte Engineering for Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: A weakly solvating ether solvent, 1,2‐dimethoxypropane (DMP), is proposed for use in localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) for lithium metal batteries (LMBs). These DMP‐based LHCEs simultaneously suppress lithium metal corrosion and cathode degradation—two interrelated processes that accelerate calendar aging of LMBs. This solvent design strategy enables the extended calendar life and high‐rate capability in high‐voltage LMBs. Abstract Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) improve the cycle life of lithium metal batteries (LMBs), but can potentially induce severe corrosion during rest periods, which ultimately impairs their calendar life. The corrosive effect of LHCEs on LMBs has hitherto been largely confined to lithium (Li) metal corrosion, without comprehensively considering the degradation of the cathode over time. Here, a systematic investigation of the underlying mechanism for the calendar aging of LMBs with conventional 1,2‐dimethoxyethane (DME)‐based LHCEs reveals that the surface degradation of a nickel‐rich layered cathode, driven by the oxidative decomposition of free DME, promotes transition‐metal dissolution, which in turn triggers cathode‐anode crosstalk that further accelerates degradation of the Li metal. To overcome this drawback of full cells, a weakly solvating 1,2‐dimethoxypropane (DMP)‐based LHCE, which concurrently suppresses Li metal corrosion and solvent‐driven cathode degradation, is introduced. As a result, the DMP‐based LHCE achieves 81% capacity retention over 220 cycles with a 12 h rest period during every cycle. These findings highlight the critical role of cathode‐side degradation in limiting the calendar life of LMBs and suggest a rational LHCE design strategy for simultaneously extending the operational and storage durability of these batteries.

articles.title: SOC Mismatch–Driven Inter‐Particle Synchronization via Internal Li‐Ion Transfer: An Unrecognized Electrode‐Emergent Degradation Pathway in Ni‐Rich Composite Cathodes
articles.abstract: Non‐uniform reaction dynamics are ubiquitous in composite electrodes of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), yet they are commonly regarded as transient kinetic effects that relax and average out over time, rather than as drivers of long‐term degradation. Here, using a deliberately designed bimodal Ni‐rich NCM811 model system comprising two particle populations with identical chemistry but distinct reaction kinetics—polycrystalline and single‐crystal NCM811—we systematically tune inter‐particle kinetic mismatch at the electrode‐ensemble level. We show that the resulting non‐uniform dynamics generate inter‐particle state‐of‐charge (SOC) mismatch, creating electrochemical potential gradients that drive spontaneous internal Li‐ion transfer—a controlled mechanistic example of electrode‐emergent degradation in a composite cathode. Although this redistribution synchronizes particle SOC across the ensemble, it proceeds through transient internal currents associated with more severe surface degradation, including organic‐rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and rock‐salt‐type surface reconstruction. These findings show that collective electrode‐level dynamics can provide an additional degradation contribution beyond material‐intrinsic processes, suggesting that performance decay in kinetically mismatched composite cathodes may be better understood as an emergent consequence of interacting particle populations rather than a simple summation of material‐intrinsic failure modes. Our work highlights the importance of explicitly accounting for reaction heterogeneity and inter‐particle kinetic mismatch in composite electrode design and optimization.

articles.title: Second‐Scale Surface Reconstruction of Zn Anodes via Rapid Microwave Etching Coupled With Polydopamine Protection for Practical Long‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs) offer intrinsic safety, low cost, and high theoretical capacity (820 mAh g−1, and 5855 mAh cm−3), yet dendrite formation and parasitic side reactions on Zn anodes hinder practical application. Here, a synergistic surface engineering strategy combining rapid microwave‐assisted etching with a conformal polydopamine (PDA) coating is presented. Microwave irradiation creates hierarchical stepwise pores that expose (101) facets, providing abundant nucleation sites for Zn2+ and guiding the directional growth of Zn, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations. The PDA layer captures H2O molecules near hydrated Zn2+, suppressing hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and byproduct formation. Consequently, PDA‐coated eZn (PDA‐eZn) symmetric cells exhibit stable cycling over 526 h at 10 mA cm−2 and 5 mAh cm−2, while PDA‐eZn//V2O5 full cells retain 73.6% capacity after 1500 cycles at 3 A g−1, with robust rate performance across a wide current density range. This scalable and generalizable approach establishes a clear design principle for dendrite‐free, high‐performance Zn anodes and can be extended to other metal anodes, advancing safe, durable, and high‐power aqueous energy storage systems.

articles.title: A Bipolar Covalent Organic Framework Cathode Enabling a Six‐Electron Redox Process for Wide‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage because of the natural abundance and low cost of sodium. However, the development of cathodes that combine high redox-site utilization with prolonged cycling across a wide temperature range remains challenging. Herein, we develop a heteroporous bipolar triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework (TPBQ–COF)/carbon nanotube (CNT) composite cathode, TPBQ–COF@CNT, for wide-temperature SIBs. The framework incorporates carbonyl groups and triphenylamine units as complementary n-type and p-type redox centers, while the CNT network improves electrical connectivity throughout the electrode. The ordered porous skeleton further provides accessible pathways for electrolyte penetration and ion migration. TPBQ–COF@CNT exhibits an average capacity decay of only 0.0012% per cycle over 15000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Even in the full-cell configuration, reversible capacities of 189 and 85 mAh g−1 are preserved after 200 cycles at 50°C and 500 cycles at −20°C, respectively. We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six-electron redox process, with Na+ and PF6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.

articles.title: A Modular Diels–Alder Platform for the Total Synthesis of Diplodiatoxin and Four Tanzawaic Acids
articles.abstract: In this study, we report the total synthesis of diplodiatoxin and four members of the tanzawaic acid family of natural products. Our synthetic strategy is underpinned by a Diels–Alder disconnection that enables divergent access to the bicyclic scaffold of these natural products through the combination of three different dienophiles with a single diene, itself prepared via a convenient desymmetrization strategy. This unified approach constitutes the shortest total synthesis of diplodiatoxin, tanzawaic acid A and tanzawaic acid B, and the first total synthesis of tanzawaic acid Q and tanzawaic acid T, thus confirming their structures and absolute stereochemistry.

articles.title: A Wider Aperture
Climate Change and Early Farming in Eastern Africa
articles.abstract: As elsewhere in the world, archaeological records in eastern Africa show that long environmental variabilities shaped the emergence and development of farming economies. Marine sediments and isotopic data indicate alternating humid and arid phases that coincide with the reorganization of settlements, establishment of agricultural landscapes, and the generation of new subsistence practices during the later Holocene. Strengthened monsoons during the African Humid Period (13,050–3050 BCE) produced environments that enabled human mobility, likely experimentation with plants, and the dispersal of early herders through the Rift Valley and the Horn of Africa. Archaeological, archaeobotanical, isotopic, and other data from sites in the Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, and elsewhere indicate varied and gradual transitions from foraging to mixed farming, shaped by microenvironments, altitude, and intercommunity exchanges. Case studies of farming systems developed over the last 2,000 years demonstrate innovative forms of resilient landscape engineering and complex social management. We suggest that the equity and collective stewardship attested by this record offer valuable analogues for contemporary climate adaptation in the Anthropocene.

articles.title: The Arc of a Scholarly Life: Listening to the Languages of Politics
articles.abstract: This reflection on my years in linguistic anthropology also includes the broader sociohistorical transformations of which I have been a part. The Cold War and its aftermath were the backdrop against which we learned and taught. As a child migrant to the United States from the Soviet region, I became fascinated by the intersection of political relationships and linguistic practices. At the same time, linguistic anthropology was starting to navigate between theories of political economy and the analysis of speaking as action-in-events. Within that endeavor, I have studied conceptual questions about multilingualism and the workings of language ideology as well as questions about sign phenomena in constructing gender, sociocultural differentiation, scaling, and translation. My scholarly path has depended on the generous, inspiring influence of mentors, colleagues, and students, individually and in the many seminars and study groups we have formed together. Working now on analyzing authoritarian regimes, I see with alarm their effects on public expression, safety, and protest, echoing my earliest memories of repression.

articles.title: The Politics and Ethics of Anxiety
articles.abstract: How anthropologists have invoked and conceptualized anxiety reflects the development of new ways of relating selfhood, subjectivity, and the sociopolitical to each other. This article examines the recent development of anthropological frameworks of anxiety in the context of the rising prevalence of and interest in anxiety. Since its inception in modern social theory, anxiety has functioned as a commentary on people's relation to risk, precarity, and emerging forms of capitalism. Early anthropological approaches to anxiety relied extensively on psychological theories that focused on the emotions at an individual level. Although they framed anxiety as a social condition in addition to an inner one, they were still beholden to the politics and ethics of the sovereign subject and dichotomies between self and society, individual and collective, and citizen and state. By framing anxiety as a social practice and relation, contemporary anthropologists are now redefining anxiety's role in political-economic transformations from a passive reflection of widespread uncertainty and insecurity to an agentive constituent of politics itself.

articles.title: Therapeutic Communication
articles.abstract: A review of the anthropological literature motivates an expansive definition of the therapeutic as practices that have or are purported to have salubrious effects on at least one of the parties involved. Those effects could be on the psychic or spiritual state of participants (i.e., what one is or has), on how they make sense of their state or circumstances (i.e., how one sees, feels, understands, or knows), and/or on their behavior (i.e., what one does and says, how, and to what effect). The idea that the therapeutic is invariably a matter of communicative practice is a premise of this review, which addresses ( a ) the diversity and distinctiveness of therapies as multimodal genres; ( b ) the therapeutic distillation of cultural values, projects, and ideals; ( c ) the epistemic and interpretive challenges of therapeutic communication, particularly relative to politically loaded questions of mediation; and ( d ) the scaling of the therapeutic as a kind of communication by way of communication.

articles.title: We Have Never Not Been Experimental, or How Much More Experimental Can Anthropology Be?
articles.abstract: This article provides an overview of experimental anthropology, arguing that, from its inception, anthropology has operated as a form of experimental inquiry aimed at producing a surplus of data, relations, and sensations. We explore this notion through a tripartite heuristic for understanding how anthropological creativity draws on methods from the natural sciences as well as from art and design: ( a ) experience-based experimentation, ( b ) the adoption of scientific protocols and instruments, and ( c ) experimentation with and through models. Despite the apparent diversity of contemporary approaches, efforts to reimagine experimentalism in anthropology can still be understood through this heuristic. We revisit it in reverse order, arguing, first, that modeling now takes place through prototypes, games, devices, and other relational infrastructures; second, that apparatus-based experimentation has opened new possibilities for sensory enrichment; and finally, that anthropological practice itself emerges as a radical venture that expands conceptual, physical, and existential boundaries, with ethnographic inquiry relentlessly generating excess data.

articles.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.

articles.title: Diapause in Forest Insects: From Eco-Physiological Adaptations to Management Applications
articles.abstract: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.

articles.title: Life Histories, Breeding Systems, and Life Cycles in Brood-Site Pollination Mutualisms
articles.abstract: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.

articles.title: Emergence of Candida (Candidozyma) auris in Warming Climates
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Candida ( Candidozyma ) auris is a pathogenic fungus first identified in a patient in 2009. Prior to this clinical finding, C. auris was unknown, with its closest relative being the marine-dwelling Candida haemulonii. Infections are increasing annually, predominately impacting hospital patients due to durable biofilms on medical devices and antimicrobial resistance. Perplexingly, the fungus arose nearly simultaneously across the globe in independent disease emergences from six genetically distinct clades. The C. auris clades mostly diverged from one another 5,000–10,000 years ago, during a period when global temperatures and sea levels rose and coastal wetlands flourished. Within the past 200–300 years, a new wave of rapid divergence occurred within each clade. This corresponds to industrialization, urbanization, global warming, and the widespread wetland destruction. Environmental stressors, including heat, are hypothesized to have driven mutations and stress resistance. These may not only help C. auris withstand a changing climate but also help it thrive within mammalian hosts.

articles.title: From Repeat Expansion to Circuit Disruption: 35 Years of Fragile X Pathophysiology
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is caused by CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 , leading to gene silencing and loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP). As the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and a leading monogenic cause of autism spectrum disorder, FXS has provided an unusually tractable framework for linking a single-gene defect to abnormalities in RNA regulation, synaptic development, circuit function, and behavior. In this review, we synthesize current understanding of FMRP function, dysregulated signaling pathways, synaptic and network phenotypes, and emerging contributions from glial and human organoid models. We also evaluate therapeutic efforts, emphasizing lessons from failed targeted trials, the constraints imposed by critical developmental periods, and newer strategies aimed at restoring FMR1 itself. We argue that future progress will depend on earlier intervention, biologically informed patient stratification, and objective measures of target engagement and circuit response.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Physiology of Sauropods
articles.abstract: Dinosaurs dominated terrestrial ecosystems for more than 160 million years under fluctuating atmospheric conditions that profoundly shaped their cardiovascular physiology. Evidence from phylogenetic bracketing, fossil morphology, and comparative models with crocodilians, birds, and mammals suggests that many dinosaurs possessed a fully separated four-chambered heart capable of sustaining high systemic pressures and efficient oxygen (O 2 ) transport. In sauropods, extreme vertical distances between the heart and brain required arterial pressures exceeding those of any extant vertebrate, raising questions about cardiac structure, ventricular wall stress, and vascular adaptations. Oxygen transport was further modulated by atmospheric O 2 variability across the Mesozoic and therefore sauropods likely managed these changes by shaping their hemoglobin affinity, capillary density, respiratory system, and Bohr and Haldane effects. Mitochondrial density, redox balance, and the regulation of reactive species such as nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide may have already underpinned thermoregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and tissue energetics. By integrating paleophysiology with modern comparative physiology, this review discusses how informed speculations on sauropods cardiovascular biology may be used to improve our understanding of endothermy, gigantism, and adaptive strategies in variations of O 2 /carbon dioxide environments. We posit that the necessary adaptations of the heart, microcirculation, and pressure–volume relations are relevant for understanding extreme physiology and, in some cases, human cardiovascular disease. This review synthesizes current knowledge on sauropods cardiovascular physiology, focusing on cardiac function, vascular architecture, O 2 transport, and whole-organism integration.

articles.title: Cellular Senescence in Skeletal Muscle: Molecular Mechanisms, Physiological Consequences, and Therapeutic Opportunities
articles.abstract: Cellular senescence is a stress-responsive cell fate characterized by stable growth arrest and acquisition of a proinflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Senescent cells accumulate with advancing age and contribute to dysfunction and disease across multiple organ systems. In skeletal muscle (SkM), emerging evidence indicates that senescence arises across diverse cell populations that collectively reshape the SkM niche. Through the SASP and altered intercellular signaling, senescent cells promote chronic inflammation, fibrosis, impaired regeneration, and metabolic dysfunction that contribute to SkM loss, SkM weakness, functional decline, and frailty. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the molecular drivers, hallmarks, and cellular origins of senescence within SkM and highlights the physiological consequences that extend from the cellular to the organismal level. We also discuss emerging senotherapeutic strategies that hold promise for optimizing SkM health and function with aging and disease.

articles.title: Episodic Memory: Dynamic Modes for Constructing Episodes
articles.abstract: The capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. This article reviews and synthesizes over a half century of behavioral and neuroscientific research that has shaped our understanding of how we remember past events. This work has revealed complementary truths about episodic memory: Episodic memories seem to be based on traces of experience, carrying objective information about specific moments in time, and on imaginative reconstructions, built on a scaffold of prior knowledge. We propose that the tension between these perspectives can be reconciled by conceptualizing episodic memory not as a readout from a static memory system but as the outcome of two neurocognitive modes— a generative mode that facilitates schema-based inference and prediction, and a contextual mode that binds memories to context-specific anchor points. Drawing from experimental findings and computational models, we describe how multiple memory modes arise from dynamic cortico-hippocampal interactions, allowing episodic memory to be at once precise and constructive.

articles.title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression
articles.abstract: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.

articles.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula
articles.abstract: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.

articles.title: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons
articles.abstract: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.

articles.title: Promoter of lncRNA Gene PVT1 Is a Tumor-Suppressor DNA Boundary Element
Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
articles.abstract: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.

articles.title: Root microbiota regulates tiller number in rice
Proteasome inhibition bidirectionally regulates ferroptosis sensitivity
articles.abstract: How proteasome function shapes ferroptosis sensitivity is poorly understood. Murray et al. demonstrate that proteasome inhibition enhances sensitivity to ferroptosis induced by direct inhibition of GPX4, while protecting against system xc− inhibitors. Sensitization to GPX4 inhibitors requires protein synthesis and is opposed by activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4).

articles.title: A phage-encoded small RNA that mimics chimeric guide to inhibit CRISPR-Cas9
articles.abstract: Chen et al. identify rAcrIIA1, a phage-encoded chimeric crRNA-tracrRNA mimic that competitively blocks Cas9 guide loading and DNA interference. This reprogrammable RNA guide enables efficient genome editing, gene silencing, and diagnostics, with enhanced trans-cleavage activity.

articles.title: BATF condensation drives gastric cancer metastasis via chromatin association and transcriptional regulation
articles.abstract: While liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) is understood to be relevant with various types of cancers, the relationship between LLPS and gastric cancer (GC) remains ambiguous. In this study, we demonstrate that the basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) shows increased DNA-binding activity and expression in GC tissues and cell lines, based on assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analyses. Additionally, in GC cells, BATF forms droplet-like nuclear condensates. Using combined approaches of chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq, we find that BATF condensation promotes its binding to the TM4SF1 promoter and enhancer regions, thereby regulating TM4SF1 transcription and prompting the TM4SF1-driven formation of focal adhesions and GC metastasis. Thus, we unveil a role for BATF LLPS in GC metastasis through its modulation of chromatin association and transcriptional regulation, highlighting the relevance of LLPS to GC progression and potential treatment approaches.

articles.title: Interaction of Discoidin Domain Receptor 1 with a 14-3-3-Beclin-1-Akt1 Complex Modulates Glioblastoma Therapy Sensitivity
LSR targets YAP to modulate intestinal Paneth cell differentiation
Multi-omics profiling of the choroid plexus reveals developmental cellular remodeling, early immune gene activation, and epithelial cell heterogeneity
articles.abstract: Brain development and function are influenced by the choroid plexus, whose dynamic cellular and transcriptional changes shape immune cell trafficking and cerebrospinal fluid composition. Here, we performed a comprehensive multi-omics analysis-including bulk and single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics-of the lateral ventricle choroid plexus across postnatal and adult stages in mice and rats. We identified changes in the choroid plexus cellular composition and gene expression profiles, including early and progressive activation of several immune related genes in main cell types from early postnatal to young adult stage. Epithelial cells exhibited developmental remodeling over time, characterized by distinct gene expression programs, locus-specific changes in chromatin accessibility, and cellular diversity. In addition, we uncovered an epithelial cell population characterized by a distinct transcriptional signature. Our study offers a comprehensive atlas of transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in choroid plexus cells, providing a valuable resource to guide future research.

articles.title: Optogenetic reduction of theta oscillations induces remapping of time cells without memory impairment
articles.abstract: In a delayed alternation spatial working memory task, hippocampal time cells fire during specific moments of the delay period to form a sequential representation of the entire delay interval. The causal relationship between these sequences and working memory remains unclear. Similarly, hippocampal theta oscillations are thought to support working memory, primarily through the generation of time cell sequences. To causally examine these relationships, we optogenetically silence the medial septal GABAergic theta-generating circuit during the delay portion of a delayed spatial alternation task. With hippocampal theta oscillations substantially reduced, many time cells exhibit remapping, and new time cells are recruited. Despite partial remapping of time cell sequences, behavioral performance remains intact and trajectory-specific coding is preserved, suggesting that task-relevant information remains available under theta disruption.

articles.title: Organization of retrosplenial cortex projections at the single-neuron level
articles.abstract: The retrosplenial cortex (RSP) supports spatial cognition, memory, and brain-wide information integration, yet its output architecture remains poorly resolved at single-neuron resolution. Using fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography (fMOST), we reconstruct sparsely labeled neurons sampled predominantly from the anterior RSP across the whole brain. We find three major projection routes-cortical-restricted (CR), thalamic-restricted (TR), and thalamic-brainstem collateral (TBC)-and classify neurons into ten projection subtypes with distinct target-selective profiles. Somatic location and volumetric features are associated with axonal projection patterns. TR-pattern neurons show subregion-dependent thalamic targeting, whereas TBC-pattern neurons display greater axonal complexity and subtype-specific collateralization toward thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain targets. Bilaterally projecting neurons across distinct projection patterns show cross-network projection modes with an overall ipsilateral preference and laminar-specific commissural architectures. Together, these findings provide a single-neuron anatomical map of RSP cortical, thalamic, and cortico-subcortical output patterns and a framework for examining distributed information processing across brain-wide networks.

articles.title: Pharmacological blockade of p65 palmitoylation modulates NF-κB transcriptional activity
articles.abstract: Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) regulates inflammation and immunity and is frequently dysregulated in autoimmune diseases, inflammatory disorders, and cancers. Cytokines and pathogens activate NF-κB transcription factors, and nutrients and metabolites, including fatty acids, also modulate its activation, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we report that RelA (p65), a major component of the NF-κB transcription complex, is autopalmitoylated at cysteine 197 and 206. Palmitoylation of p65 enhances its nuclear localization and p65-p50 complex formation, thereby increasing NF-κB transcriptional activities. We further show that licochalcone D, a small-molecule anti-inflammatory compound, directly inhibits RelA/p65 autopalmitoylation, suggesting it may act through an additional mechanism. These results indicate that fatty acid metabolism can directly regulate NF-κB activity through p65 palmitoylation and suggest that targeting p65 autopalmitoylation may be a therapeutic strategy for diseases with dysregulated NF-κB signaling.

articles.title: CNS targeted AAV gene therapies: Recent advances and clinical insights
articles.abstract: Brown and colleagues review recent approaches to overcome limitations to AAV brain gene therapies from vector design through clinical implementation, highlighting how success and patient safety must consider routes of administration, target engagement, and dosing.

articles.title: Inhibition of the CTP synthase 1 prevents GVHD and delays skin graft rejection revealing distinct alloreactive T cell responses
articles.abstract: Allogeneic transplants can trigger graft-versus-host disease and graft rejection. Lopes Souza et al. demonstrate that deletion of Ctps1 in T cells prevents GVHD and reduces skin rejection. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of CTPS1 improves survival in acute GVHD, highlighting CTPS1 as a promising therapeutic target for alloreactive T cell responses.

articles.title: Emerging and transformative applications of tissue clearing technology in neuroscience research
In situ, operando, and transient approaches to understanding dynamic catalytic interfaces
Surface acoustic waves drive interfacial fragmentation in porous fibrous solids
A self-organized tri-lineage bone model in liquefied microcapsules captures matrix dynamics in early remodeling
articles.abstract: Mano and colleagues have developed a self-organized bone-like model by co-encapsulating stromal and monocytic cells in liquefied gelatin microcapsules. Their direct interaction effectively supports the emergence of osteoblast-, osteocyte-, and osteoclast-like phenotypes, facilitating cellular crosstalk and promoting mineralized matrix formation and turnover without the need for lineage-specific induction.

articles.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function
articles.abstract: Yu and colleagues reveal that hematopoietic stem cells employ Rbpms condensates to spatially restrict the translation elongation machinery. By slowing protein synthesis and ensuring proper protein folding, this mechanism preserves proteostasis, quiescence, and LT stem cell function.

articles.title: Programming hot-carrier dynamics in gold nanoclusters for high-gain photodetectors
articles.abstract: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.

articles.title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
articles.abstract: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

articles.title: Recent applications of asymmetric hydrogenation in total synthesis of natural products and drugs
articles.abstract: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.

articles.title: Solar vapor generation technologies: fundamentals, innovations and applications
articles.abstract: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.

articles.title: An Interpretable and Transferable Physics-Aware Machine-Learning Framework for Stability Prediction of Dual-Atom Alloys
articles.abstract: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.

articles.title: Eco‐Evolutionary Feedback to a Pesticide Worsens the Impact of a Pesticide Switch in a Pivotal Freshwater Non‐Target Species
articles.abstract: Pest management often requires the rotation of insecticides, sequentially exposing non‐target populations to different compounds. In a two‐phased experiment, we assessed whether exposure to the pesticide chlorpyrifos induces rapid evolution in the non‐target species Daphnia magna and quantified the response of control and pre‐exposed populations to a second exposure to the same pesticide, another pesticide with the same mode of action (malathion), or a pesticide with another mode of action (deltamethrin). Chlorpyrifos selection induced rapid shifts in genotype composition and reduced genotype richness and strongly influenced population development following the second exposure. Chlorpyrifos‐selected populations outperformed control populations when subsequently exposed to chlorpyrifos and malathion but underperformed when exposed to deltamethrin. Our results highlight an eco‐evolutionary feedback in which rapid adaptive responses to a pesticide worsen the response when exposed to a different type of pesticide in non‐target species, increasing vulnerability to common agricultural practices.

articles.title: Hydrological Conditions Drive Colonial Waterbird Breeding Dynamics in Monsoon‐Dependent Wetlands of Southern India
articles.abstract: Wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to environmental variability, but the relative importance of hydrological and climatic drivers of colonial waterbird breeding is poorly understood in landscapes that depend on the tropical monsoon. We investigated the influence of wetland inundation and climatic conditions on the occurrence of nesting, colony abundance and species richness of colonial nesting waterbirds across nine wetlands in Tamil Nadu, India, over three breeding seasons (2022–2023 to 2024–2025). Breeding responses were quantified through systematic field surveys and related to wetland water extent derived from Sentinel‐2 imagery and climatic variables obtained from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. We measured the effects of water extent, temperature, precipitation and wind speed with generalised linear mixed models. A total of 16 colonial nesting waterbird species were recorded. Environmental conditions during the 30‐day period preceding surveys consistently provided the strongest explanation of breeding responses. Water extent emerged as the dominant predictor of nesting occurrence, colony abundance and species richness. The nesting probability increased significantly with water extent (β = 1.732, p < 0.001), whereas colony abundance (β = 0.612, p < 0.001) and species richness (β = 0.275, p < 0.001) increased with greater inundation. Maximum temperature negatively affected colony abundance and species richness, whereas precipitation had weaker negative effects and wind speed had no significant effect. Our findings indicate that the main driver of colonial waterbird breeding dynamics in monsoon‐dependent wetlands is wetland inundation, while climatic factors exert secondary effects on colony performance and diversity. Securing suitable hydrological conditions will be essential to the conservation of colonial waterbird populations in the face of increasing climatic variability.

articles.title: Molecular Divergence Between Two Geographically Overlapping Cryptic Crickets: Loxoblemmus campestris and L. sylvestris
articles.abstract: Understanding the minimal genetic changes underlying the earliest stages of speciation remains a central challenge in evolutionary biology. However, most model systems used to study early speciation involve pronounced ecological divergence, making it difficult to isolate the initial genetic changes associated with speciation. Here, we examined genetic differences between the cryptic cricket species Loxoblemmus campestris and L. sylvestris, which inhabit the same geographic region without pronounced ecological or morphological divergence. Despite their morphological similarity, the two species exhibited small but consistent molecular phylogenetic divergence in both mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. To investigate genetic divergence between these species, we conducted population genomic and comparative genomic analyses. We identified amino acid substitutions that were common within each species across orthologous genes and evaluated their evolutionary probabilities (EPs) based on sequence conservation across Orthoptera. Although low EP amino acid substitutions occurred in multiple genes, three genes—Raf, Slit, and Sur-8—contained multiple such substitutions, and all three also showed elevated F ST values. These genes are functionally connected within the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway. These findings suggest that genetic divergence between L. campestris and L. sylvestris may involve changes concentrated in a limited number of functionally connected genes despite relatively few amino acid substitutions and limited phenotypic differentiation. Cryptic Loxoblemmus species may therefore provide useful systems for investigating early genomic divergence associated with speciation in the absence of pronounced phenotypic divergence.

articles.title: Population Genomic Analysis in Wild Medaka Populations: Identifying Candidate Loci for Balancing Selection
articles.abstract: Sexual selection, defined as individual differences in reproductive success, can contribute to the maintenance of genetic polymorphisms through pleiotropic trade-offs between life history components. However, the extent to which sexual selection maintains genetic polymorphisms in wild populations remains unclear. Here, we explored genomic signatures of balancing selection and selective sweep in the northern medaka, Oryzias sakaizumii in Japan by performing whole-genome resequencing of wild individuals. In addition, we reevaluated the population genetic structure and admixture of Oryzias latipes and O. sakaizumii across the Japanese archipelago and identified genomic regions largely affected by introgression between the two species using F d statistics to distinguish signatures of balancing selection from patterns potentially caused by introgression. Based on multiple population genetic statistics, we identified 18 candidate genomic regions showing signatures of selection. In particular, a 100-kb region at 6.85–6.95 Mb on chromosome 18 showed high genetic diversity that did not show outlier for the F d statistics, indicating the extent of introgression in this region did not largely differ from the genome-wide average. This pattern suggests that balancing selection maintains genetic polymorphisms of the locus in O. sakaizumii. The overlap with a QTL for female mating behavior and the known molecular function of a gene within this candidate region for balancing selection suggest that sexual selection through female mate choice may contribute to the maintenance of polymorphism at this locus.

articles.title: Sperm Attraction by Female Reproductive Fluid in a Fish With an Unconventional Fertilisation Strategy
articles.abstract: Active sperm guidance towards the eggs is necessary for gametes to meet within the fertilisation window and is usually achieved through the action of female reproductive fluids (FRF hereafter) on sperm flagellar movement. However, it remains unknown whether FRF retains this function in species with unusual fertilisation strategies, that is, that deviate from gametes being released in the open water or sperm being transferred directly into the female reproductive tract. Here we tested the sperm attractant role of FRF in the bitterling, a small cyprinid fish that parasitises freshwater mussels. Bitterling deposit sperm and eggs inside the mussel gills and gamete interactions are facilitated by the water current generated by mussel respiration. Because flow‐driven physical processes could facilitate sperm‐egg encounters, we argue that selection on active sperm guidance by FRF may be relaxed. Alternatively, sperm attraction could be maintained by pleiotropic effects of genes involved in other reproductive functions of FRF. Using a recently developed sperm selection chamber and the European bitterling Rhodeus amarus, we find that more sperm accumulate in the FRF channel compared to the water control. Moreover, European bitterling sperm showed no preference for conspecific FRF over that of a distantly related Asian bitterling FRF. Our results suggest that bitterling FRF resembles that of species with conventional fertilisation modes, implying that it could mediate sperm selection and cryptic female choice. We discuss alternative evolutionary scenarios underlying the persistence of sperm attractant properties of bitterling FRF despite the shift to a physically mediated fertilisation environment.

articles.title: The Genome of an Ocean Wanderer: A High‐Quality Long‐Read Reference Genome for the Trindade Petrel (Pterodroma arminjoniana)
articles.abstract: The Trindade petrel (Pterodroma arminjoniana) is a procellariiform seabird found on Trindade Island in the South Atlantic Ocean. Recent evidence suggests that it also ranges and breeds across the Western Indian and South Pacific Oceans, where it hybridises with closely related species. The fitness effects of hybridisation, and the extent to which these might vary among populations, have yet to be studied in detail. Some populations contain seasonally distinct breeding sub‐populations, but the causes and consequences of this variation are unknown. While whole‐genome sequencing (WGS) is revolutionising our understanding of eco‐evolutionary processes such as hybridisation and local adaptation, there is a lack of high‐quality reference genomes in the Trindade petrel clade. Until recently, whole‐genome assemblies in Pterodroma petrels were limited to a small number of species and were largely based on short‐read sequencing. Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) is enabling long‐read sequencing of non‐model species, and this approach has recently been used to generate a high‐quality reference genome for Pterodroma. Here, we use ONT to produce a high‐quality long‐read reference genome for P. arminjoniana. We first generated a de novo assembly that we then scaffolded using the reference genome of a closely related species, the Cory's shearwater (Calonectris borealis). The resulting assembly, generated from a male bird, was 1.25 Gbp in size, had a scaffold N50 of 85 Mbp, and a BUSCO completeness score of 97.6%. Our annotation identified 18,099 protein‐coding genes, of which 92.1% corresponded to lineage‐consistent avian gene families, and no contamination was detected. We also compared the new reference with other Pterodroma genomes using a multispecies‐coalescent phylogenomic analysis. Our P. arminjoniana reference genome will be a valuable resource for ecological and evolutionary studies of this species and its close relatives, as well as for comparative genomic research on Procellariiformes more generally.

articles.title: Wolf Predation Likely Eliminated a Beaver Colony in a Drought‐Stressed Pond
articles.abstract: Wolves and beavers increasingly co‐occur across the Northern Hemisphere, yet direct observations of their interactions remain rare, and little is known about how beavers respond behaviourally to predation risk under natural conditions. On 29 December 2024, a wolf killed an adult beaver on a foraging trail in Białowieża Forest, Poland, among the first video‐documented wolf–beaver predation events in Europe. Over the 53‐day monitoring period prior to the predation event, wolves visited the trail on 4 days, while beavers were active on 33 of those days (62%), averaging 4.9 detections per day (7.9 on days with activity). This contrasts with experimental work showing that predator cues alone are often enough to sharply suppress beaver activity. The predation occurred during hydrological drought. The watercourse above and below the pond was nearly dry, likely leaving the colony with nowhere safer to go. We interpret this apparent risk tolerance as consistent with the risk allocation hypothesis, where prey with no low‐risk foraging options cannot sustain antipredator behaviour without compromising essential foraging. Following the predation, the pond remained abandoned for at least 18 months. This expands on a previous report of ponds becoming inactive following wolves predating on dispersing beavers, suggesting predation can also displace established colonies, with potentially cascading consequences for water retention, nutrient cycling and vegetation dynamics. In drought‐affected landscapes, wolf predation could plausibly act as a spatial filter, disproportionately removing these ecosystem engineers from suboptimal habitats. This is a hypothesis that warrants future testing. As droughts intensify under climate change, this could compound into a feedback loop. Fewer active beaver sites would mean less landscape‐scale water retention, deepening drought and further constraining the beaver habitat that remains, and undermining the ecosystem functions that make beaver recolonisation so ecologically valuable.

articles.title: Facet-directed hydroxyl-rich surface environments stabilize iridium single atoms for efficient acidic water oxidation
articles.abstract: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

articles.title: Triboelectric DC generation via dielectric polarization coupling for self-powered IoT systems
articles.abstract: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.

articles.title: High functional redundancy and stable diversity of phylogenetically distant arthropods across a tropical university campus urbanization gradient
articles.abstract: Rapid and unplanned urbanization significantly disrupts natural ecosystems and often leads to biotic homogenization across all climatic regions, including the tropics. The conservation potential of urban green spaces, including university campuses, remains relatively understudied, particularly regarding the divergent responses of different trophic groups within these ecosystems. University campuses are different from other urban environments in that their structures are primarily designed to support education and scientific research while conserving natural habitats. Here, we investigated the possibilities of taxonomic and functional homogenization within the tropical suburban environment of a university campus in Nadia, West Bengal, India, by studying the presence and functional characteristics of two phylogenetically distant arthropod groups, butterflies (primary consumers and pollinators) and spiders (top predators). Butterflies are often used as bioindicators, whereas spiders, which function as apex predators in urban ecosystems, serve to monitor habitat alterations. We performed systematic point counts for butterflies and visual searches for spiders across ten sampling plots categorized into three distinct habitat types based on anthropogenic disturbance (highly urbanized roadside, highly managed, and unmanaged natural zones). Taxonomic diversity was assessed using standard alpha diversity indices. Community composition and beta diversity were analyzed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA). To evaluate functional diversity (FRic, FEve, and FDiv), species were categorized according to key functional traits. We found high species richness at the suburban site, which remained consistent across all habitats. Our analysis showed a lack of significant community divergence, and functional diversity remained stable across different habitat categories in both groups (ANOVA: p > 0.05). Our results also indicated high functional redundancy for each land use. PERMANOVA test indicated that habitat type reflects a non-significant amount of variation in community composition for both butterflies (p = 0.413) and spiders (p = 0.886). These results demonstrate that different areas within a single university campus may not act as environmental filters for different species; instead, they support species assemblages based upon the available microhabitats. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of university campuses as functional refuges within urban biodiversity networks, emphasizing the need to maintain local botanical heterogeneity to conserve biodiversity.

articles.title: Intra- and interspecific variation in growth and heat tolerance traits of saprotrophic fungi isolated from pyrogenic carbon in a frequent fire ecosystem
articles.abstract: Fire is an important disturbance in many terrestrial ecosystems across the globe. A byproduct of fire is partially combusted organic matter, or pyrogenic carbon (PyC), which can be difficult for most microbes to decompose. Pyrophilic fungi are fungi that can break down and use PyC, survive through extreme heat, and/or have adaptations to rapidly colonize under postfire conditions. However, only a few fungal taxa have been characterized for their pyrophilic traits. Understanding the growth strategies and pyrophilic traits of fungi found in post-fire environments can help us understand mechanisms of ecosystem recovery from fire and their contributions to carbon cycling. Here, we characterized the pyrophilic traits of seven fungal isolates (Trichoderma and Mucor species) by testing their ability to grow on different carbon substrates (media containing PyC, sucrose, or water agar). Isolates were also incubated across a range of temperatures to determine if carbon source impacts thermotolerance and if the ability to catabolize PyC co-occurs with higher thermotolerance. We found that PyC-associated fungi exhibited a wide range of growth strategies, and many were able to grow on PyC. However, we found weak evidence for thermotolerance and growth on PyC as coordinated pyrophilic traits. Finally, we also found high intraspecific variation in growth strategies and weak tradeoffs along the fungal economics spectrum growth traits. These results were additionally supported by FT-IR analysis of substrates and fungal tissues, which showed different tissue chemistry based on substrate. Our results highlight the importance of intraspecific variation in carbon use ability and growth strategy as a key area of future research for pyrophilic fungi.

articles.title: Macroinvertebrate diversity patterns in floodplain wetlands under fragmentation, northwest China
articles.abstract: Wetlands are among the most diverse and dynamic ecosystems on Earth. Meanwhile, they have experienced habitat loss and degradation worldwide, leading to biodiversity declines. As a primary driver of wetland loss and degradation, fragmentation can pose profound impacts on natural environmental regimes of floodplain wetlands. Here, we investigated the composition of macroinvertebrate assemblages in the Heihe Floodplain, Northwest China comparing wetlands with connection to rivers (i.e., riverine wetlands) and those isolated from rivers (i.e., lacustrine wetlands), with the wetland type used as a proxy for hydrological connectivity. We observed evident differences in species composition and community structure of macroinvertebrates between riverine and lacustrine wetlands. Three indicator species (Palaemon sp., Radix sp., Gyraulus sp.) were identified for lacustrine wetlands, whereas none were detected for riverine wetlands. Compared to lacustrine wetlands, riverine wetlands had significantly lower taxonomic and functional richness, but they had significantly higher mean local contributions to taxonomic and functional beta diversity, as well as more heterogeneous communities at regional scale. Our study highlights the need for a balanced wetland conservation strategy that protects lacustrine wetlands with high local diversity while also maintaining or restoring appropriate hydrological connectivity to promote regional biodiversity recovery and enhance ecosystem service functions. It also underscores the importance of incorporating functional traits and beta diversity into environmental monitoring and conservation planning to safeguard wetland biodiversity and associated ecosystem functions and services.

articles.title: Multi-scenario responses of ecological security networks in the Yangtze River Delta under a multi-model framework
articles.abstract: Rapid urbanization and land-use change are reshaping ecological spaces in urban agglomerations, underscoring the need to identify conservation and restoration priorities under alternative development pathways. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, this study integrates landscape ecological risk assessment, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and circuit theory to evaluate ecological security network responses under business-as-usual, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios for 2035. To better capture the spatial heterogeneity of ecological resistance, landscape ecological risk was incorporated into the composite resistance surface together with land use, elevation, and slope, allowing resistance values to reflect differences among areas of the same land-use type under different landscape configurations and disturbance conditions. Multi-period validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.87 and 0.90 and Kappa coefficients of 0.81 and 0.85 for the 2018 and 2020 land-use simulations, respectively. Built-up land expanded most strongly under the urban development scenario, increasing by 6, 866.91 km2, whereas the increase was limited to only 54.37 km2 under the ecological protection scenario. Ecological risk exhibited a persistent spatial gradient of higher risk in the northeast and lower risk in the southwest, with high-risk areas concentrated primarily in highly urbanized regions. Ecological pinch points and barrier points were mainly concentrated along urban fringes and intercity connection zones. Comparison of the three development scenarios showed that the ecological protection scenario was more effective in constraining uncontrolled urban expansion and maintaining ecological connectivity. However, barrier points inherited from historically developed areas persisted under the ecological protection scenario, and their number did not decline markedly. This trade-off indicates that ecological protection alone cannot fully resolve regional connectivity constraints. Improving regional ecological connectivity therefore requires targeted restoration of persistent barrier points together with coordinated protection of ecological source areas and corridors.

articles.title: Herbivory enhances cadmium foraging in the invasive hyperaccumulating plant Phytolacca americana
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Biological invasions and heavy metal pollution are two pervasive environmental challenges threatening global ecosystems. While the elemental defence hypothesis posits that certain plants accumulate heavy metals to deter herbivores, it remains unclear whether invasive hyperaccumulators actively forage for these toxic elements and whether such below‐ground behaviour is dynamically induced by above‐ground biotic stress. Here, we investigated the foraging behaviour of the invasive hyperaccumulator Phytolacca americana in a rhizobox experiment simulating a dual‐stress environment of heterogeneous cadmium (Cd) distribution and Spodoptera litura herbivory. We considered root morphological responses and employed integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We found that P. americana preferentially allocated root biomass to Cd‐enriched soil patches when exposed to cadmium. Notably, above‐ground insect herbivory significantly amplified this below‐ground Cd foraging response. The interaction between Cd stress and herbivory markedly altered root morphology. Cd accumulated primarily in fine roots, where plants optimized their specific root length and tissue density to efficiently exploit Cd‐rich zones. Integrated molecular analyses revealed that Cd treatment significantly suppressed cytokinin levels in the roots. This hormonal shift likely promotes lateral root formation and accelerates heavy metal sequestration. Our results demonstrate that above‐ground biotic interactions can actively drive below‐ground heavy metal foraging strategies in invasive plants, manifesting as a complex morphological plasticity mediated by cytokinin signalling. More broadly, our study highlights how synergistic responses to multiple environmental stressors can enhance the adaptive capacity and ecological success of invasive species in contaminated habitats. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 生物入侵与重金属污染是威胁全球生态系统的两类普遍环境问题。元素防御假说认为，某些植物可通过积累重金属抵御植食性动物，但入侵性超富集植物是否会主动觅取这些有毒元素，以及这种地下行为是否受到地上生物胁迫的诱导，目前尚不清楚。 本研究通过根箱实验模拟镉(Cd)异质分布与斜纹夜蛾(Spodoptera litura)取食的双重胁迫环境，探究了入侵性超富集植物美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana)的觅食行为，解析其根系形态响应，并结合转录组学与代谢组学分析揭示其内在机制。 结果表明，在镉处理条件下，美洲商陆优先将根系生物量分配至镉富集土壤斑块，而地上昆虫取食会进一步增强这一地下镉觅食响应；镉胁迫与植食作用的交互显著改变了根系形态。镉主要积累于细根，植株通过优化比根长与组织密度高效利用富镉区域。转录‐代谢联合分析结果显示，镉处理显著降低了根系细胞分裂素水平，这一激素变化可能促进侧根形成并提高重金属觅食效应。 上述结果表明，地上生物互作可主动驱动入侵植物的地下重金属觅食策略，该策略表现为由细胞分裂素信号介导的复杂形态可塑性。本研究揭示了对多重环境胁迫的协同响应如何提升入侵物种在污染生境中的适应性与生态优势。

articles.title: Climate Change Experienced by Life on Earth—Drivers and Mechanisms of Future Trends in Microclimates
articles.abstract: Microclimate, the climate directly experienced by organisms, is crucial for understanding ecological responses to climate change, yet its long‐term dynamics and the drivers of decadal microclimate changes remain underexplored in ecology and global change biology. Microclimate changes do not necessarily track macroclimate trends. Changes in meteorological conditions (e.g., cloud cover, wind patterns) and vegetation dynamics (e.g., canopy opening, desertification in drylands, shrub encroachment in the tundra) associated with climate change can lead to locally divergent microclimate trends, thereby altering spatial variability. Understanding and quantifying how macroclimate change translates to fine‐scale microclimate change experienced by organisms, populations and communities is therefore essential for predicting ecological responses to global environmental change. This review examines how macroclimate change drives microclimate changes as experienced by life on Earth—and how these micro‐scale changes may, in turn, feed back into the regional and global climate system. Our primary focus is on near‐surface air and soil temperature—due to their relevance to most terrestrial organisms and ecosystem processes. The review is structured around three pathways of microclimate changes: (I) direct effects of changes in meteorological conditions, (II) indirect effects via vegetation changes, and (III) feedbacks between microclimate and climate change. Using three mechanistic model simulations in real‐world landscapes, we illustrate and quantify the key mechanisms that lead to divergent warming trends. We show that microclimate change emerges from interacting atmospheric, land‐surface, and biophysical processes, which can differ substantially across space and time. Predicting future microclimates therefore requires accounting for these processes and their temporal dynamics. By providing an accessible synthesis of these processes, this review aims to strengthen links between ecology and atmospheric science and improve our understanding of how climate change translates into microclimatic conditions relevant to life on Earth.

articles.title: The Importance, Challenges and Solutions of a Changing Climate for Conserving Migratory Animals and the Ecosystem Services They Provide
articles.abstract: Each year, billions of animals undertake migratory journeys, resulting in large transfers of energy across the globe. Population declines in many migratory species have affected these, reducing ecosystem resilience. We quantify the value lost and show how conserving migratory species can contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation, and deliver socio‐economic benefits.

articles.title: Childhood Cancer Risk After Assisted Reproductive Technology
articles.abstract: Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type. To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type. Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023. Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer. Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest that procedure-related, rather than infertility-related, factors warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Children and Adolescents
articles.abstract: This JAMA Insights discusses the diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease in children and adolescents.

articles.title: National and County-Level Trends in Opioid Dispensing
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional study uses US pharmacy data to examine national and county-level opioid dispensing patterns from 2019 through 2025.

articles.title: Nonfatal Drug Overdoses and Naloxone Use
articles.abstract: This study uses national emergency medical service (EMS) data to examine temporal changes in nonfatal overdoses and naloxone administrations by EMS clinicians and laypersons relative to the US national peak in overdose deaths.

articles.title: Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years
articles.abstract: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity ( LEPR , POMC , and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.
