In vivo virus-free lineage tracing and live imaging reveal that NeuroD1 does not reprogram microglia into neurons
articles.abstract: In situ glia-to-neuron conversion induced by a single transcription factor is a promising regenerative strategy for treating central nervous system injuries and neurodegenerative diseases. Previous studies reported that NeuroD1 can induce microglia-to-neuron cross-lineage conversion and improve recovery after brain injury. However, these findings remain controversial. To examine the ability of NeuroD1 in inducing microglia-to-neuron conversion, we employed virus-free genetic lineage-tracing systems in mice to specifically induce NeuroD1 expression in microglia and track the cell fate of NeuroD1-expressing cells at multiple timepoints. Meanwhile, we longitudinally monitored NeuroD1-expressing microglia via two-photon imaging and characterized their transcriptional profile by single-cell RNA sequencing. All observations across these methods revealed that NeuroD1-expressing cells retained their microglia identity and cannot convert into neurons, no matter under physiological and injury conditions. Instead, sustained expression of NeuroD1 facilitated microglia apoptosis in vivo. Collectively, our findings provide strong evidence that NeuroD1 alone is not sufficient to induce microglia-to-neuron conversion. This study further highlights the importance of rigorous lineage-tracing and cell fate-mapping strategies for validating in situ glia-to-neuron conversion.

articles.title: Individual dopaminergic neurons induce unique, yet overlapping combinations of behavioural modulations, including safety learning, memory retrieval, and acute locomotion
articles.abstract: Two evolutionary highly conserved functions of dopamine are to carry ‘teaching’ signals during associative learning and to control movement. In mammals and humans, these functions are generally thought to be produced by different populations of neurons. Here, we investigated in the larva of Drosophila melanogaster whether both these functions can be induced by the same individual dopaminergic neurons in the central brain. Focusing on the dopaminergic neurons of the DL1 cluster, we asked whether the optogenetic activation of individual neurons established associative punishment and/or safety memories, controlled the retrieval of the established memories, and acutely modulated locomotion. We found that each neuron had a unique yet overlapping set of behavioural effects. Several individual neurons both established a memory and modulated acute locomotion by increasing the animals’ bending and decreasing their velocity. Our results demonstrate that individual dopaminergic neurons can fulfil a surprisingly broad range of functions in different behavioural contexts. Given the highly conserved roles of the dopaminergic system across the animal kingdom, this study raises the question whether a similarly diverse functionality can be found also in other animals, including humans.

articles.title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans
articles.abstract: The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining eight pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). We found that the anterior-most INT1 cells are a translationally distinct intestinal subcompartment that is particularly enriched for immune- and stress response genes. Functional assays using novel INT1-specific genes emerging from this study reveal that these specialized cells play a previously unappreciated role in pathogen avoidance and organismal survival. A second critical function of INT1 cells is their role in sensing and responding to the contents of the gut lumen. We show that luminal pyruvate is the key signal linking bacterial nutrients in the gut to secretion of the gut insulin antagonist INS-7. These findings establish INT1 as sentinel enteroendocrine cells that integrate metabolic and immune cues to couple food status with immune and endocrine responses. Our studies also provide a rich resource for dissecting segment-specific intestinal biology, an overlooked and fertile area for future research.

articles.title: Separable downmodulation of meiotic axis protein deposition and DNA break induction at chromosome ends
articles.abstract: In many organisms, meiotic crossover recombination is suppressed near the extreme ends of chromosomes. Here, we show that multiple, often chromosome-specific, suppressive mechanisms with differing ranges contribute to the consistently low enrichment of recombination-promoting axis proteins and the downregulation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within 20 kb of telomeres in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Suppression of axis proteins is associated with cis-encoded signals and correlates with reduced coding density, although whether this sequence feature actively drives suppression remains to be determined. In addition, axis protein suppression requires the histone methyltransferase Dot1 and the Sir silencing complex. We show that Dot1 suppresses Sir complex activity at least in part independently of its canonical target, H3K79, to downmodulate axis protein deposition near chromosome ends. In parallel, the Sir complex, but not Dot1, suppresses the induction of DSBs at a small number of cryptic hotspots by limiting the openness of promoters, the preferred sites of meiotic DSB formation. Much of the reduced DSB induction near chromosome ends persists in dot1 and sir3 mutants, indicating that additional layers of regulation contribute to the robust reduction of meiotic recombination effectors near chromosome ends.

articles.title: Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS2/WS2-Nb2CTx Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
articles.abstract: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

articles.title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
articles.abstract: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

articles.title: A Review of Beyond GDP: History, Barriers, Opportunities, and Cautions
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Gross domestic product (GDP) remains the dominant measure of economic progress, despite long-standing critiques including its failure to account for environmental sustainability, inequality, and social well-being. In the context of escalating climate breakdown and rising inequality, GDP is increasingly being recognized as an inadequate metric for national prosperity. This article reviews the growing movement toward alternative measures that prioritize sustainability, inclusion, and the well-being of humans and the rest of nature. Hundreds of alternatives exist, but recent research shows significant similarity among them, forming the basis for building a broad consensus. This review explores how academics and policy makers are responding to the limitations of standard national accounts and highlights broad public support for expanding economic indicators. This review also identifies the key barriers to be overcome in order to move beyond GDP—including vested interests, institutional buy-in, and the fragmentation of alternatives—and suggests strategies to address each. By examining these barriers and evaluating potential solutions within the current political landscape, this review contributes to the discourse on how national accounting systems can better evolve to reflect the goals of a just and sustainable economy embedded in society and the rest of nature.

articles.title: Expanded Urban Innovation for the Twenty-Second Century: From Cutting Emissions to Enabling Flourishing Lives on a Thriving Planet
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Cities are central to the climate challenge, but much research on urban climate action still focuses on emissions reductions within existing systems. This literature review assesses existing research and literature, including work on human-need-driven innovation for global sustainability and the export of globally sustainable solutions. Rather than limiting urban climate action to measures aimed at reaching zero emissions, the review examines an expanded urban innovation agenda in which cities are studied as incubators and exporters of innovations that support flourishing lives for all on a flourishing planet. The review synthesizes insights from sustainability transitions, sociotechnical systems, well-being economics, artificial intelligence, and brain science. Case studies from different cities illustrate how some urban innovation agendas are already shifting. The comparison highlights how a focus on flourishing lives can mobilize start-ups, youth, and public institutions, while addressing equity and positioning cities as actors in the next generation of urban climate action.

articles.title: Governing Solar Geoengineering at Planetary Scale: Pipe Dream or Possibility?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Solar geoengineering is being suggested by some scientists as a partial solution to the climate crisis. However, these hypothetical technologies to reflect parts of incoming sunlight back out into space pose significant governance challenges, due to their ecological risks, planetary scale, and long-term consequences. This review examines the literature on solar geoengineering governance since 2020, identifying three strands of debate. The first explores emerging research governance and institutional arrangements for potential future deployment. The second, critical, strand focuses instead on institutional pathways to prohibit such technologies. A third strand analyzes the debate itself, including through the lens of science and technology studies. While proposals for solar geoengineering are developed by small groups of researchers in industrialized countries, opposition is growing in the Global South, with governments from Africa and the Pacific calling for an international nonuse agreement. This growing resistance from vulnerable nations raises pressing moral and political questions about continuing research amid mounting global dissent.

articles.title: Managing Groundwater Salinization Toward Sustainability
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Groundwater, a crucial freshwater source worldwide, is under threat of salinization due to the combined pressures of climate change and human activities, hindering sustainable development. This review explores both natural and anthropogenic sources and mechanisms of groundwater salinization (GWS). We describe the impacts of GWS on environmental and socioeconomic systems, highlighting the risks to agriculture, water quality, and public health. We also discuss monitoring and assessment techniques and knowledge gaps essential for effective management. We present successful case studies of interventions in seven countries, showcasing the feasibility and difficulty of effective management and mitigation strategies. Finally, we address sustainability challenges and outline future directions for research and policy, emphasizing the need for a paradigm shift from reactive management to proactive, holistic, and adaptive stewardship.

articles.title: Metric Selection Framework: A Method for Optimizing Multidimensional Value Assessment of Resource Recovery Systems
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: This article introduces the metric selection framework (MSF), developed as part of the CVORR+ methodology. CVORR+ is a systems-based evaluation toolkit designed to support complex sustainability assessment and decision-making. Within CVORR+, the MSF translates system analysis into decision-oriented, multidimensional metrics for monitoring, assessment, and evaluation of progress toward sustainability targets. Grounded in a value-focused decision-making approach, the framework combines expert elicitation with stakeholder engagement to ensure that metrics are system grounded, context specific, and practically relevant. Applied to England's plastic packaging system, the MSF reveals systemic inefficiencies, identifies leverage points for intervention, and informs policy design to support systemic value recovery. The case study demonstrates the heuristic and practical value of the MSF in capturing interdependencies across environmental, economic, social, and technical domains. Future developments will streamline the translation from system conceptualization to metric development, ensuring that metrics are responsive to long-term monitoring and policy-making, remain aligned with technological and regulatory shifts, and enhance the robustness and transferability of CVORR+.

articles.title: Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in Global Area-Based Conservation
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) are an emerging area-based conservation mechanism aspiring to achieve long-term and effective in situ biodiversity conservation outside traditional protected areas. Contributing toward several global biodiversity targets, they combine protection with sustainable land use and human development. This review analyzes spatial and temporal trends in OECM site designation (2010–2024), exploring governance frameworks, management, and ecological effectiveness in reducing biodiversity loss, addressing environmental change, and promoting sustainable development. Emphasis is placed on inclusivity of OECMs, particularly engagement of local communities and Indigenous Peoples in stewardship and decision-making, thereby enhancing social equity and cultural relevance. Academic and policy attention has centered on two areas: ( a ) refining the OECM framework, its definition, characteristics, and alignment with international goals (Section 3), and ( b ) evaluating governance, effectiveness, and national/subnational implementation (Section 4). While OECMs offer potential to expand global conservation, issues around governance and site-level outcomes remain underexplored and warrant attention (Section 5).

articles.title: Social Energy Futures in the Global South: Geographies, Concepts, and Praxis
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Socioenvironmental research highlights the key role of communities and organizations in promoting sustainable and democratic energy systems. However, most of this emphasis has focused on modern industrialized societies. This article reviews research on energy alternatives conceptualized and practiced by movements and communities across the Global South. Based on the surveyed literature, we propose the concept of social energy futures (SEF) as an open-ended category to reflect on the drivers and features of these alternatives. As outlined, SEF are diverse and territorially situated, commonly encompassing three components: ( a ) they are largely needs-oriented, tending to prioritize use value over exchange value; ( b ) they involve broad political processes, defining how much energy should be harvested, through which technologies, by which actors, and for which purposes; and ( c ) they are part of broader identity struggles, reflecting how social actors actively organize to counteract colonial and corporate relations amid the energy and climate crisis. Taking these findings together, we propose an SEF analytical toolkit and outline future research themes to continue developing across diverse academic, cultural, and geographical settings.

articles.abstract: Synthesis of functionalized oxymethylene ethers (f-OMEs) with unsaturated end groups as valuable building blocks in the chemical industry. This study includes experiments performed in a batch reactor, kinetic modeling and product characterization.

articles.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
articles.abstract: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.

articles.title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
articles.abstract: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.

articles.title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation
articles.abstract: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.

articles.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
articles.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.

articles.title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression
articles.abstract: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.

articles.title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
articles.abstract: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.

articles.title: A pangenomic method for establishing a synthetic somatic variant resource in HapMap mixtures
articles.abstract: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.

articles.title: Detecting low-allele-fraction mosaic mutations: A multi-institution benchmarking with cell-line mixtures
articles.abstract: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.

articles.title: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection

articles.title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects against endometritis through a tyrosol-mediated gut-uterus axis
articles.abstract: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.

articles.title: Gemella morbillorum promotes colorectal tumorigenesis through barrier disruption and invasion-dependent DNA damage
articles.abstract: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.

articles.title: Prediction of immunotherapy response using live tumor fragments from routine clinical biopsies
articles.abstract: Predicting which patients will benefit from cancer immunotherapy remains challenging. Braun et al. use live tumor tissue from routine needle and forceps biopsies to measure ex vivo immunotherapy response. Results are consistent with clinical outcomes in a small patient cohort, including patients misclassified by current biomarker tests.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of high-current tTIS targeting left sgACC for major depressive disorder: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial
articles.abstract: Wang et al. demonstrate that high-current transcranial temporal interference stimulation targeting sgACC alleviates depression safely and delivers stronger short-term therapeutic effects than low-current or sham stimulation.

articles.title: Skin fibroblast lineage tracing reveals layer-specific cooperation in wound repair
articles.abstract: Guo et al. develop a multiplex lineage-tracing platform to systematically profile fibroblasts across all five anatomical layers of the skin. They uncover a highly coordinated, multi-stage sequence of fibroblast mobilization and architectural reorganization during wound healing, demonstrating that cell-intrinsic programs predominate over local microenvironments to govern layer-specific contributions.

articles.abstract: This Tutorial Review highlights recent advances in “programmed” photocontrol of polymer materials, combining multiple wavelengths of light or pairing light with non-optical stimuli to enable fabrication and degradation at desired locations and times.

articles.title: Living on the Edge: Ecological and Evolutionary Dynamics Along Invasion Fronts
articles.abstract: Invasion fronts are the advancing edges of non‐native species' ranges and represent dynamic, non‐equilibrium boundaries where colonization, biotic interactions and rapid evolutionary processes interact. Although biological invasions are increasingly well studied, the ecological and evolutionary mechanisms operating at invasion fronts remain conceptually fragmented despite their disproportionate influence on spread dynamics, exerted impact and management. Here, we synthesize how invasion‐front geometries arise from interactions among propagule pressure, landscape permeability, long‐distance dispersal and environmental heterogeneity, producing continuous (including satellite colonies), patchy/fragmented or coalescing fronts that shift with invasion stage and spatiotemporal scales. We integrate ecological and evolutionary evidence from macro‐organisms to show how gradients from core to front can result in declining population density, increased trait divergence, spatial sorting, serial founder effects, expansion load, and behavioural and physiological differentiation. We further draw parallels with climate‐driven range expansions, while emphasizing the stronger disequilibrium and novel biotic contexts characteristic of non‐native invasion fronts. Finally, we map these dynamics onto impact trajectories, demonstrating how trait‐mediated interactions, resource reallocation and system‐level reconfiguration can emerge sequentially along the invasion gradient. By unifying ecological and evolutionary processes across appropriate spatial and temporal scales, we establish invasion fronts as powerful natural laboratories and critical leverage points for predicting, monitoring and managing biological invasions.

articles.title: Chemical ecology in conservation biological control: status and emerging challenges
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, chemical ecology has become increasingly integrated into the development of biological control programs, particularly Conservation Biological Control (CBC). Conservation Biological Control exploits a set of habitat manipulation practices to maintain and enhance the reproduction, survival, and efficacy of arthropod natural enemies that prey upon or parasitize insect pests. Specifically, chemical cues that convey information between living organisms, named semiochemicals, can enhance the management of herbivore populations by mediating interactions among plants, herbivores, predators, parasitoids, and their surrounding habitats. Nevertheless, translating mechanistic knowledge of chemically mediated interactions into reliable control of pest insect populations remains a major challenge. A central constraint is the persistent gap between results obtained under simplified laboratory conditions and outcomes observed in dynamic agroecosystems, where background odors, meteorological conditions, crop phenology, and multispecies interactions can modify semiochemical production and transmission, receiver responses, and ultimately, biological control agent efficacy. Additional priorities include moving from the study of individual compounds to ecologically realistic blends of bioactive volatiles; identifying non-target and food-web effects; integrating semiochemical-based interventions with habitat management and selective crop-protection practices; and developing standardized field metrics that connect natural enemy recruitment with predation, parasitism, herbivore population control, and reduction in crop damage. Progress will therefore require multiscale experimentation, closer integration of analytical chemistry with behavioral and field ecology that balance efficacy, ecological safety, and operational feasibility. From this perspective, CBC involves more than enhancing the abundance or activity of arthropod natural enemies: it requires the deliberate management of information flow across multitrophic levels to establish a more predictive and mechanistically grounded framework for biological herbivore population control. Here, are reviewed the principal issues that chemical ecology should address to advance CBC, focusing on how semiochemical production, transmission, and perception vary across plant genotypes, herbivore communities, natural-enemy guilds, microbiomes, agricultural practices, and landscape contexts.

articles.title: Editorial: Intensively monitored watersheds – a tool to help us understand how ecological processes function and are effected by stream and watershed restoration
articles.abstract: How much is watershed management and the protection and restoration of habitat restoration contributing to salmon and steelhead population recovery? This question has led to expansion of research and monitoring programs whose goal is to understand and quantify the contribution watershed management and habitat restoration is making to salmon populations (Diefenderfer et al. 2016). One component of this evaluation effort has been the establishment of a network of watersheds where habitat treatments are coupled with intensive, long-term monitoring to evaluate physical and biological responses to these treatments (Bennett et al. 2016). These sites have been labeled Intensively Monitored Watersheds (IMWs) (Bilby et al. 2005;Bennett et al. 2016). Data required to evaluate the ecological response to habitat actions are expensive to collect and must be gathered over many years to provide confidence in their conclusions (Roni et al. 2008). Because they are costly to implement, IMWs occur in a few select locations with the goal of enabling enough data collection over a sufficient period to develop an understanding of fish and habitat response that can be applied more broadly to restoration efforts.The IMW approach has been used for over six decades to evaluate aquatic ecosystem response to land use practices and habitat restoration. The Alsea Watershed Study, which was initiated in the 1950s, evaluated the response of Coho salmon and Cutthroat trout to alternative logging methods in three small watersheds on the Oregon coast. Results from this study provided much of the technical rationale for the establishment of forestry regulations intended to protect aquatic habitat in the Pacific Northwest. In the 1970s, an ambitious watershed-level project was initiated at Carnation Creek on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, that evaluated the response of hydrology, water quality and salmonid fish populations to logging of a previously unlogged watershed (Tschaplinski, this volume). The results of this study led to a revision of the forestry code for B.C. and influenced revisions to forestry practice rules in other areas of the Pacific Northwest. In the early 2000s multiple IMWs were established in the Pacific Northwest to evaluate the response of habitat and fish populations to freshwater and estuarine salmon habitat restoration efforts. Similar long-term studies have been undertaken in other parts of the world where salmon recovery is an important societal objective.The IMW approach as it has been applied is not without flaws and complications (Bisson et al., 2024). Logistical challenges to implementing study designs due to differences between treated and references watersheds, complexity of statistical study designs, permitting, funding, and implementing habitat treatments have all been identified over the years, but despite these difficulties IMWs have generated information useful for improving restoration strategies (Bilby et al. 2022). Furthermore, intensive. long-term monitoring at watershed scales remains one of the few tools available for empirically quantifying the contribution habitat restoration can make to salmon population recovery.What were the objectives of this special issue?The goal of this issue, "IMWs -A tool to help us understand how ecological processes of stream ecosystems and how these processes are affected by stream and watershed restoration", was to identify ecosystem changes resulting from stream and watershed habitat restoration using the IMW framework and assess salmon and steelhead response to these changes.…

articles.title: Reconstructing early hominin behavioural ecology: a modelling approach
articles.abstract: IntroductionWe use a reverse engineering approach to develop a linear programming model for the behavioural ecology of early hominins (australopithecines).MethodsOur models are based on a recently developed family of empirical models that use climate to predict how animals allocate time to core activities and, from this, whether or not they can balance their activity budget at a specific location as a guide to whether they could survive there. We first use models developed for baboons and chimpanzees to predict whether australopithecines could have survived at sites where they are known to have been present, had they been ecological baboons or ecological chimpanzees. We show that none of the hominins behaved ecologically like either baboons or chimpanzees: the models for these genera fail to predict their known distribution. We then use the equations from the baboon and chimpanzee models to build a model that predicts the known distribution of the australopithecines more precisely.ResultsThe results suggest that they had evolved their own distinctive response to environmental parameters that seems to be related to exploiting a habitat (lacustrine and riverine flood plains) that no other living primate exploits. Our analysis suggests that, in exploiting open flood plain habitats, australopithecines likely foraged as a single group for protection against predators rather than living in fission-fusion communities like modern chimpanzees. The models indicate that climate change post 2.4 Ma resulted in declining group sizes leading to eventual extinction, associated with the appearance of early Homo with novel adaptations for coping with a warmer, drier climate.DiscussionOur analyses suggest that exploiting quantitative models can offer novel insights into the behavioural biology of extinct species, thereby providing rich insights into the forces that drove evolution within particular lineages.

articles.title: Plant invasion in mountain ecosystems reduces soil micro‐food web complexity at higher elevations
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. Changes in above‐ground vegetation can drive shifts in below‐ground biota, yet the effects of plant invasions on soil micro‐food web structure and complexity along elevational gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study examined the differences between the communities of native herbaceous plants invading Ageratina adenophora along an elevational gradient in the Gaoligong Mountains. We surveyed the composition of the plant community, measured the physicochemical properties of the soil and the enzyme activities of carbon and nitrogen acquisition. The complexity of the soil micro‐food web complexity index (including bacteria, fungi, nematodes and protists) using high‐throughput sequencing and network analysis. Structural equation modelling and two‐way ANOVA were used to analyse the effects of elevation, invasion and their interaction on the micro‐food web. We found that native plant diversity, soil micro‐food web complexity and soil carbon‐ and nitrogen‐acquiring enzyme activities all increased significantly with elevation. However, invasion by A. adenophora both reduced native plant diversity and altered the original elevation pattern of the soil micro‐food web. At the highest elevation (2300 m), the complexity index of the soil micro‐food web in native communities was approximately 4.8 units higher than in invaded communities, while the activities of the C‐acquiring enzymes of the soil were 135% higher and the activities of the N‐acquiring enzymes 119% higher. The complexity of the soil micro‐food web was directly influenced by plant diversity, soil nutrient cycling capacity and multitrophic diversity, whereas environmental factors such as mean temperature and soil moisture exerted indirect effects through soil nutrient status and cycling processes. Our findings demonstrate that the invasion of A. adenophora primarily affects high‐elevation ecosystems by reducing native herbaceous plant diversity, thus reducing the complexity of the micro‐food web of the soil and altering the carbon and nitrogen cycling of the soil. This study advances the mechanistic understanding of how plant invasions impact soil food webs and associated mountain ecosystem processes, providing insights into invasion management and control strategies. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 人为活动加速了山地生态系统中的植物入侵，影响了本地植物群落的结构和功能。地上植被的变化可以驱动地下生物群落的转变，但植物入侵沿海拔梯度对土壤微食物网结构和复杂性的影响及其潜在机制仍不清楚。本研究考察了高黎贡山紫茎泽兰(Ageratina adenophora)入侵群落与本地草本植物群落沿海拔梯度的差异。我们调查了植物群落组成，测定了土壤理化性质以及碳氮获取酶活性，并利用高通量测序和网络分析评估了土壤微食物网(包括细菌、真菌、线虫和原生动物)的复杂性。采用结构方程模型和双因素方差分析解析海拔、入侵及其交互作用对微食物网的影响。研究发现，本地植物多样性、土壤微食物网复杂性以及土壤碳氮获取酶活性均随海拔升高而显著增加。然而，紫茎泽兰入侵既降低了本地植物多样性，也改变了土壤微食物网的原有海拔格局。在最高海拔(2300 m)，本地群落的土壤微食物网复杂性指数比入侵群落高约4.8个单位，而土壤碳获取酶活性高135%，氮获取酶活性高119%。土壤微食物网复杂性直接受植物多样性、土壤养分循环能力和多营养级多样性的影响，而平均气温和土壤湿度等环境因素则通过土壤养分状态和循环过程发挥间接效应。本研究推进了对植物入侵如何影响土壤食物网及相关山地生态系统过程的机制理解，为入侵管理和控制策略提供了科学依据。

articles.title: Dan Kastner (1951–2026)
articles.abstract: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.

Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.

articles.title: The binding of OTULIN restrains LUBAC activity to prevent TNF-driven immunopathology
articles.abstract: Lyu et al. show that the interaction between the deubiquitinase OTULIN and the ubiquitin ligase LUBAC restrains LUBAC autoubiquitination and activity. Disrupting this interaction enhances Met1-linked ubiquitination at the TNF receptor complex, which increases NF-κB signaling and sensitizes mice to TNF-dependent toxicity. Thus, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction restricts Met1-linked ubiquitin signaling.

articles.abstract: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.

articles.title: Your battery may not be a battery
articles.abstract: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.

articles.title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
articles.abstract: Psilocybin promotes and stabilizes new connections between neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex, especially after stress. Baker et al. show that 5-HT2A receptor signaling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediates this effect but is not required for a mouse behavioral proxy of hallucinations.

articles.title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
articles.abstract: Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect—but may not necessarily determine—transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. Here we show that sleep-control neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila (dFBNs) produce slow-wave activity (SWA) that is causally linked to sleep. The dFBN ensemble contains bistable cells whose membrane voltages oscillate between hyperpolarized DOWN and depolarized UP states. The oscillations rely on interhemispheric competition of two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses. dFBN-restricted interference with glutamate release disrupts SWA and baseline as well as rebound sleep, whereas the optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep. dFBNs generate SWA throughout the sleep–wake cycle (despite mutual antagonism with arousing dopaminergic neurons) and adjust its power to sleep need via sleep history-dependent increases in excitability and homeostatic synaptic depression. The oscillatory format permits a continuous encoding of sleep pressure but requires mechanisms that convert the amplitude-modulated signal into binary sleep–wake states.

articles.title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience
articles.abstract: This study identifies a secreted phospholipase in the hippocampal dentate gyrus that mediates an aging-sensitive compensatory mechanism promoting cognitive resilience and neuroprotection.

articles.title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis
articles.abstract: This study identifies ependymal dysfunction as a mechanism linking inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid to increased ventricular permeability and periventricular pathology in multiple sclerosis.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal
articles.abstract: Seal is an artificial intelligence framework that predicts the effects of regulatory variants in 802 brain cell states, revealing spatiotemporal gene regulation and pinpointing cell types and developmental stages associated with neuropsychiatric conditions.

articles.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
articles.abstract: The experimental realization of intrinsic 2D kagome materials with controllable flat bands has remained challenging. Now a van der Waals kagome material family is shown to host an isolated, gate-tunable flat band down to the monolayer limit.

articles.title: Reaction–diffusion competition drives anomalous relaxation of vitrimers
articles.abstract: Vitrimers—polymers that form covalent networks—show glassy behaviour with viscosity decoupled from structural relaxation. This decoupling is now found to originate from a competition between chemical exchange reactions and diffusion processes.

articles.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
articles.abstract: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. A key requirement for scaling quantum processors is the ability to perform high-fidelity operations in parallel across many qubits. However, simultaneous control remains a major challenge in silicon devices, as fidelities typically degrade under parallel operation. Here we identify microwave-drive-induced a.c.-Stark shifts as the dominant source of this degradation in a five-qubit silicon spin array. We address this by introducing a scalable mitigation protocol based solely on pairwise phase calibrations. Using tailored control pulses on a shared control line, we achieve primitive X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99% for each qubit individually, with some approaching 99.999%. Furthermore, these fidelities are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits. During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain above the widely targeted fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%. By maintaining high-fidelity control during simultaneous operation, shared qubit-control lines can support the development of large-scale semiconductor quantum processors.

articles.title: One year of Commissioner’s National Priority Vouchers
A St‐derived genome contributes to the formation of the wheat BB genome
articles.abstract: Proposed evolutionary scheme for the formation of the BB genome and hexaploid wheat. The St genome contributed to the BB formation via two independent hybridization events with the SS ancestor. Summary Although substantial efforts have been made to identify the progenitor of the wheat BB genome, the precise donor remains elusive. In this study, we first investigated the origin of the BB genome using a BB‐specific atp6 gene harboring unique 5′‐end sequences, which is present in multiple copies and partially pseudogenized in the BB genome. BLAST searches revealed that multi‐copied atp6 (pseudo)genes occur exclusively in polyploid St‐genome species. An ultrametric phylogeny constructed from genome‐wide single‐copy genes resolved the divergence of Aegilops speltoides (SS genome) and the St genome c. 4 million years ago, coinciding with the estimated origin of the BB genome. Furthermore, genome‐wide single‐nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)‐based allele matching showed that the St genome best explains BB alleles after SS, with an SS : St SNP ratio of 3 : 1, suggesting that the St genome likely contributed to the BB formation via two independent hybridization events with the SS ancestor. Finally, we identified 52 BB‐specific genes to facilitate the search for the true BB donor or the transitional hybrid. This study provides compelling evidence for the St genome's critical contribution to the BB genome and advances our understanding of how the complex hexaploid genome of bread wheat was formed and reshaped over evolutionary time.

Preparing, pairing and recovering: how angiosperms coordinate double fertilization
articles.abstract: Specific gamete interaction questions in angiosperms. Summary Double fertilization is a defining reproductive characteristic of angiosperms. During this process, two sperm cells fuse separately with the egg cell and the central cell to generate the embryo and endosperm, the two core components of the seed. Recent studies have revealed that male and female gametes are maintained in tightly regulated prefusion states and that their subsequent interaction proceeds through a series of precisely controlled steps. A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
articles.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

articles.title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
articles.abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
articles.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

articles.title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
articles.abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

articles.title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
articles.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

articles.title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
articles.abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

articles.title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
articles.abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

articles.title: [Perspectives] Richard Dadd's beguiling art
articles.abstract: The Victorian painter Richard Dadd was born in 1817. By the time of his death in 1886 he had been detained in psychiatric hospitals for 42 years. Dadd's life trajectory once promised to be very different. He began to draw seriously at the age of 13 years and was admitted to London's prestigious Royal Academy Schools when he was 19 years old. There he excelled, winning prizes in drawing and painting. But any possibility of a distinguished career evaporated in 1843 when, experiencing delusions, he tragically murdered his father and was later admitted to London's Bethlem Hospital.

You can’t see what you don’t look for: why glycan function remains in the dark
articles.abstract: A weakness in glycobiology research is the insufficient integration of approaches used to connect glycan structure to function. From glycogene knockouts to understanding glycan structures, dynamics, and interactions, to determining whether a single glycan structure underlies a specific cellular function, no single approach provides sufficient information to establish these relationships. We argue that resolving glycan structure–function relationships requires the integration of complementary approaches spanning genetics, analytical glycomics, glycoengineering, structural biology, and computational modelling. The field stands at a transition point: from cataloguing glycan structures to understanding their diverse roles in regulating the biology of health and disease. Such an integrated approach will be critical for translating structural glycan information into mechanistic insights and, ultimately, informed glycoengineering and therapeutic design.

articles.title: Back to seedlings: rethinking the slow–fast continuum across tree life stages
articles.abstract: Forest dynamics have traditionally been interpreted through the lens of adult trees, yet most mortality occurs during the seedling stage, shaping future forests. A central assumption in ecology is that demographic trade-offs, such as the slow–fast continuum, operate consistently across ontogeny. However, increasing evidence challenges this view. Seedlings experience high pest-driven mortality, strong environmental filtering, and stochastic variation in dispersal and microsite conditions, which can decouple early-life performance from adult demography. We synthesize recent developments suggesting that seedling trade-offs may either reflect a scaled-down version of adult dynamics or diverge into alternative axes, such as the recruitment–stature axis. Recognizing these shifts is important, as climate change is likely to further reshape the regeneration process and alter community assembly in future forests.

articles.title: Socioeconomics and biodiversity in cities: moving beyond patterns to mechanisms
articles.abstract: Socioeconomic status–biodiversity associations are widely reported in cities. However, most studies remain correlational and cannot distinguish whether socioeconomic status drives biodiversity change, biodiversity shapes socioeconomic outcomes, or whether observed patterns reflect biodiversity gains versus losses. We propose a unifying framework organizing established mechanisms from diverse urban research into four hypothesized causal pathways: (A) investment-driven biodiversity enhancement, (B) disinvestment-driven biodiversity degradation, (C) biodiversity-driven socioeconomic improvement, and (D) biodiversity loss reinforcing socioeconomic decline. This framework supports pathway-specific study designs and helps practitioners anticipate whether biodiversity interventions will reduce or exacerbate inequality. Shifting from pattern description to mechanism identification is essential for credible inference and for informing urban planning and governance interventions aimed at reducing environmental inequality.

articles.title: Trees alone do not make forests
articles.abstract: Forest restoration is often evaluated based on tree cover, while other dimensions of ecosystem recovery remain depleted, simplified, or incompletely reassembled. We define this mismatch as hollow forest syndrome and propose deficit profiles and an adaptive framework to diagnose recovery gaps, identify limiting processes, and guide restoration toward whole-forest recovery.

articles.title: Foveated metamers of the early visual system
articles.abstract: The ability of humans to discriminate and identify spatial patterns varies across the visual field and is generally worse in the periphery than in the fovea. This decline in performance is revealed in many kinds of tasks, from detection to recognition. A parsimonious hypothesis is that the representation of any visual feature is blurred (spatially averaged) by an amount that differs for each feature, but that in all cases increases with eccentricity. Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the ‘critical’ scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2° of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.

articles.abstract: Bovine mammary tissue can support infection and replication of diverse influenza A viruses and may provide an environment in which different viral strains can co-infect cells.

articles.title: The petal identity gene PhDEF has a major binding and regulatory action in the epidermis
articles.abstract: In flowering plants, floral organ identity is specified by the combinatorial action of homeotic genes. While the role of these genes in the early specification of organ identity is well established, their late function throughout floral organ development and in specific cell types is much less characterized. In particular, since plant organs are structured in clonally independent cell layers, whether and how homeotic identity interacts with cell layer identity is unknown. We have previously identified cell layer-specific mutants for the petal identity gene PhDEF in petunia flowers, resulting in drastically different petal phenotypes whether PhDEF is expressed in the petal epidermis or in the mesophyll. In this study, using a combination of single-cell RNA-Seq and chromatin immunoprecipitation on phdef cell layer-specific mutants, we find that PhDEF regulates a different set of target genes in the petal epidermis and mesophyll, with a major regulatory action in the epidermis. We uncover a high diversity of binding profiles in PhDEF target genes, with a complex combination of layer-specific or non-specific binding sites, and a much more prominent binding of PhDEF in the epidermis than in the mesophyll. Our study highlights that floral homeotic genes like PhDEF can have different regulatory actions in different cell contexts, here different cell layers, demonstrating that cell layer identity indeed influences the regulatory processes underlying homeotic identity.

articles.title: Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Enables Energy-Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide and Carbonate Coproduction from CO-Rich Flue Gas and Air
articles.abstract: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. However, COOR has rarely been implemented in practical paired electrolysis systems because of modest device-level performance, reliance on purified CO feedstocks, and operational instability. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Under high-current-density operation, in situ surface analysis revealed that interfacial carbonate accumulation causes anodic passivation and current decay. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.

articles.title: Tautomeric Metal-Polymer Coordination Enables Damage-Free Laminated Carbon Electrodes in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. However, mechanical stress during lamination and the large work-function mismatch between the CE and the electron transport layer (ETL) can compromise performance. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy utilizing a silver-2-mercaptobenzothiazole (Ag-MBT) metal-polymer buffer layer to enable high-efficiency inverted CE-based PSCs (C-PSCs). XPS reveals Ag-induced changes in the sulfur and nitrogen chemical environments of MBT, consistent with the formation of an Ag-MBT interfacial coordination layer involving Ag–S coordination. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.

articles.title: Unlocking Quantum Confinement in Two-/Three-Dimensional Tin-Based Perovskites for High-Efficiency Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.

Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy as a Window into the Molecular Structure and Dynamics of Electrolytes and Ionic Liquids: A Review
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.
