A spatial map of the atmospheric limb of a hot Jupiter
articles.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. Here we apply the novel transmission strings mapping method to the hot Jupiter WASP-17 b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can also map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6–12 μm. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with an approximately 650 K temperature difference between the morning ( $$85{8}_{-233}^{+434}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 85 8 − 233 + 434 K ) and evening $$1{,}52{2}_{-114}^{+116}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 1 , 52 2 − 114 + 116 K ). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H 2 O and CO 2 to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints for results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique, combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17 b, pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry.

articles.title: Reframing cancer therapy through tumor plasticity
articles.abstract: de Sauvage and colleagues discuss the latest advances in therapy-driven cancer plasticity processes and how this knowledge might be applied to clinical strategies.

articles.title: Stroke-induced astrocyte memories promote glioma progression
articles.abstract: The impact of earlier brain insults on the glioblastoma microenvironment is poorly understood. A study now shows that prior stroke alters astrocytes to promote glioblastoma growth and invasion via downregulation of calcium signaling.

articles.title: Compartment-specific PPARδ activity controls the outcome of cancer–immune cell competition and immunotherapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Cancer cells and immune cells compete for metabolic fitness within the tumor microenvironment. Here the authors show that PPARδ is instrumental in this battle and that activating it in immune cells can boost immunotherapy in resistant mouse tumors and improve human chimeric antigen receptor T cells.

articles.title: Evidence for maternal autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of preterm birth
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences. Preterm labor is linked to breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance. Rackaityte et al. report that some pregnant mothers harbor maternal autoantibodies, including those against IL-1 receptor antagonist, that may contribute to preterm delivery.

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function
articles.abstract: Editorial Expression of Concern: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function

articles.title: Making AI work in healthcare
articles.abstract: Drawing on experiences across diverse settings, this issue of Nature Medicine explores the challenges of and lessons learned from the deployment of artificial intelligence models into healthcare.

articles.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial
articles.abstract: A phase 1 trial shows that treatment of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer with personalized neoantigen vaccines combined with PD-1 blockade was feasible and led to tumor-specific immune responses in many patients and putative mechanisms of resistance related to antigen presentation were identified via cell-free DNA analysis.

articles.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: In the randomized multicenter phase 2 ZZ-FIRST trial, patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor talazoparib combined with androgen receptor inhibitor enzalutamide had an improved prostate-specific antigen response compared with enzalutamide alone, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of paired biopsies linked AR inhibition-induced suppression of HRR-related programs to proliferation arrest rather than functional HRR deficiency.

articles.title: Integrating sex as a biological variable into one’s science
articles.abstract: Addressing sex-related variation might seem like an experimental or data analysis time-sink. It’s not.

articles.title: LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
articles.abstract: The ubiquitous availability of protein structures permits replacing sequence alignment with more accurate and sensitive structure alignment algorithms. LoL-align maximizes a local log-odds score for proteins to be homologous, given their intra-protein C α − C α distances. Here we show that LoL-align is markedly more sensitive in detecting remote homologs than TM-align and Dali on single- and multidomain benchmarks and achieves better alignment quality at 5–20 × their speed. LoL-align is fully integrated into Foldseek.

articles.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
articles.abstract: This Article presents MassNet, a large-scale AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT). Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods.

articles.title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics
articles.abstract: A scalable cryogenic shock exfoliation method for the fabrication of large and uniform rhombohedral graphene flakes is demonstrated.

articles.title: Evidence for an excitonic insulator
articles.abstract: Using local probes and impurities on Ta2Pd3Te5 two experimental groups prove and characterize the presence of an excitonic gap via the impurity-induced breaking of excitonic pairing.

articles.title: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene
articles.abstract: Gate-voltage sweeps drive a first-order sliding transition between Bernal-dominant and rhombohedral–Bernal mixed stacking in marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene, which allows for non-volatile on/off switching of the low-temperature ferromagnetic phase.

articles.title: Sliding ferroelectricity scales up
articles.abstract: Wafer-scale growth of a metastable rhombohedral boron nitride polytype takes sliding ferroelectricity from handcrafted structures in the laboratory towards integrated devices.

articles.title: Ring attractor networks go full circle
articles.abstract: Clark et al. demonstrate that heterogeneous data-driven models implement head-direction selectivity through the same dynamical principles as classical ring networks. In doing so, the authors reconcile biological realism with theoretical simplicity, unifying existing frameworks and broadening the space of connectivity structures to be searched in data.

articles.title: Symmetries and continuous attractors in disordered neural circuits
articles.abstract: Head-direction cells are far more disorderly than classical continuous-attractor models allow. Clark et al. show that this disorder is nevertheless compatible with these models and that the underlying connectivity matrix hides a circular symmetry.

articles.title: A dynamic ruler for positional memory in regeneration
articles.abstract: Zebrafish can determine the amount of tissue to regrow after appendage amputation. Now, a study shows that a signal gradient that scales with the amount of tissue left to regenerate ensures that an amputated tailfin regrows to the correct length.

articles.title: Fusion digital twins from imperfect models
articles.abstract: Digital twins could transform how fusion plasmas are predicted, designed and controlled. We argue that realizing this promise requires multi-fidelity frameworks that systematically combine imperfect models and data while quantifying uncertainty.

articles.title: FDA new drug approvals in Q3 2026
Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Atomically ordered CuAuZn2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH2, while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.

articles.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
articles.abstract: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

articles.title: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes
articles.abstract: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.

articles.title: Adapting to Genomic Medicine
Adult Attention Deficit–Hyperactivity Disorder
articles.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

articles.title: Alkaptonuria
Case 29-2026: A 39-Year-Old Man with Abdominal Pain, Foot Drop, and a Spinal Mass
Chemotherapy-free Treatment of Ph-Positive ALL
Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non–Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes
articles.abstract: BackgroundContinuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.MethodsIn a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.ResultsA total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; PConclusionsAmong adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

articles.title: Continuous or Intermittent Renal-Replacement Therapy — What Is the Question?
Extended DAPT for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease
Integration-Associated Paraspinal Neoplasm after AAV Gene Therapy
Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.MethodsIn this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.ResultsThe trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.ConclusionsAmong critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

articles.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges
articles.abstract: BackgroundIn eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.MethodsWe conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, ResultsA total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).ConclusionsAmong persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

articles.title: Obinutuzumab in Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
Once-Weekly Mosnodenvir as Dengue Prophylaxis in a Human Infection Model
A suppressor screen uncovers flu as a weak mutant and chloroplastic 1O2 triggers EX1‐independent stress responses in Arabidopsis
articles.abstract: The logical basis and proposed model for 1O2 generation and dosage‐dependent signaling. See also the Commentary on this article by Grimm, 252: 1354–1356. Summary Singlet oxygen (1O2) is the main reactive oxygen species produced in chloroplasts, particularly under environmental stress conditions. Studies using the Arabidopsis conditional flu (flu1‐1) mutant have shown that chloroplastic 1O2 acts as a signal, activating retrograde signaling that eventually leads to photoinhibition or cell death. Through a forward genetic screen for suppressors using ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)‐mutagenized Arabidopsis flu1‐1/ex1 mutants, we isolated two suppressor mutants (mut1 and mut2) that restored 1O2‐induced stress responses. Using combined methods of map‐based cloning and high‐throughput sequencing, we mapped the causal mutations in both mut1 and mut2 to the FLUORESCENT (FLU) gene again. We verified that the widely used flu1‐1 is not the long‐recognized null mutant, but rather a weak allele, encoding a variant that binds weakly to GluTR1 and leads to partial shutdown of tetrapyrrole biosynthesis in the dark. We further found that the FLU‐knockout mutants produce more 1O2, activating transcriptional changes, enzymatic lipid peroxidation, and programmed cell death (PCD) even in the absence of EX1. Overexpression of SAFE1 suppressed 1O2‐induced PCD in mut2 in a dosage‐dependent manner. Collectively, our findings redefine the nature of the widely used flu1‐1 mutant and reveal that excessive 1O2 can overwhelm the inhibitory effect of endogenous SAFE1 and induce stress responses independently of EX1. 概括 单线态氧(1O2)是叶绿体中产生的主要活性氧(ROS)，在环境胁迫条件下大量产生。对拟南芥突变体flu(flu1‐1)的研究表明，叶绿体1O2可作为信号分子，激活逆行信号转导，导致光抑制或细胞死亡。 通过对EMS诱变的拟南芥flu1‐1/ex1突变体进行抑制子筛选，我们分离到了两个突变体(mut1和mut2)，它们恢复了1O2诱导的胁迫响应。结合图位克隆与高通量测序方法，我们将mut1和mut2中导致抑制子表型的突变位点均定位到FLU基因上。 长期以来，flu1‐1一直被认为是一个FLU蛋白缺失的无效突变体。我们的这项研究表明flu1‐1是一个弱等位突变体，编码一种与GluTR结合较弱的FLUA262V蛋白，部分抑制黑暗中四吡咯生物合成。FLU功能敲除突变体会产生更多的1O2，即使在缺乏EX1的情况下也能激活转录变化、酶促脂质过氧化反应和程序性细胞死亡(PCD)。在mut2中，SAFE1的过表达以剂量依赖的方式抑制了1O2诱导的程序性细胞死亡。 综上所述，本研究结果重新定义了广泛使用的flu1‐1突变体的分子本质，并揭示过量的1O2能够突破内源SAFE1的抑制作用，以不依赖EX1的方式诱导胁迫响应。

articles.title: Advancing the helox compensation method to estimate intercellular humidity in leaves of diverse species
articles.abstract: Distribution of intercellular relative humidity (left y‐axis) and the equivalent water potential of apoplastic liquid water at the evaporating site (right y‐axis) within and across species (GOHI, Gossypium hirsutum; HEAN, Helianthus annuus; HEAR, Heteromeles arbutifolia; LANO, Laurus nobilis; LITU, Liriodendron tulipifera; MAGR, Magnolia grandiflora (wi, winter (January 2026); sp, spring (May 2025)); PYHA, Pyrrosia hastata; ORSA, Oryza sativa). Symbols are results from individual nitox–helox switches (i.e. technical replicates) and colored lines are within‐species means. Summary The relative humidity in the intercellular airspaces of leaves (h) has long been thought to be saturating, but several recent studies have questioned this assumption. We present and develop a method to estimate h, describe practical considerations for its application, and demonstrate it on eight species (Gossypium hirsutum, Helianthus annuus, Heteromeles arbutifolia, Laurus nobilis, Liriodendron tulipifera, Magnolia grandiflora, Oryza sativa, and Pyrrosia hastata). N2/O2 (nitox) is replaced with He/O2 (helox), which speeds stomatal diffusion, but ambient humidity is simultaneously increased to keep transpiration rate unchanged. This allows the expressions for transpiration in nitox and helox to be set equal to one another, leading to a solution for h. We were able to rapidly switch to helox and simultaneously change humidity such that transpiration rate remained unchanged to within ±2.5% (< 0.54% in most cases). We found h ranging between 71 and 94% of saturation. Whereas other methods to estimate h either require special analytical tools (isotopic gas analysis, spectroscopically resolved fluorescence measurements with proprietary fluorophores) or special conditions (amphistomatous broad leaves with zero CO2 exchange at one leaf surface), our method requires only water vapor concentration measurements and can be performed on any leaf under nearly any conditions.

articles.title: Biocrusts contribute to shrub nitrogen nutrition via soil transfer in resource‐limited drylands
articles.abstract: Biocrusts and shrubs commonly coexist in semiarid drylands. 15N2 and 13CO2 labeling showed that biocrust‐fixed N was detected in shallow soil, shrub roots, and leaves, whereas biocrust‐fixed C remained mainly within biocrusts and soils and shrub‐fixed C was retained within plant tissues. Hyphal exclusion did not reduce shrub 15N enrichment, suggesting that N transfer was more consistent with soil‐mediated redistribution than direct hyphal transport. Together, shrub‐driven habitat amelioration and biocrust‐derived N inputs may support the functioning and stability of dryland ecosystems. Icons were obtained from Magnific (www.magnific.com; designed by Magnific). Summary Biocrusts and xeric shrubs commonly coexist in drylands, forming shrub–biocrust patches that shape soil processes and ecosystem functioning. While biocrusts are important sources of newly fixed nitrogen (N) and carbon (C), it remains unclear how C and N move between biocrusts and shrubs, whether transfer is bidirectional or asymmetric, and which pathways mediate exchange. Using whole‐atmosphere isotope pulse labeling combined with experimental manipulation of hyphal access in a semiarid shrubland, we traced biocrust‐fixed N (15N2), biocrust‐fixed C (13CO2), and shrub‐fixed C (13CO2). Biocrust‐fixed N was detected in shallow soils and subsequently in shrub roots and leaves. Restricting hyphal access did not reduce 15N enrichment in shrub aboveground tissues, indicating that N transfer over the one‐month observation period was consistent with soil‐mediated redistribution rather than being dominated by direct hyphal transport. By contrast, biocrust‐fixed C remained largely confined to biocrust and soil compartments, with no detectable incorporation into shrub tissues. Shrub‐fixed C was retained within plant tissues and did not measurably enter biocrust or soil pools. Our results therefore reveal asymmetric, element‐specific redistribution, with biocrust‐derived N moving through soil into shrub tissues but no detectable reciprocal transfer of shrub‐derived C, highlighting biocrusts as important sources of plant‐available N in resource‐limited drylands.

articles.title: Comparative genomics reveals lineage‐associated structural variation and diversification in a barley fungal pathogen
articles.abstract: Genome‐wide copy‐number variation landscape highlights structural divergence across Puccinia hordei isolates and potentially links Cyp51 amplification to fungicide insensitivity. Summary Leaf rust, caused by Puccinia hordei, is a major barley disease worldwide. Despite repeated shifts in virulence, contrasting reproductive histories, and emerging fungicide insensitivity, the genomic basis of its diversification and adaptation remains poorly understood. In this study, we generated haplotype‐resolved, chromosome‐level genome assemblies for two isolates with contrasting virulence and analyzed 41 Australian isolates collected over 54 yr (1966–2020), integrating comparative and population genomics, mating‐type gene phylogenies, chromosome‐specific k‐mer profiling, genome‐wide copy‐number variation (CNV) analysis, and gene‐expression analysis. We identified a structurally dynamic chromosome characterized by repeat‐associated rearrangements, structural variation, and lineage‐associated CNV, representing the first evidence in a rust fungus of chromosome‐scale structural diversification of this extent. Population analyses distinguished clonally expanded lineages from recombination‐associated lineages, with mating‐type gene phylogenies providing further support for lineage differentiation. More recently collected isolates showed increased duplication‐associated variation, and CNV boundaries were associated with structural‐variant breakpoints. We also identified lineage‐associated amplification of Cyp51, with increased copy number associated with higher transcript abundance, supporting a potential role in fungicide adaptation. Overall, our findings highlight structural variation, contrasting reproductive histories, and lineage‐associated CNV as important contributors to diversification in P. hordei, providing insights for future rust pathogen surveillance and management strategies.

articles.title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism in Hematite
articles.abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (Fe2O3), supported by theoretical calculations.

articles.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
articles.abstract: A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that S = 3/2 magnets alone switch abruptly between two distinct spin-liquid states, a transition that survives the thermal fluctuations that wash all the other transitions into crossovers.

articles.title: Synergistic metal halide perovskite–metal-organic framework heterostructures: interfacial engineering for stable and multifunctional next-generation devices
A new megaraptoran dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Wessex Formation, UK, and its implications for theropod evolution and biogeography
articles.abstract: Theropod dinosaur remains from the Barremian (Lower Cretaceous) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK, are rare and often fragmentary. Here, we present a previously undescribed braincase from this formation that represents a new coelurosaurian, Invictibellatrix amberina gen. et sp. nov. Phylogenetic analysis and comparative anatomy indicate that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods from this stratigraphic unit. Theropod braincases are often regarded as morphologically and phylogenetically conservative, but we demonstrate that neurocranial characters provide essential data that can help clarify the phylogenetic relationships of theropods. The sub-circular occipital condyle, sub-oval foramen magnum and presence of a sagittal nuchal crest indicate that Invictibellatrix is referable to Megaraptora, with phylogenetic analyses recovering it as an early-diverging member of this clade, within a paraphyletic array of Eurasian taxa. Incorporation of Invictibellatrix into a biogeographical analysis suggests that non-megaraptorid megaraptorans likely had a cosmopolitan distribution in the Early Cretaceous, and that the absence of megaraptorans in the Late Cretaceous of Laurasia is best explained by regional extinction. The recognition of this new genus increases our knowledge of Early Cretaceous European coelurosaurian diversity, which now includes tyrannosauroids, maniraptoriforms and megaraptorans.

articles.title: A niche construction-based approach to evolution by natural selection without reproduction—proof of concept and implications
articles.abstract: In past decades, conceptual analysis has established that evolution by natural selection (ENS) can occur without reproduction (Bouchard 2008 Philos. Sci. 75, 560–570 (doi:10.1086/594507); Papale, 2021 Synthese 198, 10 429–10 455 (doi:10.1007/s11229-020-02729-6)). The aim of this paper is to provide a computational proof of concept for this theoretical advance and to start assessing some of its conceptual upshots. To do so, we designed an agent-based model that introduces and defends a niche construction-based account of ENS without reproduction (ENSwR, pronounced like ‘answer’). Our results provide a computationally tractable proof of concept for ENSwR and a basis to reflect on some of its conceptual implications for debates regarding the origins of life. First, conceptual analysis suggests that ENSwR provides a novel explanatory framework that supports origins of life theories in which autocatalytic sets (ACSs) of chemical reactions play a central role (Xavier, Kauffman 2022 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 380, 20210244 (doi:10.1098/rsta.2021.0244)). Second, through a discussion of the hydrothermal vent theory for the origins of life, we show that ENSwR will contribute to explaining the evolutionary origins of reproduction.

articles.title: Advanced oxidation processes for 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid in aqueous media: evidence gaps, mechanistic insights and emerging directions
articles.abstract: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. Records from Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar within a documented 2020–2025 review window were screened using explicit eligibility criteria and assessed with an evidence-completeness rubric covering key reporting domains for cross-study comparison. The final corpus comprised 204 studies across photocatalytic/photo-assisted, electrochemical/electro-Fenton, Fenton-type, sulfate-radical, ozone-based, sonochemical, plasma-assisted and hybrid systems. Parent 2,4-D removal or analytical confirmation was reported in 202 studies, while carbon-based mineralization or organic-load evidence was reported in 116, transformation products in 95, residual toxicity in 27, real-water validation in 67 and reactor-scale or transferability information in 37. These patterns show stronger evidence for parent-compound disappearance than for treatment completeness, residual hazard and transferability. No AOP family was universally superior across removal, mineralization, toxicity reduction, matrix robustness, energy demand, durability and scale readiness. Future studies should standardize reporting of mineralization, transformation products, toxicity, energy boundaries, leaching, durability and reactor descriptors.

articles.title: Choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents for efficient anthocyanin recovery from black rice: process, kinetics and nanoliposomal formulation
articles.abstract: This study investigated the recovery and nanoliposomal formulation of anthocyanin-rich extracts from black rice using choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). Choline chloride/1,2-propanediol (DES2) produced the highest anthocyanin content, 85.5 ± 3.4 mg l−1, after optimization, compared with 25.7 ± 2.1 mg l−1 obtained by conventional ethanol extraction. High-resolution QTOF-MS/MS enabled the tentative assignment of cyanidin 3-O-hexoside-type and peonidin 3-O-hexoside-type compounds based on accurate precursor masses and characteristic product ions; authentic-standard confirmation was not performed. The DES2 extract showed greater apparent thermal stability than the control extract, with estimated half-lives of 30.0 and 16.0 days, respectively, at 45°C. Anti-oxidant activity was observed in DPPH and ABTS assays, with IC50 values of 0.19 ± 0.06 and 0.16 ± 0.08 mg ml−1, respectively. Preliminary antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli was detected under the tested agar-diffusion conditions, whereas activity against Staphylococcus aureus was limited. Nanoliposomal encapsulation achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 73.8 ± 4.3%, a Z-average diameter of 201.3 nm and 89.83 ± 0.65% anthocyanin retention after 28 days at 4°C. The formulation produced a larger inhibition zone against E. coli than the free extract under the assay conditions. These findings support further investigation, although release kinetics, pharmaceutical efficacy and complete-process sustainability remain unestablished.

articles.title: Coupled CFD–DEM analysis of soil cavity formation and gas diffusion during buried pipeline leakage
articles.abstract: After the leakage of a buried pipeline, the overlying soil structure deforms under the high-speed impact of escaping gas, influencing both leakage and diffusion behaviours. This deformation typically appears as a soil cavity above the leakage port, especially in medium- and low-pressure conditions. In this study, the formation process of soil cavities is investigated using CFD–DEM coupled numerical simulations. The control variable method is applied to examine how different conditions affect cavity size and gas diffusion, and the sensitivity between cavity characteristics and leakage behaviour is analysed. Results show that the leaked gas forms a high-velocity zone near the leakage port, generating negative pressure in the surrounding area. Soil cavities generally form and stabilize within 0.1 s under gas impact. Soil particle size and porosity significantly influence the cavity formation time by altering the pore structure and total pore volume. The average sensitivity coefficients of the maximum cavity width to gas leakage velocity and the highest dangerous range (HDR) are 5.71 and 18.78, respectively, indicating that larger cavity widths correspond to higher leakage velocities and greater HDR. Therefore, the maximum cavity width serves as the most appropriate indicator for evaluating soil cavities caused by buried gas pipeline leakage.

articles.title: Ecological and life history traits predict urban tolerance in North American birds
articles.abstract: Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. Additionally, understanding whether shared evolutionary history influences urban tolerance could shed light on its evolutionary origins and reveal the extent to which urban landscapes filter out entire taxonomic clades, homogenizing biodiversity. Here, we assessed the relationship between urban tolerance and eight different life history and ecological traits for 431 North American bird species. We found that birds with higher urban tolerance are longer-lived, smaller-bodied, and more likely to be sedentary or mixed migrants than birds with lower urban tolerance. Birds with higher urban tolerance also have broader environmental tolerance, based on breeding range size and estimates of range-wide variation in precipitation, consistent with their greater likelihood of being habitat generalists. We additionally detected a phylogenetic signal for urban tolerance, with several clades sharing similar urban tolerance measures. Our study identifies several mechanisms that likely underlie species differences in urban tolerance and demonstrates how urban areas can filter bird species based on their life history and ecological traits.

articles.title: Effect of odour on prey pattern aversion in jumping spiders
articles.abstract: Many animals defend themselves with toxic chemicals and use multimodal warning displays involving odours and bright colours to advertise their toxicity. Yet, how coloration and odour interact and why they so often evolve together is not well understood. Recent work in jumping spiders has shown that defensive odours from three chemically defended bugs (Order Hemiptera: Acanthocephala femorata, Mormidea sp. and Leptoglossus phyllopus) increase a foraging aversion to red prey. Here, we ask whether these odours also increase avoidance of another visual warning: high-contrast stripes. Jumping spiders (Habronattus trimaculatus) were given choices between pattern-manipulated termites (solid white and black-and-white striped) in the presence or absence of a defensive odour from one of the aforementioned bug species. We predicted that any aversion to stripes would be stronger when odour was present. Surprisingly, we found no effect of any bug odour on the spiders’ aversions to stripes. Interestingly, these odours that so strongly and consistently trigger aversion to red do not have the same effect on stripes. This highlights the different ways that odours and coloration can interact (or not) to influence predators, providing insight into the diversity of aposematic displays in nature.

articles.title: Effectiveness of multi-component, dynamic begging displays as honest signals of nestling hunger
articles.abstract: Parent–offspring communication depends on offspring signals that help parents assess need and allocate care. Nestling begging is often treated as a graded, information-rich and therefore honest signal of hunger, as predicted by costly signalling models. We quantified how effectively visual and acoustic begging components encode food deprivation in spotless starling (Sturnus unicolor) nestlings using field observations and a controlled laboratory experiment. We combined random-regression models with information-theoretic measures of uncertainty reduction and receiver-based machine-learning decoding. In wild broods, begging order and maximum postural intensity increased with deprivation time, yet posture and calling together reduced uncertainty about deprivation by less than 5%. Distinct postural levels overlapped widely among deprivation states and followed a stereotyped sequence—rapid escalation to maximum intensity followed by relaxation—yielding poor resolution of intermediate hunger. Adding components improved decoding only marginally beyond the first few cues. Parental allocation was correspondingly rapid, although display duration could provide additional information once the full bout was perceived. Discrete coding analyses confirmed that simple postural schemes were most consistent and that begging reliably distinguished only coarse, extreme hunger states. Overall, the results support partially informative (pooling) or attention-seeking signalling models in which parents rely on a small set of salient cues within a multi-component display.

articles.title: Emotional reactivity and decision-making under social deprivation: the role of trait anxiety during quarantine
articles.abstract: Social isolation measures enforced during the COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of the social environment in shaping affective states and decision-making. However, the day-to-day experience and psychological recovery from social deprivation, especially among individuals with high trait anxiety, remains poorly understood. We conducted a 10-day longitudinal study with 116 university students returning to campus, collecting approximately 31 000 momentary assessments of affect and social interactions during a 3-day quarantine and subsequent period. Quarantine increased the need for social interaction and altered patterns of social engagement, whereas trait anxiety was robustly associated with reduced positive affect and elevated negative affect. Close interactions following quarantine were associated with higher positive affect. We also administered a virtual patch-foraging task to participants during and after quarantine. Greater variability in negative affect was associated with lower patch exit thresholds, suggesting a tendency to persist in depleted patches. These findings highlight how trait anxiety shapes emotional experience and social behaviour in daily life and reveal how fluctuations in negative affect can influence sequential decision-making under uncertainty.

articles.title: Evolution of the axial skeleton of early dinosaurs and the role of meristic and homeotic processes
articles.abstract: Changes in the axial skeleton played an important role in dinosaur evolution, with some of the oldest dinosaurs showing evidence of sacralization events. The increased number of early dinosaur discoveries over the last decade provides an opportunity to better characterize this phenomenon. It has led us to revise our understanding of axial evolution in early dinosaurs. Results support that the last common ancestor of Dinosauria would probably present 9 cervical, 16 dorsal and 2 sacral vertebrae (primordials). Early saurischians maintain a consistent number of vertebrae with presacral origin, and there is no evidence of meristic changes in these dinosaurs. A more complex scenario is observed in early ornithischians (including ‘silesaurids’). An insertion between the primordials occurs early in ornithischian evolution, and it appears to be maintained in ‘traditional’ ornithischians (Saphornithischia). Unambiguous evidence supports loss and gain of presacral vertebrae in ornithischians. Inserted sacrals across all dinosaurs are associated with a loss of a corresponding dorsal vertebra, supporting that these represent trunk vertebrae moved into the sacrum rather than novel vertebral unities. Changes in the axial skeleton of early dinosaurs are dominated by homeotic processes, with meristic processes restricted to derived members.

articles.title: Influence of bone-specific material properties on finite element modelling of the skull
articles.abstract: The material properties of bone in the skull are known to be heterogeneous and orthotropic, although datasets detailing these properties on a species level are limited. Therefore, computational modelling frequently uses homogeneous, isotropic material properties to analyse stresses/strains in the skull. However, it is often unknown how the choice of bone/s from which the elastic modulus is measured, or the direction in which it is measured, influences predicted stresses/strains. This study integrated imaging and measured muscle properties to create a subject-specific finite element model of a rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) skull, to investigate the influence of modelling the elastic modulus of bone through varying levels of complexity. The results demonstrate the importance of modelling orthotropic material properties, if known. Strain distribution was insensitive to whether the same isotropic elastic modulus was used for all bones in the skull versus modelling bone-specific isotropic elastic modulus. Strain distribution was also similar when using an isotropic elastic modulus based on measurement in different orthotropic directions, albeit with a slight difference when measured in the medio-lateral direction. This highlights that isotropic, homogeneous modelling of the skull is appropriate when analysing strain distribution, although alternative material modelling should be considered when strain magnitude is of particular interest.

articles.title: Mapping groundwater-dependent vegetation in temperate climates on the example of Central Germany
articles.abstract: Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. We implement this concept by integrating for the first time to our knowledge, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration data with high-resolution remote sensing, regional geospatial data and botanical field observations. To test our framework, we trained and validated random forest models with eight predictor variables using 166 vegetation plots to identify GDV in Central Germany. Ground-truth GDV plots prefer cooler, wetter, nutrient-richer and more acidic to alkaline environments compared to non-GDV. The final model using a phreatophyte cover threshold of 25% representing GDV plots achieved a testing accuracy of 0.97, identifying 2067 km² of GDV. Currently, only 19% is protected under the EU WFD. The proposed mapping framework offers a solution for identifying GDV in temperate regions. The new GDV maps can contribute to managing groundwater resources and preserving biodiversity hotspots in regions facing increasing droughts, ultimately supporting the implementation of the EU WFD.

articles.title: Microclimatic effects on activity patterns in a montane chimpanzee population
articles.abstract: Climatic variation can shape primate activity budgets by altering the energetic and thermoregulatory costs of feeding, resting, locomotion and social behaviour. However, little is known about how chimpanzees that inhabit cool, wet montane forests adjust their activity in response to fine-scale meteorological conditions. We examined the effects of temperature, absolute humidity (water vapour pressure (WVP)), wind speed and rainfall on eastern chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii) in Nyungwe National Park, Rwanda, one of the highest-elevation chimpanzee habitats. From March 2024 to February 2025, we collected 1933 party scans and 5661 individual scans, together with scan-level microclimatic measurements. Rainfall showed the clearest behavioural association: feeding probability declined during rainfall, whereas resting increased. Wind speed was negatively associated with both locomotion and grooming, suggesting that windier conditions may constrain movement and social behaviour. Temperature, WVP and fruit availability showed no clear association with any of the four behaviours. Feeding probability was higher and resting probability lower in the wet season than in the dry season. Harmonic beta-binomial generalized linear mixed-effects models revealed pronounced daily rhythmicity in feeding and resting. Overall, Nyungwe chimpanzees maintained broadly conserved daily activity rhythms while selectively adjusting behavioural allocation in response to immediate meteorological conditions.

articles.title: New use of mononuclear Mn/Co/Ni/Cu complexes of symmetric N2O2-type Schiff base as hydrogen-evolving catalysts
articles.abstract: Development of sustainable hydrogen production methods is crucial for the future hydrogen economy. Hence, designing cheap, stable and efficient catalysts for hydrogen generation is important. Here, we present the use of the family of eight Schiff base ligand-based transition metal complexes [MnIII(Salen)Cl] 1/[CoII(Salen)], 2/[NiII(Salen)], 3/[CuII(Salen)], 4/[MnIII(CH3Salen)Cl], 5/[CoII(CH3Salen)], 6/[NiII(CH3Salen)], 7/[CuII(CH3Salen)] and 8 (Salen/N,N′-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine/H2L1; CH3Salen/N,N′-bis(o-hydroxyacetophenone)ethylenediamine/H2L2) as hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. Electrochemical studies for the complexes (in CH3CN) were carried out in the absence and presence of acids. Catalytic parameters of turnover frequency/overpotential were calculated for the electrocatalytic process. All complexes were found to be efficient HER catalysts in the presence of acids and Co/Ni/Cu complexes were more stable than the Mn complexes. The stability and efficiency order of the catalysts was 2, 4 > 6 > 7 > 3 > 8 (acetic acid); 1 > 5 (trifluoroacetic acid). Density functional theory studies provided detailed insight into the metal- versus ligand-centred redox transitions and the HER mechanism for all complexes. Successive events of electrochemical reduction (E) and protonation (C) along the HER paths were investigated, and thermodynamically feasible routes were assigned. This work provides insights into the effect of a series of earth-abundant transition metal complex structures, the performance of this series of metal centres on electrocatalysis, and the effect of pKa on reactivity. Hence, it will be of value to develop novel and promising catalysts for HER in the future.

articles.title: Ontogeny of rake mark scarring on common dolphins ( Delphinus delphis ): insights to aggression and affiliation?
articles.abstract: Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. Using a zero-inflated generalized linear mixed model, we assessed rake mark occurrence (probability of rake density > 0) and prevalence (rake density, rake marks dm−2) across the body (n = 101; dorsal/ventral, cranial/caudal, left/right) in relation to sex, age, total body length (TBL), sexual maturity, body condition (n = 101) and female reproductive status (n = 51), to infer confrontation, avoidance and lateralization. Females showed higher rake mark prevalence but lower occurrence than males, suggesting infrequent but prolonged interactions, possibly sexual coercion. Rake prevalence and occurrence increased with TBL, potentially related to increased social interactions and surface area in larger individuals. Age, sexual maturity, body condition, and female reproductive status were not strong predictors of rake mark occurrence or prevalence. Our findings highlight rake marks as potential indicators of social dynamics.

articles.title: Polyethylene biotransformation by an earthworm gut-derived Streptomyces sp.: insights into microenvironment-associated metabolism
articles.abstract: Polyethylene (PE) is a highly recalcitrant polymer that resists microbial degradation owing to its hydrophobic and chemically inert structure. In this study, a Streptomyces sp. strain MH-1, isolated from the earthworm gut, was investigated for its interaction with PE under carbon-limited conditions. The strain was associated with approximately 15% reduction in PE weight after 30 days of incubation. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) analysis revealed alterations in polymer chemistry, including a reduction in the carbonyl peak (approx. 1715 cm‒1) and a decrease in the carbonyl index from 0.19 in the control to 0.10 in treated samples. In silico analysis using a closely related Streptomyces genome as a reference framework identified putative genes associated with hydrocarbon metabolism and suggested potential oxidative and assimilatory pathways. Candidate aldehyde dehydrogenases, including bifunctional alcohol/aldehyde dehydrogenase (adhE), together with genes associated with fatty acid metabolism and β-oxidation, may indicate potential mechanisms involved in the processing of oxidation intermediates. These findings, combined with biofilm formation and growth under confined conditions, highlight the importance of PE-associated microenvironments and provide a basis for exploring microbial adaptation and potential metabolic processes involved in PE biotransformation.

articles.title: Fast Feature Field (F3): A general predictive representation of events for robot perception
articles.abstract: This paper develops a mathematical argument and algorithms for building representations of data from event-based cameras that we call Fast Feature Field (F 3 ). We learned this representation by predicting future events from past events and show that it preserves scene structure and motion information. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and is robust to noise and variations in event rates. It can be computed efficiently using ideas from multiresolution hash encoding and deep sets, achieving 120 hertz at high-definition (HD) resolution and 440 hertz at video graphics array (VGA) resolution. F 3 represents events in a contiguous spatiotemporal volume as a multichannel image, enabling a range of downstream tasks. We obtained state-of-the-art performance on optical flow estimation, semantic segmentation, and monocular metric depth estimation, on data from three robotic platforms (a car, a quadruped robot, and a flying platform) and across different lighting conditions (daytime and nighttime), environments (indoors, outdoors, urban, and off-road), and dynamic vision sensors (resolutions and event rates). Our implementations can predict these tasks at 25 to 75 hertz at HD resolution.

articles.title: MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing
articles.abstract: Autonomous drone racing represents a major frontier in robotics research. It requires an artificial intelligence (AI) that can run onboard lightweight flying robots under tight resource and time constraints while pushing the physical system to its limits. The state of the art in this area consists of a system with a stereo camera and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) that beat human drone-racing champions in a controlled indoor environment. Here, we present MonoRace, an onboard drone-racing approach that generalizes to a competition environment without any external motion tracking system, using only a monocular rolling-shutter camera and an IMU. The approach features robust state estimation that combines neural network–based gate segmentation with a drone model. Moreover, it includes an offline optimization procedure that leverages the known geometry of gates to refine any state estimation parameter. This offline optimization is based purely on onboard flight data and is important for fine-tuning the extrinsic camera calibration parameters. Furthermore, the guidance and control are performed by a neural network that forgoes inner-loop controllers by directly sending motor commands. This small network runs on the flight controller at 500 hertz. The proposed approach won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition 2025, outperforming all competing autonomous drone race teams and three world champion human pilots in a direct knockout tournament. It reached speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour on the competition track and successfully coped with problems such as camera interference and IMU saturation.

articles.title: System design of the Ultra Mobility Vehicle: A driving, balancing, and jumping bicycle robot
articles.abstract: Trials cyclists and mountain bike riders can hop, jump, balance, and drive on one or both wheels. This versatility allows them to achieve speed and energy efficiency on smooth terrain and agility over rough terrain. Inspired by these athletes, we present the design and control of a robotic platform, Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), that combines a bicycle and a reaction mass to move dynamically with minimal actuated degrees of freedom. We used a simulation-driven design optimization process to synthesize a spatial linkage topology with a focus on vertical jump height and momentum-based balancing on a single wheel contact. Using a deep reinforcement learning (RL) framework, we demonstrate zero-shot transfer of diverse athletic behaviors, including track stands, jumps, wheelies, rear-wheel hopping, and front flips. This 23.5-kilogram robot is capable of high speeds ( v max = 8 meters per second) and jumping on and over large obstacles (1-meter tall or 130% of the robot’s nominal height).

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern for the Research Article “In vivo CRISPR activation screen identifies acyl-CoA–binding protein as a driver of bone metastasis”
From code to cure: Harnessing AI for antibiotic discovery and design
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now enables the exploration of vast chemical and sequence spaces, the design of synthesizable antibiotics, and the prioritization of safe, mechanism-diverse candidates through integrated modeling and accelerated testing. Here, we survey recent advances in AI for both small-molecule and peptide antimicrobial drugs, highlight emerging data and reporting standards, and outline translational pathways and regulatory hurdles needed to bring these agents to patients.

articles.title: Innovative roadmaps for sustainable antimicrobial resistance interventions
articles.abstract: Integrated strategies to combat antibiotic-resistant bacteria and fungi require innovative commercial models, new discovery platforms, standardized genomic surveillance, and streamlined clinical trials. Machine learning and other new technologies will accelerate the development of diagnostics and therapeutics (small molecules, antibodies, and vaccines) to combat antimicrobial resistance. Next-generation approaches should align societal impact with investment to ensure rapid global public health gains.

articles.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals
articles.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual’s deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span–wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

articles.title: Orthogonal Fc engineering enables multiplexed delivery of mRNA-encoded bispecific antibodies that constrain viral escape
articles.abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)–encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)–expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

articles.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2 CV ), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

articles.title: Quinolinic acid contributes to maladaptive kidney injury and acute kidney injury–to–chronic kidney disease transition
articles.abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major clinical problem with unclear underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in tryptophan metabolism, particularly in the production of downstream metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QA), play a role in renal pathophysiology. QA, an intermediate in de novo nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis, is metabolized by quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We investigated whether QA contributes to kidney injury using models of folic acid–induced AKI-to-CKD transition and cisplatin-induced AKI, genetic and exogenous approaches to alter QA, and clinical observations. Untargeted kidney metabolomics identified QA as one of the most elevated metabolites after folic acid injury. After folic acid injury, Qprt haploinsufficiency exacerbated kidney injury and fibrosis-related gene expression; aged Qprt -haploinsufficient mice exhibited increased fibrosis-associated gene expression without overt renal dysfunction. Exogenous QA administration increased serum creatinine in uninjured mice and worsened renal dysfunction and fibrosis-related gene expression in the folic acid AKI-to-CKD model. Conversely, mice deficient in either 3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) or kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO), which reduce flux toward QA, showed improved renal outcomes after folic acid injury and cisplatin-induced AKI. Multimodal spatial metabolomics analysis of kidney biopsies from patients with AKI revealed QA accumulation in regions of inflammatory infiltration. Last, children with CKD exhibited higher urinary QA compared with healthy individuals. These findings underscore QA as a potential mediator of kidney injury and a therapeutic target for preventing the progression from AKI to CKD.

articles.title: Restoration of PP2A AαB56αC trimer formation by RPT04402 molecular glue in high-grade uterine cancer
articles.abstract: The incidence and mortality of high-grade endometrial cancers are increasing, and heterozygous hotspot mutations in PPP2R1A are drivers of the most aggressive forms of uterine cancer. PPP2R1A encodes the Aα scaffolding subunit of the heterotrimeric phosphatase PP2A. These recurrent mutations, specifically at the Pro 179 and Ser 256 residues, disrupt the binding of tumor-suppressive substrate-directing B56 and B55 subunits to the PP2A scaffolding subunit while maintaining binding to other regulatory subunits. Here, we identified a series of molecular glues that correct PP2A trimer formation in the context of the P179R (Pro 179 →Arg) and S256F (Ser 256 →Phe) mutants. A small-molecule library was designed to fit into the pocket at the binding interface of the Aα/B56α/C heterotrimer. The lead molecule, RPT04402, promoted B56α heterotrimerization to the Aα P179R and Aα S256F mutant scaffolds. In mice, RPT04402 treatment drove tumor regressions and extended median survival in multiple independent mutant cell lines and patient-derived xenografts, proving a robust single-agent activity. This activity was abrogated upon knockout of B56α. Combined, these data demonstrate that PP2A molecular glues are a promising first-in-class therapy that might benefit patients with PPP2R1A mutant uterine cancer by targeting a driver of this aggressive disease.

articles.title: Evaluation of the accuracy, completeness, and compliance of current summary reporting of adverse events to the Food and Drug Administration using the manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database: cross sectional study
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate the accuracy and completeness of adverse event summary reports for medical devices and compliance of the reports with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements.DesignCross sectional study.SettingThe FDA manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database.ParticipantsAll adverse event summary reports filed in MAUDE from July 2019 to June 2025.Main outcome measuresIdentification of device problem codes, appropriate identification as summary reports in the submission form, concordance between the number of events data field and the report narrative, and compliance with FDA reporting deadlines.Results6308 summary reports were submitted to MAUDE containing 159 503 adverse events. Use of summary reports increased from 808 to 1757 between 2020 and 2024, a factor of 1.21 per year (P<0.001). Most (91%) adverse events in summary reports were for class 3 high risk devices. Summary reports lacked descriptions of potential device related problems: 57% of reports denoted an “adverse event without identified device or use problem” and 38% of reports selected “insufficient information” in the device problem code data field. Manufacturers incorrectly checked “N” (no) in the summary report (Y/N, reporting yes/no) field for 694 summary reports (11%) and erroneously listed “n=1” under the number of events field for 423 summary reports (7%), causing an undercount of 11 902 adverse events. The majority (55%) of summary reports failed to comply with the FDA reporting deadline of 30 days after the manufacturer became aware of the adverse event.ConclusionsAdverse event summary reports in MAUDE are frequently incomplete, inaccurate, and delayed. Improvements are needed to ensure timely identification of device safety signals and uphold FDA transparency standards.

The medical system kept detainees alive to endure further torture and interrogation while ensuring their injuries could not be traced through clinical records.“HRF’s article 15 submission calls on the ICC prosecutor to investigate this system for what it is: a chain...

articles.title: Postmarketing surveillance of medical devices
articles.abstract: Medical devices often enter clinical practice on the basis of premarket studies that are smaller and shorter than those required for medicines, while device performance may depend on operator experience and real world use. Postmarketing surveillance is used to identify emerging hazards and determine whether they represent genuine increases in risk.Individual medical device reports are important in identifying hazards, providing public visibility and alerting regulators, clinicians, and researchers to previously unrecognised problems. Direct reports to the US Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA’s) Medical Device Reporting programme have provided the initial signal for many FDA medical device safety communications.1 However, spontaneous reporting systems are limited by underreporting, incomplete information, uncertain causality, and a lack of reliable information on how many patients received each device.23 These systems can generate hypotheses but cannot reliably estimate incidence or compare device performance.In the linked study (doi: 10.1136/bmj-2026-100812),4 Zhou and colleagues identify important shortcomings in adverse...

Antibody-mediated encephalitides: distinct diseases with transdisciplinary implications
articles.abstract: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. Antibody-mediated disorders targeting glial aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein are distinct nosological entities, defined by specific targets, mechanisms, syndromes, and therapeutic implications. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Evidence from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and anti-IgLON5 disease (used here as exemplars of autoimmune encephalitides) indicates that individual autoimmune encephalitides differ in demographics, triggers, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, post-acute trajectories, and treatment requirements. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. Improving patient care requires not only aetiological and mechanistic insight to enable development of targeted therapies but also strengthened cross-specialty expertise to optimise diagnosis and management.

Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. However, most health systems still treat neurotrauma (TBI and SCI, collectively) as a time-limited event, leaving long-term surveillance of these patients fragmented or absent, which leads to preventable mortality and avoidable readmissions. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of delpacibart zotadirsen in Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations amenable to exon 44 skipping in the USA (EXPLORE44): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 1/2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundThere are no approved exon skipping therapies to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to DMD variants amenable to exon 44 skipping (DMD44). Delpacibart zotadirsen (del-zota, also known as AOC 1044) is a first-in-class antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate designed to deliver an exon 44-skipping phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer to muscle to restore dystrophin expression for individuals with DMD44. EXPLORE44 was a first-in-human trial to evaluate del-zota's safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy.MethodsEXPLORE44 was a two-part randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 study in healthy adult men (aged 18-55 years; part A) and ambulatory and non-ambulatory male participants with DMD44 (aged 7-27 years; part B) at ten clinical research sites in the USA. Dosing in part B was informed by safety, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data from part A. In part B, participants with DMD44 were randomised (3:1 del-zota:placebo) within two dose cohorts to receive three intravenous doses of del-zota (5 mg/kg every 6 weeks, or 10 mg/kg every 8 weeks) or matching placebo. A computer-generated permuted-block randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent statistician with no further role in the study. Infusions were prepared by an unmasked pharmacist under supervision of the masked investigator; other site staff, participants, and sponsor team members were masked to allocation. The primary objective was safety and tolerability measured by the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events. Secondary endpoints assessing target engagement were change from baseline in exon skipping (ie, defined as the percentage of dystrophin mRNA transcripts in which exon 44 is excluded from the mature mRNA relative to total dystrophin mRNA transcripts) and dystrophin level to month 4 (5 mg/kg cohort) or month 5 (10 mg/kg cohort). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05670730) and is complete.FindingsBetween Dec 5, 2022, and June 27, 2024, we enrolled and randomly assigned 45 healthy volunteers and 26 men and boys with DMD44. In part A, three (30%) of ten healthy volunteers who received placebo and 21 (62%) of 34 who received del-zota reported at least one adverse event, none of which were severe or serious. In part B, nine participants with DMD44 received del-zota at 5 mg/kg, ten at 10 mg/kg, and seven received placebo; mean age 13·3 years (SD 4·2). 16 (84%) participants with DMD44 treated with del-zota and six (86%) treated with placebo reported at least one adverse event, most of which were mild or moderate; two participants, both in the 5 mg/kg del-zota group, discontinued due to adverse events (anaphylactic reaction and infusion-related reaction). Mean increases from baseline in exon 44 skipping were 36·6% (95% CI 20·8 to 52·4, SD 17·1, nominal p=0·0013) at 5 mg/kg, 43·4% (32·8 to 54·0, 14·9, nominal pInterpretationDel-zota had an acceptable safety profile, produced increases in exon 44 skipping and dystrophin expression, and decreased biomarkers of muscle damage in participants with DMD44. Findings from this study support further investigation of del-zota in a phase 3 study to assess efficacy and long-term safety.FundingAvidity Biosciences, A Novartis Company.
