Mitigating the toughness-efficiency trade-off in perovskite solar cells through electrospun nanofiber reinforcement
articles.abstract: Metal halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic materials but are mechanically fragile. Incorporating electrospun nylon nanofibers into the perovskite produces a mechanically reinforced photoactive composite with nearly 6-fold higher fracture energy while preserving photovoltaic performance. The nanofibers also redistribute incident light within the photoabsorber, illustrating how structural reinforcement can be introduced into a functional semiconductor without sacrificing its optoelectronic properties and enable mechanically robust, multifunctional optoelectronic materials.

articles.title: An integrated model of territory occupancy and mark‐recapture data for estimating spatial variation in survival
articles.abstract: Spatial variation in survival is central to understanding population dynamics and guiding conservation. However, assessing it is hard, since capture‐mark‐recapture (CMR) data required for such inference must be collected over large spatial extents, which is seldom possible. By contrast, territory occupancy (TO) data are typically spatially rich and widely available for territorial species, but they do not directly inform individual survival. We developed an integrated model combining CMR and TO data. The model links site‐level occupancy dynamics, governed by site persistence and colonization probabilities, to survival of the territory owner, allowing both data sources to jointly inform spatiotemporal variation in survival. An estimable scaling parameter (κ$$ \kappa $$) accommodates potential violation of a deterministic occupancy‐survival link arising from breeding dispersal or alternative colonization dynamics. We evaluated our model using simulation across different survival scenarios (constant, spatial, spatiotemporal), life histories and CMR detection probabilities, and assessed estimator robustness when the deterministic occupancy‐survival link is violated. We applied the model to long‐term peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) data in Hungary, evaluating the effects on survival of the presence of a predator (eagle owl) and the proportion of agricultural land. Survival estimated with the integrated model showed negligible bias and good coverage across all simulation scenarios, while substantially improving precision relative to CMR‐only analyses. Precision gains were largest for spatial regression coefficients (up to 80%) and temporal standard deviation parameters (up to 88%); gains increased with greater model complexity and lower detection probability. When the deterministic occupancy‐survival link was violated, κ$$ \kappa $$ adequately absorbed the discrepancy and prevented bias in survival. In the case study, integration substantially improved the precision of spatiotemporal survival estimates and revealed a negative association with eagle owl presence and a positive one with the proportion of agricultural land. Our new integrated model improves estimation of spatial and temporal variation in survival by leveraging shared information across data sources, extending spatially explicit demographic inference to systems where CMR data alone are insufficient, and thereby allowing spatial survival inference in a broader range of applications.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into chromatin modulation by the “orphan” remodeler ATRX
articles.abstract: Duan et al. solved the structure of ATRX ATPase-nucleosome complex, uncovering three distinctive features that enable ATRX to remodel nucleosomes. These newly identified features are indispensable for protecting cells from G4 stress. The work provides a framework for interpreting both known and future mutations linked to ATRX-related disorders.

articles.title: Phylogeographic Breaks With and Without Contemporary Barriers to Migration in the Lizard Acanthodactylus erythrurus
articles.abstract: Identifying phylogeographic breaks and deciphering the relative contributions of environmental extrinsic (e.g., geological barriers, ecological gradients) and organismal intrinsic (e.g., limited dispersal, reproductive incompatibilities) factors to their persistence remain challenging, especially in the absence of genomic data. Here, we address this issue using parapatric lineages of the lizard Acanthodactylus erythrurus in south‐western Morocco. A previous study based on nine nuclear loci identified two phylogeographic units (coastal vs. inland) whose separation did not align with landscape features preventing migration. The coastal lineage was inferred to evolve under isolation by distance (IBD, the regular increase of genetic differentiation with geographic distance), despite the presence of large rivers across its range. This suggests either that phylogeographic breaks do not align with landscape features, or that the restricted marker set prevented an accurate inference of phylogeographic breaks. We tested these hypotheses using RADseq data and recovered three lineages, each separated by phylogeographic breaks and narrow contact zones with restricted admixture. Coastal populations that had been previously identified to evolve under IBD actually included two lineages separated by a major, permanent river, reducing migration. The inland phylogeographic break, correctly identified by the previous study, is located in a continuously distributed habitat. Neither of the breaks aligned with steep changes in bioclimatic variables, suggesting a negligible contribution of local adaptation. We conclude that intrinsic reproductive barriers, as evidenced by narrow clines in allele frequencies at multiple loci spread over the genome, play a major role in maintaining these phylogeographic breaks. Our results also highlight the difficulty of identifying phylogeographic breaks from pre‐genomic molecular data.

articles.title: Population Genomics in a Biodiversity Hotspot: Methods and Cross‐Kingdom Insights From the 2025 Workshop in Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanic Garden, China
articles.abstract: The 2025 Population Genomics Workshop at the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden (XTBG) convened leading researchers, early‐career scientists and students to explore rapid advancements and emerging priorities in population genomics. The workshop highlighted advances in pangenomics, demographic modelling, archaeogenomics, and the integration of population variation with functional and genomic insights. It also emphasised strengthening interdisciplinary collaborations to apply genomics findings to climate‐resilient agriculture and biodiversity conservation. This report summarises key methodological discussions from the workshop and underscores their emerging relevance to plant population genomics, biodiversity conservation and climate adaptation.

articles.abstract: In Chile, the Center for Astrophysics and Associated Technologies has been working towards turning scientific investment into economic success for two decades, through the transfer of technology and techniques from astrophysics to industry. Many successful projects provide tangible examples of the real-world benefits of astronomy.

articles.title: On the coronal origin of magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind
articles.abstract: The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. These structures are frequently observed by spacecraft near the Sun, but their formation mechanism remains an open question. Using measurements from Solar Orbiter at 0.55 AU, we report heavy ion observations within a magnetic switchback that provide direct evidence of its solar source. Elevated charge-state ratios of oxygen and carbon, combined with a depletion of helium relative to protons, indicate that the switchback plasma originated from hot, closed coronal loop structures. A semi-empirical coronal model, constrained by electron temperature and density measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, traces the ion signatures to either a coronal hole boundary or loops within the coronal hole, implicating the source mechanism as interchange reconnection, where closed loops reconnect with open magnetic field and eject plasma. The proton velocity and magnetic field fluctuations of the switchback are in accordance with an outward-propagating Alfvén wave. These findings suggest that interchange reconnection and wave or turbulence mechanisms jointly govern switchback origin and propagation, respectively. Most importantly, we show that switchbacks preserve measurable signatures, carrying information about the physical processes that heat the solar atmosphere and accelerate the solar wind.

articles.title: Reduced incidence of little red dots at z < 3 based on number density and halo mass evolution
articles.abstract: Little red dots evolve from under-dense regions at z > 4 to typical environments by z ≈ 3.5, while their halo and stellar masses surge by a factor of ten. This accounts for their scarcity at low redshifts and suggests a distinct evolutionary path for little red dots compared with other active galactic nuclei.

articles.title: The formation of merging black holes via stable mass transfer in massive binary stars
articles.abstract: Detailed models for the complete evolution of mass-transferring binary stars produce merging black holes consistent with the observed masses and spins. Isolated binary evolution probably contributes to the observed gravitational-wave sources.

articles.title: Gene-driven self-morphing microtubule-based active matter
articles.abstract: Cell-free gene expression is embedded directly within a microtubule network to generate a genetically programmed active material with complementary biochemical and physical controls.

articles.title: Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
articles.abstract: Quasiparticle condensates are among the most striking solid-state manifestations of quantum physics. Coupling macroscopic real-space wavefunctions to additional degrees of freedom, such as the electron spin, would add valuable control knobs for quantum applications. While creating spin-carrying superconducting condensates has attracted enormous attention, condensates of light-matter hybrids known as exciton–polaritons have lacked an analogous spin-based perspective. Here we demonstrate magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr. Under photoexcitation, CrSBr microwires embedded in an optical cavity show the hallmarks of polariton condensation. Owing to the strong coupling between the spin order and excitonic correlation, the energy of the condensate can be tuned by up to 10.5 meV by an external magnetic field of 2 T. Our results establish CrSBr microcavities as a powerful platform for exploring magnetic control of polariton condensates and mark an essential step towards spin-controlled coherent quantum light sources.

articles.title: Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
articles.abstract: Polarization-selective excitation in SnSe reveals anisotropic valley dynamics with distinct channels: one channel with near-unity valley polarization and one channel that rapidly depolarizes through electron–phonon-mediated intervalley scattering.

articles.title: Author Correction: Natural killer T cells and CD8+ T cells are dispensable for T cell–dependent allergic airway inflammation
articles.abstract: Author Correction: Natural killer T cells and CD8+ T cells are dispensable for T cell–dependent allergic airway inflammation

articles.title: Tangermeme: a toolkit for understanding cis-regulatory logic using deep learning models
articles.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance at predicting diverse genomic modalities, yet their promise for biological discovery lies in how they are used after demonstrating their predictive performance. Here we describe the functionality of tangermeme, a highly optimized toolkit for ‘everything-but-the-model’ when it comes to genomic deep learning, and demonstrate how tangermeme can be used to distill the learned cis- regulatory patterns from models into human-interpretable insights.

articles.title: Atomic-scale visualization of three-dimensional magnetization vectors with competing spin Hamiltonian interactions
articles.abstract: A beam-shift-based 4D EMCD method is developed that can map 3D spin vectors across individual atomic planes and reveal how competing spin Hamiltonian interactions drive asymmetric spin rotation in canted antiferromagnetic YFeO3.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s disease target and drug discovery by leveraging multiomics and electronic health data
articles.abstract: Hou et al. show a drug target compendium supported by human genetic and real-world patient data for Alzheimer’s disease and validate epoxide hydrolase 2 as a causal Alzheimer’s disease target using CRISPR interference and gene editing experiments in human models.

articles.title: Picosecond current pulses probe intrinsic limit for dissipationless transport in superconductors
articles.abstract: Picosecond current pulses can propagate with zero resistance far above the conventionally defined critical current values in type-II superconductors. Such pulses have now revealed the onset of resistive transport at a higher current threshold in the s-wave superconductor NbN, associated with Cooper-pair depairing. By contrast, a gradual suppression of superconductivity is observed in YBa2Cu3O7, reflecting the d-wave nature of its superconducting state.

articles.title: Short-range excitonic correlations and enhanced excitonic susceptibility in 1T-TiSe2
articles.abstract: Excitons—bound states of electrons and holes—can spontaneously condense into a quantum coherent ground state. 1 T -TiSe 2 , a layered transition metal dichalcogenide, is a candidate for realizing this phase in a bulk material, but its putative excitonic condensation is accompanied by charge-density-wave formation that obscures signatures of excitonic instability and fluctuations in this structural transition. Here we clarify the mechanism of exciton condensation in quasi-low-dimensional systems by tracking exciton dissociation as a function of photoexcitation fluence and temperature using few-femtosecond broadband extreme-ultraviolet absorption spectroscopy. We find that short-range excitonic fluctuations emerge before long-range-order formation in the ground state. We also observe enhanced excitonic susceptibility, identified by faster exciton dissociation near the phase transition temperature, consistent with excitonic instability in this material. These results provide a framework for understanding other excitonic insulator candidates proposed in quasi-one- or quasi-two-dimensional crystals.

articles.title: Mapping the functional dark proteome in cancer
articles.abstract: The dark proteome encompasses previously undiscovered and uncharacterized protein molecules derived from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. In this Perspective, Prensner et al. describe the current understanding of the dark proteome and set out the critical questions that need to be addressed in the field to determine whether the dark proteome can fulfill its potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
articles.abstract: Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recognized as bioisosteres of diaryl ketones that preserve key electronic features while exhibiting distinct reactivity. However, synthesis of this motif largely relies on Lewis acid-promoted Friedel–Crafts reactions, which are restricted to electron-rich arenes and often suffer from low functional-group tolerance and competing side reactions. Here we report a method for the synthesis of 3,3-substituted diaryloxetanes from readily available 3-oxetanone through a cross-coupling reaction with tetrafluoropyridone as leaving group. The difunctionalization through subsequent addition of two aryl groups, one from an aryl halide, the other from an arylboronic ester, provides access to a variety of benzophenone bioisosteres. The nickel-catalysed cross-coupling at a fully substituted carbon centre is enabled through oxetanyl C–O bond oxidative addition and establishes programmable entry to 3,3-diaryloxetane bioisosteres that are synthetically challenging to access via traditional polar bond disconnection strategies. Mechanistic studies support a Ni(0)-mediated oxidative addition of the oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridine ester.

articles.title: The road to self-driving laboratories in industry
articles.abstract: In this issue, we focus on the development of self-driving laboratories for the autonomous synthesis of molecules and materials, with a particular focus on industrial considerations and applications.

articles.title: Stability, Degeneracy, and Scalability of a 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
articles.abstract: A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.

articles.title: Theory of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
articles.abstract: Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.

Soft magnetoelastic transduction: the cutting-edge frontier in energy harvesting and self-powered sensing
[Articles] Conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence in ambulatory primary care: a prospective feasibility study
articles.abstract: Although further research is needed, this study shows the initial feasibility of conversational AI in a real-world setting—assessed via conversation safety and quality, as well as user acceptance—and represents a crucial step towards clinical translation.

articles.title: [Articles] Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial
articles.abstract: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.

articles.title: [Comment] Conversational diagnostic AI in primary care: what happens after it speaks?
articles.abstract: Patients increasingly use conversational artificial intelligence (AI), including for possible diagnoses, before seeing a clinician. However, clinical evidence is lacking and is mostly synthetic. The Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer (AMIE), for example, outperformed primary care physicians in text consultations, but its patients were patient actors.1 One exception is a randomised trial of 2069 patients in which a chatbot generated histories, preliminary diagnoses, and test orders, sometimes without staff support, although its primary outcomes focused mainly on efficiency.

articles.title: [Comment] Deucrictibant: a novel oral on-demand treatment for hereditary angioedema
articles.abstract: Hereditary angioedema due to a deficiency of C1 inhibitor (HAE-C1INH) is clinically characterised by recurrent, generally unpredictable attacks of angioedema.1 Untreated episodes are often severe and prolonged, lasting up to 3–5 days and engendering considerable morbidity and even mortality.2 Unlike angioedema associated with mast cell mediators, the swelling in HAE-C1INH does not respond to antihistamines, corticosteroids, or epinephrine.

articles.title: [Correspondence] Bundibugyo virus: coordinating a cross-border response
articles.abstract: On May 15, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda declared outbreaks of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus. On May 17, 2026, the Director-General of WHO determined that the epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, approximately 48 h after the outbreak declarations.1 By Aug 26, 2026, 5815 confirmed cases and 2788 deaths had been reported, including 5794 cases and 2786 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where transmission had spread to 60 health zones across six provinces.

Roots turn decay into a chemical map
articles.abstract: Roots navigate soils where abiotic cues intersect with microbial activity. How they extract directional information from microbial processes remains unclear. Bao et al. identify saprotropism, whereby decay-generated pH gradients steer roots via the root meristem growth factor (RGF)–RGF receptor–abscisic acid signaling, revealing how ecological complexity shapes developmental decisions.

articles.title: Circulating tumor cell–immune cell clusters: dynamic engines of metastasis
articles.abstract: Circulating tumor cell (CTC) clusters are potent drivers of metastasis, exhibiting markedly greater metastatic capacity than single CTCs. Beyond homotypic CTC clusters, CTCs dynamically engage immune cells to form heterotypic clusters with enhanced metastatic fitness. Rather than passive assemblies, these clusters function as coordinated metastatic ecosystems, integrating adhesion, immune modulation, and metabolic adaptation to promote survival, plasticity, and immune evasion. Recent advances in CTC isolation, single-cell and spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence-driven analyses have enabled unprecedented resolution of these dynamic interactions. Together, these findings support a conceptual shift from isolated single-cell dissemination to multicellular cooperation as an important principle of metastasis and identify CTC–immune cell clusters as actionable targets for next-generation therapies to boost immunity and prevent metastasis.

articles.title: Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 links epigenetic plasticity to cholesterol metabolism
articles.abstract: Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2) is the catalytic subunit of Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), which mediates transcriptional repression. Kim and colleagues uncover a PRC2-independent EZH2-sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2) axis that drives cholesterol biosynthesis, revealing an epigenetic-metabolic vulnerability exploitable through targeted protein degradation.

articles.title: Integrating biology and mathematics to understand checkpoint immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) elicit durable antitumor responses in immunogenic tumors but still fail in most patients. Extensive research has elucidated how ICIs trigger a wide array of antitumor responses, yet, unexpectedly, also fuel tumor immunosuppression, a major driver of therapy failure. We argue that the sheer number of variables at play will hinder upcoming research to improve ICI performance, making the classic experimental approach exceedingly time- and resource-intensive. We posit that this problem can be solved through a bidirectional feedback loop of mathematical modeling and experimental validation. This review consolidates foundational knowledge in cancer immunology and mathematical modeling and proposes strategies that enable mathematicians and immunologists to collaborate fruitfully and expedite breakthroughs in ICI therapy.

articles.title: Protecting axonal mitochondria prevents chemotherapy-driven neuropathy
articles.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy is a poorly understood yet extraordinarily relevant obstacle to the effective implementation of cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with cancer. Recent findings from Heles et al. demonstrate that safe neuroactive molecules that promote mitochondrial fitness in axons effectively prevent peripheral neuropathy in preclinical tumor models, thereby supporting clinical translation.

articles.title: Hydroxylamine as a bridge in electrocatalytic organonitrogen synthesis
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic nitrogen fixation and nitrification exceed natural denitrification capacity, disrupting the nitrogen cycle and causing environmental pollution. Electrocatalytic inorganic-to-organic nitrogen conversion is promising for restoring this balance. However, diverse product formation makes selectivity control a key challenge. This review examines the conversion of hydroxylamine (NH2OH) as the pivotal precursor bridging inorganic nitrogen oxides (NOX−/NOX) and C–N bond formation toward value-added organonitrogen compounds. We survey the theoretical principles governing NH2OH selectivity, discuss catalytic mechanisms for subsequent C–N bond construction, and review catalyst modulation strategies for organonitrogen synthesis. By framing NH2OH as a linchpin linking denitrification and synthesis, this review outlines key challenges and provides a unified framework connecting fundamental understanding to rational catalyst design for sustainable nitrogen conversion.

articles.title: Sound asleep, yet still listening: auditory processing during human sleep
articles.abstract: Sleepers can wake to their name, but ignore louder irrelevant sounds, a paradox that suggests more than simple sensory gating. Growing evidence reveals flexible auditory coupling during human sleep, ranging from complete disconnection to high-level cognitive processing and even to physical responses. Here, we synthesize the multiple cognitive levels at which auditory stimuli are processed (or not) during human sleep and outline factors modulating this processing. Moments of sensory isolation may promote restoration and memory consolidation, while moments of environmental coupling enable threat detection. We speculate that no single optimal balance exists; rather, the ideal degree of sensory coupling shifts with individuals and contexts. Chronic dysregulation of this balance may contribute to the clinical picture of sleep disorders, including insomnia and hypersomnia.

articles.title: An Amphiphilic Proton Donor Decouples Acidity from Interfacial Reactivity for Lithium-Mediated Ammonia Synthesis
articles.abstract: Electrochemical ammonia synthesis via a lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li-NRR) faces a fundamental selectivity challenge in which proton donors that accelerate productive protonation simultaneously promote parasitic hydrogen evolution. Here, we demonstrate that 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol (TFE), an amphiphilic alcohol, mitigates this limitation by decoupling thermodynamic acidity from kinetic reactivity. Despite its high acidity, TFE suppresses parasitic reactions through rapid interfacial passivation associated with its fluorinated structure, while modulating the microstructure of a fluoride-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Blending TFE with ethanol further optimizes proton activity and hydrogen bonding, yielding a thin, uniform SEI enriched in highly crystalline LiF with reduced interfacial resistance. The optimized electrolyte achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 59.0% in a continuous-flow reactor, maintained stable performance under potential-cycling, and reached 82.8% in a high-pressure batch reactor. This study highlights proton-donor engineering as a key strategy to modulate the SEI nanostructure for selectivity in Li-NRR.

articles.title: Suppressing 2D Interfacial Reconstruction via Tetrafluoroborate Surface Engineering for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Surface passivation using two-dimensional (2D) perovskites has been widely employed to improve the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, conventional 3D/2D heterointerfaces often suffer from interfacial reconstruction caused by spacer-cation migration during operation, leading to performance degradation. Here, we investigate pseudo-halogen-modified phenethylammonium salts (PEAX, X = SCN and BF4) for surface passivation. Unlike the commonly used phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI), which forms a low-dimensional interfacial phase, PEABF4 does not induce 2D perovskite formation but instead enables non-reconstructive surface passivation. PEABF4 treatment improves energy-level alignment, carrier lifetime, charge extraction, and crystallinity and suppresses surface traps and nonradiative recombination. As a result, PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.72% with a VOC of 1.16 V, outperforming untreated and PEAI-treated devices. Furthermore, unencapsulated PEABF4-based devices retain 85.96% of their initial efficiency after 320 h of maximum power point tracking, demonstrating that pseudo-halogen engineering offers an effective route toward efficient and operationally stable PSCs.

articles.title: Targeting ZDHHC15-mediated S-acylation of CD155 reactivates anti-tumor immunity
articles.abstract: Reversible protein S-acylation regulates immune checkpoint function. Zhang et al. demonstrate that ZDHHC15-mediated S-acylation stabilizes CD155, whereas genetic or pharmacological disruption promotes CD155 degradation, enhances anti-tumor immunity, and suppresses tumor growth.

articles.title: A standardized patient-derived glioblastoma organoid platform for evaluating radiotherapy efficacy and overcoming resistance
articles.abstract: Wang et al. develop a standardized reaggregated glioblastoma organoid (rGBO) platform that enables scalable evaluation of patient-specific treatment responses. The platform links organoid radiosensitivity with patient survival, identifies response-related transcriptomic signatures, and reveals BET inhibition as a strategy to enhance radiotherapy efficacy in organoid and xenograft models.

articles.title: A translational pipeline for classification of variants of uncertain significance to support gene therapy clinical trial in OTOF-related deafness
articles.abstract: Chen et al. establish a translational functional pipeline to reclassify OTOF variants of uncertain significance. This pipeline enables definitive molecular diagnosis and eligibility for gene therapy trials; it further reveals that K1992R drives pathogenicity in the E1700Q haplotype via disrupting otoferlin localization.

articles.title: Fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine elicits convergent B cell immunodominance to uncouple protection from ADE in macaques
articles.abstract: Yang et al. demonstrate, in primates, that a fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine confers full protection with negligible dengue ADE. The response is dominated by convergent B cells orthologous to human IGHV5-10-1 whose antibodies target a distinct viral hotspot, with DENV envelope N67-linked glycan preventing cross-reactivity for safer flavivirus vaccines.

articles.title: Oral microbial nitrate metabolism is associated with lower prevalence of prediabetes
articles.abstract: Zhao et al. investigate the role of the tongue microbiome in prediabetes and glycemic dysregulation. Rothia mucilaginosa and microbial nitrate metabolism are associated with lower prediabetes prevalence and improve the prediction of prediabetes progression, highlighting oral nitrate metabolism as a potential modifiable link between the oral microbiome and metabolic health.

articles.title: Regional brain aging signatures predict mortality through neurovascular immune mechanisms
articles.abstract: Lee et al. integrate structural brain MRI with plasma proteomics to identify a three-region brain age model that predicts mortality more accurately than global measures and reveals shared immune and vascular mechanisms. These findings support regional brain aging as a scalable biomarker for precision geromedicine.

Advances in net-1,2-hydrogen atom transfer of oxygen- and nitrogen-centered radicals: mechanisms and applications in synthesis
articles.abstract: This review outlines progress in O- and N-centered radical net-1,2-HAT reactions, covering mechanisms and synthetic applications. The core mechanism, radical translocation from a heteroatom to an α-carbon, enables subsequent coupling or cascades.

articles.title: Charge dynamics in covalent organic framework photocatalysts
articles.abstract: This review discusses exciton behaviour, structural design strategies, spectroscopic probes, and charge-transfer pathways in covalent organic framework photocatalysts to advance efficient solar-to-chemical energy conversion.

articles.title: Porphyrinoids for up- and down-conversion
articles.abstract: This review summarizes the use of porphyrinoids with molecular down-converters in intramolecular SF (i-SF) and molecular up-converters in intramolecular triplet–triplet energy transfer and triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion.

articles.title: Cascade Thiol-Responsive Hydrogels Based on Poly(2-Isopropenyl-2-oxazoline) Cross-Linked with Ellman’s Reagent as Disulfide-Containing Cross-Linkers
articles.abstract: Thiol compounds play vital roles in environmental and biological systems, contributing to essential physiological processes, and there is a strong demand for methods to detect thiols and to design thiol-responsive materials. While stimuli-responsive hydrogels have been widely explored for biomedical and nonbiomedical applications, thiol-responsive hydrogels for thiol monitoring and detection remain scarcely reported. Herein, we present a straightforward strategy for synthesizing thiol-responsive hydrogels based on poly(2-isopropenyl-2-oxazoline) (PiPOx) bearing reactive 2-oxazoline side groups, cross-linked with Ellman’s reagent containing a disulfide linker. Disulfide bonds are incorporated into the hydrogel network through ester–amide junctions formed between the 2-oxazoline rings of PiPOx and the carboxylic acid groups of Ellman’s reagent. Upon exposure to thiols, the hydrogels undergo disulfide–thiol exchange reactions, releasing thiophenolate moieties and generating red coloration that enables rapid naked-eye colorimetric detection. Unexpectedly, the released thiophenolate groups further react with remaining 2-oxazoline groups of PiPOx, leading to decoloration accompanied by further evolution of the mechanical properties and enhancement of the hydrogel modulus. Consequently, a single thiol exposure induces a time-dependent cascade response involving swelling, softening, and coloration, followed by shrinking, stiffening, and decoloration. The timing of these events depends on thiol concentration, highlighting the potential of these hydrogels for time-programmable sensing and multilevel cascade-responsive materials.

articles.title: Deconvoluting the Convoluted: Structural Ramifications of Postsynthetic Linkage Modification in COF-366-Co Catalysts
articles.abstract: Postsynthetic modification (PSM) is a powerful strategy for modifying properties such as pore environment, stability and catalytic activity in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). While the chemical outcomes of PSMs are well documented, their impact on the underlying crystal lattice is rarely quantified. Yet, when translating modified COF systems toward catalytic applications, such structural changes can impact performance. In this work we interrogate precisely that blind spot for the benchmark electrocatalyst COF-366-Co. We apply three chemical PSM routes to the imine backbone: (i) quinoline cyclization (q-COF-366-Co), (ii) amine reduction (r-COF-366-Co), and (iii) nitrone oxidation (o-COF-366-Co) and investigate chemical as well as structural modifications induced by the functionalization. The catalysts are further investigated toward the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction in an attempt to decouple the multitude of convoluted aspects that affect catalytic activity, stability and selectivity such as particle size, disorder, strain, catalytic environment, and framework stability. Among the series, q-COF-366-Co showed a higher stability toward CO selectivity over time compared to the pristine COF-366-Co at −0.88 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). Investigating q-COF-366-Co further showed, however, that higher functionalization concentrations led to simultaneous increase in disorder and a lower selectivity toward CO during catalysis. This indicates that a balance must be found between functionalization and preservation of crystalline lattice, offering insights into the design importance of maintaining structural coherence when comparing COF-based materials toward applications.

articles.title: Effect of Zinc Incorporation on the Structure, Conductivity and (Electro)chemical Stability of Li6–2 x Zn x PS5X (X = Br, Cl, I) Argyrodite Solid Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Solid-state batteries (SSBs) are currently regarded as a potential alternative to dominant liquid-electrolyte Li-ion batteries, possibly offering higher energy and power densities. In this regard, lithium argyrodite solid electrolytes have received considerable attention due to their high ionic conductivity and mechanical softness allowing straightforward integration into SSB cells. However, they face issues with (electro)chemical stability leading to an accelerated capacity fade. Thus, mitigation strategies have been pursued via chemical substitution. Here we investigate the effects of Zn2+ incorporation into the argyrodite system Li6–2xZnxPS5X (X = Br, Cl, I). We show that there is limited solubility of Zn2+ reaching maximum values of x = 0.2 for Li6–2xZnxPS5Cl and Li6–2xZnxPS5Br while incorporation is not possible for Li6PS5I. Using complementary techniques of X-ray-, neutron powder diffraction and 31P magic-angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in combination with machine-learning based molecular dynamics (MD) we show that Zn2+ incorporation increases the S2–/X– site inversion for X = Br– but has virtually no effect for X = Cl–. Interestingly, the shift of certain vibrational bands observed via Raman spectroscopy measurements correlates well with an increased site disorder. Maximum ionic conductivities are detected for a Zn2+ content of x = 0.1. However, no improvement in cycle life was observed when the material was evaluated in solid-state batteries. Nevertheless, a slight enhancement in stability under ambient conditions was indicated by time-dependent H2S evolution measurements.

articles.title: Impact of Fluorine Content on Structure, Redox, and Electrochemical Performance of Disordered Rock-Salt Li1.25Mn0.5+ y /2Nb0.25– y /2O2– y F y Electrode Materials
articles.abstract: Disordered rocksalt (DRS) oxides are highly promising positive electrode materials for next-generation Li-ion batteries, yet their practical application is severely bottlenecked by the irreversibility of oxygen-redox processes. Fluorination (O2– by F– substitution) represents a powerful strategy to mitigate these drawbacks, but achieving and characterizing high-content fluorine incorporation remains a significant challenge. In this work, we demonstrate the successful mechanochemical synthesis of an extended series of Mn- and Nb-based DRS oxyfluorides, Li1.25Mn0.5+y/2Nb0.25–y/2O2–yFy (0 ≤ y ≤ 0.5). While average structure analysis via powder XRD indicates the formation of a well-disordered solid solution across the entire series, local-structure probes reveal that the ideal cubic NaCl-type model with mixed occupation of the cation and anion sites fails to fully describe the materials. Pair distribution function (PDF) and XANES analyses unveil significant local deviations, highlighted by strongly distorted Mn3+ octahedra induced by the Jahn–Teller effect, while solid-state 7Li and 19F MAS NMR spectroscopies reveal a short-range clustering tendency. Bridging the local and macroscopic scales, dark-field TEM imaging demonstrates that these local arrangements assemble into coherent crystalline nanodomains (1–5 nm), in excellent agreement with the PDF analysis. Regarding the electrochemical properties, this progressive fluorination successfully shifts the redox mechanism from irreversible oxygen oxidation toward more reversible cationic Mn3+/Mn4+ redox, reducing the irreversible capacity and substantially enhancing the average discharge voltage. However, a persistent irreversible capacity loss remains regardless of the fluorine content. This study highlights the critical role of multiscale characterization in understanding the complex local structure–property relationships of highly fluorinated DRS cathodes.

articles.title: Metal–Organic Cages as Porous Photosensitizers for Polyoxometalate Catalysts
articles.abstract: Ionic metal–organic cages (MOCs) offer a unique platform to promote the reactivity of their functional counterions by forming “porous functional salts” (PFSs), but the role of MOCs has so far been limited to structuring and porogenic agent without strong coupling of properties. Herein, we report a new PFS, built from the assembly of the stable and noble-metal-free Keggin-type polyoxometalate (POM) SiW12O404– (SiW12) with a cationic Zr-based metal–organic cage (ZrT-NH2). While pristine SiW12 did not present any porosity or light absorption in the visible light region (above 400 nm), the PFS ZrT-NH2/SiW12 presented an appreciable surface area for a POM-based material (SBET(CO2) = 143 m2/g) as well as a photoinduced electron transfer from ZrT-NH2 to SiW12, which then enabled the formation of reactive species from dissolved dioxygen molecules. This combination made the PFS ZrT-NH2/SiW12 highly potent as a photocatalyst for environmental remediation (evaluated with the model pollutant rhodamine B), as porosity led to a pollutant preconcentration and improved accessibility to the SiW12 catalytic centers, while the photosensitizing effect enabled visible light photodegradation without the need for sacrificial reagents. This method of integrating POMs and functional MOCs offers a promising strategy for the development of functional materials with enhanced porosity and activity.

articles.title: Ultrathin SiO2 Nanofibrous Membranes with Voronoi-like Nanonets for High-Flux Water Filtration and Elution-Free Microplastics Analysis
articles.abstract: Inorganic microfiltration membranes are essential for water purification and microplastics detection; however, achieving high-flux water treatment and enabling straightforward microplastics analysis remain global challenges due to the limitations in the self-supporting nature and structural tunability of inorganic materials. Here, inspired by Voronoi-like natural structures, we report a route to create silicon dioxide (SiO2) nanofibrous membranes with a Voronoi-like nanonet structure (SiO2 VNMs), in which humidity-regulated phase separation and curing generate organosilicon-derived nanonets from silicone oil solution on electrospun and calcined SiO2 fibrous scaffolds. Subsequent calcination converts the organosilicon-derived nanonets into SiO2 nanonets. Benefiting from the self-organized Voronoi-like nanonet architecture, the resulting SiO2 VNMs simultaneously exhibit small pore sizes (≈150 nm), high porosity (≥80%), and an ultrathin thickness (≈1 μm). Consequently, the SiO2 VNMs deliver high filtration flux at low pressure (>6600 L m –2 h–1 at 15 kPa), and even under gravity-driven conditions (>900 L m–2 h–1 at 0.1 m H2O), exceeding that of existing inorganic membranes (6200 L m–2 h–1 at 70 kPa), rivaling the best state-of-the-art organic membranes. Moreover, the ultrathin inorganic structure enables direct on-membrane microscopic and spectroscopic identification of microplastics without elution. This work establishes a new pathway for designing inorganic filtration membranes that integrate efficient water purification with streamlined on-membrane microplastics detection.

articles.title: Seasonal Temperature Fluctuation Enables Persistence of a Model Multi‐Trophic System
articles.abstract: Seasonal thermal fluctuation is a dominant environmental force in temperate ecosystems, yet its role in shaping community dynamics and persistence remains poorly understood. We addressed this question by tracking high‐resolution seasonal dynamics of a model system composed of host Drosophila flies and two parasitoid species attacking hosts at larval and pupal stages respectively. Both parasitoid species increased in abundance steadily during the spring. The pupal parasitoid declined in summer but resurged in autumn, whereas the larval parasitoid declined after a summer peak. The host population remained relatively stable after an initial spring increase. Modelling predicted that the system would collapse under constant cool environments due to excessive parasitism on hosts, whereas pupal parasitoids would be excluded under constant warmth. These predictions were validated by controlled laboratory mesocosm experiments. Life history assays clearly revealed that cool and warm seasons favour different parasitoid species: cooler temperatures resulted in higher mortality of immature larval parasitoids due to host immunity, whereas warmer temperatures narrowed the host exposure window and increased mortality of immature pupal parasitoids. These results demonstrate that seasonal temperature fluctuation maintains a fragile multi‐trophic motif by preventing resource overexploitation and competitive exclusion, highlighting that intra‐annual periodic forcing sustains biodiversity.

articles.title: Bias-free nitrate-to-ammonia conversion exceeding 5% solar-to-ammonia efficiency via perovskite–organic tandem photocathodes
articles.abstract: A high-photovoltage perovskite–organic tandem photocathode coupled with Cu–Ni enables bias-free nitrate-to-ammonia conversion, achieving a peak solar-to-ammonia efficiency of 5.58%.

articles.title: Dual-regulation of chlorine coordination enables a ∼2 V zinc–chlorine battery at −60 °C
articles.abstract: By dual-regulation chlorine coordination, a ∼2 V zinc–chlorine battery was achieved at −60 °C with elevated capacity.

articles.title: Stress fingerprints for electrochemical failure in lithium batteries
articles.abstract: A non-invasive optical sensing strategy enables long-term monitoring of lithium batteries, which decodes mechanical signals into stress fingerprints. These fingerprints distinguish degradation pathways, enabling early prediction of failure mechanism.

articles.title: Unlocking performance and stability in ambient air anion-exchange membrane fuel cells
articles.abstract: An ambient-air high-temperature anion-exchange membrane fuel cell utilizing electronically tuned platinum-group metal Ag-based active sites achieves an outstanding mass activity of ∼51 kW g PGM −1 , robust performance and operational stability.

articles.title: Editorial: Spatial aspects of urban animal ecology and conservation biology, volume II
articles.abstract: Ultimately, how resources are spatially distributed in landscapes, whether it is 44 green infrastructure (Hase, 2026), water surfaces (Harper and Bennet, 2025) To answer these questions researchers should take on an interdisciplinary approach to 105 urban spatial ecology and ask: How can spatial urban ecology identify the specific 106 designs, policies, and community practices that allow animal populations-not just 107 individual animals-to persist in cities under increasing disturbance and climate 108 change? 109 110

articles.title: Lithology influences soil microbial functional potential in subtropical forests
articles.abstract: Lithology shapes the Earth’s critical zone, yet its influence on microbial genomic potential in subtropical forests remains unclear. Here, we quantified soil carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and sulfur (S) cycling functional genes across three contrasting lithologies in southwest China using HT-qPCR. We found limestone soils consistently harbored significantly higher gene abundances than dolostone and clasolite soils. Random forest models explained a substantial proportion of the variation in functional gene pools ( R 2 = 0.87–0.92). Based on these identified key drivers, we propose a Nitrogen availability–Microbial resource limitation–Reactive minerals (NMR) framework, where total dissolved nitrogen fuels activity, eco-enzymatic stoichiometry reflects metabolic adaptation, and iron/aluminum oxides regulate substrate accessibility via physical protection. Overall, specific carbonate rock types should be differentiated when modeling biogeochemical cycles.

articles.title: Multi-method non-parametric assessment of river water-quality trends and change-points in the Danshui River basin, metropolitan Taipei (2010–2026)
articles.abstract: The Danshui River drains metropolitan Taipei, where two decades of expanding sewer connection and riparian constructed wetlands have targeted river pollution. Using a continuous monthly record of 1,921 samples from 11 Ministry of Environment stations (2010–2026), we assessed trends and change-points in six measured water-quality variables and the River Pollution Index (RPI), a composite index calculated from four of them, through a multi-method non-parametric design: the Mann–Kendall and seasonal Mann–Kendall tests, a variance-corrected modified test, Theil–Sen slopes, the Pettitt and sequential-Mann–Kendall change-point tests, Innovative Trend Analysis, and a synchronized-permutation Monte Carlo test of field significance. Suspended solids, ammonia, and five-day biochemical oxygen demand declined at 9, 8, and 6 of 11 stations, each field-significant (Monte Carlo p ≤ 0.006); the basin-mean River Pollution Index fell from 3.83 to 3.20 and the severely polluted sample fraction from 11.1% to 2.5% between the early (2010–2012) and late (2023–2025) sub-periods, the incomplete 2026 record excluded. These declines persisted on the 8 complete-record stations, so they are not an artifact of network turnover. Dissolved oxygen did not improve, even as water temperature rose significantly (+0.15 °C yr - ¹), so oxygen conditions merely held against a warming that lowers solubility. Against this improvement, the coliform group rose at most stations, its change-points scattered across 2013–2024 rather than forming a single step; the largest treatment plant’s effluent-coliform log-removal collapsed after 2024, and river coliform was not associated with rainfall, implicating under-disinfected point-source effluent. The basin’s management priority has shifted from organic and nutrient control toward microbial risk and disinfection.

articles.title: Dryland Soil Rewetting Induces Strong Volatile Organic Compound Emissions With Potential to Form Ozone and Aerosols
articles.abstract: Drylands cover nearly half of Earth's terrestrial surface and are expanding under climate change. Biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) significantly influence atmospheric chemistry, yet microbial VOC emissions from dryland soils remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate VOC emissions associated with petrichor—the characteristic scent following rainfall after prolonged drought—across a steep aridity gradient extending into the Negev Desert. Soil rewetting triggered strong VOC fluxes (1–3.5 nmol m−2 s−1 ground area) dominated by sesquiterpenes and benzenoids, with emission patterns and rates linked to climatic regions, soil aridity, and microbial community composition. Petrichor consisted of a complex bouquet of 58 VOCs, and emission fluxes showed a pronounced initial burst. We upscaled the results to Israel and show that petrichor emissions contribute significantly to ozone and secondary organic aerosol formation potentials, comparable in magnitude to those estimated for anthropogenic VOC sources. Soil aridity shaped VOC chemical composition and emission dynamics, indicating strong microbial and environmental controls on the fluxes. As climate change alters precipitation regimes and promotes dryland expansion, these rainfall‐driven bursts of microbial VOCs may represent an overlooked climate‐microbe feedback influencing atmospheric chemistry and radiative forcing at regional and global scales.

articles.title: Context‐dependent unimodal relationships between ectomycorrhizal dominance and tree species diversity in forest ecosystems
articles.abstract: Our study demonstrates that maintaining an asymmetrically mixed mycorrhizal strategy is critical for maximizing forest tree species diversity, rather than dominance by a single type, particularly for diversity metrics emphasizing common species under water‐ and nutrient‐limited or disturbed conditions. This finding advances our understanding of below‐ground symbiosis regulation on forest diversity, which provides a predictive framework for forest management and diversity conservation. Abstract Most trees form mycorrhizal associations with soil fungi, which regulate tree nutrient acquisition and species coexistence. The ectomycorrhizal (EcM) dominance hypothesis predicts that tree species richness decreases with increasing EcM dominance due to positive plant–soil feedback, whereas the mixed mycorrhizal hypothesis suggests that forests with mixed mycorrhizal strategies sustain more species through nutrient complementarity. In fact, the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive but act jointly to shape diversity as predicted by the asymmetrical unimodal hypothesis. Although this hypothesis has been shown to underlie forest species richness at global scales, whether it consistently favours diversity metrics that differentiate between rare and common species, and how this relationship varies with climate, soil properties and disturbance intensity, remain poorly understood. Using an extensive inventory encompassing 1133 plots in China, we examined the relationships between EcM tree dominance and Hill number‐based diversity metrics. Our results consistently exhibited asymmetrical unimodal relationships, with peak diversity occurring at intermediate EcM dominance (30%–31%), providing robust support for the asymmetrical unimodal relationship hypothesis. Notably, Shannon and Simpson diversities emphasizing common species (i.e. q = 1, 2) showed stronger responses to changes in EcM dominance than species richness (q = 0), a metric more sensitive to rare species. Importantly, these relationships were context‐dependent, being significantly stronger under conditions of lower precipitation and soil nitrogen availability and higher disturbance level. Synthesis. Our study demonstrates that maintaining an asymmetrically mixed mycorrhizal strategy is critical for maximizing forest tree species diversity, rather than dominance by a single type, particularly for diversity metrics emphasizing common species under water‐ and nutrient‐limited or disturbed conditions. This finding advances our understanding of the role of below‐ground symbiosis in regulating forest diversity and provides a predictive framework for forest management and diversity conservation.

articles.title: Functional traits modulate nitrogen addition and climate impacts on growth–mortality trade‐offs in a temperate forest experiment
articles.abstract: Our findings reveal that N enrichment reshapes sapling life‐history strategies by altering trait‐mediated resource allocation and physiological sensitivity to climatic stress, thereby reconfiguring the growth–mortality trade‐off under global change. Abstract The interspecific trade‐off between growth and mortality among tree species is a key dimension of plant life‐history strategies. Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition and climate change are transforming forest population dynamics, yet their interactive effects on sapling growth–mortality trade‐offs remain poorly understood. In this study, we used a 5‐year N addition experiment involving 39,366 saplings from 12 temperate tree species in north‐eastern China. We tested how N addition and climate together changed demographic rates and their trade‐off. We implemented a factorial N addition experiment (0, 50 and 100 kg N ha−1 year−1) and assessed how sapling performance was influenced by climate variability, functional traits, soil properties, topography and neighbourhood competition. Low‐N addition increased relative growth rates by 12.5% (plot‐community level), 6.7% (species level) and 13.3% (individual level) without a concomitant increase in mortality, whereas high N addition elevated mortality by up to 23.7% without significantly enhancing growth, indicating a shift in species' positions within the growth–mortality trade‐off space. Notably, we detected non‐additive interactions between N addition and climate: increased precipitation suppressed N‐induced growth gains but amplified mortality, while warming further constrained growth responses under N addition. A realised interspecific growth–mortality trade‐off was observed under all N treatments, but its strength varied among N addition levels, weakening under low‐N addition and partially re‐intensifying under high‐N addition. Functional traits emerged as the primary proximate driver of the growth–mortality trade‐off, mediating part of the indirect effects of N addition and climate on this demographic relationship. Synthesis. Collectively, our findings reveal that N enrichment reshapes sapling life‐history strategies by altering trait‐mediated resource allocation and physiological sensitivity to climatic stress, thereby reconfiguring the growth–mortality trade‐off under global change.

articles.title: Why finer spatial resolutions do not necessarily improve species distribution models
articles.abstract: Seeking the perfect spatial resolution should not be regarded as the holy grail of ecological modelling. In reality, no such universally optimal resolution exists. Progress is more likely to come from explicitly integrating processes operating across multiple resolutions. In particular, incorporating neighbourhood‐scale variables as predictors in SDMs represents an important step in this direction. Abstract In recent years, there has been growing criticism of using too coarse environmental data in species distribution models (SDMs), especially for sessile organisms such as plants. However, we argue that coarse‐resolution environmental predictors are not only conceptually in line with the idea of SDMs, but may often also lead to more robust and realistic models than those with resolutions approaching the sizes of individuals. We explicitly demonstrate this seeming paradox using a virtual ecologist experiment. The main reason behind this is the disequilibrium between a species' fundamental niche and its realised distribution. While this disequilibrium is well‐recognised in biogeography and metapopulation ecology, its impact on fine‐scale SDMs remains rather neglected. Contrary to recent claims, we therefore suggest that the optimal spatial resolution of predictors in SDMs should be guided less by the size of individuals and rather by the spatial extent required to sustain minimum viable populations. Synthesis: Seeking the perfect spatial resolution should not be regarded as the holy grail of ecological modelling. In reality, no such universally optimal resolution exists. Progress is more likely to come from explicitly integrating processes operating across multiple resolutions. In particular, incorporating neighbourhood‐scale variables as predictors in SDMs represents an important step in this direction.

articles.title: Distinguishing pairwise species spatial associations from multi‐species distribution patterns
articles.abstract: To understand species coexistence, measuring between‐species co‐distributional patterns is valuable. In the present study, we distinguished and separated pairwise species spatial associations (including between‐species distribution co‐occurrence and segregation) from multispecies distributional patterns (including aggregation, randomness and overdispersion) by developing and applying statistical methods that are related to the first nearest neighbour distance (NND). The proposed one‐dimensional and two‐dimensional NND metrics allow ecologists to conduct hypothesis testing on empirical biodiversity data collected via spatially constrained line transect sampling and extensive area surveys, respectively. The application of the proposed metrics on the spatial distribution patterns of common wild frogs in SW China showed that amphibian individuals from different species presented co‐occurring distributional aggregation in both suburban and remote hotspot areas. In summary, our study takes a step forward in clarifying and distinguishing between‐species co‐occurrence and segregation effects from multispecies distributional patterns. All statistics for conducting hypothesis testing on interspecific distributional associations versus multispecies distributional aggregation levels using line‐transect sampling‐based or quadrat sampling‐based biodiversity data were available in the R code of the Supporting Information for immediate application.

articles.title: Smoke signals: Measuring wildlife smoke exposure with animal‐borne and stationary sensors
articles.abstract: Wildfires are becoming larger, more frequent and more severe, producing smoke plumes that degrade air quality hundreds of kilometres away and for days to weeks after an active fire. Despite public health and safety concerns regarding wildfire smoke, we know little about how free‐ranging wildlife experience or respond to these exposures. This disconnect reflects a serious data gap in the form of sparse air‐quality monitors in the remote landscapes that wildlife occupy. Animal‐borne sensors have revolutionized wildlife ecology by quantifying how individuals respond to environmental stressors in real time, but an equivalent tool for smoke exposure has been missing. Here, we present the ‘smoke logger’, a low‐cost air‐quality measurement system for monitoring particulate matter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) that uses a laser‐scattering sensor and records sub‐hourly measurements throughout entire fire seasons. The unit can be mounted on a GPS collar, pairing air‐quality measurements with animal location, activity and other biologged data, or deployed as a stationary unit within an animal's home range to characterize ambient exposure to particulate matter associated with smoke and vehicle combustion. Within an urban‐to‐rural gradient, GPS‐collared mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) with attached smoke sensors reported PM2.5 values that varied with proximity to roads, demonstrating the sensor's ability to resolve fine‐scale pollution gradients. In a remote Utah deployment where the nearest regional monitor was 20 km away, collar readings differed from the nearest network sensor by an order of magnitude, demonstrating the limits of using existing networks to estimate exposure for wildlife research. The smoke logger opens a new pathway for wildlife research by resolving individual‐level smoke exposure at spatial and temporal scales that govern behaviour and physiology. Pairing collar‐measured PM2.5 with location, activity and physiological measurements allows ecologists to test mechanisms previously only inferred, including behavioural responses to degraded sensory environments during smoke events and sublethal health effects that persist long after visible smoke clears. The open‐source design extends to additional pollutants and microclimate variables (e.g. temperature, humidity, volatile organic compounds), and disagreement between logger readings and regional smoke products may itself be ecologically informative, flagging candidate smoke refugia invisible to coarser monitoring approaches.

articles.title: Ribosome remodeling drives translation adaptation during viral infection and cellular stress
articles.abstract: Tsai et al. discover that ribosome composition is reprogrammed in response to intrinsic and external cellular perturbations, which supports ribosome remodeling as a conserved mechanism that enables adaptive protein synthesis during pathogen infection and cellular adaptation.

articles.title: Toward interpretable foundation models for molecular biology
articles.abstract: Interpretability must be a first-class design objective for the next generation of foundation models in molecular biology. In this perspective, Varma and Ideker examine the ways in which it can be built into a model, from biological priors to architecture, and provide a checklist for authors and reviewers.

articles.title: When Clades Collide: Genomic Admixture in Blacklegged Ticks (Ixodes scapularis) From the Great Plains
articles.abstract: Ixodes scapularis ticks transmit a number of pathogens important to human health, including Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, the causative agent of Lyme disease. While I. scapularis is found across the Eastern United States, Lyme disease transmission is largely limited to the Northeast and Upper Midwest and is nearly absent in the South. This indicates that differences in northern versus southern clades of I. scapularis are associated with differences in Lyme disease transmission risk. Ixodes scapularis is undergoing range expansion, including into the Great Plains region of the United States. Determining where I. scapularis populations in the Great Plains originated can inform future risk of Lyme disease transmission in this region. In this study, we use a population genomics framework to characterize diversity, structure and B. burgdorferi infection rates of I. scapularis populations in the Great Plains region. We generated whole genome sequence data and single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) datasets from I. scapularis ticks collected in Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska and South Dakota to compare to publicly available data from across the species' range. Our analysis of 200 I. scapularis SNP datasets indicated geographically well‐defined populations that correspond to historical northern and southern ancestral clades of I. scapularis. Ticks from South Dakota, Iowa and northeastern Nebraska are genetically similar populations from the Upper Midwest, while ticks from Kansas are more genetically similar to ticks from the Southeast. Ticks collected in the east central region of Nebraska, however, represent an evenly admixed population of both northern and southern genomic backgrounds. Analysis of B. burgdorferi reads from genomic datasets shows ~50% infection rate in ticks from Iowa and northeastern Nebraska, whereas ticks from Kansas show no evidence of B. burgdorferi infection. Of note, evenly admixed ticks from the east central region of Nebraska also show no evidence of B. burgdorferi infection. These results provide further evidence that tick genomics may influence traits associated with B. burgdorferi infection status, and thus the potential for Lyme disease transmission. As the range of I. scapularis continues to expand, bringing historically isolated populations into contact, there is a clear need to understand the consequence of genomic admixture for B. burgdorferi transmission potential to inform future risk of Lyme disease in the United States.

articles.title: Pyridyl-functionalized self-assembled monolayers with tunable molecular symmetry enable efficient and robust buried interface for perovskite solar cells
A triple carbonylation cascade converts aldehydes into threofuranoses
articles.abstract: The construction of complex sugars from aldehydes is difficult. Now, a rhodium-catalysed triple-carbonylation cascade is developed that enables the direct conversion of diverse aldehydes into structurally defined 4-carbothreofuranoses in one step. This strategy overcomes long-standing challenges in iterative carbonylation and establishes a modular platform for oxygen-rich scaffold assembly.

articles.title: Controlling reactions via nucleophile sorting
articles.abstract: Controlling the regio-, chemo-, and enantioselectivity of vicinal addition across olefins remains a challenging process. Now, a palladium-catalysed system has been developed, starting from propargylic alcohol precursors, that exploits tiered nucleophilicity between inner- and outer-sphere processes for precise control over the reaction outcome.

articles.title: Evolution of dipole–dipole dynamics in cold ammonia collisions
articles.abstract: Interactions between polar molecules are expected to become increasingly strong at low collision energies through dipole–dipole forces. Now it has been shown that ammonia molecules instead exhibit suppressed dipolar interactions in the cold regime as the dipole moment effectively switches off, as shown by local maxima in the collision cross-sections.

articles.title: Orthogonal nucleophile-ordered assembly for modular access to enantiopure 1,2-amino alcohols
articles.abstract: The selective assembly of multiple chemicals into complex chiral architectures in a single operation is a long-standing challenge. Now a palladium-catalysed orthogonal strategy has been shown to sort and incorporate two native N–H/O–H nucleophiles with similar reactivity, delivering enantioenriched 1,2-amino alcohols and 1,2-diols with high selectivity.

articles.title: Retention and biosynthesis of diverse nitroarenes in Escherichia coli after combinatorial nitroreductase gene deletions
articles.abstract: Nitroarenes are unstable in microbial cultures, limiting the biomanufacturing of these industrially and pharmaceutically important chemicals. Genome engineering of nitroreductase-deficient E. coli strains has now been shown to improve nitroarene retention during fermentation, expanding access to nitro functional group chemistry in whole-cell biocatalysis, metabolic engineering and synthetic biology.

articles.title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture
articles.abstract: Carbon capture with conventional mixed-matrix membranes is limited by the inability to achieve high packing densities of porous fillers while preserving their intrinsic transport properties. Here the authors develop high-performance membranes based on single-crystal covalent organic framework fillers using a weak-interaction inlaying strategy that enables high filler loadings.

articles.title: Diverse infections transcriptionally reprogram the intestinal epithelium and epithelial–immune cell interactions
articles.abstract: In this Resource, Beiting and colleagues provide an atlas of the mouse ileum and mesenteric lymph nodes under homeostatic conditions and during enteric infection. They also present GutPath, a tool that enables interrogation of the dataset.

articles.title: Chemically moulding intermetallics in two dimensions
articles.abstract: An adsorption–conversion strategy enables the synthesis of ultrathin intermetallics across a broad compositional space, from binaries to high-entropy alloys.

articles.title: Loss-reshaped asymmetric nanolight
articles.abstract: Optical loss is usually treated as a limitation. An electrically tunable carbon-nanotube layer instead uses directional dissipation to reshape nanoscale polariton propagation.
